## Build (2026-11-08): Toggle persistence — every display toggle that reset on a fresh visit now remembers its state (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the client only: five view files (client/src/App.tsx, client/src/NetWorth.tsx, client/src/Playground.tsx, client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx, client/src/RothConversion.tsx) plus one new small hook file (client/src/persistedChoice.ts). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, saved field, input, or contract text changed — every change is display state only — so the API contract version stays 163. THE REPORT: the Tax Plan "Yearly spending" per year / per month toggle (on the guided change face's spending question) did not remember its state when the user came back, and the user asked for all of them to be fixed. THE INVENTORY METHOD: the settled inventory's sites were each verified in source as session-only state with a hardcoded default, and the build re-grepped the whole client for the same class (every enum- or boolean-valued state declaration in every view) before editing, so a toggle left session-only would be a miss; the re-grep confirmed the settled list and caught one more of the class, named below. THE TWO MECHANISMS: binary toggles persist in the app's existing server-side fold store (the generic fold state settings blob, read and written through the existing fold actions), one boolean flag each, exactly like the already-persisted unit toggles — a stored entry means the non-default pick, no entry means the current default, so a first-ever visit opens exactly as it does today. Multi-value toggles persist through the new hook, usePersistedChoice: a lazy state initializer reads this browser's localStorage, parses the stored JSON, and validates it against the toggle's allowed values, falling back to the toggle's current default on a missing, corrupt, or unknown value — never a blank or a crash; the setter writes back inside a try/catch, so storage being unavailable simply leaves the choice session-only, as before. Each toggle owns its own flag or key; no toggle's persisted state can leak into another's. THE TWELVE FIXED: four binary toggles in the fold store — (1) the Tax Plan Yearly spending unit, flag "roth.spendingPerMonth" (entry = per month; no entry = per year), the reported one; (2) the Playground spending dial unit, flag "playground.dialPerMonth" (entry = per month; no entry = per year) — a different flag from the spend readouts' own Month / Year pills flag, which is untouched; (3) the Spending quick-view mode, flag "spending.quickModeYear" (entry = the year stack; no entry = the single month); (4) the Net Worth Growth chart overlay, flag "nw.growthOn" (entry = on; no entry = off). Eight multi-value choices in the new hook, each under its own "fp." key — (5) the top-level view, "fp.topView", default the Spending view; (6) the Tax Plan face, "fp.roth.face", default the plan face; (7) the Retirement tab, "fp.retirement.tab", default the projection tab; (8) the Net Worth chart mode, "fp.nw.chartMode", default by-account; (9) the Net Worth explorer columns, "fp.nw.columnsMode", default one column per snapshot; (10) the Net Worth explorer grouping, "fp.nw.groupBy", default by account; (11) the Net Worth change period, "fp.nw.period", default since the last snapshot; and (12) the Playground face switch, "fp.playground.face", default the one-year face — the catch from the build's own re-grep: a two-face display switch of exactly the inventoried class, session-only in source, in neither the settled broken list nor the already-persisted list nor the exclusion list, so leaving it session-only would have been the miss the re-grep exists to prevent. HARD REQUIREMENTS, held: the stored amount is always the annual figure — both spending fields already write annual dollars and switching units never rewrites the stored value, and the unit remains display-only (per month still shows the annual figure divided by twelve and turns a typed monthly amount into annual at exactly monthly times twelve, as before); each persisted unit lives in its own flag or key and touches no other toggle; a missing or corrupt persisted value falls back to the current default; and nothing priced or saved changed shape — no new actions, no new record fields, the fold store and localStorage needing neither. ALREADY PERSISTED, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE AND LEFT UNTOUCHED: the Retirement spending unit (its own settings key, seeded on load and written through its own persist action); the Spending target unit (the fold store's target flag); the Playground spend readouts' Month / Year pills (the fold store's readout flag — distinct from the dial flag added here); the Tax Plan results mode (the Roth UI-state blob, switched and hydrated through its existing path); the Playground section and group folds, the projection panel, and the projection controls (the Playground form snapshot in the Roth UI-state blob — the panel's open state confirmed present in the snapshot the form saves); every other fold-store fold; and the Roth UI-state pieces (the assumptions fold, the growth baseline date, the expanded detail year, the watch-outs and assumptions panels, the custom-ceiling fold), each confirmed hydrated from, and saved back to, its blob. DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS, with their reasons: priced and experiment inputs (the Tax Plan's tax-source, residence, ceiling, survivor, and education dials; the Playground residence pick; the Retirement solver engine and target picks; the lab dials) — computation inputs, not display toggles, and remembering them across visits would silently change what a fresh visit prices; form-entry defaults (the transaction source and kind, the smoothed-bill frequency and paid-by picks, the import template and sign picks) — per-entry starting points for the next entry, not view state; pickers and selections (the month, the year-in-spending year, the explorer date ranges, the plan-preset year, the projection start year) — selections of what to look at, re-made each visit by design; the Spending explorer's grouping — seeded afresh by whichever entry point opens the explorer, each entry choosing its own starting grouping, so a remembered value would fight the entry that opened it; and transient UI (import previews, tab tips, reset confirmations, messages, editor panels, the highlight marker, the cross-view jump target, per-month typing drafts, and the December console's open overlay inside the Tax Plan — a fresh visit opens on the Tax Plan itself, as settled when the console moved in). ## Build (2026-11-08): ChatGPT review MUST-3 — a separate harvested loss no longer erases cash proceeds from a completed sale (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the December core only (server/src/decemberCore.ts — the December case assembly in decemberCaseInputs, plus one new fixture run in the December suite). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, or contract text changed, so the API contract version stays 163. This entry completes a build whose code change was written by a prior builder cut off by a runtime restart before reporting: the change was found in the tree exactly as specified, verified in place hunk by hunk rather than rewritten, and every verification leg below was run or re-run against it. THE FINDING (ChatGPT review MUST-3, settled STAND): the case assembly aggregates the year's NET capital gain — the year-to-date gain less the loss-harvest stray, among the other components — and the shared sale derivation then reconstructed the completed sale's proceeds from that NET figure. A loss harvest is a SEPARATE sale whose proceeds were reinvested: it changes the year's gain/loss ledger, never the cash the completed sale already delivered. Reconstructing the proceeds from the net gain therefore priced the cash-in short by exactly the loss. THE FIX (case assembly only): the net gain stays the figure the tax prices, unchanged. On the entered-basis branch — the only branch where a separate proceeds figure exists to preserve — the derivation now runs on the PRE-LOSS gain (the net plus the loss-harvest stray's own amount, recovered from the same stray the net already subtracts), and the loss rides the basis side instead: the basis the year's sales retired is the completed sale's basis plus the loss, so proceeds minus basis still nets to the net gain while the cash-in counts the full proceeds. On the no-basis fallback there is no separate proceeds figure to preserve — a gain alone rides as proceeds and a loss rides the basis side — so the derivation still runs on the net there, exactly as before; running it on the pre-loss gain would lose the loss entirely. With no loss harvest entered (absent, or entered at zero) the derivation is bit-identical to the old one: the pre-loss gain equals the net, and the basis carries plus zero. No other pricing path is touched — the shared derivation function itself and its load-resolution callers are unmodified. THE FIXTURE (one new run in the December suite, dec-loss-harvest-preserves-sale-proceeds — the December suite's own total grown by one; the tax census is a separate suite and its total is unchanged; synthetic throughout, built on the shared fictional sample household, every coinciding figure constructed arithmetically, never a literal): four legs. The worked-example leg, at a zero draw: the proceeds and the cash-in are the completed sale's full proceeds with AND without the separate loss harvest; only the gain/loss ledger moves — the basis carries the loss and the priced gain is the net — and a pre-fix control prices the old derivation on the net, short by exactly the loss. The headline leg, on the sample-household base: the console's solved draw and the federal tax are the same on the fixed and the pre-fix pricing (the solve prices the same net gain either way), and only the cash-in and the cash left were wrong — restored by exactly the loss; the pre-fix control is priced through the console itself, the same year with the loss netted into the entered gain assembling the exact case inputs the old derivation produced. The no-basis guard leg: with no entered basis the fallback still nets the loss — no proceeds ride, the net loss rides the basis side, and the priced gain is the net. The no-loss control leg: absent a loss harvest, and again with one entered at zero, the derivation equals the old one bit for bit. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the derivation re-read hunk by hunk against the settlement: the net gain untouched for tax, the pre-loss gain recovered from the same stray the net subtracts, the branch condition mirroring the shared derivation's own entered-basis condition exactly, the loss riding the basis side only on that branch, the no-basis fallback byte-identical to the old call; pass 2: the fixture's four legs re-read pin by pin against the settlement's worked example, and the change's scope confirmed — the derivation's outputs are consumed only as the case's proceeds and basis, no other pricing path reads them; pass 3: the executed evidence below, all run after the final source state): the project typecheck is clean for client and server on the final tree. The December suite is green at 95 of 95 — the suite's own count, grown by the one new fixture, named above — and the tax census at 588 of 588, the census run in shards whose slices sum to the suite's own total, zero failures. The regression gate stated its expectation in advance: the fixed set — the December reference case, the prior builds' worked-example legs, the sample household's full plan through both compare scenarios and the funding build, and the varied-return march and its control — contains no loss-harvest case, so ZERO differing leaves were expected, and the gate found exactly that, zero differing leaves out of 6,421, priced before (the one changed file stashed back to the anchor) and after, diffing per-year per-field to the cent. The gate was additionally extended, scratch only and never committed, with the worked example priced before and after as an explicit leg: with the loss, exactly the intended leaves differ — the proceeds, the zero-draw cash-in, the headline cash-in, and the cash left each rise by exactly the loss, and the basis rises by the same, while the priced gain, the solved draw, MAGI, the federal tax, and the credit are unchanged — and the no-loss leg is bit-identical on both trees. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build (sandbox only, never shipping — the live record was never touched): the December reference case reproduces exactly through the staged build's own pricing action (draw, MAGI, taxable income, federal tax, credit, net settle, and cash left all exact, all three cases identical, the contract version in the response provenance unchanged; the figures themselves are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries); the December suite runs live at 95 of 95, including the new fixture; and the worked example prices live through the same pricing action on the sample-household base — the sale-with-loss headline matching the fixture's headline leg to the cent on draw, MAGI, cash-in, cash left, federal tax, and credit. ## Build (2026-11-08): Bucket stacked bar — one de-duplicated horizontal bar at the top of the three-bucket readout (API contract stays 163)

No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored format, saved field, input, or contract text changed — display only, nothing here is saved and no figure feeds the engine — so the API contract version stays 163. THE SHAPE (the user's pick, option A): one horizontal stacked bar whose segments are sized by dollars. The section header, fold toggle, and every existing line of the readout — numbers, provenance taps, and both closing footnotes — are unchanged below the bar; one new footnote line sits directly under the bar. THE ARITHMETIC: the buckets are a lens by horizon, not a partition — the cash reserve sits inside the taxable pool — so the bar partitions the money DE-DUPLICATED from the section's own already-computed values. The first segment is the snapshot's Cash bucket itself. The second segment is the effective taxable pool after the exclusion LESS the cash already shown in the first segment, plus the combined pre-tax pool; the taxable remainder is floored at zero for rendering, the corner being an exclusion large enough to eat into the cash portion of the pool, in which case the bar's total is the floored sum by construction rather than the unfloored identity below. The third segment is the Roth pool. The bar's labeled total is the sum of the three rendered segments, so the bar foots to its labeled total by construction; whenever no flooring applies, that total equals the plan total less the HSA pool, HSA sitting outside the buckets — which the new footnote under the bar states in words. Segment widths are proportional to that total. The second segment is drawn as two adjacent sub-segments — the taxable remainder and the pre-tax pool — so each piece provenance-taps to its own owning field; together they read as the one second bucket. Every figure in the bar and its legend row is a provenance tap using the readout's existing jump helper: the first segment to the Cash set aside field, the taxable sub-segment to the Taxable field, the pre-tax sub-segment to the Pre-tax field, and the third segment to the Roth field, exactly as the corresponding text figures tap below. Each segment's label carries its live amount inside the segment where the segment is wide enough to hold it, and always in the legend row beneath the bar — the first bucket is a small share of the total, so at phone width its amount lives in the legend. Any figure shown in both the bar and the text is identical because both read the same computed values. THE SHORTFALL OUTLINE: the two-year target (twice the live Annual spending dial) is drawn as an outlined, hatched extension — not a filled segment and not part of the total — spanning from the free-cash position to the two-year-target position on the bar's scale. It appears only while free cash is below the target; when free cash meets or exceeds the target no outline is drawn, matching the text line that reads that the two-year target is met. Because free cash and the target are the readout's live values, the outline grows as the Cash set aside entry rises and moves as the Annual spending dial changes, with no new input of its own. NULL HANDLING: if any segment input is missing — cash, taxable, pre-tax, or Roth — the bar is omitted entirely and the text section renders exactly as before; a wrong total is never shown. ## Build (2026-11-08): Internal review round 7 SHOULD-1 — typing a year-to-date sale in-session now re-derives the displayed harvest pool (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the December core (server/src/decemberCore.ts — one extracted exported helper plus one new fixture run in the December suite) and the December view (client/src/December.tsx — the year-to-date sale, sale-basis, and taxable-cash edit handlers, plus one form helper). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, or contract text changed — the save path is untouched, so the re-derived pool never lands in the blob for unedited harvest facts — so the API contract version stays 163. THE FINDING (internal review round 7, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit, and all three reviewer probes independently re-run in the settlement, to the cent): the console's pool fact is the STARTING pool, and the shared pricer nets the year's typed sale out of it, so the starting pool must already contain the sale's proceeds — that is what the load derivation adds back, shared by load and year change. But the pool re-derived ONLY at load and at a year change: the year-to-date sale controls set only the group's edited flag and the field value, so a sale typed after load left the displayed pool at the load-derived value (derived with the sale at zero), and the pricer netted the sale out of a pool that never contained it — the available gain understated by exactly the sale's gain, the S-8 double-netting shape in-session. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's, engine-run; stated here without figures — the settlement's own note carries them): a record current pool with a year-to-date sale partway through the year. Loaded fresh, the pool derives correctly and the year prices correctly; typed in-session, the pool stays at its pre-sale value and the zero-draw harvest and non-draw MAGI read low by the sale's gain. On a smaller-household year where the zero-percent band has room at the headline draw, the console sizes the draw too big by the same amount, and the true pricing at that draw crosses the ACA cliff and forfeits the whole year's credit — the dangerous direction, the same shape as the round-6 year-change finding. A typed LOSS sale errs the other way (conservative — the draw undersized). Typing taxable funded cash has the same display staleness but NO pricing effect: the cash adds equally to the pool and to the basis dollars, so it cancels in the available gain; it rides along in the same re-derivation because the shared derivation takes the whole state, but no pricing leg requires it. The exposure is not hypothetical for this plan: its own household schedule reaches the smaller size in a later year, so its own future ACA years are exposed. THE FIX (the settlement's close, implemented exactly): first, in the December core, the year-change re-resolution's pool re-derivation block — the two per-fact blocks gated on stored-null, unedited, and display-non-null, the basis percent converting against the re-derived or kept pool — is extracted into a new EXPORTED pure helper, rederiveHarvestPool, with the exact same gates and arithmetic; the year-change re-resolution calls it instead of the inline block, a behavior-identical refactor with no other change to that function. Second, in the December view, a form helper beside the edit path converts the just-edited form to state, runs the shared helper with the console's stored provenance, the per-fact harvest edited flags, and the record facts for the form's own year, and writes the pool and basis percent back into the form exactly as the year-change handler writes its re-resolution back; it returns the form unchanged while the Tax Plan record has not loaded. The three year-to-date controls — realized capital gain/loss so far, cost basis of the sales behind that gain, and taxable cash for the year — now route through it after setting the group's edited flag, as before. The re-derivation is an overlay re-derivation, NOT a user edit of the pool: it never sets the harvest edited flags and never disturbs the year-to-date group's edited semantics; it never re-derives over a pool the user owns (edited in this console or stored non-null) and never revives a deliberately cleared pool. The round-6 behaviors are untouched: the flush-then-reset on year change and the year-to-date reset with pool re-derivation on a flip behave exactly as built, and the save still persists the stored pool for unedited harvest facts, so a reload re-derives the pool from the saved sale exactly as after a load. THE FIXTURE (one new run in the December suite, dec-ytd-typed-sale — the December suite's own total grown by one; the tax census is a separate suite and its total is unchanged; synthetic throughout, built on the shared fictional sample household, every coinciding figure constructed arithmetically, never a literal): five legs. The type-a-sale-in-session leg (larger sample household): a load with no sale derives the record's pool as-is; the sale typed in-session, modeled by running the helper over the loaded state with the typed figures, re-derives the pool and basis percent to exactly the load-with-sale values, and the zero-draw pricing and the headline figures equal the load-with-sale state's to the figure; the stale control — the same typed state WITHOUT the helper — prices the defect's understated harvest and MAGI. The draw-and-cliff leg (smaller sample household): the re-derived state's headline draw is the correct draw, its MAGI lands on the target under the cliff, its credit is kept, and its harvest at the headline equals the full zero-draw harvest; true pricing at that draw keeps the credit; the stale control's headline draw overshoots by exactly the understatement, and true pricing at the stale draw crosses the cliff with the credit gone. The loss leg: a typed loss sale re-derives the pool by its smaller proceeds with the basis percent converted on the same dollars, pricing the correct harvest against the stale control's overstatement. The funded ride-along leg: the sale typed beside taxable funded cash re-derives the pool with both add-backs, the cash at full basis converting the percent back to the record's own. The guard legs: with the harvest edited flags set, a sale edit leaves the pool and basis percent unchanged; with a stored non-null pool in provenance, they stay; with the displayed pool and basis percent cleared, they stay cleared. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the extracted helper re-read line by line against the flip's original inline blocks, gate for gate and operation for operation, and the year-change re-resolution's call site confirmed as the only change to that function; pass 2: the client wiring re-read control by control — the helper's provenance, flags, and record-facts arguments, the write-back shapes matching the year-change handler's, the three controls' routing, the edited-flag semantics untouched, the save path untouched; pass 3: the executed evidence below, all run after the final source state): the project typecheck is clean for client and server on the final tree. The December suite is green at 94 of 94 — the suite's own count, grown by the one new fixture, named above — and the tax census at 588 of 588 — the census in the full grid, the memory-killed shards re-run sequentially, zero failures. ## Build (2026-11-08): Internal review round 6 SHOULD-2 — the harvest starting pool now re-derives on a year change, and the year-to-date figures are year-stamped facts (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the December core (server/src/decemberCore.ts — shared harvest-pool derivation, stamp-aware year-to-date save, year-change re-resolution, one new fixture run in the December suite) and the December view (client/src/December.tsx — one new edited flag for the year-to-date group, set by each of its six controls and by Reset, reset on a year change, passed to the stamp-aware save). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, or contract text changed — the save still writes the same blob shape, and the provenance type gains six fields the console already carried in the form — so the API contract version stays 163. THE FINDING (internal review round 6, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit, and the worked example independently re-run in the settlement, to the cent): the load resolution derives the harvest STARTING pool from the record's current pool plus the year's year-to-date sale proceeds and taxable cash funded (the settled S-8 derivation — year-specific add-backs), but the year-change re-resolution documented the pool as year-independent and never touched it. A fresh load at a year and a flip into that year from the previous year therefore showed different starting pools for the same year and the same record, and the flipped year priced its harvest from the old year's pool. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's, engine-run, on the fictional sample household): a record current pool with a year-to-date sale behind it — the load derives a starting pool enlarged by the sale's proceeds, with the basis share converted on the same dollars; flip to the next year with no sale there and the pool stayed enlarged; a fresh load at the next year derived the un-enlarged pool. With the harvest on and the zero-percent band non-binding, the flipped year harvested more than the fresh load, overstated MAGI by the whole sale gain, and sized the draw too small by the same amount (conservative direction). The error scales with the prior year's year-to-date sale proceeds. THE YTD ENTANGLEMENT (decided in the settlement): the review's "re-derive the pool using the new year's year-to-date figures" cannot mean reading them from the record — the record carries no year-to-date figures at all. The year-to-date figures ARE year-stamped facts: the S-8 derivation's "year-to-date sale only" and the pricer's netting of "the year's taxable sales" both assume the form's figures belong to the displayed year. THE FIX (the settlement's close, as one mechanism on a year change): first, the year-to-date figure group (interest, ordinary dividends, qualified dividends, capital gain, sale basis, taxable funded cash) resets to the new year's answer — blank, since no record source carries them, until the user types them; second, the harvest starting pool (and basis percent) re-derives from the reset figures when overlay-derived (stored pool null), exactly as a fresh load would — a user-entered or previously saved non-null pool stays, consistent with the load resolution's "a non-null pool always wins" rule, and a deliberately cleared pool is never revived; third, the save preserves the year-to-date figures stamp-aware (the carry-in pattern, one edited flag for the group), so a flip-back before any save at the new year restores the old year's figures from stored provenance. The year-change handler flushes the queued save for the old year first (carrying the old year's figures under the old stamp) and only then resets the flags, the blanking itself setting no flag. The other year-to-date lines (other ordinary income, tax-exempt interest, Social Security) are not in the group and keep persisting across a flip, as before. THE FIXTURE (one new run in the December suite, dec-harvest-pool-switchback-ytd — the December suite's own total grown by one; the tax census is a separate suite and its total is unchanged; synthetic throughout, built on the shared fictional sample household, every coinciding figure constructed arithmetically, never a literal): pins the round trip through the console's own paths (save plus re-resolution plus save plus load) across its legs: the typed save leg; the load leg deriving the enlarged pool; the flip leg (the pool equals the fresh load's pool, amount and basis percent, and the year-to-date figures blank); the pricing leg (harvested gain and MAGI equal the fresh load's, while a hand-built stale-pool state prices the defect's figures); the flip-back leg (all six figures plus the pool and basis percent restore with no intervening save); the re-save and reload legs; the ordering leg (the queued payload holds the typed figures under the old year; a post-reset save persists blank); the no-re-stamp leg (an edit at the new year does not carry the old year's figures into the new year's stamp); and the guards (a saved pool stays, a deliberately cleared pool is never revived, a user-edited pool stays). Two pre-existing save round-trip fixtures were updated to pass the group's edited flag on their typed-save legs, their header comments updated: their old "plain console answer — passes it through as displayed with no edited flag" statement is superseded by the settlement (the year-to-date group now has provenance). VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the fix hunks re-read line by line against the settlement, the shared derivation identical to the load's arithmetic, the re-resolution's year-to-date reset and pool re-derivation with its gates, the stamp-aware save, the client's flag lifecycle, the preseed and placeholder provenance, the Reset path, and the two updated fixtures; pass 2: the change set re-verified hunk by hunk and the new fixture's legs pin by pin, with the pre-existing year-gated fixture unmodified beside it and no other finding's scope touched; pass 3: the executed evidence below, all run after the final source state): the project typecheck is clean for client and server. The December suite is green at 93 of 93 — the suite's own count, grown by the one new fixture — and the tax census at 588 of 588 — the census in the full grid, the two memory-killed shards re-run sequentially in finer slices, the slices summing to the suite's own total, zero failures. The regression gate priced the fixed set before and after — the December reference case, the sample household's full plan through both compare scenarios and both funding builds, and the varied-return worked example — with exactly 15 differing leaves out of 6,392, all intended and named in advance: the flip's pool and basis percent moving to the fresh-load values, the year-to-date figures blanking, the flipped pricing moving to the fresh-load figures, and the new-year save payload blanking, everything else bit-identical. The December reference case reproduces exactly in the gate probe on both trees (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). LIVE CHECKS on the staged build (sandbox only, never shipping — the live record was never touched): the December reference case reproduces exactly through the console's own pricing action (draw, MAGI, taxable income, federal tax, credit, net settle, and cash left all exact, contract 163 in the response provenance); the December suite runs live at 93 of 93, including the new fixture; the worked-example pricing leg runs live through the pricing action on the flipped state and the fresh state (harvested gain and MAGI identical to the cent, while the stale-pool control state still prices the defect's figures); and the save round trip runs live through the console's own save and load actions. ## Build (2026-11-08): Internal review round 6 SHOULD-1 — a carry-in or students typed in the session no longer survive a year change and price the wrong year (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the December view (client/src/December.tsx — the year-change handler) and the December core (server/src/decemberCore.ts — one new fixture run in the December suite). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, or contract text changed — the save still writes the same blob shape, and the flag reset is session state only — so the API contract version stays 163. THE FINDING (internal review round 6, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit, and all four legs independently re-run in the settlement, to the cent): round 5 closed the year-change path for LOADED (unedited) carry-ins and students, but NOT for values the user TYPES in the session. The edited flags are session-level state booleans, reset only on load or on a compare-and-swap conflict reload — not on save success (the save handler only adopts the new provenance) and not on year change — so a typed value keeps its display value across a flip, the year-change handler copies the re-resolved value into the form only for unedited fields, and the save's edited branch takes the display value with no stamp check at all. A value typed for one year keeps pricing the next year after a flip, and one ordinary edit there re-stamps it under the new year, where it is lost to its true year forever after a reload. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's, engine-run): a typed 2027 long-term carry-in of $10,000 — autosave under 2027 — flip to 2028 and the display KEEPS $10,000 — pricing of 2028 (married filing jointly, ages 60/58, other ordinary $100,000, an $8,000 long-term gain): with the stale carry-in MAGI $98,000, net long-term gain −$2,000, federal tax $7,400; without it MAGI $108,000, net long-term gain $8,000, federal tax $7,640. Edit anything at 2028 and the autosave re-stamps the blob to 2028 with the $10,000 carry-in. Flip back to 2027 looks fine in-session — the flag is still true — reload opens at the blob's year (2028), switch to 2027 and the display carry-in is null: permanently lost for 2027, wrongly carried by 2028. The students leg does the same with typed students of $5,000 (AOTC-eligible) plus $3,000, the record holding none: 2028 with the stale students taxes $5,540 vs $7,640 without them, and after a reload the 2027 students are gone. The draw and cliff harm is the dangerous direction, opposite to round 5's conservative one: the 2028 December draw sized off the stale carry-in is $33,346 vs the true $23,346 — $10,000 too large — and the true 2028 priced at the wrong draw lands at MAGI $159,720, over the $154,720 cliff, credit $0, against the true 2028 at the right draw at MAGI $149,720 with the credit kept; federal tax $16,026.95 vs $13,911.20, $2,115.75 more. A user who acts on the mis-sized draw forfeits the whole year's credit. The control — the loaded (unedited) round trip — still holds under the round-5 fix. THE FIX (the settlement's close, in two parts): first, on a year change, flush any save queued by a real edit at the old year — the queued payload was built from the old year's form with the old flags, so it saves the typed values under the old year's stamp; if it stayed queued, the first edit at the new year would supersede it with a payload built from the new form (flags now false) and the typed values would never land. The flush mirrors the unmount flush: clear the shared save timer so the debounce cannot fire the same payload a second time, then send through the retrying flush send — or defer behind a save still in flight, exactly as the unmount cleanup does. Second, reset the edited flags to false, so the new year starts with all flags false and the round-5 machinery (re-resolution plus stamp-aware save) governs it; the flip-back then restores from stored provenance exactly as the loaded path does. The reset is scoped to the year-dependent provenance fields (the four carry-ins plus education students) — the balances flag is untouched (round 3 settled the balances' survival deliberately) and the harvest flags are untouched (round-6 SHOULD-2, separate). The re-resolution on the flip passes all-false flags for those five fields and the display updates are unconditional for them. Two ordering requirements, both verified by a live leg: the flush runs with the old flags still in force — the payload captures the flags at queue time, so a save built after the reset would persist stored values instead of the typed display values and the typed edit would be lost — and the debounced autosave must not fire after the flip with the new form: the handler clears the shared timer and the sticky dirty flag outright, the form updates directly instead of through the edit path, and the autosave effect returns early on the new form, so no save fires with the new form until the next real edit. The reset runs only when the Tax Plan record has loaded and the re-resolution runs; when the record has not loaded, the year changes alone and the fields keep their stored values and the flags with them. OUT OF SCOPE, recorded: the balances save branch and the balances patch (preserved); the harvest pool's year behavior (round-6 SHOULD-2, separate); the first-year save-persists-null behavior (the record owns the first-year value by design — not a defect). THE FIXTURE (one new run in the December suite, dec-stored-carryin-switchback-typed — the December suite's own total grown by one; the tax census is a separate suite and its total is unchanged; synthetic throughout, built on the shared fictional sample household, every coinciding figure constructed arithmetically, never a literal): pins the typed round trip through the console's own paths (save plus re-resolution plus save plus load) — the gap the round-5 fixture (which pins only the unedited path) left open — across seven legs: the typed save leg (the edited branches take the display values, so the blob stamps the typed year and holds both values); the flip leg (with the flags reset, the display clears for both the carry-in and the students); the edit-at-the-new-year leg (the payload the edit builds stamps the new year with nulls for both fields — no re-stamp); the pricing legs to the cent (the cleared display prices the true figures; the stale carry-in and the stale students price the defect's figures); the flip-back leg (no save landed at the new year: the stored values restore exactly); the re-save and reload legs (the re-save holds both values under the typed year's stamp, and the reload holds them); and the ordering leg (the queued payload built at type time, with the old flags, holds the typed value under the typed year — while the same display saved after the flag reset, against a stored provenance that does not yet hold the value, persists null, which is why the handler flushes the queued payload before resetting the flags); plus the draw and cliff leg on the fictional sample household (the stale carry-in sizes the draw $10,000 too large and the true year at that draw lands over the cliff and forfeits the whole credit). ON THE EDIT-AT-THE-NEW-YEAR LEG, read carefully: the leg asserts on the payload the edit builds and does NOT adopt that payload as the new stored provenance before the flip-back. A landed save at the new year re-stamps the blob to the new year with nulls — the round-5 null rule, pinned by the existing fixture's mismatch legs — so no round trip, typed or loaded, can restore after a landed save at the new year. The guarantee, exactly as for the loaded path, is the round trip with no intervening save at the new year; the edit leg pins the no-re-stamp property instead. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the fix hunks re-read line by line against the settlement, the flush-before-reset with its timer clearing and deferral, the five-flag reset scoped and record-guarded, the all-false re-resolution and unconditional display updates, the balances block and harvest flags untouched; pass 2: the change set re-verified hunk by hunk and the new fixture's legs pin by pin, with the pre-existing year-gated fixture unmodified beside it and no other finding's scope touched; pass 3: the executed evidence below, all run after the final source state): the project typecheck is clean for client and server. ## Build (2026-11-07): Internal review round 5 SHOULD-1 — the December save is now stamp-aware, so a stored carry-in or student survives a year change and switch-back instead of being destroyed by it (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Changes in the December console's save path (server/src/decemberCore.ts — decemberStateForSave, plus one new fixture run in the December suite) and the December view (client/src/December.tsx — the year-change handler). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored blob format, or contract text changed — the save still writes the same blob shape, and the stamp it now consults is the saved blob's own tax year the console already derives — so the API contract version stays 163. THE FINDING (internal review round 5, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit): round 4's SHOULD-1 stamped saved December state with its tax year and gated the year-change reset so a stored carry-in restores only into its stamped year. That holds at the function level — but NOT in the live console for non-first years. The year-change handler patched the stored provenance itself to nulls whenever the stamp year differed from the new year, and there is no refill path for a non-first year's carry-in (the record overlay fills carry-ins only for the plan's first year) — so a saved non-first-year carry-in was destroyed on switch-back. The root cause is the save: decemberStateForSave persists the stored value for every unedited field with no year check at all. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's, engine-run): a saved 2027 long-term carry-in of $10,000, stamp 2027 — load 2027 and the display shows $10,000 — switch to 2028 and the display clears to null, correctly — the handler patch nulls the stored carry-in (the stamp stays 2027) — the autosave persists null — switch back to 2027 and the display carry-in is null — the save persists null — reload null. Permanently lost. Pricing of 2027 (MFJ, ages 59/57, other ordinary $100,000, an $8,000 long-term gain): with the carry-in MAGI $98,000, net long-term gain −$2,000, federal tax $7,400; without it MAGI $108,000, net long-term gain $8,000, federal tax $7,640. The console overstates MAGI by $10,000 and tax by $240, and the cliff-sized draw is $10,000 too small (conservative direction). The education leg does the same with typed students: saved 2027 students of $5,000 (AOTC-eligible) plus $3,000, the record holding no 2027 students — switch to 2028 and back and the display is null, re-saved null, reload null. Permanently lost. The control — the plan's first year — restores both carry-in and students via the record overlay, no loss. THE FIX (the settlement's close, in three parts): first, decemberStateForSave is stamp-aware — an unedited carry-in or student persists its STORED value only when the stored stamp equals the display year, otherwise it persists NULL — not the display value: on a stamp mismatch the display is either null or an overlay re-fill the save must not own (the new year's record students, and the record's first-year carry-ins when switching INTO the first year), and persisting the display would make the console own a record value and break the first-year discipline — the round-4 patch comment itself states this rule. Second, the destructive patch in the year-change handler is removed; the balances patch and the balances display update are preserved untouched. Third, a pure year change must not trigger an autosave: the handler clears the dirty flag and updates the form directly instead of through the edit path (still disarming the reset guard). The evidence for the third part, verified by direct source read: the edit path sets dirty unconditionally; the debounced autosave effect fires on every form change while dirty on a short timer; and the dirty flag is STICKY — a successful save never clears it (only the conflict path does) — so merely not setting dirty is insufficient: once anything was typed, a year flip fires an autosave persisting the cleared display under the new year, and the review's round-trip leg includes exactly this autosave step. The pending payload from any prior real edit stays queued for the unmount flush, and the next real edit re-dirties. OUT OF SCOPE, recorded: the harvest pool's save behavior (uncounted in round 5, no wrong pricing demonstrated — the pool branch keeps persisting the stored value); the balances save branch and the balances patch (preserved); the first-year save-persists-null behavior (the record owns the first-year value by design — not a defect). ## Build (2026-11-07): Internal review round 4 SHOULD-3 — a blank expected return now seeds the blended default server-side in planInputsFromSaved, never 0% (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine changes in the plan-input construction (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts — planInputsFromSaved and one optional transient on its saved-record shape), plus one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored figure, or contract text changed — the save/request schema keeps the return nullable exactly as before — so the API contract version stays 163. THE FINDING (internal review round 4, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit): planInputsFromSaved resolved a null expected return with a fall-through to zero, so a record whose return was never entered priced as no growth at all when it reached the server unseeded. The schema's own contract for the field says a null stays the blank and the caller's default applies, and every client path honors that by seeding a blank return with the blended expectation of the household's stocks mix before pricing or saving — but the server actions did no seeding: the compare action passes its base through the compare-scenario construction into planInputsFromSaved unseeded, and the server's only seeding lived in the fresh-user reset defaults. In-app paths are protected by the client seeding, which is why this is SHOULD, not MUST — but on the API surface a blank return silently priced a flat portfolio forever, which no one who leaves the return blank means. THE SETTLEMENT'S DIRECTION (decided against schema rejection, for a stated reason): when the record's return is null the household's own return is unrecoverable by any means — the blended default is what the client substitutes in the same situation — and rejection would contradict the schema's own caller's-default contract and make the server stricter than the client, so the fix seeds instead of rejecting. THE FIX: planInputsFromSaved now resolves a null return to blendedExpected of the record's stocks mix, falling back to blendedExpected(STOCKS_PCT_DEFAULT) when no mix rides the record — the identical substitution the clients apply, fallback included. The mix is an optional transient on the saved-record shape, in the same family as the yield fallbacks the shape already carries: the Roth record itself holds no mix (the household's mix lives on the Retirement record), so a caller holding both records may thread it; absent or null, the default-mix blend applies. An entered return — including an explicit zero — prices exactly as entered; only the null path moves. Every pricing path (compare, funding, the march, the optimizer candidates) builds its engine inputs from this one construction or spreads it, so the seed reaches every path exactly once. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, tax-blank-return-seeds-blended, the tax census's own total grown by one — the December suite is a separate suite and its total is unchanged; synthetic throughout — built on the shared golden compare base the census already prices, every comparison an identity between legs priced in the same run, no figure pinned as a literal): priced through the compare action's own path, the null-return base prices exactly the leg whose return is entered as the blended default — ending wealth and net cost identical to the cent, their differences zero — while the explicit-zero leg prices strictly lower ending wealth than the null leg, so null no longer coincides with zero; construction-level pins resolve null to the blended default, resolve null with a threaded half-and-half mix to that mix's blend, and pass an entered zero through untouched. ## Build (2026-11-07): Internal review round 3 SHOULD-1 — the December console no longer carries the plan's starting pre-tax balances into a later tax year (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine changes in the December console's record resolution (server/src/decemberCore.ts) and the December view (client/src/December.tsx), plus one new fixture in the December census. No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored figure, or contract text changed — the balance fields already exist on every surface that reports them; only which years the record's balances answer for moves — so the API contract version stays. THE FINDING (internal review round 3, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit): the December console's first-open preseed copied the Tax Plan record's pre-tax balances — the plan's STARTING balances — into the console's prior-Dec-31 balance fields for whatever tax year the console was set to, with no dependence on the year, and the year-change re-resolution deliberately never touched the balances (they were classified year-independent), so a future RMD-age year priced its RMD on a balance from years earlier. The record's balances never roll forward: they are the plan's start-of-plan figures. The console's tax year accepts a wide range, so a future RMD-age year is a supported choice — and its RMD then priced on a balance predating the year by the whole intervening span. The RMD is ordinary income, so the console's headline draw — cliff-sized on the understated MAGI — could overshoot by the understatement and forfeit the year's credit while the console reported the year safely under it. The everyday path is unaffected (the default year is the current year, and at the household's ages no RMD prices either way), which is why this is SHOULD, not MUST. THE FIX (the settlement's close, following the carry-in's first-year gate term for term): the record's balances answer the console only for the plan's first year (the record's execution year). The shared year-dependent overlay — used by load resolution and by year-change re-resolution alike, so the two can never disagree — now resolves the record's per-owner balances into null console fields for the first year only; for any other year the fields stay unanswered unless the user enters the true prior-year-end balance. The first-open preseed fills the balances only when the December year is the execution year, the same strict gate the carry-in preseed already uses. The year-change re-resolution takes a balances flag alongside the existing per-field flags: for an unedited balance it restores the console's own saved split, and then — only when the new year is past the plan's first year — it clears a balance that IS the record's starting balance, so the new year prices no RMD on the stale figure and the fields read blank (not entered). A balance that differs from the record's facts is the console's own answer and is never touched, including a balance the user entered for the old year; a balance the user edited in this session is never touched either. When the year moves back to the first year the overlay re-fills the balances. The client handler copies the re-resolved balances back into the form like the carry-ins, and it follows a cleared balance into the stored provenance — otherwise the next save would persist the stale starting balance for the unedited field and the reload would revive it; only a cleared or unchanged-from-stored value is written back, so a load-derived split and an overlay re-fill are never promoted into provenance. THE FIXTURE (one new fixture in the December suite, the December suite's own total grown by one — 88 to 89; the tax census is a separate suite and its total stays 586; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it and from the law table): the settlement's worked example — a fresh console for a far-future RMD-age year on the sample household — pinning the load overlay (first year resolves, later and earlier years stay unanswered, an entered value including an explicit zero always wins), the year-change clear and the round-trip re-fill, an edited balance surviving, the console's own stored balance surviving, and the RMD pricing (the stale RMD on the starting balance at the Uniform divisor for the worked-example age, and no RMD priced on the post-fix blank). The first-year case stays an approximation, as the settlement notes: even in the plan's first year the preseeded balance is the record's snapshot-era balance rather than a Dec-31 balance, so an RMD-age household opening in the first year gets an approximate RMD (months of growth, not years) — the fix confines the record's answer to the first year and does not pretend that case is exact. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the fix hunks re-read line by line against the settlement after the final state; pass 2: the change set re-verified hunk by hunk and pin by pin against the settlement and the recorded evidence — every fix hunk, the new fixture with its hand derivations checked against the gate-after engine output, the gate's intended leaves, the scrub result, and the unchanged contract; pass 3: the executed evidence below, all run after the final source state): the regression gate priced the fixed set before and after — the December reference case, the December S-8 entered, resolved, and control legs, the sample household's full plan through both compare scenarios and both funding builds, the varied-return march and its control, the worked examples, and the P-S12 and P-S5 harvest legs — and the only differences are the fix's intended changes, named in advance: the first-year load overlay resolving the balances, and the year-change clear of the preseeded starting balances. The December reference case reproduces exactly on the final tree, and the December S-8 legs are bit-identical before and after. The tax census is green on the final tree at 586 of 586 — the full suite in slices, with the concurrency-killed chunks re-run sequentially and any chunk that died even alone re-run in finer slices, the slices summing to the suite's own total — and the typecheck is clean for client and server. The December reference case reproduces exactly live through the December projection action on the console state as recorded, in all three of its cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries); nothing was saved — the action is compute-only. LIVE ACTION CHECKS on the staged build (sandbox only, never shipping): the December projection action reproduces the reference exactly; the worked example was driven live through the same action — the stale starting balance prices the stale RMD and the post-fix blank balance prices no RMD, to the cent in both cases; the year-change re-resolution and the load overlay are pinned by the census fixture, which runs the same functions the client calls. No new UI surface was added — the only visible change is a later-year console opening with blank balance fields and their existing "blank means not entered" hints, so the hands-on feel pass is a read of the unchanged balance section. ## Build (2026-11-07): Internal review round 2 SHOULD-3 — the gain harvest now nets the year's own sales, in the pricer and in the projection walk (API contract stays 163)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine changes in the single-year pricer and the projection walk (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts), the December case assembly (server/src/decemberCore.ts), one new fixture plus one re-pin in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts). THE FINDING (internal review round 2, SHOULD — settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit): pricePlaygroundYear's harvest block sized the harvest from the pool less its basis with no subtraction of the typed sale, and the projection walk repeated the defect — the template's harvest pool amount rode the spread untouched into every year, the carried basis dollars stepped up by harvested gains only and were never reduced by the year's sales, and the repeated sale's basis came from the template alone, scaled only by the balance cap — so the harvest re-priced gains the sale had already realized. The documented rule says otherwise (the v113 build note caps the harvest by the remaining pool's unrealized gain, the pool less the year's taxable sales and basis dollars), December's S-8 states the pool fact as the starting pool, and the plan march agrees (it caps its harvest by the post-settlement balance less its basis dollars). THE FIX (the settlement's close, with two corrections recorded in the fixture note): the pricer nets the year's typed sale — proceeds and retired basis — out of the pool before sizing the harvest, flooring the basis percent at zero only so an underwater pool's ratio above one hundred rides through; the walk carries the harvest pool's balance forward beside its basis dollars, passes each year's current pool and ratio to the pricer, derives the repeated sale's basis from the tracked ratio, and retires that basis after the year. December passes the starting pool straight through and the pricer does the one netting — pre-netting in December as well would net the year's sales twice, so the pre-netting is removed and every comment describing it now states the new arrangement; the load-resolution conversion of the record's current pool to the starting pool is unchanged. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, the suite's own total grown by one; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it and from the law table): the settlement's worked examples — a single-year sale-plus-harvest year pinning the remaining-gain harvest, the MAGI, and the credit, and a two-year walk pinning the first year's harvest and the second year's zero harvest, zero sale gain, and zero end balance. The settlement's second-year premise is corrected in the fixture note: its figures assumed the first year harvested the pre-fix room figure, while under the fix the first year harvests only the remaining gain, so the second year enters at a ratio of exactly one hundred rather than underwater — the pinned figures are the true post-fix ones. The P-S12 leg B pin is re-pinned as part of this build (the sale consumes the whole pool, so the harvest is zero and the sub-text still foots); the P-S5 harvest leg's loader agreement and priced flag are unchanged, and its second walked year's priced gain merely moves between the typed sale and the harvest with its total, AGI, and MAGI bit-identical. ## Build (2026-11-06): Parity re-review R2 — the Playground projection now carries the gain-harvest pool's stepped-up basis forward, so a harvest cannot repeat a gain it already realized (API contract stays 162)

All user-entered data, no external source. One engine change in the Playground projection walk (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts, projectPlaygroundYears) and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, stored figure, or contract text changed — the per-year projection inputs already carried the harvest pair; only the basis percent each walked year is priced with now moves — so the API contract version stays. THE FINDING (parity re-review SHOULD-FIX R2, settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree — the pushed HEAD plus the uncommitted R1 build — before any edit): the walk spread the original template into every year, harvest pool and basis percent included, and updated only the taxable balance after sales, so each projected year re-sized its harvest from the original unrealized gain. A harvest sells and immediately repurchases, so the proceeds rightly do not reduce the balance — but the repurchased shares carry a basis stepped up by the gain realized, and nothing carried that increase forward; the plan march has always handled it (its tier step-up and basis-dollars increase after a harvest). On the settlement's worked example the second year harvested the first year's whole gain a second time, overstating its MAGI by that gain and understating its ACA credit by the pinned shortfall. THE FIX (the settlement's close): the walk carries the harvest pool's basis dollars forward separately from the taxable balance — initialized from the template's pool and basis percent, re-derived into each year's basis percent at full precision (a percent rounded to cents would misstate the remaining gain on a large pool by whole dollars), and stepped up by each year's priced harvested gain, never past the pool. The pool amount itself still repeats as the template states it, and a template with either harvest fact absent walks bit-identically to before. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, the suite's own total grown by one; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it and from the law table): the settlement's two-year projection — joint filing at the sample ages, the sample ACA household size and family benchmark, no Social Security, no conversions, no regular sales, no return, ordinary income at two and a half times the filed ordinary dividends, and a harvest pool of five times the filed dividends at the sample basis percent. Year one harvests the pool's whole unrealized gain inside the zero-percent room and the pool's basis steps up to the whole pool, the taxable balance ending unchanged (the proceeds are reinvested, not spent); year two enters at a basis percent of one hundred — pinned on its own walked inputs — harvests nothing, and prices its MAGI at the income alone with the credit the settlement derives. ## Build (2026-11-06): Parity re-review R1 — a newly realized capital loss now carries its own carryforward out of the single-year pricer, so the Playground projection no longer drops it and the December readout reports it (API contract 161 → 162)

All user-entered data, no external source. One engine change in the shared single-year pricer (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts, pricePlaygroundYear), its contract and description text (server/src/apiContractCore.ts, server/src/actions.ts, server/src/decemberCore.ts), and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts). No action signature, request or response shape, paste payload field, database schema, or stored figure changed — the carry-out fields already exist on every surface that reports them; only their values for one input class move — but the priced behavior the contract text describes did change, so the API contract version bumps. THE FINDING (parity re-review MUST-FIX R1, settled STAND; every cited site verified against the current tree before any edit): the pricer ran the shared capital-loss ledger only when an entering carryforward was positive, so a year whose own typed sale realized a net loss, with no carry-in entered, priced its §1211(b) allowance in-year but reported a zero carry-out; the projection's year-to-year chain then carried that zero forward, and the following year priced with no allowance at all — on the settlement's worked example that alone pushed the second year's MAGI one dollar over its ACA cliff and erased its whole credit. The December console reuses the same pricer and surfaces the same carry-out fields, so its readout dropped a newly realized loss the same way. THE FIX (the settlement's close): the ledger also runs when the year's own typed result is a net loss — the harvested gain the pricer can add is never negative, so the year's total result is negative only when the typed result already is, and the gate reads the typed result alone. With a zero carry-in the ledger's trial transform is the in-year computation term for term (net result, claimed allowance, and Washington base all identical), so the loss year's own pricing does not move; only the year-end reconciliation gains a figure — the new loss's carry-out, fixed once against the year's final taxable income before the allowance, with only the used part of the allowance consumed, exactly as an entered carry-in reconciles. A year with no carry-in and no loss of its own prices and reports bit-identically to before, and the plan march, the work-years roll, and the execution-year re-solve keep their own ledger gates, untouched; the re-review's other two findings are untouched. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, the suite's own total grown by one; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it and from the law table): the settlement's two-year projection — joint filing at the sample ages, the sample ACA household size and family benchmark, no Social Security, no conversions, no return, other ordinary income one dollar over the second walked year's cliff (the cliff read from the law table in-case), a starting taxable balance and a typed sale of half the filed ordinary dividends against a basis of the filed dividends whole — a long-term loss of half the filed dividends. Year one claims the statutory allowance and carries out the loss less the allowance (taxable income before the allowance is far above the cap, so the whole allowance is used); the sale exhausts the balance, so year two's repeated sale scales to zero, but the chained carry-in — pinned on year two's own walked inputs — claims its allowance again: year two's MAGI is the other income less the allowance, under the cliff by the allowance less the one dollar, its credit is the benchmark less the second year's flat applicable percentage in its top band times that MAGI, and its ending carryforward is the entering one less the used allowance. One derivation note, verified against the engine rather than taken from the settlement: the walked first year prices its cliff off the newest guideline row (the projection's one sanctioned convention difference), so its cliff equals the second year's and it prices a credit at the first year's table's flat top-band percentage — identical before and after the fix, like every first-year figure; the settlement's no-credit first year is the single-year lookback pricing of the same template, which the fixture's single-year leg pins separately (the same carry-out, the prior guideline row's cliff, no credit, over that cliff either way) — the surface the December console reads. A utilization leg prices the same loss with no other income: the allowance is claimed in AGI but used by no taxable income, so the whole loss carries out — the reconciliation, not the claim, fixes the figure. A gain control (the same sale at a quarter of the filed dividends as basis) prices no allowance and no carry-out, exactly as before. ## Build (2026-11-06): Parity audit P-S10 — the Playground projection income chart carries the whole preferential stack, so its bars, legend, and spoken summaries foot to the MAGI line (API contract stays 160)

All user-entered data, no external source. One client rendering change — the projection chart's segment definitions in the Playground view (client/src/Playground.tsx) — and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts). No engine, pricing rule, result field, action signature, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed: every figure the corrected chart needs was already on the projected year's priced result, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S10, settled STAND; verified against the current tree before any edit): the projection chart's segment list held six segments only — interest, the non-qualified part of dividends, other ordinary income, taxable Social Security, RMD, and pre-tax money out — while the line drawn across the same bars reads each year's MAGI, which is adjusted gross income plus tax-exempt interest, with the gross income itself carrying the qualified dividends and the priced gains net of the capital-loss allowance. No bar could foot to its own line, nothing on the chart said the bars were ordinary income only, and on the settlement's worked example — one projection year carrying only the sample household's filed yield income — the bars stood below the line by exactly the whole qualified part of the dividends, before any gain, tax-exempt interest, or allowance widened or moved the gap. This is the same defect the round-2 S-9 fix closed in the Playground's single-year stack and P-S9 closed in the Tax Plan chart; the projection chart never received it. THE FIX: the segment list gains the four preferential segments, decomposed from each projected year's priced result exactly as the single-year stack decomposes them — qualified dividends as their own segment in the same colour the other two charts use; long-term gain as the positive part of the priced NET result, not the typed sale gain (the walk nets an entering loss carryforward against the year's sale before the stack prices, and a harvested gain adds to it, so the typed figure alone would overstate or understate the priced part); tax-exempt interest as its own segment; and the allowance as a hatched negative top segment in the same hatch style and slate the Tax Plan chart uses. The segments now sum to MAGI exactly as the shared pricer composes it — the ordinary pieces plus qualified dividends plus the positive net gain less the allowance make the gross income, and the tax-exempt interest completes MAGI — and the legend and each bar's spoken summary derive from the same segment list as the bars themselves, so all three foot together by construction. The chart's display-window trim, its scaling, the balances chart below it, and the walk itself are untouched; the trim's activity test already consulted the priced gains and MAGI, so no year's display window moves. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, the suite's own total grown by one; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it): four legs, each priced by the projection walk itself, the exact function the chart renders. The first leg is the settlement's worked example — the sample template year carrying only the filed yield income, projected for the template year alone: the six pre-fix segments sum to the filed interest plus the non-qualified part, MAGI is the interest plus the whole filed dividends, the fixed stack sums to MAGI exactly, and the gap the fix closes is exactly the qualified part. ## Build (2026-11-06): Parity audit P-S9 — the Tax Plan income-stack chart decomposes the preferential stack from the priced result, so its bars, legend, and spoken summaries foot to MAGI (API contract stays 160)

All user-entered data, no external source. Three display-only fields added to the plan-year detail the chart reads (server/src/taxEngine.ts), the chart's segment definitions in the Tax Plan view (client/src/RothConversion.tsx), and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no pricing input, pricing rule, action signature, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S9, settled STAND; verified against the current tree before any edit): the Tax Plan income-stack chart decomposed each year's bar from the wrong figures — its long-term gain segment read the year's GROSS realized gains, and its capital-loss allowance segment read a detail field that reports the allowance only when a loss carryforward entered the year, reading zero on a no-carry-in loss year even though pricing had taken the allowance against ordinary income. This is the same defect the round-2 S-9 fix closed in the Playground single-year stack; the Tax Plan chart never received it. On the settlement's worked shapes the bars therefore did not foot to the chart's own MAGI line: with an entering carryforward absorbing the year's gains, the bar topped the line by exactly the gross gains pricing had already netted away; in a no-carry-in loss year the bar sat below the line, showing the gross loss as a segment while omitting the allowance the year had priced. THE FIX: the plan-year detail now also carries the priced figures the decomposition needs, mirroring the single-year pricer's own result fields — the priced NET long-term result (the year-end loss ledger's net result when a carryforward entered; the gross total itself when none did, the ledger transform being the identity there), the priced capital-loss allowance in every year shape (the ledger's allowance when it ran; otherwise the same transform's no-carry-in branch — the filing status's statutory cap bounded by the year's net loss, zero when there is none — where the previously read field reported zero), and the qualified part of the year's dividend income (the part pricing puts on the preferential stack). The chart's segments now read those priced figures, following the round-2 pattern term for term: the non-qualified part of dividend income (the dividend total less its qualified part) on the ordinary stack, qualified dividends as their own segment, long-term gain as the positive part of the priced net result, and the allowance as a hatched negative top segment in the same hatch style the single-year stack uses. The legend and each bar's spoken summary derive from the same segment list as the bars themselves, so all three foot to MAGI together by construction. The year-math panels elsewhere in the view that also read this detail were left untouched — a separate surface, outside the finding's scope. THE FIXTURE (one new census fixture, the suite's own total grown by one; synthetic throughout — built on the shared fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it): three legs. A control leg — the plain sample household's first year, where nothing needs netting — pins that the decomposition moves nothing: the fixed and pre-fix stacks both sum to that year's MAGI. The carry-in leg spends exactly the filed ordinary dividends for one year, drawn from the sample taxable pool at its sample basis share, with an entering long-term carry-in of that same dividends figure: the sale's gross gains are priced and wholly absorbed by the carry-in, the year's MAGI is the negative allowance alone, the fixed stack sums to it exactly, and the pre-fix form computed in-case tops the MAGI line by exactly the gross gains. The fixture's note records one qualification against the settlement's sketch: that year has no taxable income before the allowance, so none of the priced allowance is used and the loss carries out whole rather than reduced by it — the overshoot the finding is about does not depend on the difference. The no-carry-in loss leg reuses the census's own underwater construction at its dividend-income leg — a pool swept by surplus to a basis above its balance, then halved by a negative return, so the year's spending sale realizes a loss with no carry-in: pricing takes the capped allowance, the fixed stack sums to MAGI exactly, and the pre-fix form computed in-case sits below the line with its allowance segment at zero. The fixture's arithmetic replicates the chart's segment definitions term for term beside the engine's priced detail, so the chart's footing is pinned, not just the engine's figures. ## Build (2026-11-06): Parity audit P-S8 — the remembered projection template carries the full input set, so a reload reprices the projection identically; the is-current check compares through the full mapping (API contract 159 → 160)

All user-entered data, no external source. The stored projection template's shape and parser (server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts), the template mapping moved into a new shared core (server/src/projTemplateCore.ts) that the Playground imports (client/src/Playground.tsx), the API contract version (server/src/actions.ts), the contract prose (server/src/apiContractCore.ts), one new tax-census fixture and one extended UI-state fixture (server/src/taxFixtures.ts, server/src/extendedFixtures.ts) — no engine, pricing rule, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed; the stored template rides the existing UI-state write, whose request schema now names the added fields, so the API contract moves 159 → 160. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S8, settled STAND; verified against the current tree before any edit): the remembered projection template — the snapshot the projection chart runs from, stored with the Playground's UI state — was written through a mapping that carried only the base dials: the filing and ages, the income and Social Security dials, the conversion and spending draw, the stock sale, the pre-tax balances, the beneficiary facts, the ACA household size and benchmark, the state rate and residence, the itemized components, the education rows, and inflation. Every other fact the form's own input builder supplies was dropped on save: the ACA filing-settlement facts (the advance credit taken, the coverage-month reduction, the enrollment premium the settlement caps at), both health premiums, all four loss carry-ins (the federal short/long pair and each character's Washington portion), the RMD already received, the dependent's MAGI, both funding draws, the reinvested-yield flag, the annual spending, and the gain-harvest pair. On reload the restored template repriced every projected year without those facts — silently, because the panel's is-current check compared the stored template against the live dials through the same lossy mapping, so the two lossy forms agreed and nothing announced the change. P-S4 and P-S5 both recorded the symptom from their own surfaces. THE FIX: the mapping now carries every field of the engine's year inputs the walk reads, in both directions, and lives in a shared server core the view imports, so the accuracy fixtures pin the exact production functions the view calls rather than a copy.
