Within a session nothing changes: a template captured and used without a reload priced identically before this build. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (one new census fixture; synthetic throughout — built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, every figure its own or constructed arithmetically from it): a joint template year late in life, both Medicare flags explicitly off against the age rule so the marketplace prices, the primary's pre-tax balance set from the filed dividends at the age's Uniform divisor so the gross RMD is exactly the filed dividends, two fifths of it already received and inside other ordinary income, a stock sale at half the filed dividends, entering carry-ins at multiples of the sale gain, the advance taken at a third of the family benchmark, the enrollment premium distinct from the marketplace premium, a dependent MAGI, both funding draws, the yield reinvested, the sample annual spending, and a per-person Medicare premium that prices only in the second leg where an override turns Medicare on. The extended UI-state fixture's template case now stores the full shape and round-trips it field for field, plus a legacy-shape leg pinning each added fact at its no-fact value with the base dials intact. ## Build (2026-11-06): P-S6 (parity audit SHOULD) — a compare scenario with an explicit taxable override no longer inherits the base's snapshot-threaded cash sleeve (API contract stays 159)

All user-entered data, no external source. One fix-up block in the shared compare-scenario construction (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no action signature, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE DEFECT (settlement S6, verified against the current tree before any edit): the spend-from-cash sleeve is a snapshot-derived transient, threaded onto a plan only when its taxable balance follows the snapshot — the action layer threads the snapshot's cash bucket less the exclusion on that path alone, and the Tax Plan save path writes a zero sleeve beside a typed taxable balance. The compare construction merged each scenario's overrides over the resolved base and re-derived the blank-yield fallback from the scenario's own pool, but carried the base's sleeve verbatim, so a scenario with an explicit taxable override priced a pool with no snapshot context while spending the base pool's sleeve out of it: on the settlement's worked example its first spending year took the full cash share from the phantom sleeve, never realized the gain the direct pricing of the same shape realizes, and read low on federal tax by the settlement's first-order amount and on ACA MAGI by the whole unrealized gain. THE FIX: the construction now revisits the sleeve beside the fallback re-derivation — when a scenario's overrides carry an explicit taxable balance (an explicit null included: it prices the pool at zero, where no sleeve can spend) and do not themselves supply a sleeve, the merged sleeve is reset to zero, the sleeve an explicit balance implies under the app's own construction rules. A sleeve a scenario supplies itself is a passable transient, used exactly as supplied and never overwritten — the same rule the fallback re-derivation gives a scenario-supplied fallback. A scenario that leaves the taxable balance untouched keeps the base's sleeve bit-identically, its pool being the base's pool; basis-tiers mode is unaffected either way, because the engine derives the tiers sleeve from the cash tier and ignores the transient. The Monte Carlo stats path builds its scenarios through the same construction and inherits the correction. THE FIXTURE (compare-sleeve-revisit-s6) is built on the shared fictional sample household in its resolved compare shape, with flagged variations the note states: spending from the first march year, so the priced pool is the entered pool at its entered basis (the settlement's posture, before any work-year surplus could land at a full basis); an other-ordinary-income level constructed from the sample figures that fills the zero-percent gains band on the ordinary stack alone, so every priced gain lands at the year's preferential rate; no marketplace benchmark entered, the case isolating the sleeve while ACA MAGI is still priced and pinned; and the explicit pool taken as a fixed fraction of the sample taxable balance. It pins the revisited sleeve at zero on the merged shape, on the engine inputs, and on the sleeve derivation; the first march year spending its whole deficit by sale with no cash share; the pre-fix form reproduced through the passable transient — the same explicit pool carrying its own sleeve at the base's threaded size — and the gain, MAGI, and tax deltas against it, the tax delta exactly the preferential rate times the gain delta and the gain delta the settlement's first-order term plus the tax-channel feedback the note derives (the corrected leg's larger bill is itself paid by gain-realizing sales, where the inherited-sleeve leg pays part of its bill out of the sleeve at no gain); the untouched scenario's sleeve and first year bit-identical; an explicit-null override's sleeve revisited with its zero pool; a scenario's own smaller sleeve standing exactly as supplied; and the tiers leg's derived sleeve and first year unchanged. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the settlement and audit texts re-read and every cited site verified against the current tree, the defect reproduced on a scratch probe across the no-override, explicit, own-sleeve, null, and tiers legs before the edit; pass 2: the same probe re-run after the edit — the untouched and tiers legs bit-identical, the explicit leg's sleeve zero with its first year repriced, a scenario-supplied sleeve standing at both sizes tried — and the fixture's hand derivation re-checked against the priced figures; pass 3: the full-suite results below, the live action checks, the change set confirmed to be exactly the one construction block, the one fixture, and its sample-household imports inside the pre-existing uncommitted set, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server and client) on the final tree; tax census fully green on the chunked source grid — every chunk passing with its teeth check ok and each chunk's reported suite total agreeing, the suite's own total grown by the one new fixture; supporting suites all green — the extended fixtures, the retirement fixtures and their teeth check, the December console fixtures, both CAS suites, and the UI-state fixtures (the standalone whole-suite tax teeth helper was killed by this machine's known memory limit, the standing limitation the chunked census exists to route around; the census carries its own teeth check per chunk, all ok). The December reference case reproduced exactly live through the projection action in all three of its cases against the stored console state (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). Live action check on the worked example: a compare run on the fixture's base prices the untouched scenario with the threaded sleeve in its echo, and the explicit-pool scenario with a zero sleeve in its echo — not the inherited size — its first-year federal tax and AGI matching the fixture's pins to the cent, and its first-year tax above the fixture-pinned pre-fix form by exactly the pinned delta. The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. No hands-on feel pass: no client surface is touched — the change is server-side scenario construction only. ## Build (2026-11-05): Follow-up re-pin (P-S4 scope) — one older projection fixture re-pinned to the corrected P-S4(d) Medicare-override semantics; no engine change (API contract stays 159)

All user-entered data, no external source. ## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-S5 — the projection-year loader loads the projected year's full inputs, so post-capture dial edits no longer leak into a loaded year (API contract stays 159)

All user-entered data, no external source. Finding (parity audit S5, settlement verdict STAND): the projection-year loader (loadProjYear in client/src/Playground.tsx) set only a listed subset of the projected year's inputs — filing status and tax year, both ages, the two Social Security dials, the conversion and spending draw (the draw added by R3-M1 / P-M4), stock sold and basis, both pre-tax balances, and the ACA household size. Everything else the bar had priced stayed at whatever the form was already holding: all five income dials, the ACA benchmark, both health-premium dials, the advance credit taken and the coverage-month reduction, all four capital-loss carry-ins, the RMD already received, the dependent MAGI, both funding draws, the reinvested-yield flag, the state rate and residence, all four itemized components, the education rows, and both sole-beneficiary facts. The failure direction is post-capture edits: capture a template, then edit a dial, and clicking a bar loaded a year priced with the edit instead of the bar's own inputs. Worked example from the settlement, on the fictional sample household: a template captured with interest at the sample's smaller round figure, the interest dial then edited up by an amount ten times that figure, and the loaded year's AGI came out higher than the bar by exactly the edit's increase, because the loader never set the interest dial at all. Fix: the loader now loads the projected year's full inputs, field for field like the paste loader — filing status, tax year, both ages; the five income dials with their provenance recorded as typed (the paste loader's reading, so a later Tax year change never re-derives over them); both Social Security dials; the conversion and the spending draw; stock sold and basis; both pre-tax balances; the ACA household size, the benchmark (its source record cleared, as the paste loader clears it), both health-premium dials with the enrollment premium riding the marketplace premium dial exactly as the form's own input builder reads it, the advance credit taken, and the coverage-month reduction; all four loss carry-ins — for a year past the first, the walk's chained entering ledger, not the template's original figure; the RMD already received; the dependent MAGI; both funding draws; the reinvested-yield flag; the state rate, residence, all four itemized components, and the education rows; and both sole-beneficiary facts. Two inputs have no dial of their own and ride the session holds the paste loader already uses: the year's annual spending (held the P-S2 way — a stored-restored template carries no spending figure, so the hold clears and the record-or-dial resolution applies, exactly as before this build) and the gain-harvest pair (held the P-S3 way when either fact is present, cleared when neither is). The two Medicare checkboxes are tri-state, so the loader resolves each as the year's own override-or-follow-age answer — an explicit answer only where the projected year's flag disagrees with that year's age rule, follow-age otherwise — which is also what carries the P-S4(d) walk override into a loaded year. One sanctioned difference remains, unchanged from before this build: the single-year pricer applies its one-year lookback ACA convention while the walk prices under the caller's convention, so a loaded projected year can price its credit under the single-year rule — the loader's job is that the year's inputs are the bar's, and they now are. The cash-left strip's wording now says "the loaded year" where it said "the pasted year", since a projection load holds spending through the same slot. No paste-format, action-signature, schema, or engine change; the API contract stays 159. New census fixture tax-engines-playground-projection-loader-full-inputs-ps5 (suite total 571 → 572), its figures constructed arithmetically from the shared fictional sample household's filed-return and plan constants and the sample ACA benchmarks — no household figure anywhere as a literal: a multi-year walk of a fully populated template whose projected year carries something on nearly every input, hand-derived bar identities for AGI, MAGI, and ACA MAGI, and a loader reconstruction (every dial field re-read from the projected year's stored inputs and repriced through the production single-year Playground pricer) agreeing with the bar on AGI, MAGI, ACA MAGI, federal tax, net tax bill, ACA credit, cash in, cash left after tax, cash left after health premiums, cash left against spending, priced gains, and net health premium with a total difference of zero cents; the worked-example leg (the loaded year repriced with the interest edit applied) landing higher than the bar by exactly the edit's increase, on both AGI and ACA MAGI; a benchmark leg (the loaded year repriced with the single-person benchmark in place of the family's) dropping the priced credit by exactly the two benchmarks' difference; a pre-fix-subset leg (only the old subset carried, everything else at a fresh form's blank) pricing AGI at the conversion plus the sale gain alone, short of the bar by exactly the dropped income components, with no federal tax — the stale-leak shape pinned from the other side; carriage pins on the projected year's chained carry-in (the template's figure exhausted in the first year), its cash draw (the template's whole draw spent in the first year), and its Roth draw; a harvest leg (the projected year prices its bar's harvested gain exactly, and the same year with the harvest facts dropped prices none); an education-and-state leg (a typed state rate and one eligible student ride the load, agreeing with its bar on AGI, federal tax, state tax, and net tax bill to the cent); and a Medicare-override leg (a template year whose primary is explicitly on Medicare before the age rule would put them there, walked one year — the bar's gross health premium is the marketplace premium plus the whole per-person Medicare premium, the loader's override-or-follow-age resolution loads the same, and a follow-age-only load prices the marketplace premium alone, short by the whole per-person premium). A source-invariant comment block in the fixture pins the client half (the full field list, the typed provenance, the two holds, the Medicare resolution), the same pattern as the P-M4 fixture, since the census cannot execute the client loader. Teeth: corrupting any of six key pins (the worked-example difference, the zero load difference, the Medicare legs, the subset shortfall, the benchmark credit drop, the no-harvest-facts gain) makes the fixture fail, verified. Verification (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the loader re-read field by field against the form's own input builder, the paste loader, and the settlement text, including the Medicare resolution, the hold semantics, and the one sanctioned ACA-convention difference; pass 2: the full change set and every verification result below re-read end to end, with the changed-file set confirmed to be exactly the two files this build owns inside the pre-existing uncommitted set; pass 3: the live drives, the feel pass, the counts, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server and client) on the final tree; tax census run over the chunked source grid — 571 of 572 fixtures pass, including the new one — with one pre-existing failure in an older projection fixture (proj-from-age-early-late-and-clear), proven unrelated to this build three ways: it passes at the pushed HEAD the parity builds anchor on; it fails in this tree with this build's changes present but passes in a scratch copy of this same tree with only the P-S4(d) Medicare-override walk carry neutralized, because that fixture's template states an explicit Medicare-off answer at an age past the age rule, which under the P-S4 semantics now carries through the walk as an override — the fixture predates those semantics and repairing it belongs to the P-S4 finding's scope, not this one, so it is reported here rather than fixed. One census chunk was killed by the known chunk-size memory limit on this machine and its fixtures were re-run in finer slices, all passing. Supporting suites via the staged build's self-check action all green: December fixtures, extended fixtures, retirement fixtures (both Trinity mixes inside tolerance), Roth CAS fixtures, Retirement CAS fixtures, UI-state fixtures, and the integrity suite with no violations. The December reference case reproduced exactly live (all three cases, headline and alternates) against the stored console state, read and never written (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). Live action checks: the new fixture's projected year priced through the production action surface reproduced its bar exactly — AGI, MAGI, ACA MAGI, federal tax, ACA credit, cash in, and every cash-left figure — and the same request carrying the post-capture interest edit priced AGI and ACA MAGI higher by exactly the edit's increase, the settlement's worked example reproduced through the live actions. Hands-on feel pass at phone width in the staged build: starting from the remembered template, the interest dial was edited up to a large round figure after capture (the form repriced around the edit), then a later projection bar was tapped — the loaded year came back with the template's own interest figure on the dial, its income summary restored, and its tax and MAGI matching the bar's label to the dollar; before this fix the dial would have kept the edited figure and priced the loaded year off the bar by the edit. One qualification the feel pass surfaced, belonging to a separate queued finding and deliberately not fixed here: in that sandbox session the panel's template had passed through the remembered-form storage round-trip, whose template mapping (per finding S8) omits the December-era facts — the entering carry-ins, the RMD already received, the funding draws, and the premium facts — so a template re-captured from that restored form would project without those facts, while the loader itself, given a projected year carrying them, is the behavior pinned by the fixture and reproduced in the live checks above; S8's own build owns that mapping. The staged audit's one advisory is pre-existing and unrelated: a phone-width horizontal scroller inside the Spending Quick view chart, recorded by earlier builds and left as-is. Scrub: boundary-aware scrub (patterns.txt + patterns-supplement.txt, scrub-push workspace) over this entry AS WRITTEN, after it was written, confirms ZERO matches; every amount above is stated as a relation to the fictional sample household's figures or as a statutory constant, and no household figure appears. Contract: stays 159 — no action signature or paste-contract change (the loader is client code over the same inputs type). Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-S4 — the Playground projection stops repeating one-year facts into every future year: loss carry-ins chain, cash/Roth draws no longer repeat without a balance behind them, the Medicare override is carried, and the RMD-already-received balance half is pinned as already closed by R3-S2 (API contract stays 159)

All user-entered data, no external source. The projection walk in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (projectPlaygroundYears) and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no client code, action, paste payload, December surface, database schema, or stored figure changed, and no action signature or paste contract changed, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S4, settled STAND in substance with one sub-case rejected as written): the projection repeated one-year facts into every future year in four ways. VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE (the pushed HEAD plus the uncommitted P-M2/P-M3/P-M4/P-M5/P-S1/P-S2/P-S3 builds, which moved nearby code), the four sub-cases stand as follows. (a) RMD ALREADY RECEIVED — REJECTED AS WRITTEN, AND ALREADY CLOSED IN ITS REAL HALF: the finding's income half is wrong — the received amount sits inside the entered other-ordinary income by the input contract, so the repeated income cancels the repeated netting exactly and no projected year's income is understated; the proposed close (zeroing the netting after the template year) would overstate each year's AGI by the received amount. The balance half was real at the audit's anchor, where the walk depleted the pre-tax balance by the priced result's NET RMD, but the R3-S2 per-owner rewrite already closed it in the current tree: the walk's balance math reads each owner's GROSS RMD (the same two per-owner calls the single-year pricer makes) and never the net, so the balance already depletes by the gross figure the settlement prescribes. No code change; the fixture pins the disposition, including the rejected close as a counterfactual. (b) LOSS CARRY-INS NEVER CHAINED — STOOD: the walk re-supplied the template's entering carry-ins to every projected year, so a banked loss sheltered the same gains year after year instead of being used up. THE FIX: the walk now carries four chain state values (federal short-term and long-term, Washington short-term and long-term), seeded from the template, supplied to each year's priced inputs in place of the template's, and replaced after each priced year with that year's own priced carry-outs — the pricer's loss ledger already computes the carry-outs every year; the walk simply stopped discarding them. A template with no carry-ins walks bit-identically (a control leg pins this). (c) CASH/ROTH DRAWS REPEATED WITH NO BALANCE BEHIND THEM — STOOD: the template's cash and Roth funding draws were re-supplied to every projected year, manufacturing spendable cash the tracked balances never funded (the walk tracks no cash balance at all, and it never subtracted the Roth draw from the tracked Roth balance, which grew undrawn while the draw repeated). THE FIX: the cash draw prices in the walk's first year only — the year the template describes — and is zero thereafter, there being no tracked cash balance that could fund a repeat; the Roth draw prices in the first year in full and in each later year only up to the tracked Roth balance at that year, and each year's priced Roth draw now leaves the tracked Roth balance (floored at zero) before that balance grows, so the draw both shrinks and is capped by the balance behind it. The year's priced inputs now carry these draw figures explicitly, zero included, where they previously carried the template's by spread. (d) THE MEDICARE OVERRIDE DISCARDED FOR THE AGE RULE — STOOD: the walk re-derived both Medicare flags from each year's age, so a template year that explicitly answered the Medicare question (on Medicare before the age threshold, or off it past the threshold) had its answer silently replaced in every projected year — most visibly, a per-person Medicare premium priced from the threshold age even when the template year already paid it, and priced at all in later years when the template year had explicitly opted out. THE FIX: a template flag counts as an override exactly when it disagrees with the age rule at the template's own age, and an override is then carried to every projected year in both directions; a flag that merely agrees with the rule is the follow-age default and the walk keeps pricing each year by that year's own age, exactly as before. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (one new fixture, four legs; synthetic throughout — every leg built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts or constructed arithmetically from its figures in-case, never written as a figure of its own): (A) an RMD year late in life on the Uniform table, the pre-tax balance set to a multiple of the household's filed ordinary dividends so the first year's gross RMD is a round multiple of them, the already-received amount a fixed fraction of that gross and sitting inside the entered other-ordinary income as the contract requires — the first year pins gross, net, AGI, and an end balance depleted by the GROSS (with the anchor's net-depletion form computed in-case beside it), and the second year pins the cancellation: its AGI equals its gross RMD exactly, while the rejected close (netting zeroed) is computed in-case and overstates that AGI by the received amount. (B) a working-age year with other-ordinary income at a multiple of the filed dividends and a stock sale each year at a fraction of them against the sample taxable balance, entering with a short-term carry-in of a multiple of the yearly gain — the chain uses the carry-in up over three years (each year's entering carry-in is the prior year's carry-out; the gain is fully sheltered while the carry-in lasts, the statutory allowance prices against ordinary income until the carry-in runs out, and the third year's tax is the settlement's figure for this shape), with the pre-fix repeated-carry-in form computed in-case (its third year still shelters the whole gain and takes the allowance) and a no-carry-in control whose second year starts empty and prices its gain whole. (C) a no-income year at the sample spending with a cash draw and a Roth draw set from the filed dividend figures against the sample Roth balance at a zero return — the cash dial prices in the template year and zero after, the Roth draw prices in full each year while the balance lasts and the tracked Roth balance falls by exactly each year's draw, the first walked year reproduces the single-year pricer's own result for the template to the cent, and an exhaustion leg (the starting Roth balance set to a smaller filed figure) caps the second year's draw at what is left and the third year's at zero. (D) a joint year with the primary on Medicare before the threshold age by explicit override and the spouse not, a per-person Medicare premium set as a fraction of the filed dividends, walked past both spouses' threshold crossings — the override flag and the premium price from the template year on (the pre-fix age rule pricing no premium in the two years before the primary's threshold), the spouse's premium joins at her own threshold age and the premium doubles, a follow-age control (no override: the flag off before the threshold) walks bit-identically to the pre-fix form, and an override-off leg (a template past the threshold with Medicare explicitly off) keeps the flag off in later years and prices only the spouse's premium when she crosses. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (570 → 571 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-projection-one-year-facts-ps4, pinning all four legs end to end, each leg's pre-fix or rejected form computed in-case beside the corrected one so the delta is pinned, not just the new figures. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the finding and settlement re-read against the current tree, sub-case (a)'s disposition re-traced through the R3-S2 walk code and confirmed in the anchor's own history (the anchor subtracted the net figure; the current tree subtracts each owner's gross), the chain/draw/override edits confined to the walk's state, its per-year inputs, and the Roth end-balance line, with every downstream consumer (stop rules, replace mode, balance caps, the year loader) re-traced; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the live drives, the feel pass, the counts re-read, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 571/571 on the chunked source grid (24 chunks, every fixture exactly once, teeth ok on every chunk); supporting suites via the staged build's self-check action: December 88/88, extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 with both Trinity mixes inside tolerance, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations. Corruption teeth: seven of the new fixture's pins (the second RMD year's end balance, the chain's third-year entering carry-in and third-year tax, the second year's cash dial, the exhaustion leg's second-year Roth dial, the override leg's premium at the template age, the override-off leg's flag past the threshold) each fail the fixture when mutated. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the combined worked-example year (the carry-in, cash-draw, and Roth-draw facts of legs B and C on one year) prices the chained first year exactly — the statutory allowance against ordinary income, federal tax at the sheltered figure, cash in counting both draws, cash left of the cash in less the tax — with provenance reporting API contract 159 and its emitted paste carrying the carry-in and both draws in full; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. HANDS-ON FEEL PASS on the staged build at phone width, driven in the audit sandbox (its writes never ship): pasting the live action's own emitted worked-example paste into the Playground's paste box loaded it with the loaded note printed, and the single-year strip priced the year exactly as the live check (cash left per month at the year's cash left less its sheltered tax, over twelve); switching to the projection face and re-running from the year above re-based the walk on the pasted template year. One qualification the feel pass surfaced, belonging to a separate queued finding and deliberately not fixed here: in that sandbox session the panel's template had passed through the remembered-form storage round-trip, whose template mapping (per finding S8) omits the December-era facts — the entering carry-ins, the RMD already received, the funding draws, and the premium facts — so the projected years displayed there priced from a template without those facts, while the walk itself, given a template carrying them, is the behavior pinned by the fixture and reproduced in the live checks above; S8's own build owns that mapping. The staged audit's one advisory is pre-existing and unrelated: a phone-width horizontal scroller inside the Spending Quick view chart, recorded by earlier builds and left as-is. SCRUB: boundary-aware scrub (patterns.txt + patterns-supplement.txt, scrub-push workspace) over this entry AS WRITTEN, after it was written, confirms ZERO matches; every amount above is stated as a relation to the fictional sample household's figures or as a statutory constant, and no household figure appears. CONTRACT: stays 159 — no action signature or paste-contract change (the walk is projection logic over the same inputs type, shared by the client and the contract path). Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-S3 — runPlaygroundYear and the Playground paste carry the gain-harvest facts end to end; the spending-draw half was already closed by R3-M1 and is now pinned through the API path (API contract 158 → 159)

All user-entered data, no external source. The runPlaygroundYear request schema and input mapping in server/src/apiContractCore.ts, the paste path in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (payload type, field list, optional-field list, emitter, parser), the paste and result response schemas and API_CONTRACT_VERSION in server/src/actions.ts, the Playground paste loader's session hold in client/src/Playground.tsx, and the tax census in server/src/taxFixtures.ts (one new fixture, one key-count pin updated) — no database schema, stored figure, pricing rule, or other action changed. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S3, settled STAND): runPlaygroundYear and the paste could not carry a spending draw or harvest facts — the action schema silently stripped unknown keys, and a hand-built paste carrying them was refused outright. VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE, the finding's two halves stand differently. THE DRAW HALF WAS ALREADY CLOSED: R3-M1 (contract v155, in the pushed HEAD) put spendingDraw in the request schema and its mapping, in the paste payload, its field list, and its parser, and on the Playground form as a dial the loader sets — so this build changes nothing for the draw and instead pins it through the API path in the new fixture, beside the harvest it closes. THE HARVEST HALF STOOD OPEN: the two gain-harvest facts (harvestPoolAmount, the taxable pool available to sell; harvestPoolBasisPct, that pool's blended basis) have lived in the pricer's inputs since the December console began supplying them (build v113) and the pricer sizes the year's harvest from them, but the request schema named neither (a caller sending them had them silently stripped and priced an un-harvested year), the paste field list and emitter carried neither (and the parser refused a hand-built paste carrying them as fields the loader does not know), and the action's result response schema never named the harvestedGain the pricer returns, so it was stripped on the way out as well. THE FIX, SERVER SIDE: the request schema accepts both facts as optional nullables (the pool a non-negative dollar figure; the basis a percent from 0 to 100 — an out-of-range value fails validation like every other out-of-range figure in the schema, instead of being stripped), the mapping carries them verbatim into the engine inputs, and the result response schema carries harvestedGain, so the priced harvest is visible in the response and already inside the response's gains, AGI, and MAGI figures. The paste payload carries both facts always-present and null-when-unset, like every other unset dial; the field list names them; the optional-field list names them, so a paste written before this build carries neither key and loads with them absent (no harvest, exactly as before); the parser accepts the pool through the same optional-money validation as the other carried facts and the basis through a percent validation (a present basis outside 0–100, or a negative pool, refuses the whole paste), returning both in the engine inputs' own spelling (unset = undefined, so the round-trip identity holds); and the action's paste payload response schema carries both, so the emitted pasteText is not stripped on the way out. THE FIX, LOADER SIDE: the Playground form has no harvest dial — the facts are the December console's, not a form entry — so, mirroring the P-S2 spending hold, the paste loader holds the pasted pair in session state and the form's input builder supplies it to the pricer on every pricing while the hold lasts; the hold is set on every paste load (a legacy paste holds two nulls — no harvest — and so clears any earlier hold) and clears beside the spending hold at every other loader (the remembered-form restore, reset, a projection year, the prefill, the as-filed year, a blank year, a saved-plan year), the one exception being the Spending field's own edit, which clears only the spending hold because editing spending says nothing about a pasted harvest. The projection template deliberately does not carry the facts: a paste-loaded harvest never leaks into the projection walk, whose years price from the template's own dials exactly as before. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; every figure the household's own or constructed arithmetically from it, never written as a figure of its own): a 2026 joint year, ages 58 / 56, whose only income is other ordinary income of four times the household's filed ordinary dividends, with the harvest facts set to the household's sample taxable pool at its sample basis percentage. Hand-derived: the ordinary taxable income is the income less the $32,200 standard deduction, leaving $51,100 of room under the 0% capital-gains band top, so the pricer harvests exactly that room — harvested gain $51,100, AGI and MAGI $131,100, federal tax $5,240 unchanged (every harvested dollar lands inside the 0% band), cash in equal to the entered income alone (a harvest brings in no cash), and the priced long-term gains equal to the harvested gain. Controls: the bare year (no facts) harvests nothing at the same tax; the pool alone, the basis alone, and a basis of 100% (a pool with no unrealized gain) each harvest nothing. THE BRIEF'S DRAW EXAMPLE rides the same construction through the contract path: the same year-shape carrying a spending draw of the same four-times-dividends amount in place of the income prices AGI and cash in of the whole draw — exactly the draw above the same request with the key absent, which prices both at zero — with federal tax $5,240 and cash left of the draw less that tax; and the draw and the harvest facts together price the harvest example's AGI with cash in of the whole draw. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (569 → 570 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-harvest-facts-ps3, pinning the worked example's direct pricing, the bare and one-fact-only and full-basis controls, the contract path accepting and pricing both facts while rejecting a negative pool, a negative basis, and a basis above 100, the contract path's draw leg and stripped control and combined draw-plus-harvest leg, the payload's carriage of both facts through a JSON round-trip and reprice, a hand-augmented payload (the paste the old parser refused) loading and pricing the same harvest, a hand-built payload carrying the draw and the harvest facts together, a pre-P-S3 payload (both keys deleted) and a null-carrying payload each loading with the facts unset at the control figures, the paste refusals, and the December console's agreement — the console's own inputs for the same facts price the identical harvest and AGI through the contract path, to the cent. The mt-pg3-playground-statelessness pin's payload key count moves 48 → 50 with its note extended, because the payload now carries two more fields. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: every stage of both paths re-traced against the finding (request schema, mapping, response schemas, payload type and its Omit list, field list, optional-field list, emitter, parser validation and return spelling, the loader's hold, its set site, its clear sites, and both pricing consumers' dependency lists), which confirmed the draw half already closed at every stage and the projection template's non-carriage; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the live drives, the feel pass, the counts re-read, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 570/570 on the chunked source grid (every fixture exactly once — a parallel batch's chunks were partly memory-killed on this machine, a known transient, and the missing ranges then passed in full run serially in finer slices); supporting suites via the staged build's self-check action: December 88/88, extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 with both Trinity mixes inside tolerance, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear carrying a spending draw of the worked example's amount and no other income returns AGI and cash in of the whole draw, federal tax $5,240, and cash left of the draw less that tax, exactly the draw above the same request with the key absent (AGI and cash in of zero), with provenance reporting API contract 159 and its paste carrying the draw with both harvest keys null; the same action carrying the harvest facts returns the harvested gain of $51,100 inside AGI and MAGI of $131,100 at the same $5,240 tax, its paste carrying both facts; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. HANDS-ON FEEL PASS on the staged build at phone width, driven in the audit sandbox (its writes never ship): pasting the action's own emitted harvest paste into the Playground's paste box and loading it printed the loaded note and priced the strip at the harvest figures (the year's tax and a MAGI of the full AGI including the harvested gain); then loading a legacy paste (the same payload with the two harvest keys deleted) cleared the hold — the strip fell back to a MAGI of the entered income alone with the tax unchanged and no error shown. The staged audit's one advisory is pre-existing and unrelated: a phone-width horizontal scroller inside the Spending Quick view chart, recorded by earlier builds and left as-is. SCRUB: boundary-aware scrub (patterns.txt + patterns-supplement.txt, scrub-push workspace) over this entry AS WRITTEN, after it was written, confirms ZERO matches; every figure above is the worked example's synthetic construction or the fictional sample household's and its derived pins. CONTRACT: 158 → 159 — the action signature and the paste contract both changed (the request now accepts the two harvest facts, the response now carries the harvested gain, and the payload, its field list, and the parser now carry the facts), with the runPlaygroundYear contract paragraph extended to state the carriage, the sizing rule, and the worked example. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-S2 — the Playground paste carries annualSpending end to end, and the loader holds the pasted figure for the session so a pasted year keeps its own spending comparison (API contract 157 → 158)

All user-entered data, no external source. The paste path in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (payload type, field list, optional-field list, emitter, parser), the paste response schema and API_CONTRACT_VERSION in server/src/actions.ts, the runPlaygroundYear contract paragraph in server/src/apiContractCore.ts, the Playground paste loader and spending resolution in client/src/Playground.tsx, and the tax census in server/src/taxFixtures.ts (one new fixture, one key-count pin updated) — no database schema, stored figure, pricing rule, or other action changed. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S2, settled STAND): the paste path dropped annualSpending, the year's spending. The payload type never omitted the field — the emitter simply never emitted it; the field list named no spending key; and the parser refused a hand-added spending key as a field the loader does not know. Spending never prices into tax, but it is the subtrahend of the result's "enough for the year" comparison (cash left after tax less annual spending), and the Playground resolves that comparison's spending from the live Tax Plan record whenever the priced inputs carry none — so a pasted year replayed its verdict against whatever spending the record happened to hold at replay time: changed when the record's figure differed from the priced year's, and vanished entirely when the record carried none. THE FIX, SERVER SIDE: annualSpending now rides the payload always-present and null-when-unset, like every other unset dial; the field list names it; the optional-field list names it, so a paste written before this build carries no such key and loads with it absent (no spending carried, exactly as before); the parser accepts it through the same optional-money validation as the other carried facts (a present value must be a valid non-negative dollar figure or the whole paste is refused) and returns it in the engine inputs' own spelling (unset = undefined, so the round-trip identity holds); and the action's paste payload response schema carries it, so the emitted pasteText is not stripped on the way out. THE FIX, LOADER SIDE: the Playground's Spending field is a write-through to the Tax Plan record — the plan's spending lives in the record and the field edits it in place — so the paste loader must NOT set that field from a paste: doing so would silently rewrite the saved plan's spending, breaking the loaders' standing contract that loading a year sets dials only and never writes the saved record. Instead the loader holds the pasted figure in session state, and one resolution — the held figure when a paste supplied one (a held null when the pasted year itself carried no spending), otherwise the field's own record resolution exactly as before — feeds both the priced inputs and the play strip, so the strip and the year card keep agreeing (the S-7 invariant). The hold clears when the Spending field itself is edited (from then on the field's figure rules), on every other loader (the remembered-form restore, the prefill, the as-filed year, a blank year, a saved-plan year, a projection year), on reset, and on a legacy paste (no key, so nothing is held); while a hold is active the verdict's info note names the figure's source as the annual spending the pasted year was priced with, and the Spending section's own header summary shows the resolved figure. The hold is session-only, like the paste-loaded flag beside it: it is not part of the remembered form, so a page reload resolves the comparison from the record again — the recorded limit of this close, accepted because persisting it would mean either writing the record (forbidden above) or remembering a second, divergent spending source. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): a 2026 joint year, ages 58 / 56, whose only income is other ordinary income of four times the household's filed ordinary dividends, priced with the household's annual spending figure. Hand-derived: federal tax $5,240 (the income less the $32,200 standard deduction, $2,480 at 10% and the rest at 12%), cash left after tax $74,760, and the verdict is the cash left less the full sample spending. The record-side replay — the same year priced against a record holding four fifths of the sample spending, the construction the live checks used — returns a verdict exactly one fifth of the sample spending too high, with tax and cash left identical (spending never prices into tax); and a year priced with no spending at all returns no verdict, its payload carrying the spending as null. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (568 → 569 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-paste-annual-spending-ps2, pinning the worked example's direct pricing and verdict, the record-side control (the pre-fix replay at four fifths of the sample spending) and the bare control (no spending, no verdict), the payload's carriage of the spending through a JSON round-trip and reprice at the priced verdict, a hand-augmented payload (the paste the old parser refused) loading and pricing the same verdict, a pre-P-S2 payload (the key deleted) loading with it unset at the control figures, a payload carrying the key as null loading with the verdict null, a negative spending refusing the whole paste, and the contract path accepting, carrying, and pricing the field while rejecting a negative one — every figure the sample household's own or constructed arithmetically from it (the record-side figure as four fifths of the sample spending, never written as a figure of its own). The mt-pg3-playground-statelessness pin's payload key count moves 47 → 48 with its note extended, because the payload now carries one more field. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: every stage of the paste path and every loader re-traced against the finding and the settlement (payload type, field list, optional-field list, emitter, parser validation and return spelling, the response schema, the loader's hold and all eight of its clear sites, the one resolution feeding both pricing consumers), which caught the PG3 key-count pin this build moves; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the live drives, the feel pass, the counts re-read, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 569/569 on the chunked source grid (24 chunks of 24 fixtures, every fixture exactly once, teeth ok on every chunk, the suite's own total agreeing at 569 on every chunk); supporting suites via the staged build's self-check action: December 88/88, extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 with both Trinity mixes inside tolerance, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations. Corruption teeth: six of the new fixture's pins (the direct verdict, the paste-round-trip verdict, the verdict error delta, the legacy verdict's absence of a carried figure, the contract path's carriage, the null carriage) each fail the fixture when mutated, and the updated PG3 key-count pin passes on the final tree. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the worked example returns federal tax $5,240, cash left after tax $74,760, the spending echoed whole, and the verdict at the cash left less the full sample spending, with provenance reporting API contract 158; its pastePayload and pasteText both carry the spending, so the emitted paste reproduces its own verdict; the same year priced with the stored record's own spending figure returns the verdict exactly one fifth of the sample spending higher with tax and cash left identical — the pre-fix replay error, reproduced live; the same year with no spending returns a null verdict and a payload carrying the spending as null; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. HANDS-ON FEEL PASS on the staged build at phone width, driven in the audit sandbox (its writes never ship): pasting the action's own emitted worked-example paste into the Playground's paste box and loading it printed the loaded note and priced the strip with the PASTED spending figure and the monthly share of the pasted verdict (cash left after tax at its monthly share beside it), while the record's own figure stayed in place underneath — proven by then loading a legacy paste (the same payload with the spending key deleted), which cleared the hold: the strip fell back to the record's spending figure and the record-side verdict, the dials and tax figures otherwise unchanged. The staged audit's one advisory is pre-existing and unrelated: a phone-width horizontal scroller inside the Spending Quick view chart, recorded by earlier builds and left as-is. SCRUB: boundary-aware scrub (patterns.txt + patterns-supplement.txt, scrub-push workspace) over this entry AS WRITTEN, after it was written, confirms ZERO matches; every figure above is the worked example's synthetic construction or the fictional sample household's and its derived pins, and the record-side figure is named only as a fraction of the sample figure. CONTRACT: 157 → 158 — the paste contract changed (the payload, its field list, and the parser now carry the annual spending, and the response schema carries it), with the runPlaygroundYear contract paragraph extended to state the carriage, the loader's session hold, and the worked example. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-S1 — the Playground's client-priced saved-plan sleeve exclusion: the cited patch was already corrected by R3-S3; this build pins the settlement's distinct worked example (API contract stays 157)

All user-entered data, no external source. One new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no client, server engine, action, paste payload, December surface, database schema, or stored figure changed, and no action signature or paste contract changed, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE FINDING (parity audit SHOULD-FIX S1, settled STAND): the Playground prices the saved plan's years in the client from the shared saved-record construction patched with its own sleeve resolution, and the audit — written against the tree before round 3 — found that patch threading the snapshot's FULL Cash bucket as the spend-from-cash sleeve with no exclusion subtraction, while the server threads snapshot cash less the exclude-from-plan amount and the Tax Plan's local builder mirrors it; on the settlement's worked example the phantom sleeve spent excluded cash in the second year that the corrected threading instead draws from Taxable, a sale gap whose gain prices at the settlement's stated tax delta. VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE: the cited patch site already carries the correction — round 3's R3-S3 build landed it in the current HEAD, and the patch now resolves the sleeve as the snapshot's Cash bucket less the exclude-from-plan amount, floored at zero, on the snapshot-followed path, and zero beside an explicit taxable balance, exactly the resolution this finding asks for; an exhaustive search found no second sleeve-threading site (the Tax Plan builder, the December harvest pool, and the server's own balance resolution all already subtract the exclusion). The settlement's distinctness claim predates that landing, so no client change remains to make; what was missing is the pin — R3-S3's fixture pins a full-exclusion shape at a full cash percentage over a single spending year, while this finding's worked example (a partial exclusion, a partial cash percentage, spending past the first year) was pinned nowhere. THE PIN (one new census fixture, tax-engines-playground-sleeve-exclusion-ps1, after the R3-S3 fixture; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, the exclusion constructed arithmetically as a fraction of the household's cash bucket and the tax leg's other ordinary income as a multiple of its filed ordinary dividends, never written as figures of their own): the corrected threading sizes the sleeve at cash less the exclusion and the pre-fix threading (the full cash bucket, computed in-case beside it) is carried through the same shared construction the server paths execute; the two forms agree through the first year and diverge in the second exactly as the settlement states — the corrected year's cash spend is the settlement's smaller figure and the pre-fix year's the larger, the difference being the phantom excluded cash, and the corrected year sells exactly that much more from Taxable. The march's gain delta stands slightly above the settlement's flat-basis sketch, and the fixture's note derives why: the engine's single pool does not hold a flat basis — a sleeve spend debits the pool with full-basis cash dollars while tax-debit sales remove basis at each year's own rate — so by the second year every sold dollar realizes a slightly higher gain share in both forms alike; the year-two sales themselves match the settlement exactly. The tax leg prices the march's two second-year sales as single Playground years through the runPlaygroundYear contract path with each sale's basis entered at the pool's basis percentage, so the single-year pricer realizes the flat rate and the federal tax delta is the settlement's figure to the cent. Controls: with no exclusion the corrected threading resolves the full cash bucket, bit-identical to the pre-fix construction; beside an explicit taxable balance the exclusion is inert and the sleeve is zero. VERIFICATION: three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass one: every sleeve-threading site re-traced across the client and server, confirming the correction in place and no second site; pass two: the full suite results re-read; pass three: the live drives, counts, and scrub re-checked) plus a hands-on feel pass at phone width on the staged build — the Playground's saved-plan preset card lists the client-priced years, loading the chosen year populated the dials and showed the load note, and the saved plan was not changed. Typecheck clean (client and server). Tax census 568/568 green on the chunked source grid (chunks of 24 fixtures, one chunk split finer where the runner was killed under memory pressure); supporting suites via the source runners: extended 161/161, retirement 63/63, December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20. Corruption teeth: five of the new fixture's pins (the derived sleeve, the resolved pool, the second-year cash spend, the march gain delta, the tax delta) each fail the fixture when mutated. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the worked example's two second-year forms returns the fixture's tax-leg figures to the cent — the corrected form's AGI and federal tax above the pre-fix form's by exactly the pinned deltas — with provenance reporting the current API contract version; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries); runAccuracySelfCheck reports data integrity 0 violations. The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. ## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-M5 — "Start from my numbers" prefill carries the four record facts (API contract stays 157)

All user-entered data, no external source. The prefill source and the prefill itself in client/src/Playground.tsx, plus one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no server engine, action, paste payload, December surface, database schema, or stored figure changed, and no action signature or paste contract changed, so the API contract stays at its current version. THE FINDING (parity audit MUST-FIX M5, settled STAND, with the settlement's two corrections applied): the Playground's "Start from my numbers" prefill set none of the four record facts — other ordinary income, tax-exempt interest, the entering loss carry-ins, and the health premiums — while the record's own pricing carries all four every year, so a year started from the user's numbers priced as though none of them existed. Correction one: the audit's second worked example understated its deltas (it omitted the loss allowance from the gap); the settlement's reworked gap is the larger one, and the fixture pins that corrected gap and the top of the settlement's corrected tax range. Correction two: the audit's contrast sentence is false for health premiums — the saved-year loader does NOT set the health dials either — so the health pin compares the prefilled year against the march year's own priced net premium, never the loader. THE FIX: the prefill source now resolves the four facts from the saved record (blank where the record has nothing entered, so a record carrying none of them prefills exactly as before), and the prefill sets the other-ordinary and tax-exempt dials from the record's annual amounts; the four carry-in dials from the march year's own entering ledger lines when the march prices the chosen year, and from the record's entering lines otherwise, blank at zero exactly as the saved-year loader leaves them; the marketplace health dial by the same marketplace pick as the benchmark — the household amount when both spouses are on the marketplace, the single amount when exactly one is — falling back to the loaded benchmark when the record's premium term is active but the picked tier has no entered amount (the march's own fallback for a missing tier amount), and blank when neither spouse is on the marketplace or no premium term is entered; and the Medicare dial from the record's per-person amount, which the pricer counts per person on Medicare. The year-specific dials (conversion, stock sale, advance credit taken, RMD already received, dependent MAGI, funding draws) are deliberately untouched — they have no record source. One subtlety the fixture pins explicitly: the form always supplies an advance-credit-taken value, so on the form path the settlement prices inside the net tax bill and the form's net premium reads as the gross, while the march's net (gross less the kept credit, capped at the gross) is the reading when no advance credit is supplied; the pin compares the no-advance-credit construction against the march year's net to the cent and separately pins the two constructions' cash left after health premiums equal. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; every coinciding amount constructed arithmetically from the household's filed-return figures, never written as a figure of its own): five legs. (A) A working year carrying the other-ordinary and tax-exempt amounts and the banked losses: the march's detail and the prefilled year agree on all four facts, the carried-in losses price the statutory loss allowance against ordinary income, and against a construction missing only the other-ordinary / tax-exempt pair the AGI delta is the other-ordinary amount alone (tax-exempt interest never enters AGI) while the MAGI and ACA MAGI deltas are the two amounts together. (B) The settlement's corrected example: other ordinary income at seven times the household's filed ordinary dividends, the same banked losses, and a typed stock gain on the prefilled form: the ledger nets the gain (long-term carry-in first, short-term against the remainder), the allowance prices, the leftover short-term loss carries out, and the march chain is pinned at the source (the first year enters with the record's lines and leaves its own remainders, and the next year enters with exactly those); against the no-carry construction the AGI and MAGI gaps are the settlement's corrected gap and the federal-tax gap is the top of the settlement's corrected range — the absorbed gain at the year's gains rate plus the allowance at the year's ordinary rate. (C) A retired marketplace year (yields at zero, tax-exempt interest at five times the filed ordinary dividends, the household marketplace premium entered): the prefilled year reproduces the march year's AGI, ACA MAGI, and kept credit to the cent, its no-advance-credit net premium equals the march year's net premium to the cent, and the form construction's cash left after health premiums equals the other construction's to the cent; the bare construction prices no premium at all and its cash left after health premiums equals its cash left after tax — the audit's third-example identity. (D) The same record in a both-on-Medicare year: the per-person Medicare premium reproduces the march's gross and net exactly, and the bare construction prices none. (E) The premium pick's other branches: the single amount in a split year (one spouse on Medicare, one on the marketplace) reproduces the march's gross, credit, and net to the cent; and with no marketplace amount entered at all (the Medicare amount alone activating the premium term) both the march and the prefill fall back to the year's benchmark, reproduced to the cent. The household's saved record currently has none of the four facts entered — those fields ship blank and were never filled in — so for that record the prefill resolves all four blank and prices identically to the record itself, verified live; the carry itself is pinned by the fixture and by live pricings of the worked example.

## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-M4 — the projection walk starts each year from the template's total money out (API contract stays 157)

All user-entered data, no external source. One base line and its comment in projectPlaygroundYears (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) and one new fixture in the tax census (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no client code, action, paste payload, December surface, database schema, or stored figure changed. THE FINDING (parity audit MUST-FIX M4, settled STAND): a draw-mode projected year loses its money out entirely. Settled before building, against the current tree (74cd25b + the uncommitted P-M2/P-M3 builds): the finding's named site — the projection-year loader in client/src/Playground.tsx (loadProjYear) — already reads the loaded year's priced inputs and sets BOTH money dials, the spending draw included: the R3-M1 build made it do so and its entry says so. The loss that remains is one step earlier, in the walk itself: projectPlaygroundYears started each projected year's money out from the template's conversion dial alone, so a template whose money out rides the draw dial — the natural shape since the money-out dial split, and the shape the form itself produces — projected years whose priced money out, AGI, and cash-in are all zero, in either money-out kind; loading such a year then faithfully loaded the zero the walk had priced. No other finding owns the walk base, so the close is the walk base alone. THE FIX: each year's money out now starts from the template's TOTAL pre-tax money out — the conversion plus the spending draw, each floored at zero — the same sum the pricer's own moneyOut and the form's "Pre-tax money out" figure carry; everything downstream is untouched (the stop rules, the replace mode in which Social Security and RMDs shrink the money out, and the pre-tax balance caps apply to the total exactly as they applied to the conversion alone; the money-out kind still decides which one dial the total rides in each projected year), and a template carrying its money out on the conversion dial alone — every template written before this build — walks bit-identically to before. A comment at the site records the mechanism and this build. The loader needed no change: it already sets both dials from the loaded year's own priced inputs, and the fixture pins the invariant that relies on — a projected draw year's priced money out equals its conversion plus its spending draw, so the two dials the loader sets rebuild the year's money out exactly. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; the draw is the R3-M1 construction — four times the household's filed ordinary dividends, never written as a figure of its own, and coinciding with no real balance): a 2026 template year, MFJ, ages 60 and 49, no income beyond the draw, no credits, premiums, or state tax, the sample pre-tax balance, 0% return, repeat mode. Priced with the money-out kind set to a draw, the year carries money out of the draw amount riding the draw dial alone (conversion $0), AGI of the draw amount, federal tax $5,240, cash-in of the full draw, and cash left of the draw less $5,240; priced as a conversion instead, the same total rides the conversion dial, cash-in is $0, and the year's end Roth balance grows by the draw. Walked one year on, the second year starts from the sample pre-tax balance less the draw and again prices money out of the draw amount, on the draw dial, with cash-in the draw amount. A mixed template (the conversion dial set to the filed ordinary dividends beside the same draw) walks the two together: money out and AGI of the two dials' sum, federal tax $7,640, cash left of the sum less $7,640. A small-balance leg (the pre-tax balance set to twice the filed ordinary dividends) caps the year's money out — and the draw dial it rides — at the balance and ends the pre-tax money at zero. The fixture also reproduces both pre-fix failures in constructed form: the year's priced inputs with the draw dial zeroed (what the pre-fix reading of the year amounted to) price money out, AGI, and cash left of $0, and a template with the draw dial absent (the pre-fix walk's view of the template) projects a first year with money out $0 under the old base. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (565 → 566 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-projection-draw-money-out-pm4, pinning the worked example end to end — the draw-kind year, the repricing of the loaded year's inputs with the two money dials re-read exactly as the loader re-reads them (identical to the cent), the pre-fix loader form and the pre-fix walk form (both $0), the walked second year, the conversion-kind control, the mixed template, a conversion-dial-only control (bit-identical to the worked example, pinning that pre-existing templates are unmoved), and the balance-cap leg — with a source-invariant comment recording the client half the server-side suite cannot execute (the loader's two setter lines and the form builder always supplying the draw), the same division as the other loader fixtures. Teeth: corrupting any of the seven probed pins (draw dial, money out, loaded cash left, mixed tax, capped money out, conversion-kind end Roth, second-year start balance) fails the fixture. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the settlement and finding re-read against the current tree, the diff confined to the walk base and the fixture, the caps/stop/replace ordering re-traced, and the conversion-only bit-identity argued and pinned; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the live drives, the feel pass, the counts re-read, and the scrub over this entry as written): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 566/566 on the chunked source grid (24 chunks, teeth passing on every chunk, the suite's own total agreeing at 566 on every chunk); supporting suites all green — extended fixtures 161/161 (teeth passing), December reference suite 88/88, retirement fixtures 63/63 with both Trinity mixes inside tolerance, Roth revision CAS 15/15, retirement-plan CAS 16/16, Playground UI-state 20/20. The packaged harness run reports 344/349 with its five failures confined to its own census-total checks: its coarser census chunks are memory-killed on this machine (exit 137 at roughly 95 fixtures per chunk), the same transient P-M2 and P-M3 recorded, and the census is covered by the source-grid runs above; every other packaged suite it ran passed. LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the worked-example year reproduces it exactly (AGI and MAGI of the draw amount, federal tax $5,240, cash-in the draw amount, cash left of the draw less $5,240, the draw dial echoed in full, provenance reporting API contract 157); runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries); runAccuracySelfCheck's integrity suite reports 0 violations (snapshot totals, bucket splits, bill-version chains, payment references, cash-out items). The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. HANDS-ON FEEL PASS on the staged build at phone width, driven in the audit sandbox (its writes never ship): a year built on the draw dial alone priced cash left of the draw less its tax in the single-year strip; the projection captured from that year, with the money-out kind set to a draw, priced every year's bar at MAGI of the full draw amount (before this build the same bars priced $0); tapping the following year's bar loaded it into the single-year view with its summary pricing the same MAGI and tax, its readout carrying money out and AGI of the draw amount and taxable income of the draw less the $32,200 standard deduction, and the strip's cash left unchanged. No label, field, or layout changed. ## Build (2026-11-05): Parity audit P-M3 — the Playground paste carries acaEnrollmentPremiumAnnual end to end (API contract 156 → 157)

THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; built on the fictional sample household in server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): a 2026 joint year, ages 58 / 56, household of 2, whose only income is other ordinary income of four times the household's filed ordinary dividends, against a benchmark premium constructed so the priced credit is exactly $15,000 — the benchmark less the top band's 9.96% of that MAGI — with an enrollment premium of $12,000 (three fifths of the filed dividends), advance credit taken of the same $12,000, and a distinct marketplace health premium of $25,000 (the sample couple benchmark) entered as the premium readout's own fact. Hand-derived: the final credit caps at the enrollment premium, which equals the advance taken, so no credit is still due and no repayment is owed — the net tax bill is the whole federal tax of $5,240 (the income less the $32,200 standard deduction, $2,480 at 10% and the rest at 12%), cash left after tax is $74,760, the net health premium is $13,000 (the gross less the advance taken), and cash left after health premiums is $61,760. The pre-fix replay — the enrollment premium dropped — prices the final credit uncapped: $3,000 of it still due, a net tax bill of $2,240, and cash left of $77,760 — $3,000 too high (cash left after health premiums likewise $3,000 too high at $64,760) — while the health premium readout itself is unchanged, the two facts being distinct. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 3 R3-S3 — the Playground's saved-plan march now sizes the spend-from-cash sleeve from the exclusion-adjusted cash (API contract unchanged at 155)

All user-entered data, no external source. One client correction in client/src/Playground.tsx (the pgSavedPlanYears construction's spendFromCashSleeveStart patch), plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no server code, action signature, request or response shape, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed, so API_CONTRACT_VERSION stays 155. THE FINDING (engines review round 3, SHOULD-FIX, settled STAND): the Tax Plan subtracts the exclude-from-plan amount from the snapshot cash before sizing the spend-from-cash sleeve — resolveArgsBalances threads the Cash bucket less the exclusion, floored at $0, and the Tax Plan's local builder and save payload mirror that resolution term for term — but the Playground's saved-plan march threaded the snapshot's FULL Cash bucket as the sleeve. The march's included pool was already correct (the prefill's pool resolution subtracts the exclusion), so whenever an exclusion consumed part or all of the cash, the march priced a sleeve larger than the cash actually left in the pool and spent the year's spending out of zero-income cash the exclusion had already removed. The affected path requires snapshot-following balances, a cash exclusion, and an enabled sleeve; tier-derived sleeves take a different path. THE FIX: pgSavedPlanYears now reuses the exclusion-adjusted sleeve resolution when constructing the march — on the snapshot-followed path (saved.taxableCents null) the sleeve is max(0, snapshot Cash less max(0, the record's exclusion)) in cents, divided by 100, and beside an explicit taxable balance it stays $0 — the same two branches the server and the Tax Plan take. In tiers mode the engine derives the sleeve from the pool's 100%-basis cash tier and the threaded field is inert, so that path is untouched (the fixture's tiers leg pins it). THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic): a snapshot taxable-plus-cash pool of $200,000 including $100,000 of cash; an exclusion of $100,000; a 100% single-pool basis; the cash spending percentage at 100; annual spending of $60,000; a pre-tax-first draw order; a 2026 joint household below 65 with no other income or credits. Correct: included pool $100,000, remaining cash sleeve $0, the $60,000 funded from pre-tax, federal tax $2,840 (the draw less the $32,200 standard deduction, taxed $2,480 at 10% and the rest at 12%). The pre-fix march claimed a $100,000 sleeve and funded the $60,000 from zero-income cash — federal tax $0. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (561 → 562 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-saved-plan-sleeve-exclusion-r3s3, on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts), in seven legs. (1) WORKED EXAMPLE: through the shared resolution construction (resolvePlanBalances, the exclusion-adjusted threading, planInputsFromSaved) the pool resolves to $100,000 and the threaded sleeve to $0; the corrected first march year funds the whole spending from pre-tax (cash spend $0, pre-tax draw $60,000, AGI $60,000, federal tax $2,840 paid from the pool at its 100% basis) and the sleeve ends at $0. (2) PRE-FIX FORM: the same record with the sleeve threaded as the full cash bucket, computed in-case — derived sleeve $100,000, the $60,000 spent from cash, no pre-tax draw, federal tax $0, sleeve ending at $40,000. (3) PARTIAL EXCLUSION (half the cash bucket): pool $150,000, sleeve $50,000; the year pays $50,000 from cash and the remaining $10,000 pre-tax, its AGI sits under the standard deduction so its tax is $0, and the sleeve ends empty — the sleeve is cash-minus-exclusion at every size, not all-or-nothing. (4) NO-EXCLUSION CONTROL: pool $200,000, sleeve the full $100,000, the cash funding correct and the tax $0 — bit-identical to the pre-fix construction, which only ever diverged when an exclusion applied. (5) OVER-EXCLUSION (the exclusion at one and a half times the cash bucket): the sleeve floors at $0, the pool falls to $50,000, and the year again draws its spending pre-tax at the same $2,840. (6) EXPLICIT-BALANCE CONTROL: the entered pool stands with the exclusion inert, the construction's sleeve beside an explicit balance is $0, and the tax is $2,840. (7) TIERS: with half the pool in a 100%-basis cash tier, the derived sleeve is $50,000 whatever the threaded field carries ($0 or the full cash amount). A source-invariant comment above the fixture documents the client half — the pgSavedPlanYears patch's own expression of the same resolution — which this server-side suite cannot execute.
