## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 3 R3-S2 — the multi-year Playground projection tracks both owners' pre-tax balances and RMD clocks through the walk (API contract unchanged at 155)

All user-entered data, no external source. One engine correction in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (projectPlaygroundYears and the projection header comments that state its balance rule), plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no client file, action signature, request or response shape, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed, so API_CONTRACT_VERSION stays 155. THE FINDING (engines review round 3, SHOULD-FIX, settled STAND): the projection walk combined the primary's and spouse's pre-tax balances into one balance, priced a single RMD on the primary's clock (the primary's age, birth year, and divisor), and nulled the spouse balance in each projected year's inputs before calling the single-year pricer — so the spouse's money was charged RMDs at the primary's divisor in every year, including years when the spouse owed no RMD at all, and the invented RMD income and cash then fed the walk's draw-mode arrivals, its balance caps, and every later year's balances. The single-year pricer itself was already correct (it prices each entered balance on its own clock); only the walk fed it a combined balance. THE FIX: the walk now tracks the two balances apart for its whole length. Each year's RMDs are the sum of the same two rmdForYear calls the pricer makes — the primary's on the primary's balance (Joint Life when the spouse is the primary's sole beneficiary and more than 10 years younger), the spouse's on the spouse's balance with the roles swapped (Joint Life only when the primary is the spouse's sole beneficiary, the reciprocal fact, and more than 10 years younger) — and that sum is what the replace-mode arrivals, the baseline arrival, and the balance caps read. Each projected year's inputs carry the split (the primary's walked balance on the primary field, the spouse's on the spouse field, a side never entered staying blank), so the pricer prices the two RMDs itself and loading a projected year now loads both balances. The money out still caps against the combined balance left after the two RMDs (the pricer's own cap is on the total) and the stop floor still guards the combined balance; the money out drains the primary's post-RMD balance first and the spouse's second — the plan march's own allocation for conversions and pre-tax draws — and each owner's remainder grows separately at the entered return, each rounded as the march rounds its per-owner ends. The reported starting and ending pre-tax figures remain the combined totals the balances chart draws. A template with only one balance entered walks exactly as before (the unentered side is zero throughout), a template with no balance entered prices no RMD and caps nothing, and a stale spouse balance on a non-joint template still never enters the walk (the S-12 gate, through the same countedSpousePretax the pricer uses). THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic): a 2046 joint year, primary 75 and spouse 64, spouse sole beneficiary, each owner holding $253,000 pre-tax. The repository's Joint Life divisor for 75 / 64 is 25.3, so the primary's RMD is $253,000 ÷ 25.3 = $10,000; the spouse, at 64, is below the RMD age and owes $0. The corrected projection RMD is $10,000; the pre-fix walk priced the combined $506,000 at that same divisor for $20,000 — a whole invented second RMD, which also left the walked balance $10,000 lower. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (560 → 561 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-projection-split-rmd-clocks-r3s2, on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts), in seven legs. (1) WORKED EXAMPLE: the 2046 RMD is $10,000, the spouse-only repricing of that year's inputs is $0, the pre-fix combined form computed in-case is $20,000, the year's inputs carry the $253,000 / $253,000 split, and the combined figures start at $506,000 and end at $496,000; the next year (76 / 65) loads the walked split ($243,000 primary, spouse still $253,000) and prices $243,000 ÷ 24.4 = $9,959.02, ending at $486,040.98; the projected first year equals the single-year pricer on the same inputs. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 3 R3-S1 — a blank heir rate now resolves to one shared default in both plan-input builders, including the preserved-balance exit fallback (API contract unchanged at 155)

All user-entered data, no external source. One new shared constant in server/src/rothSeed.ts (DEFAULT_HEIR_RATE_PCT, the rate a BLANK heir rate resolves to), consumed by the server's planInputsFromSaved in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (its heir fallback and its preserved-balance exit chain, replacing the hard-coded literal) and by the Tax Plan's local input builder in client/src/RothConversion.tsx (its heir fallback and its blank exit-rate chain, replacing the seed-rate fallback), re-exported through client/src/rothShared.tsx, plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no action signature, request or response shape, paste contract, database schema, seed value, or stored figure changed, so API_CONTRACT_VERSION stays 155. An explicitly entered rate never passed through either fallback and was unaffected. THE FIX: both builders now fall back to the one shared constant, whose value is the server builder's previous fallback — verified against the stored Tax Plan record before changing anything: the record's own entered heir rate carries that same value, so the server side and the record agree and the local seed-rate fallback was the outlier. Every other consumer that reads an already-resolved rate (the score's exit-rate passthrough, the scenario clamp, the reserve readout) is untouched, because those read resolved inputs, not blank ones. THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic): a no-conversion scenario ending with a round seven-figure pre-tax balance, no preserved reserve, and a blank heir rate — its net cost is its terminal cost alone (no tax, penalty, surcharge, credit, or premium prices), the local form priced that terminal at the seed rate and the server form at the shared default, and the disagreement was the rate gap times the ending balance (verified live below on the exact example). ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 3 R3-M2 — entered marketplace premiums cap the retained ACA credit (year readout, lifetime total, and lifetime score), not just the funding (API contract unchanged at 155)

All user-entered data, no external source. One engine correction in server/src/taxEngine.ts (the retained-credit assignment in simulateRothPlan, plus the comments that state the rule at the health premium term's input fields, the year row, and the lifetime totals), one comment correction in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (netCostBreakdown's health premium fields), contract-text clarifications in server/src/apiContractCore.ts (the health premium semantics gains the retained-credit cap; the ACA semantics' documented long-horizon scope limit gains the entered-premium exception it always implied), and ONE new tax-census fixture — no action signature, request or response shape, paste contract, database schema, or stored figure changed, and no client file touched, so API_CONTRACT_VERSION stays 155 (the bump rule is signatures and paste contracts; neither moved). THE FINDING (engines review round 3, MUST-FIX, settled STAND): the enrollment-premium cap (Form 8962's lesser-of — the credit never exceeds the premium of the plan actually enrolled in) was applied in two of the three places the march prices a credit: the year's FUNDING nets the settlement's credit capped at the gross marketplace premium (so the funded net premium is right), and the single-year pricer's filing settlement caps its final credit at the enrollment premium. But the march's RETAINED credit — acaCreditKept, which is the year readout, the lifetime total (lifetimeAcaKept), and the exact figure the lifetime score subtracts beside the lifetime GROSS premium in netCostBreakdown — stayed the uncapped benchmark-based credit. Whenever the entered plan cost less than the benchmark credit, the score's premium-minus-credit went negative by the excess and the score invented a benefit beyond the premium paid, distorting every comparison among cheaper-than-benchmark plans. THE FIX: at the one assignment that produces the retained credit, when the health premium term prices a marketplace premium for the year (healthAcaThisYear), the retained credit is the benchmark-based credit capped at that year's marketplace gross — the entered tier amount (household when both spouses are on the marketplace, single when exactly one is), or the benchmark fallback for a null tier amount, against which the benchmark-based credit can never exceed anyway, so the fallback case is bit-identical. The Medicare part of the gross never enters the cap (no credit offsets it). Everything downstream — the year rows, runRothCompare's per-year and lifetime acaCreditCents, runRothFunding, the optimizer and Monte Carlo scores (all read the same priced result), and the client totals that sum the year rows — inherits the capped figure from that one assignment; the funding rows do not move at all (they already netted the capped credit, verified below: the multi-year leg's lifetime net premium is identical before and after). The settlement's internal credit, the fill and cliff machinery, the detail block's benchmark facts (cliff, poverty line, applicable percentage), and the single-year pricer's aca.credit readout (the benchmark-based estimate by its documented definition — the December layer caps that figure itself, and its settlement and health readouts already cap) are all untouched. A plan that does not enter the term has no enrollment premium to cap against and keeps the benchmark-based credit bit-identically — the blank-premium case is out of this finding's scope by the settlement's own terms, and the fixture's control leg pins that. THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic): one retired 2026 year, joint ages 60 / 49, household of two, ordinary income and benchmark both described only as the settlement stated them (its income figure and benchmark figure coincide with listed household figures and are not restated here — the fixture constructs its own versions arithmetically, below); the benchmark-based credit is the benchmark less 9.96% of the income, the entered marketplace premium is below it, so the capped credit is the premium itself, the funded net premium is $0, and with the year's federal tax of $5,240 and no other score components the corrected score is $5,240 — before the fix it read $4,032 less, the invented excess (verified live below on the exact example). FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (557 → 558 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-aca-credit-enrollment-cap-r3m2, on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts), in four legs. (1) ONE-YEAR CAPPED LEG: a 2026 joint year at ages 60 / 49, household of two, the sample couple benchmark, ordinary income of four times the household's filed ordinary dividends (constructed arithmetically in-case, never written as a figure of its own), and an entered marketplace household premium of three quarters of those filed dividends (also constructed) — hand-derived: the benchmark-based credit is $17,032 (the benchmark less 9.96% of the income) and federal tax $5,240; corrected, the retained credit is the entered premium itself, gross equals it, net is $0, the score's premium-minus-credit is $0, and the score is the tax alone, $5,240 (before the fix the year kept $17,032 and scored $2,032 below the tax). (2) CONTROL: the same year with the term not entered keeps the benchmark-based $17,032 and scores the tax less that credit, bit-identical to before. (3) MULTI-YEAR LEG: the sample household's own plan with the term entered low (marketplace household $10,000, single $8,000, Medicare base $3,600 per person): the cap binds in the three both-on-marketplace years (each retained credit is the $10,000 premium, each funded net $0), the spouse-only year's priced credit $5,700.94 sits under its single premium and is untouched, and the lifetime identity gross − net − retained credit is $0 to the cent (gross $262,000, net $220,741.36, retained $41,258.64; before the fix the identity was negative by the three capped years' excesses and the score was understated by that same total) with the score's premium-minus-credit equal to the lifetime net premium. (4) PLAYGROUND LEG: the single-year pricer on the one-year shape with the premium on both dials its construction feeds — its aca.credit stays the benchmark-based $17,032 by definition while its money readouts cap (gross the entered premium, net $0, the credit toward the premium — gross less net — the entered premium itself, tax $5,240, cash left after health premiums equal to cash left after tax). Carriage changes in client/src/Playground.tsx (the form, the remembered state's application, the saved-year and projection-year loaders, and the readouts that key on money out), server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (the result echo and the paste payload / parser), server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts (the remembered form and the projection template), server/src/apiContractCore.ts (the runPlaygroundYear request and the playground-year convention), and server/src/actions.ts (the result and paste response shapes, the action description, and the version bump), plus ONE new tax-census fixture and one key-count re-pin — no engine pricing, database schema, or stored figure changed: the pricer has priced the M-2 money-out split (a conversion is ordinary income and never spendable cash; a draw taken for spending is ordinary income AND cash in) since round 2, and the December console has passed its draw on the spendingDraw dial since the split. Only the Playground's carriage of the draw was missing. THE FINDING (engines review round 3, MUST-FIX, settled STAND — a regression from the incomplete M-2 split, not the original conversion-overcount finding): the Playground's form path never got the draw half. buildPgInputs supplied conversion but no spendingDraw; the one money-out dial was labelled draw-or-conversion but fed the conversion alone; the saved-year loader folded the march's conversion plus its extra pre-tax draw onto that conversion dial; the projection-year loader copied only the conversion, dropping a draw-mode year's amount whole (the walk rides it on the inputs' spendingDraw); and the paste payload omitted the draw entirely. A draw year priced through the Playground therefore counted none of the draw as cash in, and the Playground and December disagreed by the entire draw — directly on the planned pre-tax-funded retirement years. THE FIX: the money-out section now carries two dials — "Pre-tax draw for spending" and "Conversion to Roth" — and the split rides every carriage path: buildPgInputs always supplies spendingDraw from its dial (blank = $0, bit-identical to before); the remembered form stores it (a pre-R3-M1 blob reads it blank); the projection template carries it; the saved-year loader puts the march's conversion on the conversion dial and its extra pre-tax draw on the draw dial (its preset note now names the split); the projection-year loader sets both dials from the year's inputs; the paste payload emits the draw always-present (null when unset) and the parser accepts it as an optional non-negative figure, spells unset as absent so round-trip identity holds (the S-2 / S-6 spelling), and loads it onto the draw dial — a pre-R3-M1 paste loads with it unset, exactly as before; and the runPlaygroundYear request accepts spendingDraw (optional; absent prices exactly as before) while the result — engine and action response alike — echoes spendingDraw beside conversion, so the split that priced is on the record. The readouts that keyed on the conversion alone as "the money out" now read the priced sum: the income-stack segment and its legend row, the projection income chart's money-out segment, the section header summary (which names the split when a draw is typed), the takeaway and landing-explainer gates, the plain-year sentence, and the can't-hold balance-cap comparison; the conversion-cost paragraph keeps pricing the conversion's own marginal cost (the pricer has always held the draw fixed for it) and says so when a draw is present. The two fill solvers are untouched: they still vary the conversion alone, with any draw held fixed, as the pricer's contract has always stated. THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE (synthetic; its draw constructed arithmetically from the shared fictional sample household, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts — four times the household's filed ordinary dividends, never written as a figure of its own): a 2026 joint year, ages 60 / 49, no other income, credits, premiums, or state tax. The draw less the $32,200 standard deduction is taxed $2,480 at 10% and the rest at 12% — federal tax $5,240. CORRECTED: cash in is the whole draw and cash left after tax is the draw less $5,240. THE PRE-FIX MAPPING (the same amount on the conversion dial): tax identical at $5,240, cash in $0, cash left −$5,240. THE MIXED YEAR (the draw plus a conversion of the filed ordinary dividends, $20,000): both parts price as income — AGI $100,000, taxable $67,800, federal tax $7,640 — while cash in counts the draw alone, so cash left is the draw less $7,640: the conversion is income but not cash in, and the draw is both. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (556 → 557 — the suite's own count): tax-engines-playground-spending-draw-r3m1, pinning the draw leg (AGI, taxable, tax $5,240, cash in, cash left, both echoes), the conversion-only control (identical tax, cash in $0, cash left −$5,240), the mixed leg (AGI $100,000, tax $7,640, cash in the draw alone, cash left, both echoes), the paste legs (the draw rides through and reprices the mixed figures; a key-deleted legacy payload loads unset and prices its money out all conversion), and the API legs (the contract path carries the draw and prices the corrected cash left; a negative draw is rejected at validation). ONE RE-PIN: mt-pg3-playground-statelessness's interchange-payload key count moves 41 → 42 (the payload gains exactly the one new field; its note's field history gains the R3-M1 clause) — no priced figure in it moves. ONE PRE-EXISTING FIXTURE UPDATE: the extended suite's stored-template literal gains the template's new spendingDraw field at $0 (the field the lenient reader defaults for older blobs) — no figure in it moves. CONTRACT: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 154 → 155 — the request and paste contracts changed, so the bump is owed: the playground-year convention gains the PRE-TAX SPENDING DRAW paragraph with the worked and mixed examples, and the runPlaygroundYear description gains the matching paragraph. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: every carriage site re-traced (buildPgInputs and its dependency lists, the form snapshot and its apply path, Reset and Blank year, the paste loader, both year loaders, the template's stored round-trip, the paste emit / parse / key lists, both UI-state schemas and their lenient readers, the request schema and its inputs mapping, both response shapes, and every readout that keyed on the conversion alone), with the fill solvers' conversion-only variation confirmed against the pricer's own comment; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the scrub, the live drives, and the counts re-read): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 557/557 on the chunked source grid with teeth ok on every chunk and suiteTotal 557 agreeing everywhere (the coarse 93-fixture slices OOM-killed on this machine, as on prior builds, so the grid ran at 24 fixtures per chunk — every fixture exactly once); extended 161/161, retirement 63/63, December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20 — all via the source runners; data integrity 0 violations via runAccuracySelfCheck on the staged build. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 N-1 — the Playground's prefill now carries the reciprocal beneficiary fact, so a prefilled year prices the spouse's RMD on the Joint table when the record establishes it (API contract 153 → 154)

All user-entered data, no external source. Carriage changes in client/src/Playground.tsx, server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (paste payload / parser), server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts (remembered form and projection template), server/src/apiContractCore.ts (the runPlaygroundYear request), and server/src/actions.ts (the paste response shape and version bump), plus ONE new tax-census fixture and one key-count re-pin — no engine pricing, schema, or stored figure changed: the pricer has always gated the spouse branch's RMD table on the reciprocal fact (primarySoleBeneficiaryOfSpouse — the primary is the sole beneficiary of the SPOUSE's pre-tax accounts; the round-3 fix), and the engine's own plan paths already carried it. THE FINDING (settled STAND): every Playground surface dropped the fact. The 'Start from my numbers' prefill source carried only the first beneficiary fact (spouseSoleBeneficiary — the spouse is the PRIMARY's sole beneficiary, which selects only the primary's table), there was no form state for the reciprocal fact, buildPgInputs never passed it, the remembered form and the paste payload had no field for it, and the runPlaygroundYear request accepted neither the fact nor the spouse's balance — so a prefilled year always priced the spouse's RMD on the Uniform Lifetime Table even when the saved plan record established reciprocity, and the action could not price a spouse RMD at all. THE FIX: the fact now rides every carriage path the first fact rides — pgPrefillSourceFrom resolves it from the saved plan record and prefillPlayground loads it into the new pgPrimarySoleBeneficiaryOfSpouse form state (not a visible dial, like its twin); buildPgInputs passes it to the pricer; the saved-plan-year loader sets it from the plan inputs it loads; the remembered form (playgroundFormState) and the projection template carry it (a pre-N-1 stored blob reads it as null — not established); the paste payload emits it always-present (null when unset) and the parser accepts a boolean or null, refuses a non-boolean, and spells an unset fact as absent so paste round-trip identity holds (the S-2/S-6 spelling); and the runPlaygroundYear request accepts both the fact and pretaxBalanceSpouse (optional, bit-identical when absent) while the action's paste response now carries both fields its own payload emits. The projection walk is deliberately untouched: it nulls the spouse balance and prices a combined RMD, so the fact is inert there. THE SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE (the settlement's own; the shared fictional sample household's joint filing pattern, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts, with the settlement's synthetic ages and balance — no household's figures): 2026, MFJ, the primary aged 75 and the spouse aged 90, both on Medicare, no entered income, and the spouse's own prior-Dec-31 pre-tax balance of $500,000. Hand-derived: the spouse's RMD prices on her own clock with the roles swapped, so the beneficiary whose age can select the Joint table is the primary, 15 years younger — more than the 10 the Joint rule requires. CORRECTED (the reciprocal fact established, as the fixed prefill carries it): the Joint and Last Survivor divisor at (90, 75) is 15.4, so her RMD is $500,000 ÷ 15.4 = $32,467.53. THE DEFECT, priced as the control (the fact absent — the pre-fix prefill's construction): the Uniform divisor at 90 is 12.2, so her RMD is $500,000 ÷ 12.2 = $40,983.61 — $8,516.08 more of forced income. The first fact alone does not establish reciprocity: spouseSoleBeneficiary true with the reciprocal fact false prices the identical Uniform figure. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (553 → 554 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 553 was written before follow-up #4 landed, the same one-behind pattern S-2, S-9, follow-up #3 and follow-up #4 recorded about their own briefs): tax-engines-playground-spouse-rmd-reciprocal-n1, pinning the corrected Joint pricing (RMD $32,467.53, divisor 15.4, table joint, AGI $32,467.53, tax $0), the Uniform control ($40,983.61, divisor 12.2, gap $8,516.08), the first-fact-only and explicit-false legs (both Uniform), the paste legs (the fact and the spouse's balance ride through and reprice Joint; a payload with the fact's key deleted — a pre-N-1 paste — loads unset and prices Uniform), and the API legs (the contract path carries both fields and prices Joint; the balance without the fact prices Uniform; a negative spouse balance and a non-boolean fact are rejected at validation). ONE RE-PIN: mt-pg3-playground-statelessness's interchange-payload key count moves 40 → 41 (the payload gains exactly the one new field; its note's field history gains the N-1 clause) — no priced figure in it moves. CONTRACT: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 153 → 154 — the playground-year convention gains the SPOUSE'S RMD AND THE RECIPROCAL BENEFICIARY FACT paragraph with the synthetic example, and the runPlaygroundYear description gains the matching paragraph (it also records that the request accepted neither field before this build). VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: every carriage site re-traced (prefill source, prefill, buildPgInputs and its three dependency lists, the remembered-form snapshot and its apply path, the projection template's stored round-trip, the saved-plan-year loader, the paste loader, Reset and Blank year, the paste emit / parse / key lists, both UI-state schemas and their lenient readers, the request schema and its inputs mapping, the paste response shape), with the projection walk's exclusion decided from its combined-RMD construction; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the scrub, the live drives, and the counts re-read): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 554/554 on the source grid (140-fixture slices, with the optimizer-heavy 140–280 range re-run in 35- and 12-fixture chunks after the standing OOM kills on this machine — every chunk full-pass); extended 161/161, retirement 63/63, December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20 — all via the source runners; packaged harness 349/349 (its full runner, including its own chunked census gate, exited clean; its main process also run directly from the built bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax, 349/349). LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the synthetic example returns the corrected spouse RMD exactly (rmdSpouse $32,467.53, divisor 15.4, table joint, AGI $32,467.53, federal tax $0), with provenance reporting API contract 154 and the response's paste payload carrying pretaxBalanceSpouse $500,000 and primarySoleBeneficiaryOfSpouse true; the same call without the fact returns the Uniform control exactly ($40,983.61, divisor 12.2, table uniform); runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries); runAccuracySelfCheck reports data integrity 0 violations. The stored December state and Tax Plan record were only read, never written. SCRUB: boundary-aware scrub (patterns.txt + patterns-supplement.txt, scrub-push workspace) over everything this build introduced — the Playground.tsx carriage blocks, the rothOptimizer.ts payload/parser blocks, the rothUiStateCore.ts schema and reader lines, the apiContractCore.ts request fields and convention paragraph, the actions.ts version line, paste shape and description paragraph, the extendedFixtures.ts template line, the new fixture and the PG3 re-pin, and this entry — confirms ZERO matches (the two whole-file grep hits are pre-existing text from earlier builds: the Month/Year toggle attribution comment in Playground.tsx, first name only, also recorded by S-4, and a statutory/sample passage in the contract file that predates this build); every figure above is the settlement's synthetic example or the fictional sample household's. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 follow-up #4 — a saved-plan year loaded into the Playground now carries its entering loss carryforward (the federal pair and the Washington-attributable portions), so the loaded year prices the march row exactly (API contract 152 → 153)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client loader change in client/src/Playground.tsx, display-only detail surfacing in server/src/taxEngine.ts, contract text in server/src/apiContractCore.ts with the version bump in server/src/actions.ts, and ONE new tax-census fixture — no engine pricing, schema, stored figure, or action signature changed. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the Playground's carry-in dials exist (S-2) and buildPgInputs passes them, but loadPgSavedPlanYear never set them, so a loaded year priced its gains gross and its ordinary income without the §1211(b) allowance the march claimed — on the settlement's worked example the loaded year read AGI and ACA MAGI $3,000 high and federal tax $360 high. THE FIX: the loader now sets the four carry-in dials from the loaded year's own detail — the federal pair from lossCarryInSt / lossCarryInLt (blank when $0, the S-6 funding-dial shape) — and the loaded-year note names the banked loss it carried in, with its Washington part when there is one. THE WASHINGTON QUALIFICATION, answered plainly (the brief asked whether the Washington half is needed to reproduce the march row and to include it if so): IT IS NEEDED. RothYearDetail surfaced only the absorbed Washington part (lossWaAbsorbed), so the entering Washington-attributable portions had no source; a loader copying only the federal pair reproduces every federal figure but prices a Washington year's excise on the gross gains (the fixture's Washington leg: state tax $18,338.91 against the march's $4,338.91 — overstated by exactly the 7% excise on the $200,000 Washington absorption). This build therefore adds four display-only lines to RothYearDetail — lossCarryInWaSt / lossCarryInWaLt entering and lossCarryOutWaSt / lossCarryOutWaLt leaving, by character — populated from the ledger state the march already threads (the year's carryInWaSt / carryInWaLt snapshot; the year-end ledFinal.waCarryOut), so no ledger replay from plan inputs was needed and no priced figure moves: the march's WA sub-state was always computed, only unsurfaced. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 follow-up #3 — the march now deducts the losses its own underwater-basis sales realize: the §1211(b) allowance on a loss-only taxable withdrawal, in both the netting transform and the settlement reprice gate (API contract unchanged, 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine change in server/src/taxEngine.ts (two hunks) plus ONE new tax-census fixture and three re-pins — no client, action signature, schema, or stored figure changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (152). THE FINDING (settled STAND): the underwater-basis fix makes the march's taxable sales realize losses, but the march never deducted them. (1) ledgerFields — the one netting transform every march pricing pass runs through — returned the negative ltcg on a loss-only taxable withdrawal but no current-year loss allowance when no carryforward entered, so priceYear defaulted the allowance to $0. (2) The settlement's reprice gate fired only when the priced gains total or the extra pre-tax draw was POSITIVE, so a loss-only withdrawal never repriced at all. The single-year pricer already did both right (pricePlaygroundYear's gainsFieldsFor returns capitalLossAllowance min($3,000, −grossGains) on a loss); the march was the only path that omitted it. THE FIX: ledgerFields now returns capitalLossAllowance min(capitalLossAllowanceCap, max(0, −grossGains)) on its no-carry-in branch, and the gate fires on a NONZERO gains total (pricedGainsTotal !== 0) instead of a positive one — a $0 total still skips, since the opening pricing already is the round's pricing at $0 of draw income. Both halves are independently necessary, verified by isolation during the build: a gate-only engine and a ledger-only engine each still price the pre-fix figures on the worked example. SCOPE BOUNDARY (the settlement's explicit exclusion): the carry-OUT ledger still runs only when a carry-in entered — a no-carry-in year's loss beyond the $3,000 allowance is banked nowhere, in the march or the Playground; that remainder is a separate, unreported question this build does not touch, and the new fixture pins lossAllowance and lossCarryOutLt at $0 on every leg. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's own, on the shared fictional sample household): 2026 MFJ, other ordinary income $50,000, spending the income plus a $30,000 gap, taxable-first, Do Nothing, no conversions, no carry-in, no yields, zero state tax. The pool opens 2026 at $100,000 against $200,000 of preserved basis — constructed inside the run: the plan starts in 2025 (pre-retirement, no spending) with Taxable at 100% basis sized so 2025's after-tax surplus sweeps the basis to exactly $200,000 on a $200,000 balance, and a −50% 2025 return in the return series halves the balance while the basis dollars stand. The year's first pricing taxes $17,800 at 10% = $1,780; sales fund the $30,000 gap plus that tax — $31,780 of sales realizing a $31,780 loss. CORRECTED: AGI and ACA MAGI $47,000, federal tax $1,480. BEFORE THE FIX the march kept AGI $50,000 and tax $1,780 — $300 overcharged, ACA MAGI overstated by $3,000. MORE INCOME LEVELS (same construction, spending always the income plus $30,000): the correction is the marginal rate × $3,000 — $20,000 of income: AGI $17,000, tax $0 before and after ($0 overcharge, pinning the allowance's AGI effect below the deduction); $90,000 (12%): AGI $87,000, tax $6,080 against $6,440 ($360); $150,000 (22%): AGI $147,000, tax $14,680 against $15,340 ($660); $250,000 (24%): AGI $247,000, tax $36,748 against $37,468 ($720; this leg's 2025 surplus exceeds a $200,000 opening basis, so its decline is −75% from $400,000 of basis over the same $100,000 balance — the allowance caps at $3,000 either way). Pre-fix figures for every leg were reproduced by driving a pristine pre-fix engine copy: AGI equalled income on every leg and the overcharges matched the marginal-rate rule exactly. NEW FIXTURE tax-march-loss-only-allowance-followup3 pins all five march legs plus the Playground agreement leg (pricePlaygroundYear on the worked leg's year — $50,000 of other ordinary income, the $31,780 sale against its $63,560 basis — returns AGI $47,000, tax $1,480, allowance $3,000, identical to the corrected march). CENSUS COUNT NOTE: the brief's verification line said 551; the tree already held 551 fixtures before this build (the same one-behind pattern S-2 and S-9 recorded), so with the one new fixture the census is 552. THREE RE-PINS, each a pre-existing fixture whose priced figures move BECAUSE the corrected march now claims the allowance its sales earn — each mechanism verified independently during the build (per-year or per-path diffs against a pristine pre-fix engine copy; each fixture passes alone on the pre-fix engine and fails on the fixed one): (a) mc-check-seeded-small-n — 28 of 40 paths diverge, and every sampled first divergence is a loss year whose AGI moves by exactly −min($3,000, the year's loss); re-pinned medianAdvantage $136,525.75, p10 −$12,128.87, p90 $475,130.91, winnerMedianNetCost $155,284.56 (wins 33, win rate 82.5%, and Do Nothing's median unmoved). (b) gift-kiddie-form-8615-stack-boundary — the parents' with-gift pool is underwater (the gift outflow removed $100,000 of balance but only $20,000 of basis), so their yearly tax sales realize losses the corrected march now claims (2035: $2,174.69 in full, under the cap), which widens the 0% gains space their taxable income leaves and lowers the child's Form 8615 stack tax; re-pinned childTax $10,683.80, netToChild $89,316.20, hand-verified from the parents' corrected 2035 detail ($125,025.31 AGI; 0% space $6,074.69; 15% × ($77,300 − $6,074.69) = $10,683.80). (c) tax-yield-tiers-exceeds-return-basis-uncapped — the first divergence is 2044 (2043 ends identical on both engines: basis $2,064,134.23 over a $2,014,395.98 balance), where a −$3,050.88 realized loss now claims the $3,000 allowance (AGI −$3,000 exactly, tax −$924.00) and every later year moves downstream; re-pinned the 2050 bundle (taxable end $1,968,998.75, basis $1,919,489.06, federal tax $20,742.23, dividend and interest $79,370.78 each) and the 2046-excess pin flips to 0 because the corrected path's 2046 pool no longer ends underwater — the follow-up #2 property itself (reinvested yield basis lands in full, floored at $0) is unchanged and still pinned by its unmoved hand-derived sibling fixture. LIVE ACTION CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear on the worked example's year reproduces AGI $47,000, federal tax $1,480, capitalLossAllowance $3,000 exactly; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries), and runAccuracySelfCheck reports December 88/88 and integrity 0. One honest limitation: the march leg itself cannot be driven through the live funding actions, because the action schema caps taxableBasisPct at 100 and the underwater opening exists only via the engine's per-year return series — the march correction is therefore pinned at the engine/fixture layer (five legs, census-green) with the live Playground action reproducing the same year's pricing to the cent. Boundary-aware scrub of everything this build introduced (both engine hunks, the new fixture, the three re-pin paragraphs, and this entry) confirms ZERO matches; the only whole-line hits when extracting the full re-pinned notes are pre-existing text from earlier builds (the gift note's long-standing gain figure and the tiers note's entered-benchmark figure), not this build's additions. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-12 — a stale spouse pre-tax balance no longer inflates the fill solvers' draw cap after a switch to single filing (API contract unchanged, 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine change in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts and server/src/decemberCore.ts plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no client, action signature, schema, or stored figure changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (152). THE FINDING (settled STAND): the pre-tax balance pair was totalled without regard to filing status in the shared single-year pricing module — a spouse balance typed while filing jointly stayed on the dial after the filing switched to single (or head of household), and every total summed it in, so the solver's draw cap priced money the filer does not hold. THE SETTLEMENT'S WORKED EXAMPLE: a single filer (2026, age 58, household of 1, the sample household's single benchmark $17,500, no other income) holding $50,000 of pre-tax with a stale $200,000 spouse balance — the cap read $250,000 and the ACA cliff fill returned $62,600, the whole household-of-1 cliff room (FPL $15,650 × 4; the settlement corrects the review's "$100,000 of MAGI room", which needs a household of 4 or more — at household 1 the mechanism's room is $62,600), a draw $12,600 larger than everything the filer holds; the bracket fill returned $121,800 on the same stale cap, and the pricer's conversionExceedsBalance read false at a $62,600 conversion. THE FIX: one gate, countedSpousePretax in rothOptimizer.ts — the spouse's balance counts toward a year's pre-tax total only when the filing status is MFJ — applied at every total of the pair in the module: (1) pricePlaygroundYear's balance total, so conversionExceedsBalance and rmdPriced read the filer's balance alone (the spouse RMD branch was already joint-gated and is unchanged; its own read sits inside that gate); (2) projectPlaygroundYears' combined walk balance; (3) solvePlaygroundBracketFill's cap; (4) solvePlaygroundAcaCliffFill's cap — the December headline's solver, whose console inputs carry the entered split verbatim, so the December draw is corrected by the same gate with no change to how the console state is stored or carried. The paste payload and parser still carry the spouse balance verbatim (carriage, not a total — a replayed paste must restore the same dial state, and the gate applies when it prices). One December total is gated in place for the same reason: computeDecemberProjection's enteredTotalBalance, which decides whether a $0 headline is blamed on an entered $0 balance, now adds the spouse balance only on an MFJ state — counting the stale balance there would have suppressed the empty-balance naming for a single filer whose own entered balance is $0. NOT CHANGED: any MFJ pricing (the spouse balance counts in full — the fixture's MFJ control is bit-identical, and the stored December reference case below is an MFJ state whose figures do not move); any stored record (the December state and Tax Plan record were read only, never written — the exclusion is priced, never stored, and no stored spouse balance is cleared or rewritten anywhere); the null-balance contract (no balance entered still caps nothing — a single filer with NO primary balance entered keeps that standing reading, there being no held balance to price); and the plan march (its per-spouse balances already follow each year's own filing status through the survivor machinery). CORRECTED PRICING on the worked example: cap $50,000; the cliff fill returns $50,000 with no buffer and with a $5,000 buffer (the cap binds below the $57,600 target), the bracket fill returns $50,000, a $62,600 conversion prices conversionExceedsBalance true while the $50,000 fill prices it false, head of household prices the same exclusion, and at age 75 the primary's RMD runs on the $50,000 alone ($2,032.52, Uniform divisor 24.6) with the bracket cap at $47,967.48. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (550 → 551 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 550 was the pre-S-12 count, the same off-by-one the S-8…S-11 entries recorded about their own briefs): tax-engines-solver-cap-stale-spouse-balance-s12, pinning the corrected cap and draw on the worked example (cliff and room $62,600, both fills at $50,000, the buffer leg, MAGI at the fill $50,000, the exceeds-balance pair), the bare control (no spouse balance entered — the identical $50,000, so the stale balance is fully excluded), the head-of-household leg, the MFJ control (cliff $84,600, fill $84,600, the joint cap not binding), the age-75 RMD leg, and a December leg through computeDecemberProjection (headline and likely-case max draw $50,000). The balances are the settlement's own round figures; the benchmarks are the shared fictional sample household's (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts). VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: every total of the balance pair in rothOptimizer.ts re-grepped and traced to the one gate (the pricer's total, the walk's combined balance, both solver caps), the carriage sites classified (paste emit / parse / key lists carry the value verbatim by design), every caller of the two solvers re-read (the Playground's fill chips and the December headline, per-case, and harvest-free solves — all priced through the gated solvers), the one December total of the pair gated in place, and the null-semantics edge walked (primary unentered + stale spouse → no total, the standing uncapped reading); pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the scrub, the live drives, and the counts re-read, including re-running the December suite and both live December drives after the enteredTotalBalance gate landed): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 551/551 on the 24-chunk source grid (23/23 on every full chunk, 22/22 on the last, teeth ok and suiteTotal 551 agreeing everywhere; the new fixture also passed standalone, before and after the December gate); extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations — all via runAccuracySelfCheck on the staged build; packaged harness 349/349 (the harness's own 6-chunk census OOM-killed chunks 1–2 at exit 137 — the standing limitation on this machine, as in S-6 / S-8 / S-9 / S-11 — so its main process was run from the built bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax; the census is the source-grid run above). ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-11 — Year funding's deep view names unpaid tax, so a gap that is really tax owed is no longer labelled a generic shortfall (API contract unchanged, 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. Presentation only in client/src/RothConversion.tsx (the Year funding deep view — the expanded per-year panel) plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no engine, pricing, schema, stored figure, or action changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (152). THE FINDING (settled STAND): the funding identity is sources + spendShortfall + unpaidTax = totalNeed, and the funding row has carried unpaidTaxCents all along, but the deep view never rendered it: its needs column showed a "Spending not covered" line for the shortfall and nothing for unpaid tax, and its only gap text was "Short by {need − sources} — the plan's balances could not cover this year's needs." A year whose spending was fully covered and whose entire gap was an unpayable tax bill therefore read as a generic shortfall, with no line anywhere saying tax was owed. THE FIX, all in the deep view's expanded year panel: (1) the needs column gains an "Unpaid tax — still owed" line at the row's unpaidTaxCents whenever it is positive, beside the pre-existing "Spending not covered" line; (2) the verdict sentence now names what the gap is made of — when the spending shortfall is $0 and unpaid tax is positive it reads that the year's spending was covered in full but the named amount of its tax bill could not be paid and is tax still owed, not spending the plan fell short on; when both are positive it names both parts; the pure-spending-shortfall wording is unchanged; (3) a footing line under the verdict states the identity in the view's own figures — funded {sources} + spending not covered {shortfall} + unpaid tax {unpaid} = total need — which always foots to the cent because buildRothFunding reconciles the cent-rounding residue onto a source, never onto the shortfall or the unpaid tax. NOT CHANGED: the year table above the panel (its "Short" badge still marks any underfunded year), any priced figure, the funding identity itself, and every other view. THE SETTLEMENT'S EXAMPLE, reproduced exactly: the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; samplePlanInputs with every balance $0, otherOrdinaryAnnual $200,000, annualSpending $278,000, inflationPct 0 and expectedReturnPct 0, Do Nothing). In 2039 the primary is 71 and the spouse 69, both drawing Social Security ($48,000 + $30,000 = $78,000) and both on Medicare; cash income $278,000 exactly equals the $278,000 spending need, so spending is covered in full, no surplus cash remains, and no account holds a cent to debit — the whole tax bill is unpaid: 85% of the benefits taxable ($66,300), AGI / MAGI $266,300, standard deduction $35,500 ($32,200 MFJ + two $1,650 age-65 additions, flat at 0% inflation), taxable income $230,800, federal tax $40,588.00, IRMAA $2,296.80 — total need $320,884.80, sources $278,000, spendShortfall $0, unpaid tax $42,884.80. Before the fix this year showed exactly "Short by $42,884.80" with no tax line; the corrected view shows the unpaid-tax line at $42,884.80, the tax-owed verdict, and the footing $278,000 + $0 + $42,884.80 = $320,884.80. FIXTURE: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (549 → 550 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 549 was the pre-S-11 count, S-10 having landed at 549, the same off-by-one S-10's entry recorded about its own brief): tax-year-funding-deep-view-unpaid-tax-s11, pinning the 2039 funding row the corrected view renders from (need, spending, federal tax, IRMAA, sources, shortfall, unpaid, the pre-fix "Short by" figure, the corrected view's unpaid-tax line, and the identity gap 0); the view is a direct rendering of those fields, the same division as the S-9 chart fixture. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the view's sourcesTotal traced term for term against buildRothFunding's twelve source fields, the footing's exactness traced to the residue rule (residue lands on a source only, so sources + shortfall + unpaid = need holds in cents on every row), and all four shortfall/unpaid sign combinations walked through the new verdict branches, including the unreachable both-zero gap the identity rules out; pass 2: the full-suite results below; pass 3: the scrub, the live drives, and the counts re-read): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 550/550 (the packaged harness's 6-chunk grid passed chunks 0/3/4/5 for 366 fixtures and OOM-killed chunks 1–2 at exit 137 — the standing limitation on this machine, as in S-6/S-8/S-9 — so the lost ranges [92, 276) were re-run on the 24-chunk grid, chunks 4–11, 23/23 each with teeth ok and suiteTotal 550 agreeing everywhere; the new fixture also passed standalone); extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations — all via runAccuracySelfCheck on the staged build; packaged harness 349/349 (its main process run from the built bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax, the census covered as above). LIVE CHECKS on the staged build: runRothFunding on the fixture's exact payload reproduces the corrected deep view's row to the cent (2039: totalNeedCents 32088480, sources $278,000 across Social Security and other income, spendShortfallCents 0, unpaidTaxCents 4288480, federalTaxCents 4058800, irmaaCents 229680, identity exact, provenance contract 152); runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-10 — priceExecutionYear carries the marginal-rate guardrail, so the execution year fills to the same conversion as the march (API contract unchanged, 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine change in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts (priceExecutionYear and its fill-target re-solve, executionFillTarget), the one caller in client/src/RothConversion.tsx, and ONE new tax-census fixture — no action signature, schema, or stored figure changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (152). RESTART NOTE: the first S-10 builder was killed by a daemon restart before reporting; its implementation survived in the tree intact, and this re-dispatched pass verified it end to end and finished the record (the S-4 pattern). THE FINDING (settled STAND): priceExecutionYear dropped the marginal-rate guardrail — its one-year strategy literal carried ceilings only, no guardrail key, and its fill-target re-solve priced the ceilings alone, so on a guardrail plan the execution year filled straight through the Social Security torpedo zone the plan's own march stopped in. THE FIX: (1) priceExecutionYear takes the saved strategy's guardrail flag as a new optional trailing parameter (absent / false prices bit-identically to before — every pre-existing caller and fixture is untouched) and the one-year strategy literal now carries the guardrail key, so the one-year march prices with the same marginal-rate stop as the plan's own march (its fill, ceiling convergence, and cliff / IRMAA grow-backs all read the strategy's guardrail through the one guardrailTargetPct derivation in simulateRothPlan); (2) executionFillTarget carries the same guardrail target — the strategy's bracket ceiling rate, when the guardrail is on and a bracket ceiling exists, the exact rule the march applies per year — and names the target with the guardrail's own label when the guardrail is what stopped it (when a ceiling binds first and the two targets agree, the ceiling's label stands); (3) the re-solve's settled base now also carries the year's yield income (interest plus the plan's qualified split of its dividends) exactly as the sim priced it — the guardrail's stop is defined on step costs, and the §86 provisional income driving the torpedo steps includes that yield, so a base without it misplaced the zone by tens of thousands; (4) the Roth view's execution-year caller passes the same guardrailOn flag its currentStrategy carries. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (shared fictional sample household, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; samplePlanInputs with birthYearSpouse 1978, acaHouseholdSize 5, annualSpending 60000 — the M-5 shape), strategy Fill to the top of the 22% bracket WITH the guardrail; the torpedo year is 2035 (the primary, born 1968, is 67 and the sample $48,000 benefit switches on). The march converts exactly $16,400 in 2035, bound by the guardrail. The execution year, priced standalone from the march's own entering state (the 2034 year-end balances as the execution balances, YTD $0): AFTER the fix it converts exactly $16,400 with $16,400 of remaining room, both its fill bound label and its fill target label reading the guardrail — the agreement the fixture pins (march fill $16,400 = execution-year fill $16,400); BEFORE the fix (the fixture's control legs — guardrail false, and the omitted-parameter default, which price bit-identically) it converted $155,100 with a $157,100 fill target, a $138,700 / $140,700 disagreement for the same plan and year (the settlement measured the same defect from the plan's starting balances at $162,300 / $185,700; the entering-state construction is the like-for-like form of the same comparison). ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-9 — the Playground income-stack chart labels qualified dividends correctly and carries the §1211(b) allowance, so the rendered stack foots to AGI (API contract unchanged, 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. Presentation only in client/src/Playground.tsx (buildStackModel and its two render sites) plus ONE new tax-census fixture — no engine, pricing, schema, stored figure, or action changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (152). THE FINDING (settled STAND): the income-stack chart decomposed pg.ltcgPriced by the TYPED sale gain — whenever pg.stockGain < 0 it drew ONE segment labelled "Long-term gains (net)" for the whole ltcgPriced, and no segment anywhere carried the §1211(b) capital-loss allowance, even though the model's own grossTotal subtracted it. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the settlement's own; shared fictional sample household, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): 2026, MFJ, ages 58 / 56, household 4, no benchmark, no state rate; the household's filed figures (interest $1,500, ordinary dividends $20,000 of which $15,000 qualified) plus a stock sale that LOST $5,000 (sold $20,000 against a $25,000 basis). Qualified dividends never net against a capital loss (round-7 R7-1), so ltcgPriced is the whole $15,000, the §1211(b) allowance is $3,000, and AGI is $18,500 — but the pre-fix chart drew "Long-term gains (net) $15,000" (no gains exist in the year at all; every dollar is qualified dividends) over ordinary segments of $6,500, a rendered stack of $21,500, overstated by exactly the $3,000 allowance, while the additive rows directly below footed to AGI correctly. THE FIX: the gains stack is now decomposed from the priced result's own components, each segment gated on its own priced figure — a "Qualified dividends" segment of pg.qualifiedDividends; a "Long-term gain" segment of max(0, pg.ltcgNet), the PRICED net capital gain, not the typed sale gain (an entering loss carryforward nets against the sale before the stack prices and a harvested gain adds to it, so the typed figure alone could overstate the priced part by the absorbed carry-in or omit a harvested gain entirely — the same defect class, closed by the same sourcing); and, when pg.capitalLossAllowance > 0, a NEGATIVE "Capital-loss allowance (§1211(b))" segment of −the allowance, hatched like the deductions and drawn over the stack's tail (the gainsPos left edge takes the lower of the two cumulative edges — the ordPos convention for negative amounts), with the legend swatch hatched to match. The segments therefore sum to gainsTotal − capitalLossAllowance and the rendered stack — bar, legend, and the gains bar's aria-label alike — foots to grossTotal (AGI). A no-loss year draws exactly the segments it drew before (same keys, labels, colours, order, positions); a pure-loss year with no dividends still draws no gains bar, but its legend now carries the allowance chip, so the legend foots to AGI there too. NOT CHANGED: any priced figure, the additive rows under the chart (already correct), the projection income chart (a different model over segDefs), the Roth view's stack, and every stored figure. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-8 — the December harvest pool field and its record resolution supply the starting pool, so the harvested gain prices correctly (API contract 151 → 152)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the December console's harvestPoolAmount means the STARTING pool — the pool at the start of the December year, before the year's own taxable sales — because decemberCaseInputs nets the year's sales and its 100%-basis taxable cash out of it to size the harvest from the REMAINING pool (round-17 defect 1). But both paths that supply the field supplied a CURRENT pool: the field's own wording ("Taxable pool available to sell") invited the pool as it stands, and load resolution filled a null fact from the Tax Plan record's pool as it stands when read (its entered taxable balance, or the latest snapshot's Taxable + Cash less the exclude-from-plan amount) — a pool the year's sales have already shrunk. Entering or resolving the current pool therefore netted the year's sales out a SECOND time and under-priced the harvest: in the settlement's worked example the double netting left a $0 remaining pool. THE WORKED EXAMPLE (the round-17 remaining-pool shape; fictional figures): 2026, MFJ, ages 60/58, household 2, benchmark $20,000, APTC taken $10,000, buffer $5,000 (cliff $84,600, target MAGI $79,600); other ordinary income $65,000 and the year's own sale — a $5,860 gain on $17,580 of basis (proceeds $23,440). The starting pool $40,000 at 75% basis ($30,000 of basis, $10,000 unrealized) stands at $16,560 with $12,420 of basis after that sale — a remaining unrealized gain of exactly $4,140, which fits whole inside the 0% room ($98,900 − $32,800 of ordinary taxable income = $66,100). CORRECTED: harvest $4,140, MAGI at a $0 draw $75,000, headline draw $4,600 landing MAGI at the $79,600 target, final credit $12,071.84. AS SUPPLIED BEFORE THE FIX (the current pool $16,560 in the field): remaining pool max(0, $16,560 − $23,440) = $0, harvest $0, MAGI at a $0 draw $70,860 (understated by exactly the $4,140 of unharvested gain), headline draw $8,740 (overstated by the same $4,140 — absorbed by the $5,000 buffer here; a larger gain or a smaller buffer breaches the cliff). At the headline the two pricings' MAGI and credit agree — the draw absorbs the whole error, which is why the settlement's credit claim holds at a fixed draw, not at the headline. THE FIX: (1) the field now asks for the starting pool — the December console's field is labelled "Taxable pool at the start of the year", its hint states the start-of-year-before-this-year's-sales meaning and that the console subtracts the year's sales itself, the Gain harvest section intro says the same, and the bill's harvested-gain jump link names the field by its new label; (2) load resolution (resolveDecemberStateAtLoad in server/src/decemberCore.ts) CONVERTS the record's current-pool fact to the starting pool before supplying it — the current pool plus the year's year-to-date sale (proceeds and basis from decemberSaleAmounts, the ONE sale derivation, now factored out of decemberCaseInputs so the conversion inverts the netting exactly) plus the year's 100%-basis taxable cash, with the basis % converted on the same dollars (the record's basis dollars + the basis the year's sale used + the taxable cash, over the starting pool) — so the remaining pool the harvest sizes from is the record's own current pool at its own basis, to the cent. The add-back is the year-to-date sale only: still-to-come distributions and checklist amounts have not left the pool yet, so a resolved starting pool behaves exactly like a user-entered one. Per-field discipline is unchanged (an entered console value, a $0 pool included, always wins; an unedited save persists the stored values, never the overlay; the toggle never resolves); a record that answers the basis but not the pool cannot be converted (its basis dollars are unknown) and its % resolves as entered. DecemberRecordFacts keeps the current-pool meaning — the conversion lives in the resolution, and recordFactsOf's comment says so — and the first-open preseed is unchanged (a first-open console has no year-to-date sale entered yet, so the record's pool preseeds as it stands and the field's start-of-year label governs it from there). The three December action descriptions now state the starting-pool meaning and the load conversion, and API_CONTRACT_VERSION moves 151 → 152 for that published-semantics change. FIXTURES: ONE NEW FIXTURE in the tax census (546 → 547 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 546 was written before S-7's fixture landed, the same off-by-one S-7's entry recorded): tax-engines-december-harvest-starting-pool-s8, with the PG3/S-7-pattern source-invariant comment above it for the render-level half (the field's label and hint cannot execute in the server-side suite). It pins all three legs of the worked example through computeDecemberProjection — the entered starting pool (harvest $4,140 at a $0 draw and at the headline, draw $4,600, non-draw MAGI $75,000, MAGI at headline $79,600, credit $12,071.84), the resolved leg (record facts $16,560 / 75% + the year's sale in the state resolve to $40,000 / 75% and price identically), and the control (the current pool entered as the field stood: harvest $0, draw $8,740, non-draw MAGI $70,860, credit at headline unchanged $12,071.84), with the two deltas pinned at exactly $4,140 (magiUnderstated / drawOverstated). The existing December fixture dec-harvest-resolution-and-save-rules gains conversion legs in place (the December count is unchanged at 88): the worked example's conversion ($16,560 at 75% → $40,000 at 75%), the taxable-cash conversion ($10,000 of 100%-basis cash → a $50,000 starting pool at 80%), the gain-only sale (proceeds added back alone → $22,420 at 55.4%), and the basis-only record (resolves as entered, no pool invented). VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the conversion traced against decemberCaseInputs' netting term by term (the helper's two branches reproduce the original saleProceeds / saleBasisDollars derivation exactly, and the December + tax suites confirm no priced figure moved anywhere else); pass 2: every surface naming the field re-read (label, hint, section intro, the bill jump link's aria-label, recordFactsOf, the preseed comment, the three action descriptions) and the per-field / save-provenance discipline re-checked against decemberStateForSave; pass 3: the full-suite results and live drives re-read): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; tax census 547/547 in six source chunks with teeth ok on every chunk and suiteTotal 547 agreeing (the packaged harness's own 6-chunk census run OOM-killed chunks 1–2, exit 137 — the standing limitation on this machine, as in the S-6 build — so the census was run as sequential source chunks and the harness's main process was run from its built bundle: 349/349 checks passed, including its describeApi version check against the new contract 152); extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations — all via runAccuracySelfCheck on the staged build. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-7 — the Playground strip and the Tax-for-the-year card read the same spending while the Spending dial is being edited (API contract unchanged, 151)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the Playground's sticky strip and its Tax-for-the-year card showed two different "Left after a year's spending" figures while the Spending dial was being edited — the card priced the local dial (buildPgInputs has fed the pricing pgSpendingCents since v145: the dial's figure while it parses to a positive amount, else the record's), while the strip (build v154) deliberately read the Tax Plan record alone (pgAnnualSpendingCents) so a stale local figure could never show there. The strip remains display arithmetic over the priced result (cash left minus that spending); the card keeps printing the engine's own cashLeftVsSpending, the r2 of the same subtraction over the same two inputs, so the two agree to the cent in Year mode and in the shared Month mode (each divides its own annual figure by 12). ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-5 — buildSavePayload sends the spend-from-cash sleeve, so the Lab, Year funding, the optimizer, and the Monte Carlo check price the sleeve the Plan tab and the strip price (no API contract change — the compute schemas already accepted the field; live drives report contract 150, unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the spend-from-cash sleeve was priced on the Plan tab (its local planInputs derive spendFromCashSleeveStart from the snapshot's Cash bucket) and on the ending strip (its payload is the saved record, whose null taxable balance lets the server thread the sleeve in resolveArgsBalances), but $0 in the Strategy Lab, Year funding, the optimizer, and the Monte Carlo check: those runs are built on buildSavePayload, which sends EFFECTIVE balances (an explicit taxableCents), so the server's snapshot threading never engages and the payload carried no sleeve — the cash share of each year's spending need was funded by taxable sales instead, realizing gains the Plan tab never priced (on the settlement's worked example, $7,200 of gains on the substituted $18,000 in 2030 alone). THE FIX (client/src/RothConversion.tsx only — no server pricing, no action schema, no stored value changed): (1) buildSavePayload now sends spendFromCashSleeveCents, derived in cents exactly as the local pricing derives it and as the server threads it — the snapshot's Cash bucket less the exclusion, floored at $0, and $0 beside a typed taxable balance (the engine caps it at the pool; in tiers mode the engine derives the sleeve from the tiers and the value is inert). Every working-form compute request spreads buildSavePayload (the Lab, Year funding, the optimizer, the Monte Carlo check — and, consistently, the work-years and gift compares), so all of them now price the sleeve the Plan tab prices. (2) PlanPayload's type gains the field as an optional compute-only transient. It is NOT a saved field: no writer's schema carries it, so the writers strip it at their boundary and it is never stored; and the two builders that face a writer or the saved-shape comparison omit it explicitly — buildInputsPayload (the plan record's writer payload keeps exactly its saved shape) and currentPlanPayload (planMatchesScenario still compares saved-shape identity only: a scenario record carries no sleeve, and a loaded scenario prices with the base payload's sleeve inherited through the compare merge). NOT CHANGED: the saved plan record and every stored figure; the strip and the what-if baselines (already correct through the saved-record path); the Plan tab's local pricing; December; the Playground. ONE NEW FIXTURE (tax census 543 → 544 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 543 was the count it expected this build to reach, the tree having reached 543 when S-4 landed), built entirely on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): tax-spend-cash-plan-funding-agreement-s5 — the household (MFJ, born 1968/1970, pre-tax $1,500,000, Roth $400,000, HSA $75,000, spending $180,000/yr, retire 62, window 62–73, Social Security $48,000 / $30,000 at 67, protect-min $50,000, preserve $250,000, heir rate 24%) with its taxable money carried as the folded pool the working form prices (Taxable $2,000,000 + Cash $100,000 = $2,100,000 at the household's 60% basis) and spendFromCashPct 10, with inflation and expected return held at 0 and yields and benchmarks blank (the case's stated simplifications) so 2030 — the first spending year — needs exactly $180,000 and every taxable sale prices at exactly 40% gains. WITH the sleeve riding the payload (spendFromCashSleeveCents 10000000, the household's $100,000 Cash bucket): the Plan-tab march (simulateRothPlan on the compare build's inputs under the plan's own strategy) pays 2030 cashSpend $18,000 (10% × $180,000), the Year funding rows (buildRothFunding on the same build) report the same 1800000 cents, 2030 MAGI agrees to the cent ($64,800 on both surfaces), Taxable sells only the remaining $162,000 for spending with draw gains exactly 40% × $162,000 = $64,800 (no taxable-sale gains substituted for the cash share; the federal tax is $0, the gains inside the 0% band, so no tax sale adds a second channel), the sleeve pays $18,000 a year through 2034 and its last $10,000 in 2035, and the funding identity foots every year in its documented form (the 0%-return shape runs dry in 2061–2063, so the shortfall term is real). THE PRE-FIX PAYLOAD (the identical shape with no sleeve key at all): 2030 cashSpendCents $0, the whole $180,000 sold (exactly $18,000 more), draw gains $72,000 and MAGI $72,000 (exactly $7,200 = 40% × $18,000 more on both) — the disagreement, pinned as the counterfactual. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes — pass 1: the derivation traced against planInputs and resolveArgsBalances term for term, every buildSavePayload consumer classified as compute / writer / comparison, and the writers' stripping confirmed against their schemas and handlers; pass 2: the full suites and live drives on the staged build; pass 3: the final tree re-typechecked, the new fixture re-run, the census identity leg corrected to the documented footing after its first run exposed the shortfall years, and the diff re-read, including reverting an edit that had landed on the neighbouring x50 fixture's identity sum and re-applying it to this fixture only): typecheck clean (server + client); tax census 544/544 on the 12-chunk source grid with teeth ok on every chunk; extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data integrity 0 violations — all through runAccuracySelfCheck on the staged build; packaged harness main checks 349/349 (run directly from the bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax, the census covered on the source grid). LIVE ACTION CHECKS on the staged build: runRothFunding on the worked-example payload exactly as buildSavePayload now sends it (yields entered as 0 so the stored record's blank-yield fallback cannot move the example) prices 2030 at cashSpendCents 1800000, MAGI 6480000 cents, Taxable sold for spending 16200000 cents, draw gains 6480000 cents, and its effectiveInputs echo carries the $100,000 sleeve; the identical payload with the sleeve key deleted (the pre-fix shape) prices 2030 cashSpendCents $0 with MAGI and draw gains of 7200000 cents — exactly $7,200 higher; runPlanYearDetail for 2030 on the sleeve payload reads cashSpend $18,000, MAGI $64,800, and the sleeve ending at $82,000 — the Plan tab's figures, in agreement with Year funding; runRothCompare's scenario echo carries the sleeve and its 2030 AGI agrees at $64,800 (the optimizer and Monte Carlo check consume the same payload field through the same planInputsFromSaved construction, pinned by the pre-existing tax-spend-cash-optimizer-passthrough fixture in the census); runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's added regions (the PlanPayload type block and the buildSavePayload / buildInputsPayload / currentPlanPayload hunks in client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the sampleHousehold import block and the new fixture in server/src/taxFixtures.ts, and this entry) for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches, and a whole-file sweep of both changed source files for the names, phone, and emails is likewise zero. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-4 — the Playground prices future years with the march's inflation/deflation treatment for statute-fixed amounts (API contract 149 → 150)

All user-entered data, no external source. (This build was re-dispatched after a daemon restart killed the first S-4 builder before it reported; the implementation had survived in the tree intact, and this pass verified it end to end, ran the live checks, and wrote this entry.) THE FINDING (settled STAND): the Playground priced future years at inflation 0 while the plan march deflates statute-fixed amounts, so the two disagreed on taxable Social Security, tax, and NIIT by amounts that grow with the horizon, and the cliff / bracket fill solvers solved to different conversions. THE FIX — one new optional fact, inflationPct, carried end to end, absent/null pricing bit-identically to before: (1) THE ENGINE (pricePlaygroundYear in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts): the caller's rate, when usable (finite, above −100%), resolves once and feeds the shared priceYear pass and every IRMAA tier call in the pricing — exactly the helpers and the rate the march feeds its own — so the year's §86 Social Security thresholds, §1411 NIIT thresholds, senior-deduction amount and phase-out, SALT caps, and premium-year IRMAA lines price at their deflated values; the result echoes the rate priced with (inflationPct, 0 when none was supplied). The cliff / bracket fill solvers price through this same function on the same inputs object, so they solve to the march's conversions with no solver change. (2) THE PLAYGROUND (client/src/Playground.tsx): buildPgInputs ALWAYS supplies the rate — the saved plan's own inflationPct resolved on the prefill source (inflation's home record is the Tax Plan; there is deliberately no second Playground dial), falling back to the plan default of 2.5% until a plan rate loads; the year hint for a year past the law table now names the deflation treatment and the rate; the projection template carries the rate (projTemplateToStored / projTemplateFromStored) so projected years price deflated too. (3) THE PASTE + ACTION PATHS: playgroundPastePayload emits the rate and parsePlaygroundPaste validates a present value as a percent, refusing one at or below −100% (outside the deflation factor's domain), spelled as undefined when unset — the S-2/S-3 pattern; a pre-S-4 paste carries no such key and prices the bare figures exactly as before. playgroundYearIn / playgroundInputsFromArgs (server/src/apiContractCore.ts) carry the rate (request schema: number > −100 or null), the runPlaygroundYear response and its paste payload carry it (server/src/actions.ts), the projection-template state gains it leniently (server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts — a blob written before it parses null and prices undeflated), the published playgroundYearSemantics convention gains the INFLATION paragraph naming the fixture, and the API contract version rises 149 → 150. ONE NEW FIXTURE (tax census 542 → 543 — the suite's own count; the dispatch brief's 542 was the count before this build, the tree having reached it when S-3 landed), built entirely on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): tax-engines-playground-inflation-s4 — a standalone 2035 bundle (MFJ 67/65, both on Medicare, interest $1,500, ordinary dividends $20,000 of which $15,000 qualified, other ordinary $23,500, the sample $48,000 benefit in pay; Social Security inside the §86 phase-in) whose corrected pricing (rate 2.5 supplied) reads taxable Social Security $33,507.13, AGI $78,507.13, federal tax $2,864.86, NIIT $0, against the bare construction's $27,250 / $2,175 — gaps of $6,257.13 of AGI and $689.86 of tax — with the march's own per-year pass (priceYear on the same components at 2.5%) reproducing the corrected figures to the cent on SS-taxable, AGI, tax, and NIIT; the same bundle at 2043 (both sample benefits in pay) reads corrected SS-taxable $50,764.08 and tax $4,935.69 against bare $40,000 / $3,644 — the Social Security gap grown to $10,764.08 — again equal to the march's own pass exactly; the sample plan's Do Nothing march 2043 year, loaded the S-3 loader's way, agrees with the march to the cent on SS-taxable, federal tax, and NIIT ($769.40 — the bare construction prices NIIT $0 and a federal tax short by exactly the NIIT); a 2035 bracket fill (10% top $24,800) solves to $30,158.30 corrected, landing at $24,799.98 of ordinary taxable income in the 10% bracket, against the bare fill $33,540.54 which priced with the march's treatment lands at $31,057.13, in the 12% bracket; and the paste/API carriage pins (the rate rides through and parses back, a key-deleted legacy paste prices the bare SS figure, the contract path prices the corrected 2035 figures, and a rate of −100 is refused). The PG3 paste key-count pin rises 37 → 38 keys for the new field. VERIFICATION: three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1: the engine resolution and every consumer of the resolved rate — the priceYear pass, the IRMAA tier calls, the fill solvers spreading the same inputs — traced against the march's own feeding of the same helpers; pass 2: every carriage surface — paste payload and parser spelling, template store round-trip, request/response schemas, the contract prose and version, the Playground's always-supply site and its year hint; pass 3: scope — absent/null prices bit-identically everywhere, December's current-year pricing untouched since its deflation factor is 1 at any rate); typecheck clean (client + server); packaged harness fully green — tax census 543/543 across the six chunks with teeth ok on every chunk, extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, extended and retirement teeth pass (exactly one deliberate failure each), data integrity 0 violations, packaged harness 349/349 checks. LIVE ACTION CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear reproduces the corrected 2035 bundle to the cent (SS-taxable $33,507.13, AGI $78,507.13, federal tax $2,864.86, NIIT $0, rate echoed 2.5, paste payload carrying the rate, provenance contract 150) and the corrected 2043 bundle (SS-taxable $50,764.08, federal tax $4,935.69); runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly in all three cases (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries).
