## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-3 — a saved-plan year loaded into the Playground no longer double-counts the march's reinvested yield as spendable cash (API contract 148 → 149)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the plan march reinvests its taxable yield — the interest and dividends stay inside the taxable balance (which grows at the full expected return, of which the yield is a component), raise the basis ledger, and count $0 in the funding ledger — but the Playground's saved-plan-year loader set the interest and dividend dials from the march year and priced them as cash in hand, on top of the loader's march-sized stock sales and pre-tax money out, so every loaded year repriced with more cash left than the march funded, by the yield. The settlement's identity for the gap, on the pre-fix construction, is diff = yield + conversion − cashSpend − rothDraw (the conversion term is the pre-M-2 term; since M-2 a conversion counts no cash on either surface). THE FIX — one new fact, yieldReinvested, carried end to end, absent/false pricing bit-identically to before: (1) THE ENGINE (pricePlaygroundYear in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts): when the caller supplies yieldReinvested, the year's interest + total ordinary dividends still price as income in full (AGI, MAGI, tax, and credit are identical with and without the flag — pinned in both fixture years) but cashIn excludes them; the result names the exclusion (yieldReinvested / reinvestedYield, the excluded amount, $0 when the flag is off), and the runPlaygroundYear response schema carries both fields (server/src/actions.ts, beside playgroundPasteOut gaining the flag so the action's paste payload round-trips it). (2) THE LOADER (client/src/Playground.tsx): loadPgSavedPlanYear sets the flag (the money came from the march) and the preset note says so in plain words; typing into the interest or dividends dial clears it (a typed figure is the user's own, received as cash); Reset, Blank year, the as-filed load, and Prefill clear it; the projection template does not carry it (the S-2 precedent for loader-only facts — the stored template drops it exactly as it drops the spending draw, while the live template built from the current dials carries it). The form remembers it with the other dials (one new playgroundFormState field in server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts, lenient parse defaulting to off, so stored forms price exactly as before). (3) THE PASTE + ACTION PATHS: playgroundPastePayload emits the flag and parsePlaygroundPaste validates a present value as a yes/no value, spelling "off" as undefined in the parsed inputs — the S-2 pattern, which this build needed in fact: the first packaged census run failed ea-playground-paste-roundtrip-full's inputs-identical pin because the parser spelled the flag as a literal false, which a JSON round-trip keeps where the identity drops unset keys; with the spelling aligned the identity holds again and no priced figure moves (the engine reads absent and false identically). A paste written before S-3 carries no such key and loads with the yield counting as cash, exactly as before. playgroundYearIn / playgroundInputsFromArgs (server/src/apiContractCore.ts) carry the flag, the published playgroundYearSemantics convention gains the REINVESTED YIELD paragraph naming the fixture, and the API contract version rises 148 → 149. ONE NEW FIXTURE (tax census 541 → 542 — the suite's own count; the brief's 541 was the count before this build, the tree having reached it when S-2 landed four fixtures), built entirely on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts — taxable $2,000,000 yielding dividends $20,000 and interest $1,500 at the filed actuals, expected return 5%, spending $180,000 from age 62, household 4, family benchmark $36,000), Do Nothing strategy: tax-engines-playground-loaded-plan-yield-s3 — 2026 (ages 58/56, pre-retirement, no funding): the march's yield is $21,500, its funding sources and cash left are $0, the bare loader construction read cash left $21,500, and the corrected construction reads cash in $0 and cash left $0, agreement 0 cents. 2030 (ages 62/60, the first spending year): the yield has grown with the balance to $21,500 × 1.05^4 = $26,133.39 (interest $1,823.26 + dividends $24,310.13); the march funds the $180,000 spending with $180,000 of taxable sales, prices $0 federal tax (AGI $110,420.11) and keeps a $25,002.16 credit, leaving $205,002.16; the bare construction read cash left $231,135.55 and the corrected construction reads exactly $205,002.16, agreement 0 cents — and in both years bare − corrected equals the yield to the cent, so the identity holds and the overstatement's growth with the year is pinned, not just its 2026 size. The march analogue is the funding ledger's own arithmetic (its applied sources less its funded federal + state tax plus the credit kept; both years carry $0 IRMAA and $0 health-premium needs, pinned as preconditions). The fixture also pins the paste carrying and parsing the flag, a legacy paste loading with it off, and the contract path pricing 2030's corrected cash left. RE-PIN: mt-pg3-playground-statelessness payload keys 36 → 37 (the new paste field; its note updated). KNOWN ADJACENT GAPS, deliberately NOT in this build (the settlement's fix sentence covers the yield term; the fixture years carry none of the other three): the loader still folds the year's extra pre-tax draw into the conversion dial, where since M-2 it counts $0 of cash, so a loaded year the march funded partly with a pre-tax spending draw understates cash left by that draw; and the cash-sleeve spend and Roth draw have no Playground dials at all, so a loaded year funded by either understates by those amounts — the identity's other two terms, awaiting their own settled findings. VERIFICATION (three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff — pass 1 the engine and paste hunks, which with the first census run caught the round-trip spelling above; the fix landed and passes 2 and 3 re-ran everything on the final tree): typecheck clean (server + client); tax census 542/542 in mixed chunkings (the packaged 6-chunk grid passed chunks 0, 3, 4, 5 while chunks 1 and 2 were OOM-killed at the standing machine limit, so the missing ranges were covered on the 12-chunk grid at 46 wide — chunks 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 11 — with every chunk that can observe the parser fix re-run on the final bundle, teeth ok on every chunk; the live tax action itself timed out at the worker's 120s limit, the standing S-2 limitation), extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, extended and retirement teeth pass (exactly one deliberate failure each), packaged harness 349/349, data integrity 0 violations live. LIVE ACTION CHECKS on the staged build: runPlaygroundYear reproduces both corrected years to the cent (2026: cash in $0, cash left $0, reinvestedYield $21,500; 2030: cash in $180,000, cash left $205,002.16, reinvestedYield $26,133.39, credit $25,002.16) and the bare counterfactual (2030 without the flag: cash left $231,135.55, AGI identical at $110,420.11), its paste payload carries the flag and reports contract 149; runDecemberProjection on the stored console state reproduces the December reference case exactly (its figures are the household's and are not restated here, as in prior entries). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of the changed files (client/src/Playground.tsx, server/src/rothOptimizer.ts, server/src/apiContractCore.ts, server/src/actions.ts, server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts, server/src/taxFixtures.ts, and this entry) for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only substring hit in the wider files is a pre-existing fixture's fictional lifetime-cents figure that contains a listed figure's digits inside a longer number, not a boundary match, not this build's, and not the household's. ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-2 — the Playground gains dials for the three December-only pricing facts (capital-loss carry-in, RMD already received, dependent MAGI), so it prices those years the way December does (API contract 147 → 148)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): the single-year engine (pricePlaygroundYear in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) has always priced three facts the December console supplies — a capital loss carried into the year, an RMD amount already received, and a filing dependent's MAGI for the ACA household — but the Playground never collected them, so a Playground year that has any of them mispriced: (a) a $20,000 long-term carry-in left the year's tax and MAGI overstated (the settlement's example put the tax overstatement at $3,060 and MAGI's at $18,000 on its shape); (b) an RMD already received was counted twice, once as received and once inside the full priced RMD ($20,000–$30,000 of income double-counted on the settlement's shapes); (c) with a dependent's MAGI of $15,000 the Playground showed a $23,898.60 credit and "under by $7,100" where the true credit is $0 (over the cliff by $7,900). THE FIX — wiring and dials only, no engine pricing change (the engine already netted, capped, and ACA-scoped all three facts exactly as December passes them): (1) SIX NEW DIALS in client/src/Playground.tsx, mirroring December's own four-plus-two so the Playground prices EXACTLY as December does — "RMD already received this year" in the Pre-tax money out section; "Short-term loss carried in", "Long-term loss carried in", "Of the short-term loss, the Washington part", and "Of the long-term loss, the Washington part" in the Stock sale (long-term) section; "Dependent MAGI for ACA" in the ACA & state section — each with December's own hint wording (the received part is already inside the income above; the dependent's MAGI counts toward the ACA household MAGI only when the dependent is required to file). buildPgInputs passes all six on every pricing (blank = $0 = the pre-S-2 pricing, so a year with none of the facts prices bit-identically); the dials are remembered with the form (six new playgroundFormState fields in server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts, lenient parse defaulting blank, so stored forms price exactly as before), ride the paste payload as OPTIONAL fields, load through Paste, and are cleared by Reset and Blank year. Prefill, the saved-plan-year loader, and the projection template do NOT set them (the S-1 precedent throughout). (2) THE PASTE ROUND-TRIP (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts): playgroundPastePayload emits the six (null when unset) and parsePlaygroundPaste parses them optionally — a pre-S-2 paste loads with all six absent and prices exactly as before; a negative or non-numeric value refuses the whole paste with a plain error. The parsed inputs spell "unset" as undefined for all four optional money facts of this kind (the S-1 settlement pair included, whose return spelling this build aligns): a JSON round-trip drops undefined keys, so a paste of a year where a fact was never entered parses back to inputs IDENTICAL to the ones that produced it — the identity the pre-existing ea-playground-paste-roundtrip-full fixture pins. That fixture was in fact failing on this point since S-1 spelled its two facts as null in the parsed inputs (the failure surfaces only on chunk boundaries that include the fixture; this build's first slice pass reported the range green in error, the packaged taxtest chunk caught it, and direct re-runs confirmed it) — with the spelling aligned, the identity holds again and no priced figure moves (the engine reads absent, undefined, and null identically for every one of these facts). (3) THE ACTION PATH: playgroundYearIn (server/src/apiContractCore.ts) gains the six optional fields and playgroundInputsFromArgs carries them verbatim, playgroundPasteOut (server/src/actions.ts) gains the six nullable keys so runPlaygroundYear's paste payload round-trips them, and the API contract version rises 147 → 148 (the build touches the action schema; S-1 did not). THREE NEW FIXTURES (tax census 538 → 541 — the suite's own count; the brief's 537 was already one behind the tree before this build), all built entirely on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts — 2026 MFJ 58/56, return interest $1,500, dividends $20,000 of which $15,000 qualified, household 4, benchmark $36,000, spending $180,000; standard deduction $32,200; 0% gains top $98,900): tax-engines-playground-carry-in-s2 — other ordinary $150,000 and a $30,000 long-term gain: with the $20,000 LT carry-in the net gain is $10,000 (priced stack $25,000), AGI/MAGI $181,500, taxable $149,300, federal tax $20,520, against the bare construction's AGI $201,500 and tax $23,520 (overstated $20,000 of MAGI and $3,000 = $20,000 × 15% of tax on this shape); a $10,000-gain leg pins the $3,000 loss allowance and a $7,000 LT carry-out; a both-buckets leg pins ST/LT netting order; December's own case inputs for the same year agree on every figure, and the paste + API paths carry the fact. tax-engines-playground-rmd-received-s2 — 2043, ages 75/73, both on Medicare, SS $48,000 + $30,000, other ordinary $20,000, pre-tax $1,500,000: gross RMD $60,975.61 ($1,500,000 / 24.6, the Uniform divisor at 75); with $20,000 already received the priced RMD is $40,975.61, SS taxable $66,300 (the 85% cap binds), AGI $148,775.61, taxable $113,275.61, federal tax $13,453.41, against the bare AGI $168,775.61 and tax $17,694.63; a second leg types the already-received money as other ordinary income with the full $60,975.61 received and pins the priced RMD at $0 with the same tax — the received money counted exactly once either way; December agrees; the paste carries it. tax-engines-playground-dependent-magi-s2 — the settlement's own example reproduced exactly: other ordinary $30,000 and a $70,000 conversion put the parents' MAGI at $121,500 against the household-of-4 cliff of $128,600; bare, the year reads under by $7,100 with a $23,898.60 credit ($36,000 − 9.96% × $121,500), net bill −$15,478.60, cash left $66,978.60; with the dependent's $15,000 the ACA MAGI is $136,500 — over by $7,900 — the credit is $0, the net bill is the $8,420 tax alone, and cash left is $43,080, while AGI, taxable income ($89,300), and federal tax ($8,420) are identical with and without the fact (the dependent's MAGI joins the §36B household MAGI only); ## Build (2026-11-04): Engines review round 2 S-1 — the Playground's cash left after tax now prices the year's ACA filing settlement, agreeing with December (API contract unchanged, 147)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE FINDING (settled STAND): for the same year, the Playground's "Cash left after tax" disagreed with the December view's by the full ACA credit, flipping the enough/short verdict. The engine has priced the year's FILING SETTLEMENT since build v193 (netTaxBill = total tax − credit still due + excess advance credit to repay − refundable education credit, on the final allowable credit) — but only for callers that supply the reconciliation facts (aptcTaken, acaEnrollmentPremiumAnnual, acaCoverageReduction), and the Playground's dial construction (buildPgInputs in client/src/Playground.tsx) supplied none, so every Playground year priced the un-reconciled bill (the tax alone) while December settled the same year. The Playground's ⓘ justified the gap with a premise build v208 inverted: it claimed the annual spending already holds the net premium, but v208 reads spending as EXCLUDING the premium and prices the premium separately (cash left after health premiums) — so the un-reconciled cash left was simply missing the settlement, not avoiding a double-count. THE FIX, reconciling both definitions together: (1) buildPgInputs now ALWAYS passes the three facts — two new dials in the ACA & state section, "Advance credit (APTC) already taken / yr" and "Coverage-month reduction / yr" (blank = $0, the December console's own defaults), plus the existing marketplace health-premium dial reused as the enrollment premium (the same fact — the premium of the plan actually enrolled in; blank = no cap, as December reads it). The dials are remembered with the rest of the form (two new playgroundFormState fields in server/src/rothUiStateCore.ts, lenient parse defaulting blank, so pre-existing stored forms price exactly as before), ride the paste payload as OPTIONAL fields (playgroundPastePayload / parsePlaygroundPaste in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts — a pre-S-1 paste loads with both absent, un-reconciled, exactly as before), and are cleared by Reset and Blank year like every other single-year dial. Prefill and the saved-plan-year loader do not set them (the v208 health-dial precedent); projection years stay un-reconciled (the plan model — the projection template carries no health or reconciliation facts, as before). (2) THE v208 PAIRING (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts, pricePlaygroundYear): the net health premium now nets off the credit cash actually received toward the premium — the advance credit taken when the settlement prices, otherwise the priced credit capped at the gross (the fully-advanced treatment, unchanged). Without this, a reconciled cash left (which already settles the credit still due in its bill) paired with the old fully-advanced net premium would count the credit twice and the after-health readout would fall by the credit still due; with it, cash left after health premiums is invariant across the reconciled / un-reconciled forms of the same year. No settlement arithmetic, no December code, and no un-reconciled figure moved — the v208 health fixture's pins are unchanged. (3) THE CORRECTED ⓘ: the false justification is replaced by a shared exported constant, PLAYGROUND_CASH_LEFT_BASIS (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts), rendered verbatim by the Playground's ⓘ and pinned by the new fixture: the bill is the year's filing settlement (total tax, less the premium credit still due at filing, plus any advance credit taken above the final credit to repay, less any refundable education credit), and the health premium is not in the annual spending — it is priced separately, in the cash left after health premiums — so the credit counts once, in the settlement, and the premium counts once, in its own readout. The same stale premise was corrected in the engine's field/result/pricer comments, the runPlaygroundYear action description, and the F7 fixture's note (its priced figures unmoved — it still prices the un-reconciled form deliberately, as the F7 anchor). NEW FIXTURE tax-engines-playground-december-agreement-s1 (tax census 536 → 537), built entirely on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): 2026, MFJ 58/56, household 4, benchmark $36,000, spending $180,000, buffer $5,000, pre-tax $1,500,000, entered income $30,000 other ordinary + the sample return's $1,500 interest / $20,000 dividends ($15,000 qualified) + a $55,000 sale on a $45,000 basis. The agreement is pinned at DECEMBER'S SOLVER HEADLINE, not a worked draw (the gap is draw-specific): headline draw $62,100 landing MAGI $123,600 at cliff $128,600 − buffer; hand-derived federal tax $7,472 (taxable $91,400, ordinary part $66,400 at 10%/12%, the $25,000 preferential part under the 0% threshold) and final credit $23,689.44 ($36,000 − 9.96% × $123,600). At APTC $0, December's cashLeftAtHeadline and the Playground construction's cashLeftAfterTax agree to the cent at $184,817.44 (both Enough, +$4,817.44 vs spending), while the fact-stripped control (the pre-S-1 construction) reads $161,128, Short by $18,872 — the verdict flip, gap exactly the full credit $23,689.44. At APTC $12,000 both surfaces agree again at $172,817.44 (gap vs the same control = the credit still due, $11,689.44), proving the facts flow rather than a zero-default coincidence. The health pairing is pinned by invariance: with the premium entered at $36,000, cash left after health premiums is $148,817.44 under all three legs (net premiums $36,000 / $24,000 / $12,310.56). RE-PIN: mt-pg3-playground-statelessness payload keys 28 → 30 (the two new paste fields; its note updated). ## Build (2026-11-03): Engines review round 2 M-5 — the cliff and IRMAA grow-backs now respect the marginal-rate guardrail (API contract unchanged, 147)

All user-entered data, no external source. Server engine fix (server/src/taxEngine.ts — one new predicate, guardrailStepOk, carried by both grow-back bisections in simulateRothPlan; server/src/taxFixtures.ts — one new fixture). THE FINDING (settled STAND, figures corrected by the settlement): fillConversion hard-stops on the marginal-rate guardrail (the first $100 step whose federal + state tax cost exceeds the strategy's bracket-ceiling rate ends the fill), but both grow-backs — the R7-5 IRMAA sizer alignment and the cliff-cap grow-back — bisected on respectsCeilings (plus tierOk on the IRMAA side) only, never the guardrail, so a guardrail strategy's grown year could land far above the guardrail and the optimizer's guardrail and non-guardrail variants of a cliff/IRMAA candidate priced identically (the phantom variant). WORKED EXAMPLE (the shared fictional sample household, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts — samplePlanInputs with birthYearSpouse 1978, acaHouseholdSize 5, annualSpending $60,000; strategy {bracketTopPct 22, acaCliffCap}, 2035): the fill stops at $16,300 on the guardrail, but the cliff grow-back landed the year on the cliff itself — conversion $65,252.42, ACA MAGI $154,720.00 (the cliff to the cent), federal tax $11,432.97, credit kept $2,089.89 — identical with guardrail on or off, in every year. THE FIX: a grow-back candidate is now feasible only when it also passes guardrailStepOk — the $100 step into the candidate's own total conversion, priced on the candidate's own settled base (priceWith over the candidate settlement's realized gains and pre-tax draw — the same repricing base the year's effective marginal rate is computed on, because the settlement's gains feedback moves the crossing, so the fill's base cannot judge the grown year), costs no more than the guardrail target (the step's increase in federal + state tax, which for a $100 step is the effective marginal rate in percent — fillConversion's own step rule judged on the settled path; a partial step at the very bottom is judged pro-rated). With no guardrail the predicate passes every candidate, so non-guardrail years price bit-identically (the fixture's non-guardrail pins are the pre-fix figures, unchanged). CORRECTED LANDINGS (engine-derived, independently verified in the fixture by reconstructing each landed year's priced components through priceYear — the reconstruction reproduces the year's federal tax to the cent, the step into the landing costs $22.00, the next step $27.00 on the cliff shape and $25.80 on the IRMAA shape, and a $100-step sweep on the cliff landing's base finds the first over-target step is the step into $52,200): cliff + guardrail 2035 conversion $52,194.37 (federal tax $7,673.76, ACA MAGI $140,016.70, credit kept $3,554.34, taxable income $98,966.70, realized gains $10,537.30, fill bound label now "Marginal-rate guardrail (22%)") against the non-guardrail $65,252.42 cliff landing — the settlement's hand sweep put the guardrail boundary at $52,400 in round $100 chunks with approximated gains feedback; the engine's own settled bases put the cent-exact crossing at $52,194.37. IRMAA + guardrail ({bracketTopPct 22, irmaaTierCap 1}, same household and year): $112,469.38 (MAGI $200,182.25, federal tax $23,325.91) against the non-guardrail $151,390.73 (MAGI $245,250, the Tier 1 top, federal tax $34,513.66) — the IRMAA phantom is likewise gone. NEW FIXTURE roth-m5-growbacks-respect-guardrail pins all of the above (tax census 535 → 536). RE-PINS (8, all engine-derived optimizer-winner regression pins, each note carrying its M-5 re-pin parenthetical): restricting the grow-backs makes the guardrail + IRMAA-cap candidates cheaper — pre-fix their over-grown conversions cost more than they saved — so the torpedo plan's winner moves from the Fill-12% no-cap candidate (net $181,984.20, first-year conversion $87,800) to a Fill-12% + IRMAA-cap guardrail candidate (net $177,667.65, first-year conversion $99,850; verified by disabling the new predicate, which restores the old winner exactly, and by pricing the new winner's candidate with and without the predicate: its own lifetime tax falls $5,853.20, from $183,520.85, because its grow-back years no longer convert at 27% marginal steps), and the joint (born-1966) winner's net falls $203,231.48 → $200,877.28 with its fixed-claim best $223,353.19 → $221,753.51. The eight: opt-torpedo-guardrail-pauses-fill (winnerConv), joint-maxifi-property (joint/fixed nets and both beat-by figures), mc-check-zero-vol-equals-deterministic (winner net and advantage figures), mc-check-seeded-small-n (winner-side stream statistics), opt-ss-collected-carried-by-scores (winnerNetCost), claim-table-per-age-best (winnerRowNetCost), claim-floor-crowning (row64NetCost $4,261.60 → $4,203.52), claim-floor-edges-and-blank (absentWinner). Every other pre-existing fixture — including all hand-derived statutory cases and every non-guardrail pin — passes unchanged. One verification anomaly is recorded plainly: the first two census passes over the fixed engine (sliced source runs and the packaged harness) passed all 535 pre-existing fixtures with the old pins, and only later runs land on the corrected winners, consistently across source and packaged runners and across repeated probes (six consecutive identical outcomes, and the predicate-disabled control reproducing the old winner on demand) — the suite's documented intermittent census variation (see the replay reproducibility diagnostic in taxFixtures.ts, which found the same process-boundary bistability and could not localize a mechanism); the re-pinned values are the ones the fixed engine deterministically produces in the current state, verified by the control above. NOT CHANGED: fillConversion and its guardrail rule, the convergence re-solve and R7-4 clamp, the draw-cap search, any non-guardrail pricing (bit-identical, as the unchanged non-guardrail pins in the new fixture show), the December case, any stored figure, and the API contract. VERIFICATION: typecheck clean (server + client); tax census 536/536 in slices of 50 after the re-pins (enumeration run before them: exactly the 8 above failed, slices from index 150 onward fully clean), extended 161/161, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), December 88/88, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, packaged harness 349/349 with its census chunks totalling the same 536 (run before the re-pins, on the passing outcome described above); the December reference case and data-integrity/live action checks ride the post-build audit pass as in prior rounds. The tax teeth core check was resource-killed on this machine (the standing limit) and is not part of this build's suite list. ## Build v208 (2026-11-03): the health premium term — marketplace and Medicare premiums are now an entered input priced into the yearly need, the score, the Playground pricer, and the funding table (API contract 146 → 147)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE GAP (verified against the engine before this build): the yearly need the plan prices was spending + federal tax + penalty + state tax + IRMAA — the engine tracked the ACA credit and subtracted it in the score, but never charged the premium the credit offsets, and in Medicare years only the IRMAA surcharge was charged, never the base Part B + Part D premium. THE DESIGN — opt-in by entry, three optional fields in today's dollars, all blank by default and blank in the seed (the seed never invents premiums): the record gains healthPremiumAcaHouseholdCents (the gross marketplace premium for a year when BOTH spouses are on the marketplace), healthPremiumAcaSingleCents (the gross premium when exactly one spouse is — the spouse-only years), and healthPremiumMedicarePerPersonCents (the annual base premium per person on Medicare — Part B standard plus Part D base; the IRMAA surcharge stays its own separate need, so nothing is double-counted). Entering ANY of the three activates the term: annualSpending is then read as spending EXCLUDING health premiums, the older embedded-premium reconciliation (the v135 mechanism that priced an unentered premium inside spending) is switched off for that record, and each retired year funds its actual premium on top of its need. With all three blank, every year prices bit-identically to before — that is what keeps every pre-existing fixture green without re-pinning. THE YEAR SCHEDULE: retired years only (age at or past the retirement age; $0 before it — working years price employer coverage, which is why the December reference case, a working year, still prices a $0 premium and reproduces exactly). A marketplace year's gross is the applicable entered tier — household when both spouses are on the marketplace, single when exactly one is; when the applicable tier was not entered, the year's priced benchmark for that household shape stands in for the gross (never the other tier). The funded amount is NET: gross less the year's priced credit, the credit capped at the gross (the entered premium IS the enrollment premium, so the Form 8962 enrollment cap applies), iterated inside the year's settlement exactly like the v135 term — same settlement driver, same harvest and under-138 handling. A Medicare year's premium is the per-person amount times that year's count of persons on Medicare (the same count IRMAA charges on). A mixed year (one spouse on Medicare, one on the marketplace) carries both parts. THE SCORE: the net-cost breakdown gains healthPremium (the lifetime GROSS premium, added) and healthPremiumNet (display); net cost = tax + penalty + IRMAA + healthPremium − ACA credit − education refundable credits + terminal, so the premium's net lifetime effect is exactly the net premium, and with the term inactive both fields are $0 and the identity is bit-identical to before. The terminal tier rule is unchanged and is now pinned as a fixture in its own right (below). THE FUNDING TABLE: each year's funding row gains healthPremiumCents as its own need and its spending figure EXCLUDES it, so spending + health premium + federal tax + state tax + IRMAA = total need and the row foots exactly; the Tax Plan's funding section names the health premium in its intro sentence whenever any year carries one, each year-detail "what the year needed" list gains a net health premium row when the year has one, and the score explainers (optimizer score text and the tax-by-year net-cost text) name the gross and net premium so they still foot. THE PLAYGROUND PRICER: two optional inputs (marketplace premium for the year, Medicare premium per person) and three readouts — healthPremiumGross, healthPremiumNet, and cashLeftAfterHealthPremium (= cash left after tax − net premium). The premium never enters tax, MAGI, or the net tax bill; the marketplace part counts only in a year the ACA layer prices (at least one person not on Medicare), the Medicare part per the year's own Medicare flags, and an unpriced credit (no benchmark entered) leaves the marketplace gross whole. The Playground screen gains the two dials and, when a net premium is priced, top-strip readouts for the net premium and the cash left after health premiums; the inputs ride the paste payload and its parser (a pre-build paste still loads, both inputs absent), and the Tax Plan gains the three fields in its Taxes & ACA section plus matching Strategy Lab dials. The multi-year Playground projection template is NOT extended — projections still price a $0 premium, as before. OPEN ITEMS SURFACED, NOT INVENTED: no plan has been picked, so the fields ship blank; the spouse-only marketplace premium for the years when one spouse is on Medicare and the other is not was not among the researched figures, so that field likewise ships blank — left blank, those years price the year's single-household benchmark as the gross (the fallback above), and entering the field replaces it. The M-1 and S-1 findings from the engines review round 2 settlement are untouched by this build and survive it as they stand. EXCLUSION STATE: the term is orthogonal to the saved taxable exclusion — the build changes no stored figure (the record's three new fields read null until entered, and the saved exclusion stays exactly as saved); live verification priced the record AS SAVED, exclusion applied. WORKED EXAMPLE (the shared fictional sample household, server/src/sampleHousehold.ts — retire at 62, benchmarks $36,000 family / $25,000 couple / $17,500 single): with household $40,000, single $22,000, and Medicare $3,600 per person entered, the priced gross is $0 in 2029 (still working), $40,000 in 2030 (both on the marketplace, household of 4), $25,600 in 2033 (household stepped down to 2, so the couple benchmark stands in for the unentered couple shape — $22,000 single does not apply while both are on), $7,200 in 2035 (both on Medicare, 2 × $3,600), and $7,200 in the final year 2063; the net is $15,731.54 in 2030 (gross less that year's priced credit), the full $40,000 in 2032 (MAGI over the cliff, no credit), $20,550.31 in 2033, and $7,200 in 2035; lifetime gross $380,000 = 3 × $40,000 + 2 × $25,600 + 29 × $7,200, lifetime net $321,697.83, and gross − net − credit kept = $0 exactly. At preserve $250,000 / 10% the score's healthPremium is $380,000, its net $321,697.83, and net cost $2,010,544.45 (the inactive control prices $1,633,475.05 with a $0 lifetime gross); the 2030 funding row carries health 1,573,154c, spending 18,000,000c, total need 19,573,154c, identity gap 0, and 2033 carries health 2,055,031c. TERMINAL TIER FIXTURE (the rule the re-price resolved, pinned directly on the score function with a stub plan result): terminal = the preserve rate × min(ending pre-tax, the preserve) + the heir rate × max(0, ending pre-tax − the preserve) — at an $800,000 ending balance, a $500,000 preserve at 10%, and a 22% heir rate: preserved $500,000, excess $300,000, terminal on the preserved part $50,000, on the excess $66,000, terminal $116,000, net cost $116,000; below the floor (ending $300,000) the terminal is $30,000 with a $0 excess. PLAYGROUND FIXTURE (2026, MFJ ages 60/58, other ordinary income $60,000, household of 2, benchmark $25,000): marketplace premium $30,000 entered — gross $30,000, net $10,678.47 (priced credit $19,321.53), cash left after health premiums $46,481.53, federal tax and net tax bill both $2,840 (the premium moves no tax figure); mixed year (one on Medicare, $3,600 per person also entered) — gross $33,600, net $14,278.47; both on Medicare — gross = net $7,200; not entered — $0 / $0 and cash left after health premiums equals cash left after tax; the paste payload carries both inputs and a pre-build paste loads with both null. FALLBACK SHAPES (derived by running the engine on the sample household): Medicare-only entered — 2030 gross is the family benchmark $36,000, 2033 is the single benchmark $17,500 + $3,600 = $21,100, 2035 is $7,200; single-only entered — 2030 gross is the family benchmark $36,000, 2033 is the entered $22,000, 2035 is $0. NEW FIXTURES: health-premium-schedule-score-and-funding, health-premium-terminal-tier-rule, health-premium-playground-readouts (tax census 531 → 534), and api-health-premium-semantics-content (extended 160 → 161) pinning the published HEALTH_PREMIUM_SEMANTICS text; the amended SCORE_IDENTITIES text (the net-cost identity now names the lifetime gross premium) passes its existing content fixture. VERIFICATION: typecheck clean (server + client); suites green — tax census 534/534 in six chunks with teeth ok (chunks re-run solo after the combined run was OOM-killed under memory contention, the standing transient pattern on this machine), extended 161/161, retirement 63/63, December 86/86 (the December reference case reproduces through its suite — its inputs are scrubbed from the repo, so it is not re-run live, and no December or working-year pricing changed), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data-integrity 0 violations, packaged harness 349/349; describeApi on the staged build reports contract 147 with the health premium semantics published and no action missing a purpose. Live drives on the sandbox (compute-only, nothing saved — the record re-read afterwards still shows the three fields null): runRothCompare on the record as saved priced the no-premium baseline with healthPremiumCents and healthPremiumNetCents both 0 and its score identity footing to the cent; the flat-bump comparison scenario (the step-(a) method: the same net premium added to every year's spending) likewise carried a $0 premium term, confirming the term and the bump are distinct mechanisms; the year-specific scenario (illustrative inputs: marketplace household $36,000, single $20,000, Medicare $2,902.68 per person — the Part B + Part D sum) priced a lifetime gross whose excess over the net equals the lifetime credit kept to the cent, a score identity footing to the cent, $0 premium in the working years, a net marketplace premium in the both-on years equal to gross − that year's credit to the cent, spouse-only years carrying the single gross plus one Medicare per-person amount, and both-on-Medicare years carrying exactly two per-person amounts — the schedule's Medicare years price BELOW the flat method's every-year charge, the divergence in the direction the schedule implies, while in the both-on-marketplace years the schedule funds the entered premium net of the year's credit, the same mechanism the flat method approximates with its fixed net figure. runPlaygroundYear on the staged build reproduced the Playground fixture's marketplace year exactly (gross, net, cash left after health premiums, and the unmoved tax figures). Three consecutive clean internal review passes over the changed hunks (pass 1 found and fixed one code/text mismatch — the marketplace fallback now stands in the year's benchmark for an unentered applicable tier, never the other entered tier, matching the published contract text; passes 2 and 3 clean, covering the settlement iteration, the funding split, the score identity, the response plumbing, the paste round-trip, and the client wiring). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of the changed files, this entry, and the resulting diff for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figures this entry carries are the fictional sample household's, the fixture shapes', the illustrative drive inputs, and the terminal rule's parameters. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build v207 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 4 R4-S7 — the December console gains the unmount flush and save retry it lacked: a queued save now survives leaving the console, deferred behind any in-flight save, and a failed save re-arms a 3-second retry of the same payload (API contract unchanged, 146)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only save-path fix (client/src/December.tsx — the console's autosave/unmount machinery only) — no pricing, no engine behaviour, no December case, no settlement or display behaviour, no API contract, and no stored figure changed. THE FINDING (re-audit round 4, R4-S7, graded SHOULD to match the program's grading of the identical Playground defect as SHOULD-6): the console renders inside the Tax Plan view only while open, so pressing "← Tax Plan" unmounts it; its autosave was a bare 700 ms debounce whose effect cleanup only cleared the timer, with no unmount flush anywhere in the file, and its per-call onError only set the "Could not save" note — dirty stayed set but the effect re-ran only on a form change, so a failed save never retried on its own. Worked example: edit a console entry (e.g. the taxable cash funded for the year) and press "← Tax Plan" within 700 ms — the timer died with the component, nothing was sent, and reopening rehydrated the old stored value; and a save that failed while the console was open was lost the same way on leaving. THE FIX, mirroring the MUST-3/4/5 and SHOULD-6 pattern the other writers carry: (1) the autosave effect now stores every payload it builds in pendingDecSaveRef before arming the debounce on the shared decSaveTimerRef, and fires through sendDecSave, whose per-call handlers own the queue — success drops the payload (identity-checked, so a newer queued payload is never dropped by an older save's landing) and says "Saved" guarded on res.ok exactly as before (build v63's note rule untouched); error sets the same "Could not save — your entries stay on this screen." note and re-arms a 3 s retry of the SAME payload on the shared timer, chained per failure, superseded by any newer edit exactly as in the other writers. (2) A new unmount-flush effect sends whatever is still queued as the console goes away, through sendDecFlushWithRetry — the ONE retrying flush send, whose per-call onError re-arms a 3 s retry of the same payload on decFlushRetryTimerRef, a timer no cleanup clears, so flush retries outlive the view; each attempt reads its CAS base live from revisionRef, so a retry rides the base the previous save adopted. (3) A payload queued behind a save still in flight at unmount is DEFERRED behind it (the S-3 pattern, deferredDecFlushRef) instead of fired concurrently under the same not-yet-advanced base: the in-flight call's per-call handlers fire it on a landed save or on an error (base unchanged; the queued payload supersedes the failed one) and drop it on a conflict; the slot carries the v196 give-up timer (DEFERRED_FLUSH_GIVE_UP_MS 30000, the other views' bound) so a hung in-flight save cannot strand it. (4) A conflict follows the deliberate-drop path with NO retry, exactly like the other flushes: the mutation-level conflict handler (unchanged in behaviour — it still reloads the stored state into the form and shows the same note) now also drops the queued payload and any deferred flush and disarms the give-up timer, since all are the same stale form's snapshots. In-flight tracking is identity-guarded on settle, so an older overlapping send cannot clear a newer send's marker. NOT CHANGED: a successful save's behaviour end to end (same mutation, same revision adoption, same provenance update, same query invalidation, same notes); the conflict reload itself; the reset flow (it queues through the same autosave effect, so a reset now also flushes on unmount — it is a user edit like any other); hydration and the first-open preseed (the preseed now also flushes if the console is closed inside the debounce — the preseed was always meant to be saved); every priced figure, the settlement, and all display rendering. VERIFICATION: typecheck clean (server + client) and the staged build clean; suites green — December 86/86, extended 160/160, retirement 63/63, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 20/20, data-integrity 0 violations, tax census 531/531 run in slices from the source runner (the single-call action run times out at the worker limit — standing limitation S-2), packaged harness green (its six taxtest chunks 89/89/89/89/89/86 = the same 531 with teeth ok, plus the main harness 349/349; two chunks OOM-killed under memory contention with the audit browser resident were re-run solo against the same bundle and passed, exit 0 being a full pass by taxtest's own contract); action-level drive on the sandbox — a save of the stored state with one field edited landed at the next revision and re-read persisted, a stale-base save of a different value was refused as a conflict carrying the landed state and wrote nothing, and the sandbox blob was then restored to its prior contents through the same action (the live record was never written); three consecutive clean internal review passes over the changed hunks (queue identity checks, deferred-slot consumption on success/error/conflict, timer ownership — the flush retry timer is cleared by nothing, the shared save timer's supersede semantics match the other writers). The December reference case is untouched by construction (no pricing or decemberCore code changed; its reproduction rides the December suite above — the reference inputs are scrubbed from the repo, so as in prior rounds it is not re-run live). The rendered unmount race (edit, press "← Tax Plan" inside the debounce, reopen, confirm persisted) could NOT be driven in this build's audit probe: the harness cannot scroll the console back up (its wheel moves down-page only, its key events do not move focus), and its page timers do not advance outside ~100 ms settles, so no queued edit could be carried to the back button; what the probe did establish is that action POSTs from the page land (a fold toggle persisted through setUiFoldState) and that the console renders and hydrates exactly as before. The flush/retry behaviour therefore rests on the code's identity with the sibling implementations that were live-verified in builds v149–v196, the review passes, and the suites above. ## Build v204 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 4 R4-S1 — the December projected tax bill's ACA credit row now states the credit still due, so its rows foot to the settlement whenever advance credit was taken (API contract unchanged, 146)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only display fix (client/src/December.tsx — the "Projected tax bill" card's ACA credit row and its deriving comment only) — no priced figure, no settlement, no engine behaviour, no December case, no API contract, and no stored figure changed. THE FINDING (re-audit round 4, R4-S1; the scope note build v192 recorded and left open): the bill's credit row stated the full final allowable credit (creditAtHeadline), while the settlement in server/src/decemberCore.ts nets only the credit still due — settlement = total tax − creditStillDue + excessAptcRepayment − refundable education credit, where creditStillDue = max(0, effective final credit − APTC taken) and the excess repayment is max(0, APTC taken − effective final credit) in 2026 and later. Whenever APTC taken was above $0 the listed rows therefore missed the settlement by exactly final credit − credit still due = min(APTC taken, effective final credit). On the fictional dec-tax-bill-headline-case household (spouse 75 on Medicare, RMD $8,692.58, posted $75,000, benchmark $20,000, APTC taken $12,000, headline draw $0): total tax $4,765.11, final credit $11,664.22, credit still due $0, repayment $335.78, settlement $5,100.89 — the old rows read $4,765.11 − $11,664.22 + $335.78 = −$6,563.33, implying a refund where $5,100.89 is owed (a sign flip), off by $11,664.22. The partial-APTC control (the 2025 fixture shape (ii) of dec-tax-bill-2025-reconciliation: tax $7,743, final credit $11,500, APTC taken $5,000, still due $6,500, repayment $0, settlement $1,243) read −$3,757 under the old row, off by the $5,000 taken; the no-APTC control (dec-tax-bill-no-aptc: still due = the full $11,664.22 credit, settlement −$6,899.11) footed exactly, proving APTC taken is the sole mover. THE FIX: the credit row now carries creditStillDue — the settlement's own term — sourced as `likelyCase.creditStillDue ?? likelyCase.creditAtHeadline` (the fallback is defensive only: creditStillDue is a number whenever the final credit is priced, and null only when the credit is unpriced, in which case the row is not shown, exactly as before), and its label reads "ACA premium credit still due" whenever advance credit was taken, keeping "ACA premium credit" when none was. The rows now foot in every regime: no APTC (still due = final credit; the row is byte-identical to before, so the December reference case — no APTC taken — reproduces exactly), partial APTC (total tax − still due − refundable education credit = settlement), and full/excess APTC (still due $0 shown, and the existing "Advance credit to repay" row adds the excess back: total tax − $0 + repayment − refundable education credit = settlement). The known-zero-credit shape (creditAtHeadline null, credit still due $0) still shows no credit row and foots through the repayment row alone; an unpriced credit still shows no settlement figure at all. NOT CHANGED: the final allowable credit itself, which stays stated on the per-case summary cards below the bill ("Final credit"); the settlement and every priced value; any other row's value, label, sign, or render condition; any pricing, engine behaviour, the December case, or any stored figure. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): re-derivation from the code — creditStillDue and excessAptcRepayment are complementary halves of the same reconciliation (for 2026+: −creditStillDue + excess = −final credit + APTC taken), so substituting still due for final credit in the row makes the listed rows sum to the settlement identically in all three regimes, and with APTC taken $0 the substitution is value- and label-identical; three consecutive clean internal review passes over the hunk (regime-by-regime footing traced, including the state-tax-shown subtotal reading and the pre-2026 shapes whose settlement is shown only when APTC is at or below the final credit); scrub of the changed files and this entry for the household's real figures returned zero matches — this entry carries only the fictional fixture figures above. Staged for the Verify stage per the program's standing pattern (builds v185–v203): the sandbox action-level drive confirming the bill's rows foot on the full-APTC, partial-APTC, and no-APTC fixture shapes, the December reference-case exact reproduction, and the full suites.

## Build v203 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 NICE-3 — the December harvest note's trailing clause is now derived from the two figures the note itself states, so equal figures are stated as equal instead of being described as the draw taking room (API contract unchanged, 146)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only wording fix (client/src/December.tsx — the Gain harvest section's likely-case harvest note and its new deriving comment only) — no priced figure, no settlement, no engine behaviour, no December case, and no stored figure changed. THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, NICE-3): the harvest note stated the likely case's harvested gain before any December draw and at the headline draw, then always closed with "— the draw takes room the harvest would otherwise use" — a claim of a difference the note's own figures do not support whenever the two figures are equal. RE-DERIVATION from the code: each case carries harvestedGainAtZeroDraw and harvestedGainAtHeadline (decemberCore.ts, read straight off pricePlaygroundYear's harvestedGain at a $0 draw and at the headline draw), and the harvest is the largest gain inside the 0% band capped by the remaining pool's unrealized gain — so the headline figure is SMALLER only when the headline draw's ordinary income actually shrinks the 0% room the harvest fits in, and it is EQUAL whenever the pool's unrealized gain caps the harvest at both draws (or the headline draw is $0, or there is no cliff and the headline pricing IS the $0-draw pricing). The equal case is not exotic: on the fictional December fixture household (2026 MFJ, ages 60/58, $65,000 of ordinary income, a $40,000 taxable pool at 75% basis — $10,000 of unrealized gain — $10,000 of advance credit taken), computeDecemberProjection solves a $4,600 headline draw and the likely case harvests $10,000 at a $0 draw and $10,000 at the headline draw (the dec-harvest-f3-acceptance fixture pins both figures at $10,000): the old note showed "$10,000 … $10,000 — the draw takes room the harvest would otherwise use", contradicting itself, because the $10,000 pool cap binds at both draws and the $66,100 of 0% room is never the binding cap. The differing case is real too, and rarer than it looks: the headline draw is cliff-sized, and a cliff target sits far below the 0% band's top for a small household, so the draw cannot reach the harvest's room — the figures differ only when the cliff sits above the band's top, as with a household of 5 on the same fixture shape (a $500,000 pool at 0% basis over the same $65,000 of ordinary income): the harvest is $66,100 at a $0 draw (the full 0% room) and $0 at the $80,600 headline draw the larger cliff solves, because that draw's ordinary income consumes the whole band — there the original clause is exactly right. THE FIX — wording only: the note's trailing clause is now selected by comparing the two figures it states. A smaller headline figure keeps the original clause byte-identically ("the draw takes room the harvest would otherwise use."); equal figures now read "the same amount as before any draw, so the headline draw takes no room from the harvest."; and a larger headline figure (not reachable under the current sizing, where the draw can only shrink or leave the 0% room, but stated so the clause can never contradict the figures in any case) reads "more than before any draw, so the headline draw leaves the harvest more room than a $0 draw does." A comment at the render records the derivation. NOT CHANGED: both figures and their whole-dollar statement, the note's render condition (the likely case's $0-draw harvest above $0), every other December wording, any pricing, the settlement, the December case, and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): direct engine probes on the final tree reproduce both shapes — the fixture household above prices headline draw $4,600 with harvested gains $10,000 / $10,000 (equal, so the note now closes with the same-amount clause), and the household-of-5 room-bound shape prices harvested gains $66,100 at a $0 draw and $0 at its $80,600 headline draw (differing, so the note keeps the original takes-room clause); the clause selection is a pure comparison of the same two fields the note renders, traced for all three branches. Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's changed files and of this entry for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figures this build carries are the fictional fixture household's $65,000 / $40,000 / $10,000 / $4,600 and the differing shape's $500,000 / $66,100 / $80,600. Three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1: the two fields re-derived from decemberCaseInputs / pricePlaygroundYear and the equal-vs-smaller conditions traced through the pool cap, the 0% room, and the cliff solver, including why a small household's cliff-sized draw cannot shrink a pool-capped harvest; pass 2: every clause branch checked against its figures — smaller keeps the original wording, equal states sameness and no room taken, larger states more room — and the note's grammar read whole in each branch; pass 3: scope — the diff is confined to the one note's trailing clause plus its comment in December.tsx and this entry; no formatter, no figure, no server file, no other wording touched). VERIFICATION (staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern in builds v185–v202): the rendered drive (open the December screen on a case whose two harvest figures are equal and confirm the trailing clause states sameness with no takes-room claim, and on a case whose figures differ confirm the original clause still shows), the December reference-case reproduction, and the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness). Typecheck is exercised by the exit build itself. Nothing committed or pushed. The re-audit is not dispatched until NICE-3 is resolved.

## Build v202 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 NICE-2 — the Retirement success explainer no longer overstates the never-runs-out rule at an exact-$0 landing: landing at exactly $0 is stated as what the code counts it — succeeding, with the portfolio empty — and the failure case is stated as a year whose spending exceeds the money on hand (API contract unchanged, 146)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only wording fix (client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx — the intro Explainer's summary line and its body paragraph only) — no success determination, no priced figure, no engine behaviour, no December case, and no stored figure changed. THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, NICE-2): the Retirement success explainer stated the never-runs-out rule too strongly — "a plan succeeds if the money never runs out" and "a run that sits at $0 and is later refilled by income still counts as not succeeding, because the money did run out" — which is false at the exact-$0 boundary: a portfolio that lands at exactly $0 HAS run out of money, yet the code can count that run as succeeding. RE-DERIVATION from the code: the headline success rule is runNeverRunsOut (server/src/retirementEngines.ts), which fails a run only when a retired year's net withdrawal EXCEEDS the balance on hand when it comes due (net > bal, strictly); a year whose net withdrawal exactly equals the balance is fully funded, the balance becomes $0, and the run continues to count toward neverOutSuccessRate — including when that exact-$0 year is the final year (an exact-$0 landing at the end age counts as succeeding, with nothing left over) and including when a later year's surplus income refills the portfolio from $0. Conversely, the explainer's refill sentence is true only for the shortfall case: a year whose spending exceeds the balance on hand leaves that year's spending not fully funded (simulateDetailed floors the balance at $0), and the run fails on the spot even if later income refills it. THE FIX — wording only, both faces of the one explainer: the summary now reads "a plan succeeds if every year's spending is fully funded through the end age, even a landing at exactly $0"; the body now states the rule as "the money never comes up short in any year", states the exact-$0 case explicitly ("A run that lands at exactly $0 still counts as succeeding when that year's spending was fully funded by the money on hand: the portfolio is empty, but no year's spending went unfunded"), and states the failure case as its code condition ("a year's spending exceeds the money on hand to fund it — even if the portfolio then sits at $0 and later income refills it, that year's spending was not fully funded, so the money did run out in the sense that matters here"). NOT CHANGED: runNeverRunsOut and every success determination (Historical / Monte Carlo neverOutSuccessRate, the solver's scoring, the Projection tab's own at-risk rule — ending ≤ $0 — which is a separate surface with its own settled wording, untouched), any priced figure, the December case, and every stored figure; the internal code comment near the at-risk derivation that paraphrases the rule for maintainers is not user-facing explainer copy and is untouched. No worked example on the sample household is needed: the boundary is arithmetic, not household-specific — a one-year plan whose single retired year's net withdrawal exactly equals its starting portfolio lands at exactly $0 and runNeverRunsOut returns true, while the same plan with spending one cent higher fails. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): the rule re-derived line by line from runNeverRunsOut's funding test and simulateDetailed's $0 floor, and the new wording checked sentence by sentence against both branches of that test (exact equality → succeeding, portfolio empty; strict excess → not succeeding, refill notwithstanding). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's changed files and of this entry for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figure this build carries is $0. Three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1: the success rule re-derived from the engine — the strict-greater funding test, the $0 floor, and the refill mechanics; pass 2: every sentence of the new explainer traced against that rule, including the mid-plan exact-$0-then-refill case the old wording misdescribed; pass 3: scope — the diff is confined to the two explainer strings in RetirementCalc.tsx plus this entry; no engine file, no success computation, no other explainer or pill wording touched). VERIFICATION (staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern in builds v185–v201): the action-level / rendered drive (construct a Retirement scenario that lands at exactly $0 and confirm the explainer on screen accurately describes that landing — succeeding with the portfolio empty, no never-runs-out overstatement — and confirm a scenario that stays above $0 still shows the same corrected explainer), the December reference-case reproduction, and the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness). Typecheck is exercised by the exit build itself. Nothing committed or pushed. NICE-3 is not dispatched until NICE-2 is resolved.

## Build v201 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 NICE-1 — negative tax-return actuals are rejected at parse, reported on the planner response, and never surface as negative prefill dollars (API contract 145 → 146)

All user-entered data, no external source. Server fix (server/src/taxReturnCore.ts — the ONE parse, a new rejection reporter, and the prefill mapping; server/src/actions.ts — the taxReturn response block, readRothBlob, loadRothPlannerResponse, the getRothPlanner purpose text, and the contract version; server/src/apiContractCore.ts — the TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS text and its header comment; server/src/taxFixtures.ts — one new fixture; server/src/extendedFixtures.ts — the semantics-content fixture's phrases 25 → 27 and its note) plus one client render (client/src/Playground.tsx — a visible note beside the prefill controls when a rejection is reported). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, NICE-1): the tax-return actuals parse accepted negative values, so a negative actual passed through and surfaced as a negative prefill dollar amount in the Playground dials — a negative income figure where none can exist. RE-DERIVATION from the code: parseRothTaxReturn's amount reader accepted any finite number, and taxReturnPrefillDollars divided whatever it was handed by 100, so on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts) a stored line 2b of −150000c — the sample $1,500 interest figure sign-flipped, e.g. by a mistyped or sign-flipped entry — prefilled the Interest dial at −$1,500. The two derived percentages were already safe (impliedYieldPctsFromTaxReturn and qualifiedDividendSharePctFromTaxReturn each guard a negative line to null), so pricing never read the negative; only the parse and the prefill mapping passed it through. THE FIX — rejection at the ONE parse, reported, with the fallback the provenance rules already define: (1) parseRothTaxReturn's amount reader now requires a finite NON-NEGATIVE number — a negative stored amount reads as not entered (null), exactly like a line never typed, while $0 still parses as an entered $0; every reader of the stored shape (getRothPlanner, resolveArgsBalances, readStoredTaxReturn, the client's plan-input constructions via the response) goes through this parse, so the rejection holds on every path at once. (2) A new reporter in the same module, rejectedNegativeTaxReturnActuals, reads the same raw shape with the same finiteness test and returns one entry per rejected line (interest / qualifiedDividends / ordinaryDividends) with its stored negative cents, so the parse and the report can never disagree; readRothBlob computes it from the raw inputs it already holds, and getRothPlanner's taxReturn block carries it as rejectedNegativeActuals beside the parsed amounts (where a rejected line reads null) — the rejection is surfaced, never silently dropped. (3) taxReturnPrefillDollars states the guarantee itself: a negative cents value maps to null at the mapping too, so no shape it is handed can produce a negative prefill dollar. (4) The Playground renders the report: when rejectedNegativeActuals is non-empty, a warn note beside the "Start from my numbers" controls names each rejected line in plain terms (taxable interest (line 2b) / qualified dividends (line 3a) / ordinary dividends (line 3b)) with its stored value, and says the line counts as not entered — its dial uses the plan's estimate where the plan prices the year — with the other return figures used as stored. THE FALLBACK, per the existing provenance rules (resolvePgIncomeForYear, unchanged): a rejected line resolves exactly as an unentered line — the return year takes the return's figure, which is now blank for that line; a year the saved plan prices takes the plan's priced estimate; an unpriced non-return year carries the return figures forward, blank for that line — never a negative dollar, and the derived percentages treat the line as unentered, as they already did. NOT CHANGED: any pricing or engine behaviour (the derivations' negative guards were already null-yielding, so no priced figure moves), the December case, any stored figure, and the saveRothInputs writer — deliberately: the writer still stores what it is given, because the defect class is a value already in (or crafted into) the stored record, and the ONE lenient parse every reader shares is the gate the codebase's stored-shape convention prescribes (the same convention that nulls an out-of-range return year); refusing at the writer would also make the stored-negative state unreachable through the app's own actions, leaving the parse path unverifiable end to end. A normal positive actual prefills exactly as before (pinned by the new fixture's positive control and the untouched tax-return-prefill-mapping fixture). NEW FIXTURE tax-return-negative-actuals-rejected-nice1 pins the mechanism on the sample household's return (38 fields): the mixed sign-flip (only the flipped line nulls, at parse and at prefill; the report names it with its stored cents; the other lines' prefill, implied yields, and share are untouched), the all-negative shape (three nulls, three reports, no yields, no share), the negative-ordinary shape (the total reads unentered — dividend yield and share null, interest side untouched), the positive control (parses and prefills exactly, empty report), the $0 control ($0 is entered, never rejected, implies 0% yields), and the mapping guard (a negative shape handed to the mapping directly still maps to null). The tax census is now 531 (530 + the new fixture). VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): typecheck clean (server + client); the new fixture passes on the final tree (38/38 fields) and the semantics-content fixture passes at 27 phrases; TEETH — with the pre-fix amount reader and mapping temporarily restored, the new fixture fails on exactly 7 fields (the flipped line's parsed and prefilled values in the mixed, all-negative, and negative-ordinary shapes, plus the mapping guard) and passes with the fix; the neighbouring tax-return fixtures (prefill mapping, saved-shape round-trip, pricing identity) pass unchanged. Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's changed files and of this entry for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figures this entry carries are the fictional sample household's $1,500 / $15,000 / $20,000 and their cents forms. Three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1: the parse, reporter, and mapping re-derived line by line against the pre-fix behaviour — the rejection set the reporter returns is exactly the set the parse nulls, by shared finiteness test on the same raw shape; pass 2: every consumer of the stored shape traced — getRothPlanner, resolveArgsBalances' threading, readStoredTaxReturn, the client plan-input constructions and prefill source — all read through the one parse or the response it feeds, and the write-through payloads' spread of the taxReturn block already carries response-only fields (the derived percentages) that the writer strips, so the new report field rides the same safe path; pass 3: scope — no engine file, no pricing, no stored figure, no writer schema touched; the diff is the parse, the reporter, the mapping guard, the response plumbing, the contract prose/version, two fixtures, the one client note, and this entry). VERIFICATION (staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern in builds v185–v200): the action-level drive (on the sandbox copy, save a record whose line 2b is the sign-flipped negative via saveRothInputs, then confirm getRothPlanner reports the line as null with rejectedNegativeActuals naming it and its stored cents, and that the Playground prefill resolution for the affected line falls back per the provenance rules — priced-year estimate, blank at the return year — never a negative dollar; confirm a normal positive actual still prefills exactly as before), the December reference-case reproduction, and the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness). ## Build v200 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-11 — the Plan total's label now names BOTH buckets it excludes (College / 529 AND Non-Taxable), so the label explains the full difference from the Net Worth snapshot total (API contract unchanged, 145)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only labeling fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx — the planTotalHeader suffix and the plan-face Plan total button's suffix + aria-label; client/src/Playground.tsx — the same Plan total figure's mirrored suffix ×2, its aria-label, and its header comment) — no priced value, no total, no engine, no action signature, and no stored value changed by the build itself. THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-11): the Tax Plan screen carries two totals — the latest Net Worth snapshot's total (snap.totalCents, every bucket) and the Plan total (planTotalCents) — and the Plan total's only exclusion label read "(excl. 529)", which explains only part of the difference between them. ## Build v199 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-10 — a tax year earlier than the law table now prices under the OLDEST published law row (the earliest law the table holds), never under a later year's law (API contract 144 → 145)

All user-entered data, no external source. Server fix (server/src/taxLaw.ts — the lawForYear lookup, a derived EARLIEST_LAW pointer, and the table's convention comment; server/src/apiContractCore.ts — the law-table provenance convention; server/src/actions.ts — the contract version and the runPlaygroundYear fallback wording; server/src/taxFixtures.ts — one new fixture, one guard note rescoped, the import line) — no action signature, no schema, no stored value changed by the build itself; the December case untouched (its year prices under its own 2026 row). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-10): lawForYear resolved EVERY year with no published row to CURRENT_LAW, the newest row — the carry-forward rule meant for years past the table also swallowed years BEFORE it, so a 2023 or 2024 year was silently taxed with 2026 brackets, standard deduction, and thresholds (the table's oldest row is 2025).
