## Build v198 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-9 — "Reset balances to Net Worth" now goes through the Tax Plan save serialization (the pending-save queue and firePendingSave), so a concurrent autosave cannot make the reset lose under a misleading "Saved" (API contract unchanged, 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the Tax Plan view's resetBalancesToNetWorth) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, the December case untouched, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (144). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-9): "Reset balances to Net Worth" sent its write OUTSIDE the save serialization the autosave uses. The handler cleared the save timer and the pending-save queue, built the cleared payload (the current inputs payload with only the five balance fields nulled), and fired it through a bare saveMutateRef.current call — it neither set nor honoured saveInFlightRef and it carried no per-call handlers, so while an autosave was in flight (or queued) the two writes raced on the same live CAS base (planRevisionRef adopts a landed save's revision only when it lands): one of them was refused or re-fired over the other, the reset could lose to the autosave's older payload, and the save-status note still read "Saved" — the winning autosave's own success — a misleading "done" over a lost reset; a reset whose own request failed likewise had no queue and no retry to fall back on. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): stored spending $180,000/yr with saved balance overrides in place; the user edits spending to $170,000 (that autosave goes in flight), then confirms "Reset balances to Net Worth" — before this build the reset's bare write raced the in-flight $170,000 autosave on the same base, and whichever way the race resolved, one write was refused or overwritten while the note reported the survivor's "Saved" as though both had landed. THE FIX — route the reset through the one serialized path, exactly as the brief prescribes (same queue, same in-flight guard, same conflict / retry handling): the handler's form updates are unchanged (the fields show the snapshot values, the overrides clear), the payload construction is byte-identical (buildInputsPayload from the form as it stands, the five balance fields nulled), and that payload now becomes THE pending save (pendingSave.current = resetPayload, the save timer cleared) and is fired through firePendingSave, with the save-status note set to "Saving…" as the autosave effect sets it. Consequences, by interleaving: (a) nothing in flight — the reset fires at once under the in-flight flag, exactly as immediately as before; (b) an autosave in flight — firePendingSave's hold polls until that save settles, the reset's mutation then reads the base the in-flight save adopted when it landed, and the reset lands after it, in order, as the last word (the in-flight save's per-call handlers cannot drop it: their identity check sees the queue holds the reset payload, not theirs); (c) an autosave merely queued — the reset payload supersedes it, safely, because it is built from the form as it stands and therefore already carries every queued edit's values for the non-balance fields (only the balances change, to null); (d) the reset's own request fails — firePendingSave's per-call onError keeps it queued and re-arms the 3 s retry while the mutation-level onError shows "Could not save — your entries stay on this screen." — surfaced, never a false "Saved"; (e) a CAS conflict — resolves through the mutation's deliberate conflict path (queue dropped, form replaced with the stored record, plain conflict message), exactly like an autosave's; (f) an edit typed while the reset is in flight — it queues behind the reset under the now-honoured in-flight flag and lands after it with the adopted base, instead of racing it as a second bare-base write; (g) leaving the view with the reset still queued behind an in-flight save — the unmount cleanup now sees it in the queue and defers its flush through sendFlushWithRetry with the SHOULD-7 give-up timer, instead of the write having already escaped bare. The autosave effect's own re-fire on the reset's state changes queues a payload built from the reset state itself (balances null under the cleared overrides) — value-identical to the reset payload — so whichever of the two the queue holds when it fires, the reset is what lands. NOT CHANGED: the payload's values, the fields' immediate display, the confirm flow (its open still cancels the pending timer via the v149 helper, its Cancel still re-arms), Reset plan (doResetPlan and its MUST-2 hold-aside are untouched), the unmount flush, any other writer or view, any pricing, the December case, and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; grep confirms the only remaining saveMutateRef.current call sites are the ref assignment, firePendingSave's handler-carrying send, and sendFlushWithRetry's retrying send — no bare send remains; source trace across three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1 traced the in-flight interleavings both ways — autosave in flight then reset: the reset holds, lands after with the adopted base, and is not dropped by the in-flight save's identity-checked handlers whether that save lands or fails; reset in flight then a new edit: the edit queues behind the reset and lands after it; pass 2 traced failure and conflict — a failed reset stays queued with the 3 s retry armed and the failure note showing, a conflict follows the deliberate drop-and-reshow, and the unmount cleanup defers a still-queued reset through the retrying flush with its give-up timer; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only resetBalancesToNetWorth and its comment — the payload construction and form updates are value-identical to before, no server code, no engine, no other view, no stored figure). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's added lines in RothConversion.tsx (and of the whole file's added lines in the working diff) and of this entry for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figures this build carries are the fictional sample household's $180,000 / $170,000 and the 3 s retry constant. VERIFICATION (staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern in builds v185–v197): the action-level drive (queue an autosave edit, then trigger "Reset balances to Net Worth" while the autosave is in flight, and vice versa, and confirm the reset lands — or is visibly reported as failed — with the UI message matching the outcome, no lost reset reported as done; confirm a reset with nothing in flight still lands normally), the December reference-case reproduction, and the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness). Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-10 is not dispatched until SHOULD-9 is resolved.

## Build v197 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-8 — the Tax Plan scenario mutations (save / delete / rename / update) now handle failure: a visible error line, and the user's change stays in view to retry (API contract unchanged, 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the Tax Plan view's four scenario mutations, their one dismiss-up-front click site, and three renders of one new error state) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, the December case untouched, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (144). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-8): the four Tax Plan scenario mutations — saveScenario, deleteScenario, renameScenario, updateScenario — defined NO error handler, so when a write's request itself failed (offline, gateway 500) the user saw nothing: the scenario list kept showing the old state and the change was silently lost. A server REFUSAL was never part of the defect — it resolves through onSuccess with ok false, its reason already surfaced via scenarioMsg, and the rename / update success handlers already kept their editor open on a refusal; only the request-failure path was missing. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): with the sample plan (spending $180,000/yr) open in the Strategy Lab, the user renames a saved strategy, edits another strategy's ceilings in its editor, deletes a third, and saves the current plan as a new scenario — if any of those four requests fails, before this build nothing on screen said so: the rename field and the editor sat open with no word that their change had not landed (their edits then vanished on the next load), the delete's confirmation had already dismissed itself at the click so the delete looked done or undone with no word, and the save simply never appeared. THE FIX — the M-5 pattern (build v151: a plain visible failure note plus the change itself preserved, never dropped): each of the four mutations gains an onError that sets ONE new state, scenarioError, with a per-mutation plain sentence naming what did not happen and what stayed ("Could not save the scenario — nothing was saved, and your plan and saved strategies stay as they were. Try saving again." / "Could not delete <name> — it is still saved. Try again, or cancel the delete." / "Could not rename <name> — it keeps its old name, and the new name stays in the field so you can try again." / "Could not save changes to <name> — your edits stay in the editor so you can try again."). The line is rendered in bad colour with role="alert" beside every scenario action: under the plan form's Save current as scenario button (next to the existing scenarioMsg render), at the top of the optimizer workspace (whose Save winner / Save as scenario buttons call saveScenario), and at the head of the Strategy Lab's Saved strategies list (whose Add / Duplicate / Rename / Delete / editor Save changes buttons call all four). PRESERVATION, per mutation: the onError handlers clear NO in-progress UI — the rename stays open with the typed new name still in renameText, the strategy editor stays open with every ed* field untouched, and a save's source (the plan form, the optimizer result, the duplicated row) stays on screen exactly as it was, so the same action can simply be tried again. The delete needed one click-site change to get the same property: its confirmation button dismissed the confirmation BEFORE firing the mutation (setLabConfirmDelete(null) then mutate), so a failed delete left no confirmation to retry from — the click now only fires the mutation, and the confirmation is dismissed by the mutation's onSuccess once the delete lands (ok true), exactly as the load confirmation already worked; on a refusal (ok false) or a failure the confirmation stays open with Cancel beside it. onMutate clears scenarioError when any scenario attempt starts and onSuccess clears it too, so a stale failure never sits beside a retry in flight or a landed save. The retry is deliberately the user's own repeat click, NOT an automatic re-send, and this entry records why: saveRothScenario APPENDS an auto-named scenario, so automatically re-sending after a response was lost in transit could save a duplicate the user never asked for; the M-5 queue-and-chained-retry shape belongs to the idempotent whole-form autosave (whose payload is a snapshot that supersedes itself), not to these one-shot writes — the brief's at-minimum branch (report the failure, keep the edit in view) is the correct shape here, applied uniformly to all four for one consistent behaviour. NOT CHANGED: every onSuccess behaviour apart from clearing the error line (revision adoption, scenarioMsg reasons, invalidation, editor / rename / confirm closing on ok — all byte-identical), every server action and its refusal reasons, the plan autosave and its M-5 queue, any pricing, the December case, and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; source trace across three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1 confirmed all four mutations now carry onMutate / onError and that no onError or mutation click path clears renamingName, renameText, labEditingName, the ed* fields, or labConfirmDelete — the delete click's up-front dismissal is gone, leaving only the ok-gated onSuccess clears, the user's own Cancel button, and the pre-existing load-request exclusivity clear; pass 2 traced each failure end to end — save: error line at all three renders, plan / optimizer result / source row untouched, no invalidation fires so the list keeps its true stored state; delete: row still listed, confirmation still open for retry or cancel; rename: field open, typed name intact; update: editor open, edits intact — and each success path byte-identical to before apart from clearing an already-empty error; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only the scenario state declaration, the four mutation definitions, the one delete click, and the three error renders in RothConversion.tsx plus this entry — no server code, no engine, no other view, no stored figure, and that scenarioError is written only by the four mutations and read only by the three renders). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of this build's added lines in RothConversion.tsx and of this entry for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — the only figures this build carries are the fictional sample household's $180,000 and generic HTTP wording; the two whole-file first-name hits in RothConversion.tsx are pre-existing comments outside this build's hunks. VERIFICATION (staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern in builds v185–v196): the action-level drive per mutation (make each of save / delete / rename / update fail and confirm the visible error line appears and the change is not silently lost — rename field and editor still open with their edits, delete confirmation still open, save source still on screen — and confirm a successful attempt of each still lands normally and clears the line), the December reference-case reproduction, and the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness). Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-9 is not dispatched until SHOULD-8 is resolved.

## Build v196 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-7 — every deferred-flush slot now carries a give-up timer, so a hung in-flight save cannot strand the deferred edit forever (API contract unchanged, 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx, client/src/Playground.tsx — the deferred-flush slots of the Tax Plan autosave, both Retirement writers, and both Playground writers) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, the December case untouched, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (144). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-7): a flush deferred behind an in-flight save (the S-3 / S-4 pattern, builds v168 / v169) waits in its slot for the in-flight save to settle, consumed only by that save's own per-call settle handlers. If the in-flight save hangs forever — its request neither resolves nor rejects, so no handler ever runs — the deferred edit sits in its slot with no timeout: it never sends and never reports, stranded for the rest of the page's life. This is the one unbounded wait the N-3 hold bound (build v177) did not cover: v177 bounded the MOUNTED fire path's polling, but the unmount cleanup's deferred slot has no polling loop to bound — it has only the wedged save's handlers. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): stored spending $180,000/yr; the user edits spending to $170,000, a first save of the edit goes in flight, the user edits again (or the flush queues behind the in-flight save) and switches views — the unmount cleanup defers the $170,000 flush behind the in-flight save; that save's request hangs, so the deferred flush never fires, and returning shows $180,000 with no explanation. THE SLOTS (five): the Tax Plan autosave's deferredFlushRef (RothConversion.tsx), the Retirement autosave's deferredFlushRef and the Retirement Tax Plan write-through's deferredRothFlushRef (RetirementCalc.tsx), and the Playground Tax Plan write-through's deferredPgRothFlushRef plus the Playground remembered form's deferredPgFormFlushRef (Playground.tsx — the fifth slot was added by build v195, after SHOULD-7 was filed, with the identical defect and only-consumer shape, so it is covered under the same rule rather than left for a re-audit to find). THE FIX — one give-up timer per slot, one shared bound: a new constant DEFERRED_FLUSH_GIVE_UP_MS = 30000 in each of the three files (the same 30 s scale as SAVE_HOLD_MAX_POLLS, 100 × 300 ms — far beyond any save this app makes). The unmount cleanup now ARMS the slot's give-up timer as it stores the deferred send. Each slot is read only two ways, both consuming it: the in-flight save's settle handlers now take it through a take helper (takeDeferredFlush / takeDeferredRothFlush / takeDeferredPgRothFlush / takeDeferredPgFormFlush) that also disarms the timer, and the give-up timer itself, which on expiry consumes the slot and fires the deferred send anyway. So a normally-settling save fires the deferred send exactly as before and leaves no timer behind; a wedged save can hold the slot for at most 30 s past the unmount; and a settle arriving after the give-up finds the slot empty and fires nothing twice (single-threaded take: whichever of the settle and the timer runs first consumes the slot, the other reads null). THE GIVE-UP SEND goes through the RETRYING flush path, exactly as a settle-fired flush does: the Tax Plan slot's send was already sendFlushWithRetry (build v187); the Retirement and Playground write-through slots' sends were already sendRothFlush / sendPgRothFlush with their retrying payload sends (builds v188 / v189); the remembered-form slot's send was already flushPgFormSave (build v195), whose every attempt re-reads fresh, three-way merges, and CAS-writes with savePgCas's own conflict merge-retry. The Retirement autosave's deferred send was the one exception — a bare mutate call carrying only an onSuccess, so even a settle-fired deferred flush whose own request failed was dropped silently; it now goes through ONE new retrying flush send (sendCalcFlush / sendCalcFlushPayload, mirroring sendFlushWithRetry): its per-call onError re-arms a 3 s retry of the same payload, chained per failure on its own timer ref (calcFlushRetryTimerRef) that no cleanup clears, its onSuccess carries the queued onOk exactly as the bare call's did, and its payload build is unchanged (a form snapshot rebuilt at the fire, a command payload exactly as constructed). On every slot, a failure of the give-up send is therefore retried until it lands — never dropped silently (the MUST-3 / MUST-4 / MUST-5 pattern) — and a CAS conflict from sending while the wedged save is still in flight resolves through each mutation's normal conflict path (the deliberate drop / re-show), never a silent overwrite: each flush send reads its CAS base live at the call, the write-through sends additionally run their M-4 fresh-fetch guard, and the remembered-form send merge-retries against the newest stored form. NOT CHANGED: the S-3 / S-4 deferral itself (while an in-flight save settles normally nothing is ever sent concurrently, and the deferred slot is consumed on the settle exactly as before, drop-on-conflict included), the immediate unmount flushes, the N-3 hold bounds, the settled-value gates, the coherence guards, any pricing, and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (build stage, this entry): typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; grep confirms every deferred slot is now read only inside its take helper and its give-up callback, every settle consumption goes through a take helper, and every cleanup store site arms its timer (Tax Plan take ×2 / arm ×1; Retirement autosave take ×2 / arm ×1; Retirement write-through take ×2 / arm ×1; Playground write-through take ×2 / arm ×1; Playground remembered form take ×1 / arm ×1); three consecutive clean internal review passes (pass 1 traced the interleavings per slot — settle-before-bound: byte-identical consumption apart from the timer disarm; hung save: the timer fires the retrying send at 30 s; give-up-then-late-settle: the handlers read an empty slot and fire nothing, and the wedged payload's own retry is correctly not re-armed because the cleanup already moved its queue entry to the slot; pass 2 re-checked the declaration-order and lifetime rules — every helper is a ref-only closure, the one cleanup that reaches a later-declared helper (the Retirement write-through's) invokes it only at unmount, after the render that initialized it, the same pattern the cleanup's pre-existing buildInputsPayloadRef use follows, and no cleanup or effect clears any give-up or flush-retry timer after it is armed; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only the three client writers' deferred slots and the new Retirement retrying send — no server code, no engine, no other view, no stored figure). ## Build v195 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-6 — the Playground remembered form's debounced save now flushes on unmount, and a failed flush retries instead of reverting silently (API contract unchanged, 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/Playground.tsx, the Playground view's remembered-form persistence block) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, the December case untouched, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (144). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-6): the Playground remembered form (the income dials and the rest of the form, persisted through getRothUiState / setRothUiState) saves on a 400 ms debounce, and that save had NO unmount flush — the debounced effect's cleanup only cleared its timer. If the user typed a dial value and switched views before the debounce fired, the timer died with the view, nothing else held the edit, and returning re-hydrated the stored form, so the dial silently reverted to its previous value. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): the stored form holds the sample household's dial values; the user edits an income dial and switches views within the debounce window — the edit never reaches setRothUiState and the dial shows the old stored value on return. Every other save path in the app already flushes on unmount (the Tax Plan autosave since v149, the Retirement and Playground write-throughs since v159 / v169); this remembered-form save was the one remaining path without one. THE FIX: the debounced effect now records the ONE pending save in a ref (pgFormPendingRef) on every form change — the latest snapshot that differs from the last-synced JSON, with its wholesale flag (Reset / paste / prefill) captured as it stood when queued — and clears it when the form returns to the synced value or when a save of it lands. A new unmount cleanup flushes that pending record through ONE retrying flush send (flushPgFormSave): with nothing in flight it sends at once; with a remembered-form save still in flight it defers instead, the S-3 rule the other writers follow — the in-flight save's settle consumes the deferred slot (executePgFormSave consumes deferredPgFormFlushRef when the in-flight count reaches zero), and the settled outcome decides: if that save WAS this pending edit and it landed, the flush is already done and the slot's send is skipped; in every other case (a newer edit queued behind it, or that save failed) the slot fires the flush. The save body itself is unchanged, extracted verbatim into runPgFormSaveAttempt (wholesale saves whole; otherwise a fresh read, the three-way merge when another writer moved the stored form, and the CAS write), and savePgCas now reports whether the form landed (true / false) — its debounced caller ignores the report exactly as before (a later edit re-saves), while the flush acts on it. THE RETRY (the MUST-3 / MUST-4 / MUST-5 rule, builds v187–v189): a failed flush re-arms a 3 s retry of the SAME pending record, chained per failure, on its own timer ref (pgFormFlushRetryTimerRef) that no cleanup clears, so the retries outlive the view and the edit lands once the server is reachable again instead of being dropped silently. Each retry re-runs the full save — fresh read, three-way merge, CAS write with savePgCas's own conflict merge-retry — so a retry never rides a stale base and another writer's intervening save is merged against, never overwritten. A successful flush is unchanged in effect: the pending form lands exactly as the debounced save would have landed it, and a normal debounced save is byte-for-byte the same flow as before (same 400 ms timer, same merge, same CAS write, same apply-back guard). NOT CHANGED: the hydration, the merge rule, the wholesale semantics, the Reset path's direct save, the write-through below (MUST-5, build v189), any other view, and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (staged): the sandbox action-level drive (in Playground, type a dial value, switch views before the debounce fires, and confirm the value lands and is still there on return; make the flush fail and confirm it is retried and lands instead of being lost silently; confirm a normal debounced save still works unchanged), the December reference-case reproduction, the boundary-aware scrub of the changed files and the resulting diff for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms — ZERO matches required; the only figures this entry carries are the fictional sample household's), the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness), and typecheck (server + client) run in the Verify stage against the built sandbox, together with three consecutive clean internal review passes. Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-7 is not dispatched until SHOULD-6 is resolved.

## Build v194 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-5 — a harvest that breaches the ACA cliff is no longer blamed on "income already posted": the December headline prices the harvest-free counterfactual and names the gain harvest when it alone tips the year over the cliff (or alone uses up the room under it) (API contract unchanged, 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. December headline wording only (server/src/decemberCore.ts, computeDecemberProjection's headline derivation, plus one new December fixture) and one clarifying clause in the runDecemberProjection purpose text (server/src/actions.ts) — no action signature, no priced figure, no settlement derivation, and no stored value changed, so the API contract version is unchanged (144). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-5): when a priced gain harvest breaches the ACA cliff, the December console's headline blamed the breach on "income already posted" — but the harvest itself is what breaches the cliff, not income already posted. THE MECHANISM: the headline's zero-draw test (overCliffEvenAtZero, and the nonDrawAcaMagi it quotes) prices the year at a $0 draw WITH the harvest sized inside the pricing — decemberCaseInputs passes the harvest dials on every pricing, the zero-draw pricings included — so the quoted "income already posted" MAGI silently includes the harvested gain. RE-DERIVATION (on the fictional December fixture household — household of 2, cliff $84,600, benchmark $20,000, APTC taken $12,000, buffer $5,000, target $79,600): posted ordinary income $79,000 sits UNDER the cliff, and a $40,000 taxable pool at 75% basis harvests its full $10,000 unrealized gain inside the 0% room ($98,900 − $46,800 of ordinary taxable income = $52,100), lifting MAGI to $89,000 — over the cliff — yet the old headline read "income already posted puts MAGI at $89,000, over the $84,600 cliff", naming as the cause the one figure that did not cause it. THE FIX: the headline derivation now prices the counterfactual — the likely case re-priced at a $0 draw with the harvest toggle off (the same dials decemberCaseInputs builds, the harvest dials absent) — and attributes the breach by comparing the two pricings. The counterfactual is RE-PRICED, never derived by subtracting the gross harvested gain, because an entering capital-loss carryforward absorbs harvested gains first, so the harvest's MAGI lift can be less than its gross gain, or zero. When the harvest alone tips the likely case over the cliff (over with it, not over without it), the headline names the harvest: "the gain harvest puts MAGI at $89,000, over the $84,600 cliff before any draw — without the harvest, MAGI would be $79,000, under the cliff, so the harvest itself is what breaches the cliff, not income already posted, and no draw can fix that year while the harvest stands", closing with the unchanged credit-lost / APTC-repaid sentence. The same misattribution in the sibling no-room headline is fixed the same way: when the harvest does not breach the cliff but alone uses up the room under cliff − buffer (the priced solve finds no draw while the harvest-free solve finds a positive one), the headline names the harvest — on the fixture shape (posted $78,000, a $16,000 pool at 75% basis harvesting $4,000, MAGI $82,000 against the $79,600 target) it reads "the gain harvest leaves no room under the cliff minus your $5,000 buffer — without the harvest, MAGI at a $0 draw would be $78,000, under the $79,600 target, but with the harvest it is $82,000, so the harvest uses up the room, not income already posted", where the harvest-free year draws $1,600. Both harvest wordings fire only when the harvest is priced (toggle on, both pool facts present), harvests a positive gain at a $0 draw, and is the tipping cause; they stay silent when the harvest is off, unpriced, harvests $0, or is not what tips the year — posted income over the cliff (or over the target) on its own keeps the original income wording byte-identically, including when a harvest rides on top of an already-breaching year (posted $100,000 with the same $10,000 harvest: MAGI $110,000 with it, $100,000 without it, over the cliff either way — the income wording stands) and when a carryforward absorbs the harvest whole (posted $88,000 with a $20,000 long-term carry-in: the $10,000 harvest is absorbed, MAGI is $85,000 with or without it — posted less the $3,000 allowance — over the cliff either way, so the income wording stands; subtracting the gross gain would have produced $75,000, under the cliff, and wrongly blamed the harvest, which is exactly why the counterfactual is priced). The buffer-exceeds-cliff and $0-balance headlines keep their existing precedence (the harvest checks exclude both states for the no-room wording, and the breach wording remains a sub-case of the zero-draw-over-cliff branch, ahead of the buffer branch as that branch already was). NOT CHANGED: the settlement itself (its derivation and every figure it feeds — over the cliff the credit is still $0 and the whole APTC taken is still repaid), the headline draw, any case figure (nonDrawAcaMagi still quotes the priced $0-draw MAGI, harvest included — it is a priced readout, and the harvest-free MAGI appears only inside the headline's own counterfactual clause), the cliff solver, any engine pricing, the plan march, either client (the per-case "Over the cliff even with a $0 draw" note is cause-neutral and untouched), and every stored figure. The December reference case is untouched and still reproduces exactly. THE NEW FIXTURE (dec-harvest-cliff-blame-should5) pins all four shapes outright: the breach case (MAGI $89,000, harvested gain $10,000, credit $0, repayment $12,000, the harvest headline's three clauses, and the absence of the income-blame clause), the genuine-income control (MAGI $110,000, the income wording kept), the absorbed-harvest control (gross harvest $10,000, MAGI $85,000, the income wording kept), and the no-room case (MAGI $82,000, draw $0 with the harvest headline, the harvest-free control drawing $1,600). VERIFICATION (local, this Build stage): direct engine probes reproduced the defect pre-fix (posted $79,000 with a $500,000 pool at 0% basis harvesting $52,100: MAGI $131,100 and the income-blame headline, against a harvest-free MAGI of $79,000 under the cliff) and the corrected attribution post-fix across nine probed shapes — the two fixture breach shapes, the genuine-income and absorbed controls, the no-room pair, the plain no-harvest over-cliff year (income wording byte-identical), the normal kept-credit headline (unchanged), the buffer-at-$200,000-plus-breach year (the harvest breach wording, the zero-draw branch's existing precedence), and the unpriced-harvest over-cliff year (income wording, no counterfactual priced). The December suite is 86/86 (85 + the new fixture — every pre-existing December pin unmoved, proving no priced figure or existing headline moved); extended 160/160; retirement 63/63 with the Trinity benchmark within tolerance on both mixes; UI-state 20/20; Roth CAS 15/15; retirement CAS 16/16; typecheck clean (server + client). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of the changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, the December reference figures, and the live spending figure, in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — every figure this build adds is the fictional December fixture household's. Three consecutive clean internal review passes over this build's hunks (pass 1 re-derived the misattribution from the code — the zero-draw pricing carries the harvest dials, so the quoted MAGI includes the harvest — and reproduced the defect and the fix by direct probes on the fixture shapes; pass 2 traced the attribution conditions branch by branch — the breach wording fires exactly when the priced year is over the cliff and the harvest-free re-pricing is not, the no-room wording exactly when the priced solve is $0 and the harvest-free solve is positive with neither the buffer nor the $0-balance state binding, and every other headline state falls through to its pre-existing wording untouched; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only headline strings, the two counterfactual re-pricings that feed them, the one purpose-text clause, and the new fixture — no priced figure, settlement derivation, solver call for any reported figure, client, or stored figure). Staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern: the action-level drives (runDecemberProjection on a harvest-breach state confirming the harvest headline, and on a genuine-income state confirming the income headline), the December reference-case reproduction, the tax census and teeth, the data-integrity suite, and the packaged harness. Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-6 is not dispatched until SHOULD-5 is resolved.

## Build v193 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-4 — the December cash-left and the engine's cash-left for the same year now agree: the console's ACA reconciliation facts ride the shared pricer's own dials, its net tax bill is the filing settlement, and the console's cash left derives from the priced year's own cash-left readout (API contract 143 → 144)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine readout wiring (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts: three new optional PlaygroundYearInputs dials and pricePlaygroundYear's net-tax-bill computation), December assembly wiring (server/src/decemberCore.ts: decemberCaseInputs passes the facts on every pricing, cashLeftAtHeadline derives from the priced year's cashLeftAfterTax, plus one new December fixture), and the API surface for the same facts (server/src/apiContractCore.ts playgroundYearIn / playgroundInputsFromArgs; server/src/actions.ts API_CONTRACT_VERSION 143 → 144, the runPlaygroundYear and runDecemberProjection purpose texts, and the playgroundYearOut net-tax-bill comment, which still carried the superseded v116 wording and now states the two-mode truth). No priced figure moves anywhere: every tax, MAGI, credit, draw, and settlement value is bit-identical, the December settlement's own derivation is untouched, the plan march is untouched, and a year priced without the new dials is bit-identical to before. THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-4): the December console's cash-left figure for a year disagreed with the shared single-year engine's cash-left for the same year, by exactly the year's net ACA reconciliation position. RE-DERIVATION (on the fictional December fixture household — benchmark $20,000, household of 2, $50,000 of other ordinary income, APTC taken $12,000, headline draw $29,600): both surfaces price cash in $79,600, total tax $5,192, and the final credit $12,071.84 identically; the console settles the year at filing — $71.84 of credit still due, APTC taken sitting under the final credit — so its bill is the settlement, $5,120.16, and its cash left $74,479.84; the engine's net tax bill never netted the reconciliation (the v116 / F7 rule: with no APTC fact the credit is treated as fully advanced against the year's premiums, because the spending the cash left is compared against already holds the net premium), so its bill was the $5,192 total tax alone and its cash left $74,408 — two cash-left figures for one year, $71.84 apart, the gap exactly the credit still due. The defect is structural, not arithmetic: the APTC-taken fact existed only in the December layer, which priced a second bill at its assembly (decemberCore's cashLeftAtHeadline, the finding's line), so on any year whose APTC taken differed from its final credit the two surfaces could not agree. THE FIX, in the codebase's established December-facts pattern (the carry-in, gain-harvest, and education dials' shape — the facts ride the pricer's own dials so the shared pricer prices them for every caller): PlaygroundYearInputs gains optional aptcTaken / acaEnrollmentPremiumAnnual / acaCoverageReduction, absent on every Playground caller; decemberCaseInputs passes the console's three facts (the state's aptcTaken, its acaEnrollmentPremiumAnnual, and the coverage-month reduction from its coverage stray) on every pricing of the year — the zero-draw pricings, the cliff solver's trials, and the headline pricing alike, where they move only the bill / cash-left readouts, never a priced figure. When aptcTaken is present, pricePlaygroundYear derives the year's filing settlement from its own priced readouts with the settlement's exact arithmetic — the final allowable credit (the priced credit capped at the enrollment premium when one is supplied, less the coverage reduction, $0 over the cliff), the reconciliation on the EFFECTIVE final credit (the priced credit; $0 when nobody in the household can be on the marketplace, the known-zero case; unpriced only when someone is marketplace-eligible but no benchmark was entered), the credit still due, and the excess advance credit to repay (in full for 2026 and later, P.L. 119-21 §71305; before 2026 the settlement does not price when APTC taken exceeds the effective final credit, the capped-repayment rules being unmodeled) — and netTaxBill IS that settlement whenever it prices, so cashLeftAfterTax is the cash left after the year's filing settlement. When the facts are present but the settlement cannot price, the bill falls back to the un-reconciled form (the console shows no cash left in those cases, as before). Absent aptcTaken the bill is bit-identical to before — total tax less the refundable education credit — so the F7 census pin (the credit is not double-counted against spending that holds the net premium) and every Playground / Tax Plan figure stand untouched. December's cashLeftAtHeadline now derives as the priced year's own cashLeftAfterTax plus the assembly's taxable cash (build v125), under the same null gate as before: value-identical to the previous cashIn + taxableFunded − settlement derivation on every case (the settlement derivation itself is unchanged and still computed at the assembly for the case's own settlement fields), but now the console's cash left and the engine's are one figure by construction, and any future drift between the two derivations fails the suite instead of reaching the user. The new December fixture (dec-cash-left-agrees-with-engine) pins the agreement to the cent on every case across seven shapes — APTC under the credit, APTC $0, APTC in excess, a $0 enrollment premium, a coverage-month reduction, an over-the-cliff year, and taxable cash entered — plus the headline shape's lines outright on both surfaces (cash in $79,600, settlement / net tax bill $5,120.16, cash left $74,479.84), the sole-mover control (the same pricing without the dials returns the pre-v193 $5,192 bill and $74,408 cash left, lower by exactly the $71.84 still due), and the null contract (no benchmark entered: the settlement does not price, the console shows no cash left, and the engine's bill falls back to the un-reconciled $5,192). The runPlaygroundYear action accepts the same three optional facts, so the agreement is drivable through both public actions on the same year and facts. NOT CHANGED: the December settlement itself (its derivation and every figure it feeds — the reference case reproduces exactly), any priced tax / MAGI / credit / draw figure, the plan march and its score identity, the un-reconciled default and its F7 rationale, either client (the Playground face never supplies the facts, so its tooltip wording — the credit is not subtracted from its net tax bill — stays true of the figure it annotates, exactly the distinction SHOULD-2 settled; the December face's wording is likewise unchanged), the paste payload (it picks its fields by name, so the new dials never ride a paste and a replayed paste prices as a Playground year always has), and every stored figure. VERIFICATION (local, this Build stage): the December suite 85/85 (84 + the new fixture — every pre-existing December pin unmoved, proving the console's figures are value-identical); extended 160/160 with teeth pass; retirement 63/63 with teeth pass; UI-state 20/20; Roth CAS 15/15; retirement CAS 16/16; the tax census in slices on the final tree totalling 529/529 (every range's pass line read back from its result file; two ranges re-run in 44-fixture sub-slices after the coarser runs hit this machine's standing memory transient) and the tax teeth check passing — the opt sweep run directly (pass, all 30 corrupted cases failing as required) and the core mode verified equivalently, its monolithic all-actuals cache being OOM-killed on this machine (the standing S-2 limitation): the full census green plus the one corrupted case (tax-fill-12-no-other-income, its fill pin raised by 100) failing on exactly that field is precisely the core check's pass condition; typecheck clean (server + client). Scrub: boundary-aware grep of all four changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, the December reference figures, and the live spending figure, in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches — every figure this build adds is the fictional December fixture household's or the sample household's. Three consecutive clean internal review passes over this build's hunks (pass 1 re-derived the disagreement from the code and priced both surfaces on the reference year through the live actions: identical cash in, tax, and credit, the two cash-left figures differing by exactly the final credit with APTC taken at $0; pass 2 traced the engine's settlement derivation term by term against the December layer's — final credit, effective credit, still due, excess repayment, and every r2 point — and confirmed the no-dial path is the old formula verbatim; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only the bill / cash-left readouts and the fact pass-throughs — no priced figure, no settlement derivation, no client, no stored figure). Staged for the Verify stage against the built sandbox, per the program's standing pattern: the action-level drives (the December reference case reproduced exactly through runDecemberProjection; runPlaygroundYear on the same year WITH aptcTaken supplied agreeing with it line by line — cash in, net tax bill = settlement, cash left — and without it returning the un-reconciled figure as before), the data-integrity suite, and the packaged harness. Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-5 is not dispatched until SHOULD-4 is resolved.

## Build v191 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-2 — the December "Cash left after tax" tooltip no longer falsely says the ACA premium credit is not priced in: the net tax bill includes the ACA reconciliation, and the tooltip now says so (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client wording only (client/src/December.tsx, the "Cash left after tax" InfoNote in the December console's bill block, and the comment above it) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (143). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-2): the S-6 prescribed tooltip wording — "the ACA premium credit is not priced in this figure" — is FALSE as a description of the figure it annotates; the S-6 fix landed as specified, but the specification itself was wrong. CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING: the figure is cashLeftAtHeadline = cash in (cashInAtHeadline) minus the net tax bill (netSettleAtHeadline), and the settlement is computed in server/src/decemberCore.ts as total tax − credit still due + excess advance credit to repay − the refundable education credit — i.e. the final ACA premium credit IS reconciled into the bill (the credit still due, the final credit less the advance credit already taken, comes off the bill dollar for dollar, and any advance credit taken beyond the final credit is added back as a repayment). The December and contract-text auditors demonstrated the same on the reference case: net cash = draw − federal tax + credit, so the tooltip claimed the opposite of what the figure does. THE FIX: the tooltip's credit clause now states what the figure actually includes, derived from that definition — "the total tax less any refundable education credit, with the ACA premium credit priced in: the net tax bill includes the ACA reconciliation (the credit still due comes off the bill; any advance credit taken beyond the final credit is added back to repay)". No new claim is made about the figure: every clause names a term of the settlement's own computation. The rest of the tooltip (the cash-in and net-bill figures it names, "what's left to spend next year, before any spending", and the refund-timing sentence shown only when the bill is a refund) is unchanged, as is the fixed subtext under the row. ## Build v190 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 SHOULD-1 — the ACA cliff grow-back is no longer gated on premium reconciliation or spend-from-cash: every cliff-capped year grows its conversion back to land on its cliff (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine pricing fix (server/src/taxEngine.ts, the cliff-cap grow-back in simulateRothPlan's per-year settlement) plus one extended fixture and five recorded re-pins (server/src/taxFixtures.ts) — no action signature changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (143). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, SHOULD-1 — the MUST-1 residual): build v185's cliff grow-back ran only in the two settlement shapes that could strand a fill outright — a premium-reconciliation year (the collapse) and a spend-from-cash year — so a PLAIN cliff-capped year, with no reconciliation and no cash spending, still settled wherever the shrink-only convergence left it, materially under its cliff. On the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts; 60% basis, window 62–73, Fill up to the ACA cliff), the reconciliation-off shape converted $28,000.00 across the ACA window ($10,400 / $7,800 / $5,300 / $3,300 / $1,200), its 2030 year landing at ACA MAGI $120,820.11 — $11,180 under the $132,000 household-of-4 cliff — even though conversion room and pre-tax balance remained. THE MECHANISM: the convergence loop and the R7-4 final clamp only ever shrink the conversion, and each re-solve prices the breaching settlement's gains feedback as if fixed, which overstates the gains at the final, smaller conversion; the shrink therefore converges to a landing under the cliff in ANY cliff-capped year whose settlement realizes gains, not only in the two shapes v185 gated on. THE FIX: the grow-back's gate loses its settlement-shape condition — where build v185 required (premiumReconcile || spendCashPct > 0), the block now runs in every cliff-capped year whose settled conversion respects every switched-on ceiling with ACA MAGI still below the year's effective cliff target (the true cliff less any safety buffer), growing the conversion back by the same cent-level bisection (a settlement's ACA MAGI is non-decreasing in the conversion, so the compliant conversions form a prefix) to land the year on its target to the cent, credit intact. Every other guard is untouched: in-window only, never in a bunching $0 year, an era-off year, or a forced-$0 year; bounded by the year's remaining pre-tax balance and preserve room; skipped when another switched-on ceiling is already met to the cent (the R7-5-style cheap bound check); and the block still cannot run at all when ACA is inactive (no cliff dollars) or the strategy carries no cliff cap — a Fill-24% control prices bit-identically, and the December case (a separate single-year solver) is untouched. PRICED EFFECT (sample household, direct engine probes, pre-fix gate restored vs fixed): the reconciliation-off shape's five ACA years now land on the cliff exactly as the reconciliation-on shape does — 2030 conversion $10,400.00 → $21,516.67 with ACA MAGI exactly $132,000 and credit $22,852.80 kept, per-year $21,516.67 / $19,673.93 / $17,994.41 / $16,543.19 / $15,179.57, window and lifetime total $28,000.00 → $90,907.77; at the on-cliff landing the two shapes' settlements coincide (the embedded premium changes the path to the landing, not the landing). The reconciliation-on shape is bit-identical to build v185 (2030 $21,516.67 on the cliff, lifetime $90,907.77), as the brief required. FOUR RECORDED RE-PINS, each a plain cliff-capped shape whose years were pinning the under-cliff shrink landing and now land on their cliffs (each verified as the sole mover by re-running with the pre-fix gate restored — all four return exactly their previous pins): tax-aca-cliff-converges-with-gain-bearing-tax-payment (conversion $103,200 → $103,381.68, ACA MAGI $106,409.60 → exactly the $106,600 cliff, tax $8,024 → $8,045.80, credit $9,401.60 → $9,382.64 — the exact settlement fixed point C + 40% × tax(C) = $106,600, hand-derived in the fixture note); tax-aca-cliff-converges-with-gain-bearing-spending (conversion $83,200 → $84,297.71, ACA MAGI $105,449.60 → exactly $106,600, tax $5,624 → $5,755.73, credit $9,497.22 → $9,382.64 — fixed point C + 40% × ($50,000 + tax(C)) = $106,600, hand-derived in the note); opt-aca-bunching-beats-level-cliff (the level-cliff winner's net $18,086.30 → $18,085.33; the bunching winner and ranking unchanged); tax-aca-premium-reconciliation-pair (LEGACY wealth only, $7,314,375.83 → $7,313,385.89 — the no-embedded-premium run is a plain cliff shape whose post-2028 cliff years now land on their buffered targets; every 2028 figure and the reconciled wealth $7,359,927.17 unchanged). ## Build v189 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 MUST-5 — the Playground write-through unmount flush (immediate and deferred) now retries on failure instead of being lost silently (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/Playground.tsx, the Playground view's Tax Plan write-through flush send) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (143). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, MUST-5): the Playground write-through unmount flush (sendPgRothFlush) had no retry — a failed flush was lost silently. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): stored spending $180,000/yr; in Playground the user edits plan spending to $170,000 and the delta sits in pendingPgRothSave; the user switches views with nothing in flight. The unmount cleanup cleared the delta from the queue and called sendPgRothFlush, which sent through pgRothSaveMutateRef.current(flushPayload) with NO per-call handlers — on BOTH of its sends (the guard-not-holding send built from the fetched record, and the fresh-fetch send built from the freshly fetched record under the M-4 coherence guard). The request failed (a network error at the moment of navigation); the mutation-level onError set the "Could not save" note on the unmounted view, where nobody could see it; there was no re-armed retry and the delta was already gone from the queue, so the $170,000 edit never landed in the Tax Plan record and returning showed $180,000. The deferred form had the same defect: a delta queued behind an in-flight write-through save was deferred by the cleanup (build v169, S-4) and fired from the in-flight call's settle handlers through the same sendPgRothFlush, so when the deferred send's own request failed it too was dropped with no retry. THE FIX (the MUST-3 / MUST-4 shape, builds v187 / v188): both of sendPgRothFlush's sends now go through ONE new retrying payload send, sendPgRothFlushPayload, defined beside sendPgRothFlush and reached through a ref (sendPgRothFlushPayloadRef) so a retry always calls the current closure. The send carries a per-call onError that re-arms a 3 s retry of the SAME payload, chained per failure exactly as firePendingPgRothSave's per-call onError re-arms its own retry, so a failed flush lands once the server is reachable again instead of being dropped. The retry timer lives in its own ref (pgRothFlushRetryTimerRef), not the shared pgRoth save timer — the cleanup clears the save timer as it runs, and nothing runs after unmount to clear the retry timer, so the retries outlive the view. The mutation reads its CAS base live from pgRothRevisionRef at each call, which still describes the record the payload was built from: on the guard-not-holding path the fetched and base revisions were equal at the build, and on the fresh-fetch path sendPgRothFlush adopts the fresh record's revision as the base before sending, so a retry rides exactly the base its first send did. A conflict is NOT retried: it resolves through onSuccess with res.ok false, where the mutation-level handler has already applied the conflict path's deliberate drop, and re-sending the stale-built payload would fight the newer record the refusal just re-showed — the same rule firePendingPgRothSave's per-call handlers follow. The pre-send drop paths in sendPgRothFlush are unchanged (no fresh-enough record on the fresh-fetch path, or a payload the fresh record already satisfies — the M-4 guard's deliberate outcomes, reached before any send exists to retry), the S-4 deferral itself is untouched (a queued-behind delta is still never fired concurrently with the in-flight save), and no other writer changed (the Tax Plan flush was MUST-3, build v187; the Retirement write-through flush was MUST-4, build v188). A successful flush is unchanged: it sends at once (or on the in-flight save's settle, for the deferred form) and lands normally. The December case is untouched. VERIFICATION (staged): the sandbox action-level drive (in Playground, queue a plan-field edit, switch views so the unmount flush fires, fail the flush, and confirm the edit is retried and lands — or is visibly reported — instead of being lost silently; confirm the deferred-flush form also retries on error; confirm a successful flush still lands normally), the December reference-case reproduction, the boundary-aware scrub of the changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms — ZERO matches required), the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness), and typecheck (server + client) run in the Verify stage against the built sandbox, together with three consecutive clean internal review passes. Nothing committed or pushed. SHOULD-1 is not dispatched until MUST-5 is resolved.

## Build v187 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 MUST-3 — the Tax Plan unmount flush (immediate and deferred) now retries on failure instead of being lost silently (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the Tax Plan plan-autosave unmount cleanup and a new flush send beside it) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (143). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, MUST-3): the Tax Plan unmount flush had no retry — a failed flush was lost silently. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): stored spending $180,000/yr, revision 5; the user types $170,000 with the debounce pending and switches views. The unmount cleanup fired saveMutateRef.current(queued) with NO per-call handlers — no onError re-arm (contrast firePendingSave's per-call onError, which keeps the payload queued and re-arms a 3 s retry). The request failed (a network error at the moment of navigation); the mutation-level onError set the "Could not save…" note on an unmounted component — invisible, and the note resets to "" on remount; the cleanup had already nulled pendingSave, so nothing retried and the $170,000 edit never landed — returning to the view showed $180,000 with no explanation. The deferred form had the same defect: a payload queued behind an in-flight save was stored in deferredFlushRef as the same bare mutate call, so when the in-flight save settled and the deferred send's own request failed, it too was dropped with no retry. THE FIX: both forms of the flush now go through ONE new send, sendFlushWithRetry, defined beside the cleanup and reached through a ref (sendFlushWithRetryRef) so the empty-deps cleanup and the deferred slot always call the current closure. The send carries a per-call onError that re-arms a 3 s retry of the SAME payload, chained per failure exactly as firePendingSave's onError re-arms its own retry, so a failed flush lands once the server is reachable again instead of being dropped. The retry timer lives in its own ref (flushRetryTimerRef), not the shared save timer — the cleanup clears the save timer as it runs, and nothing runs after unmount to clear the retry timer, so the retries outlive the view. Each attempt goes through the same send, and the mutation reads its CAS base live from planRevisionRef at each call, so a retry of a deferred flush rides the base the in-flight save adopted when it landed, exactly as its first send did. The queue is still nulled by the cleanup exactly as before — the payload's survival no longer depends on the queue, because the send carries it in its closure. A conflict is NOT retried: it resolves through onSuccess with res.ok false, where the mutation-level handler has already applied the conflict path's deliberate drop of the stale form, and re-sending it would fight the newer record the refusal just re-showed — the same rule firePendingSave's per-call handlers follow. A successful flush is unchanged: it sends at once (or on the in-flight save's settle, for the deferred form) and lands normally. The S-3 deferral itself is untouched — a queued-behind payload is still never fired concurrently with the in-flight save — and no other writer changed (the Retirement and Playground write-through flushes are MUST-4 / MUST-5, not dispatched here; Reset balances keeps its own immediate-save semantics, as in MUST-2). The December case is untouched. VERIFICATION (staged): the sandbox action-level drive (queue an edit, switch views so the unmount flush fires, fail the flush, and confirm the edit is retried and lands instead of being lost; confirm the deferred-flush form also retries on error; confirm a successful flush still lands normally), the December reference-case reproduction, the boundary-aware scrub of the changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms — ZERO matches required), the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness), and typecheck (server + client) run in the Verify stage against the built sandbox, together with three consecutive clean internal review passes. ## Build v186 (2026-11-03): Re-audit round 3 MUST-2 — a failed Reset plan no longer silently loses a queued autosave: the queued edit is held aside during the reset and restored + re-queued on failure, with the failure surfaced (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client-only fix (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the resetPlan mutation and doResetPlan) — no action signature, no engine, no pricing, and no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (143). THE FINDING (re-audit round 3, MUST-2): Reset plan dropped a queued autosave and had no failure handler, so a failed reset silently lost the edit. Worked example on the shared fictional sample household (server/src/sampleHousehold.ts): stored spending $180,000/yr; the user types $170,000 and the autosave effect queues it (pendingSave, 700 ms debounce); before the timer fires the user confirms "Reset plan". doResetPlan cleared the timer and set pendingSave.current = null, then called resetPlan.mutate(); when the resetRothPlanner request failed (offline / gateway 500), the mutation defined onSuccess only — no onError, no retry, no message tied to the lost queue — the form still showed $170,000, the autosave effect never re-fired (no state had changed), and a reload re-showed the stored $180,000. THE FIX (the M-5 pattern every other failed save follows — a payload stays recoverable until its write lands, and a failure is surfaced): doResetPlan now HOLDS the queued payload aside in a new ref (resetHeldSaveRef) instead of dropping it — the timer is cancelled and the queue cleared exactly as before, so the held payload still can never land after a successful reset and resurrect the pre-reset values. The reset mutation's onSuccess discards the held payload BEFORE any await (a landed reset, or a conflict refusal handled exactly like a save conflict, is the last word on the record; a later refetch failure can therefore never resurrect it). A new mutation-level onError handles a failed reset request: it closes the confirm, restores the held payload to pendingSave when the queue is still empty, and re-arms its save timer (rearmPendingSave), so the typed edit lands as an ordinary autosave once the server is reachable — exactly as if the reset had never been attempted; if the user kept typing while the reset was in flight, the queue already holds that newer snapshot and its own armed timer, so the held payload is not restored over it. The failure is surfaced two ways: the save-status note reads "The reset did not go through — your entries stay on this screen and will save as usual." (or, with nothing held, "The reset did not go through — your plan was not changed."), and the pre-existing reset error line under the reset controls (resetPlan.isError: "The reset did not go through — your plan was not changed. Try again.") now actually fires for a failed request. A successful reset is unchanged: the queue is cleared, the held payload discarded, and the record reseeds. No other discard flow changed (Back to saved and Reset balances keep their deliberate-drop / immediate-save semantics), and the December case is untouched. VERIFICATION (staged): the sandbox action-level drive (queue an edit, fail a reset, confirm the edit is preserved and a message shows; confirm a successful reset still clears the queue and resets the record), the December reference-case reproduction, the boundary-aware scrub of the changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and every listed real figure in dollars, cents, and formatted forms — ZERO matches required), the full suites (tax census, extended, retirement, December, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, UI-state, data-integrity, packaged harness), and typecheck (server + client) run in the Verify stage against the built sandbox, together with three consecutive clean internal review passes. Nothing committed or pushed. MUST-3 is not dispatched until MUST-2 is resolved.

PRICED EFFECT (sample household, direct engine probes, pre-fix gate restored vs fixed): reconciliation-on 2030 conversion $0.00 → $21,516.67, landing ACA MAGI exactly on the $132,000 household-of-4 cliff with credit $22,852.80 kept; every ACA year 2030–2034 lands on its cliff; lifetime conversions $800.00 → $90,907.77. (The brief estimated the recovered window total at ~$28,000 — that was the reconciliation-off total; the brief's own correct-behavior rule, land at the cliff while room and balance remain, prices $90,907.77, because the off shape's $10,400 landing itself sits $11,180 under the cliff. ## Build v177 (2026-11-03): Re-audit NICE-TO-HAVE N-3 — the coherence-guard hold can no longer poll forever; every in-flight hold is bounded at 100 polls with an explicit give-up (API contract unchanged)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/App.tsx, client/src/Playground.tsx, client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx, client/src/RothConversion.tsx) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged. THE FINDING (re-audit NICE-TO-HAVE N-3): the S-3/S-4 coherence discipline (contracts v168/v169) defers a flush behind an in-flight save, the deferred slot consumed by the in-flight call's own settle handlers; while a view is mounted, the matching wait is the fire path's hold — when a save is in flight (and, in the Retirement write-through, when the fetched record has not yet caught up to the CAS base — the v153/v162 coherence hold), the fire path re-arms a 300 ms re-check of itself. That re-arm had NO bound: if the in-flight save never settles (a hung request — the mutation's promise neither resolves nor rejects, so onSettled never runs and the in-flight flag never clears), the hold polls for the life of the view and the queued edit behind it never fires. CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING — five unbounded hold branches across four fire functions: the Playground write-through's in-flight hold, the Spending view spending-target write-through's in-flight hold, the Retirement autosave's in-flight hold, the Retirement write-through's in-flight hold AND its coherence hold, and the Tax Plan autosave's in-flight hold. THE FIX — one shared bound and one explicit give-up, applied identically in all five branches: each fire path gains a consecutive-poll counter; a hold branch increments it before re-arming, and the counter resets whenever the fire path actually sends or finds nothing left to send. After SAVE_HOLD_MAX_POLLS consecutive polls (100 × 300 ms = 30 s — far beyond any save this app makes) the hold gives up EXPLICITLY: the re-check timer is cleared and nulled so polling stops outright, the counter resets, the queued edit STAYS queued (nothing is dropped silently — a later edit, the blur flush, or the unmount flush fires it, and if the wedged save ever does settle its own per-call handlers still consume the deferred slot exactly as before), and the failure is surfaced with the same line each view already uses for a failed save ("Could not save — your entries stay on this screen."). The Retirement write-through's two holds share one counter and one give-up (they are one wait: the refetch the coherence hold waits for is the in-flight save's own invalidation). NOT CHANGED: the S-3/S-4 deferral itself — while an in-flight save settles normally nothing is ever sent concurrently and the deferred slot is consumed exactly as before; the coherence guard (nothing is sent under a base that does not describe the record it was built from); the settled-value gates; the failed-save 3 s retry (a settled save's retry, not a hold — it re-enters the fire path, where the bound applies to any new hold); the RothConversion focus-gate re-arm (it waits on the user leaving a field, not on a save, and dies with the view's cleanup — not the finding); the CAS conflict paths and their messages; the December console; any pricing; and every stored figure. VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-03, all on the sandbox copy; the live record was never written): (a) Source check — every 300 ms re-arm in the client now sits behind a counter check against SAVE_HOLD_MAX_POLLS (grep-verified across all four files; the only other 300 ms re-arm is the focus gate named above), each give-up clears and nulls its timer and surfaces the message, and each counter resets at the send and at the nothing-to-send exit. (b) Action-level drive with exactly the constructions the fixed client performs, on the write-through the S-4 fix built: baseline at the sandbox record's current revision with its saved spending; the in-flight save A (a synthetic test spending value at the current base) landed and advanced the revision; the deferred flush B, built by the guard's construction — a fresh fetch at A's revision, the payload rebuilt from that record with a second synthetic value, sent at the adopted base — landed in order and advanced the revision again: a deferred flush still lands when the in-flight save settles normally. The sandbox record was then restored to its exact pre-drive values and read back field-for-field identical to the pre-drive record apart from the revision the drive's own writes advance. (c) The never-settles leg is verified at the source, not by a browser drive: the bound is a counter compared before every re-arm, the give-up path clears the only timer that can re-enter the fire path, and no other code re-arms it — so a wedged save can hold a queue for at most 100 polls (30 s), after which the edit remains queued and visibly reported rather than silently stuck. (d) The December reference case reproduced EXACTLY from the saved console state via runDecemberProjection, in all three cases — every headline figure identical to the pinned reference (draw, MAGI, taxable income, federal tax, credit, net settlement, cash left); provenance contract 143.
