WHAT THE THREADING ALREADY DID (unchanged): taxReturnCore's one derivation computes the implied dividend/interest yields and the qualified share from the stored return actuals over a taxable pool; resolveArgsBalances threaded them onto the payload as transient fields; planInputsFromSaved stood a fallback in only for a blank yield field (an entered yield, even an explicit 0%, always wins) and passed the share as the engine's qualified-share field (absent = the engine's 100%-qualified default); pricePlaygroundYear priced the qualified figure clamped to the ordinary total but returned only the clamped figure, losing the entered pair. THE FIX — surface exactly those values, and accept them inbound: (1) getRothPlanner's taxReturn block gains derivedImpliedDividendYieldPct / derivedImpliedInterestYieldPct / derivedQualifiedDividendSharePct: the one taxReturnCore derivations evaluated over the resolved taxable pool at load (an explicit entered taxable balance when there is one, otherwise the latest snapshot's Taxable + Cash less any exclusion — the same resolution the saved-plan loader uses); the implied yields are null when there is no saved record or no positive pool, mirroring the threading condition exactly, and the share is null when no record is stored. (2) Every compute response's effectiveInputs gains six fields via a new withThreadedEcho wrapper (apiContractCore), applied where the existing spend-from-cash sleeve echo is applied — the shared computeEffectiveInputs path (optimizer, Monte-Carlo check/stats, work-years, gift, plan-year detail, funding, including their failure branches) and each runRothCompare scenario: the threaded yieldFallbackDividendPct / yieldFallbackInterestPct / qualifiedDividendSharePct read off the very payload (or merged scenario shape) that was priced, and effectiveDividendYieldPct / effectiveInterestYieldPct / effectiveQualifiedDividendPct read off the engine inputs built from that same shape — the echo reports what the engine actually used and never re-derives; where an entered yield wins, the effective field shows the entered value with the fallback still visible beside it. (3) The Playground year result gains ordinaryDividendsEntered / qualifiedDividendsEntered / qualifiedDividendsWasClamped / qualifiedDividendsExcess, read in pricePlaygroundYear's return off its own inputs and its already-computed clamped figure: the entered pair, whether the S-8/S-11 clamp bound, and by how much. PASSABILITY: the three transients are now optional fields on every compute action's base payload (bounds matching the saved yield fields' convention: yields 0–10000, share 0–100) and optional keys in compare scenario overrides; resolveArgsBalances never overwrites a caller-supplied transient with the record derivation (its per-side needs check is now "yield blank AND fallback absent"; a supplied share was already respected), and buildCompareScenario's per-scenario fallback re-derivation (v139 S-2) never overwrites a fallback a scenario's own overrides supply (present in the overrides, an explicit null included), and re-derives an inherited fallback only when it cannot describe the scenario — when the merged shape carries none yet, or when the scenario's pool differs from the base's pool (the S-2 case); with the pool unchanged, an inherited or base-supplied fallback stands exactly as threaded. (The first cut of this guard filled only still-absent sides, which broke the pinned S-2 fixture — a pool-changing scenario must re-derive over its own pool even when it inherits base fallbacks; the fixture caught it in the packaged census and the precedence above is the corrected rule, re-verified live: a half-pool scenario's echoed fallbacks double the base's, the same filed dollars over half the pool.) The saved record shape and every writer are unchanged — the transients stay unstored, following the sleeve-echo precedent. NOT CHANGED: the M-1 fallback derivation, the S-8/S-11 clamp logic, any pricing path, the December console (its inputs are already the console state getDecemberProjection returns, and its pair clamp already warns), and every stored figure. The contract's taxReturn and Playground-year semantics and the four affected action purposes gained the matching sentences (append-only; no existing wording removed). VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-02, all on the sandbox copy; the live record was never written): (a) Action-level drives: getRothPlanner's taxReturn block returns the derived implied yields and qualified share for the saved record; runRothFunding on the saved plan (blank yields) echoes threaded values identical to the planner's derived values and effective values identical to the threaded ones, with the entered yield fields still null in the echo; the same funding call with caller-supplied fallbacks and share echoes the supplied values unchanged as threaded and prices them as the effective values; runRothCompare's baseline scenario carries the same threaded/effective echo and reproduces the standing 5% anchors exactly, and a scenario overriding only the qualified share keeps the base fallbacks, prices its own effective share, and costs more, as a lower qualified share should; a half-pool scenario re-derives its fallbacks over its own pool, echoed at exactly double the base's percentages; runPlaygroundYear with a fictional impossible pair (qualified above ordinary) echoes the entered pair with the clamp flagged and the excess stated while the priced qualified figure equals the total, and a fictional possible pair echoes unclamped with zero excess. (b) December reference case reproduced EXACTLY (December suite 82/82, including the headline reference fixture). (c) Scrub: a boundary-aware scrub of this build's changed files for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and the real figures in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches. (d) Suites, all green: December 82/82, extended 159/159, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, data-integrity 0 violations; tax census and the packaged harness via the packaged runner (the live tax suite exceeds the action timeout, the standing limitation). (e) Typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree. (f) Three consecutive clean internal review passes over this build's hunks. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build v170 (2026-11-02): Re-audit SHOULD S-5 — the UI-state retry loop can no longer land a superseded value (API contract unchanged, 140)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the Tax Plan view's persistUiState — the Roth UI-state writer) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (140). The Tax Plan autosave, the Retirement writers, and the Playground write-through are untouched (S-3/S-4 fixed those in v168/v169). THE DEFECT (re-audit 2026-11-02 SHOULD S-5, NEW): CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING — persistUiState's S-6 bounded retry loop (up to 5 attempts) retries a conflicted UI-state write at the server's fresh revision, but its payload is the snapshot taken when the save was issued. While the loop sat between attempts, a newer edit of the SAME field in the same view could be issued and land; the loop's next attempt then sent the older snapshot at the fresh revision the newer write had just stored, silently overwriting the newer value. The server merges fields into the current blob, so no CAS check can see this: the retry's base is current, only its value is stale. THE FIX — the S-3/S-4 discipline (defer behind the in-flight save; never send a stale payload): (1) every issued write is stamped synchronously at issue time with a sequence number recorded as the latest for each logical field it carries (a new uiStateFieldKeys helper: a section toggle is one field keyed by its section id, its open riding with it; every other present key is its own field; a key present with a null value still counts — presence, not truthiness); a newer issue for a field replaces that field's stamp, which is what makes the earlier write superseded. (2) Writes run one at a time through a chain (uiStateChainRef): a write issued while another is in flight defers behind it and reads its CAS base only when its turn comes, so it bases itself on the revision the in-flight write landed — never firing concurrently under the same not-yet-advanced base. (3) Before EVERY send — the first attempt and each retry alike — the write re-checks its stamp against the latest stamp for every field it carries; if a newer write has superseded any of them, the write is dropped and never sends (again), and the newer write, itself queued on the chain, lands its own value, so the field ends at the newest value either way. A write no newer write has superseded retries exactly as before up to the S-6 bound: a conflict from another writer (the Playground, another tab) does not supersede a field, so cross-writer retries still land. Stamps are per-field, so a newer write of a different field never drops this one — it defers behind it on the chain and lands after it, in issue order. NOT CHANGED: the S-6 attempt bound, the conflict response handling, the base-fetch on a null tracked revision, the silent-failure semantics, every call site of saveUiState, any other writer, the December console, any pricing, and every stored figure; the 5% anchors do not move. VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-02, all on the sandbox copy; the live record was never written): (a) Action-level drive with exactly the constructions the fixed client performs, on the detailYear field, sandbox baseline rev 1109 (detailYear at its saved value): STILL-CURRENT leg — a save at a stale base was refused with conflict:true carrying rev 1109, and its retry at the fresh base 1109 landed (rev 1110), the field holding the retried value: a retry nothing superseded still lands. SUPERSEDED leg — a second save (a different detail year) at the now-stale base 1109 was refused with conflict:true carrying rev 1110 and the first value; under S-6 its retry would have sent that older value at base 1110. A newer edit of the same field (a third detail year) then landed at base 1110 (rev 1111), and the stored state read back holding the NEWER value at rev 1111 — the superseded retry is dropped by the fixed client before it sends, so it never lands. The sandbox blob was then restored to its exact pre-drive values (the saved detail year, written at base 1111 → rev 1112) and read back field-for-field identical to the pre-drive blob apart from the revision the restore writes themselves advance. Source confirmation: persistUiState's send sits behind the loop-head supersede check on every attempt (grep/read-verified) — there is no path from the retry loop to setRothUiState that does not re-check the stamp first, and every write's run is chained behind the writes issued before it. (b) December reference case reproduced EXACTLY from the saved console state via runDecemberProjection, in all three cases; provenance contract 140. (c) Scrub: a boundary-aware scrub of this build's changed hunks (the uiStateFieldKeys helper and the persistUiState block in RothConversion.tsx) for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and the real figures in dollars, cents, and formatted forms) confirms ZERO matches. (d) Suites, all green: via runAccuracySelfCheck on the sandbox — December 82/82, extended 159/159, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, data-integrity 0 violations (5 checks); tax census 527/527 with teeth ok on every slice (the 6-chunk packaged run passed chunks 0, 1, 3, 4 at 88/88 and chunk 5 standalone at 87/87, while chunk 2 was OOM-killed at exit 137, the standing transient on this machine, so chunk 2's range was re-run on the 12-chunk grid as chunks 4 and 5, 44/44 each with teeth ok and suiteTotal 527 — the full range covered with no gaps); packaged harness main checks 349/349 (run directly from the bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax). (e) Typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree. (f) Three consecutive clean internal review passes over this build's hunks (pass 1 traced the interleavings — same-field supersede drops at the loop head and the newer write lands off the chain; different-field writes defer and land in issue order; a cross-writer conflict neither supersedes nor drops, so the still-current retry lands at the S-6 bound exactly as before; an already-sent attempt that lands before the newer issue is overwritten in order by the deferred newer write, so the stored value still ends newest; pass 2 re-read the field-key derivation against every saveUiState call site — the section/open pair keys as one field, null-valued keys (a cleared detail year or baseline name) still key their field, and the non-retry paths are byte-for-byte the pre-v170 paths apart from the chain deferral and a supersede check that is a no-op when nothing newer was issued; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only RothConversion.tsx's UI-state writer — no server code, no other view, no stored figure). ONE LIMIT, recorded plainly (the same limit the S-3/S-4 passes recorded): the literal in-browser interleaving — a save sitting in its retry loop inside a live page while a second toggle fires — could not be driven in a browser, because the audit probe's page and the action sandbox are separate data copies; the case is verified by the action-level execution of the exact payload constructions above plus the source-level confirmation that the loop head re-checks the stamp before every send and that writes are chained, not by a browser run. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build v169 (2026-11-02): Re-audit SHOULD S-4 — the Playground's Tax Plan write-through gains an unmount flush (API contract unchanged, 140)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/Playground.tsx, the Spending dial's Tax Plan write-through) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (140). The Tax Plan autosave and the Retirement writers are untouched (S-3 fixed those in v168). THE DEFECT (re-audit 2026-11-02 SHOULD S-4, NEW): CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING — the Playground's write-through had NO unmount flush at all, unlike the other three writers. Its queue holds only the spending delta and the fire path sends it at once when the field is unfocused or on blur when focused (the settled-value gate), but nothing ran on unmount: an edit still queued when the view went away — held by the gate with its field still focused, waiting out the fire path's in-flight re-check timer, or re-armed on the failed-save retry timer — was lost silently, the timers died with the view, and the record kept the old value. THE FIX — the S-3 pattern plus the M-4 coherence guard, mirroring the Retirement write-through (v159/v162/v168) piece for piece: (1) a new unmount cleanup flushes a queued edit focused or not (leaving the view IS the settle; the queue holds only parsed values, so no half-typed value can persist) — the pending edit may BE the save currently in flight (the v151 rule), told apart by a new in-flight delta ref, and only an edit queued behind it is flushed. (2) With nothing in flight the flush sends at once through the ONE flush send (sendPgRothFlush); with a save in flight the cleanup stores the send in a deferred slot (deferredPgRothFlushRef) instead of firing it concurrently under the same not-yet-advanced CAS base, and the in-flight call's own per-call handlers consume the slot as that save settles — firing it under the newly adopted base when the save lands, firing it as a supersede when the save errors (no retry of the failed payload is armed: the queue no longer holds it), and dropping it when the save conflicts (the conflict path's deliberate-drop semantics — the deferred edit belongs to the same stale form). On every mounted fire the slot is null, so the fire path is otherwise byte-for-byte the v151/v152 path. (3) The flush send runs the M-4 coherence guard (the Retirement write-through's v162 rule): a new fetched-revision ref tracks the freshest fetched record beside the CAS base ref; guard not holding (the two agree) the payload builds from the fetched record and sends at once; guard holding, the record is fetched fresh, the payload is rebuilt from THAT record (buildPgRothSavePayload gains the optional record parameter its Retirement sibling already had), its revision is adopted as the base, and only then does the send go out — if the fresh fetch fails, or still returns a record older than the base, the edit is dropped rather than sent stale. After a landed save the deferred send reaches the guard holding, so the fresh-fetch path is its normal route and its payload already contains the just-landed save's values for every field outside the edit. NOT CHANGED: the settled-value gate, the blur flush, the queue's delta-only shape and revert-drop, the failed-save retry and its timing, the CAS conflict path and its message, any other writer, the December console, any pricing, and every stored figure; the 5% anchors do not move. VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-02, all on the sandbox copy; the live record was never written): (a) Action-level drive with exactly the constructions the fixed client performs: baseline rev 317 at the saved spending; the in-flight save A (a raised spending value at base 317) landed, rev 318; the deferred flush B, built by the guard's construction — a fresh fetch (rev 318), the payload rebuilt from that record with a still-higher spending value, sent at the adopted base 318 — landed, rev 319: the newest edit lands IN ORDER under the newly adopted base instead of being refused. A conflicting flush (a third value sent at the now-stale base 318) was refused with conflict:true, the refusal's record carrying rev 319 and B's value — the conflicting send is dropped and never lands, the semantics the client's per-call handler implements by dropping the slot on res.ok false. The sandbox record was then restored to its exact pre-drive values (rev 320, spending restored to the saved value, read back field-for-field identical to the pre-drive record). Source confirmation: no bare mutate remains in the Playground write-through's unmount cleanup (grep-verified) — every cleanup send is either the nothing-in-flight immediate send through the ONE guarded flush send or the deferred slot. (b) December reference case reproduced EXACTLY from the saved console state via runDecemberProjection, in all three cases; provenance contract 140. (c) Scrub: a boundary-aware scrub of the whole Playground.tsx pending diff for the household's figures (names, phone, email, and the real figures in dollars, cents, and formatted forms — the stored return actuals, the current and former spending, the truncated and full pool balances, the snapshot total, the cash bucket, salary, Social Security, and benchmark figures) confirms ZERO matches. (d) Suites, all green: via runAccuracySelfCheck on the sandbox — December 82/82, extended 159/159, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, data-integrity 0 violations (5 checks); tax census 527/527 with teeth ok on every slice (the 6-chunk packaged run passed chunks 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 — 439 fixtures — while chunk 2 was OOM-killed at exit 137, the standing transient on this machine, so chunk 2's range [176, 264) was re-run on the 12-chunk grid as chunks 4 and 5, 44/44 each with teeth ok and suiteTotal 527 — the full range covered with no gaps); packaged harness main checks 349/349 (run directly from the bundle with FPKG_SKIP=tax). (e) Typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree. (f) Three consecutive clean internal review passes over this build's hunks (pass 1 traced the interleaving — landed: deferred fires through the guard's fresh-fetch path under the adopted base; error: deferred supersedes with no double-send of the failed payload; conflict: slot dropped; in-flight-identity, retry-arming, and timer-clearing edges all match the sibling writers; pass 2 re-read the non-flush paths — fire path, queue, gate, blur flush, and conflict path byte-for-byte the pre-v169 paths apart from consuming a slot that is null on every mounted fire, and the payload builder's new parameter defaults to the fetched record for every existing caller; pass 3 confirmed the diff touches only Playground.tsx's write-through section — no server code, no other view, no stored figure — and that every timer and mutate use stays inside that section). ONE LIMIT, recorded plainly (the same limit the M-3/M-4/M-5/S-3 passes recorded): the literal two-request browser interleaving at unmount could not be driven — the audit probe's page and the action sandbox are separate data copies — so the case is verified by the action-level execution of the exact payload constructions above plus the source-level confirmation that the cleanup can only defer or send through the guarded flush send, never fire concurrently, not by a browser run. ## Build v168 (2026-11-02): Re-audit SHOULD S-3 — unmount flushes no longer fire a queued-behind save concurrently with the in-flight save (API contract unchanged, 140)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/RothConversion.tsx, the Tax Plan autosave; client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx, BOTH writers — the Retirement record's own autosave and its Tax Plan write-through) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (140). THE DEFECT (re-audit 2026-11-02 SHOULD S-3, NEW): CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE SOURCE BEFORE FIXING — all three unmount flushes fired a save queued behind the in-flight save CONCURRENTLY with it. The Tax Plan cleanup sent the queued payload by bare mutate whenever it was not the in-flight payload itself; the Retirement autosave cleanup did the same explicitly when saveInFlightRef was set (its header comment claimed a refusal "only re-bases the next mount's load"); the Retirement write-through cleanup sent its rebuilt payload (or its guard-holding fresh-fetch send) by bare mutate whenever the queued delta was not the in-flight delta. Each writer's mutation reads its CAS base LIVE from its revision ref at the call, and that ref adopts the in-flight save's returned revision only when the save lands — so the flush and the in-flight save carry the SAME base. The server's guarded commit accepts exactly one of two same-base saves and refuses the other with the conflict shape; when the refused one is the flush, its conflict handling (queue drop, form re-hydrate, message) runs on an UNMOUNTED view, the queue was already cleared by the cleanup, and no retry exists — the newest edit, the very one the flush exists to preserve, is silently lost. When the flush happens to win the race, the in-flight (older) save is refused instead, its own conflict handling equally invisible. Which edit survives is a coin flip on network timing. WORKED EXAMPLE, MEASURED PRE-FIX at the action level on the sandbox (the exact payload constructions the client sends): baseline rev 312, at the saved spending; the in-flight save A (a raised spending value at base 312) landed, rev 313; the flush save B (a still-higher spending value at the SAME base 312 — the base the concurrent flush's mutation reads before A settles) was REFUSED with conflict:true, the refusal's record carrying A's value — stored holds the older edit, the newer flush edit is gone. THE FIX — defer, never fire concurrently: each writer gains a deferred-flush slot (deferredFlushRef; deferredRothFlushRef for the write-through). The cleanup now branches on the in-flight flag it already tracks: nothing in flight → the flush sends at once, exactly as before; a save in flight → the cleanup stores the send in the slot and clears the queue, and the IN-FLIGHT call's own per-call handlers consume the slot as that save settles (the handlers are attached to every fire-path call, and the slot is only ever set by the cleanup, so no mounted fire can consume it): on a LANDED save (res.ok) they fire the deferred send — the mutation-level handler has already adopted the new revision, so the send reads the NEW base and the queued edit lands on top of, in order; on an ERROR they fire it too — nothing landed, the base is unchanged, and the queued payload supersedes the failed save outright (no retry of the failed payload is armed: the queue no longer holds it); on a CONFLICT they DROP it — the conflict path's deliberate drop of the stale form's queued edits covers the deferred send, which is that same form's newest snapshot and must not ride out under the adopted base over the newer record the conflict just re-showed. Per writer: the Tax Plan's deferred send is the captured queued payload (the form's final whole-form snapshot). The Retirement autosave's deferred send captures the queued payload with its onOk and its form/command kind — a form snapshot is rebuilt at the deferred fire (the v163 discipline; the unmounted form is frozen, so the rebuild reads the same final values), a submitSave command payload is sent exactly as constructed with its onOk riding along as in the fire path. The write-through's flush send is factored into ONE sendRothFlush (the v162 guard-holding body, verbatim: guard not holding → build from the fetched record and send; guard holding → fresh-fetch, rebuild from that record, adopt its revision, send; no fresh-enough record → drop) shared by the immediate flush and the deferred flush, so both run identical guard code; after a landed save the deferred send reaches it with the guard holding, and the fresh-fetch path rebuilds its payload from the record that save just landed. ## Build v163 (2026-11-02): The Retirement view's own autosave surfaces a failed save, keeps it queued, and retries (re-audit MUST M-NEW-3)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx, the saveRetirementCalc autosave) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (138). The Tax Plan write-through save paths in the same file are NOT touched. THE DEFECT (re-audit 2026-11-02 M-NEW-3, NEW — not a re-report): the Retirement view's own autosave was the fourth writer carrying the exact M-5 defect (build v151 fixed it for the three saveRothInputs writers). Its save mutation had onSuccess only — no onError — and firePendingSave cleared the queue before the call (pendingSave.current = null). A failed autosave (offline, gateway 500) dropped the payload silently, showed nothing, and nothing re-queued until the next edit; a reload reverted the form to the old record. submitSave (Reset to defaults, Load scenario / Back to my plan) rides the same path, so a failed reset save was equally silent. THE FIX, mirroring the M-5 fix and the December console's onError (December.tsx:1017): (1) the save mutation gains an onError that sets the shared plan-message line to "Could not save — your entries stay on this screen.", and its onSuccess (ok branch) clears exactly that note when a later save lands, the same completion discipline the write-through applies to the shared line; (2) firePendingSave no longer clears the queue at the call — the save stays queued until it succeeds, the per-call onSuccess drops it only if the queue still holds that same payload (never a newer one queued behind it), and the per-call onError re-arms an automatic retry on the view's save timer (3s), exactly the write-through's shape; (3) the retry rebuilds from the freshest state instead of re-sending a stale snapshot: a new pendingSaveIsFormRef marks the autosave's own form snapshots, and firePendingSave rebuilds those at EVERY fire via buildInputsPayloadRef (the current form), so a retry sends the form as it now stands — the M-3/M-4 rebuild discipline in the only form this whole-form writer admits. A submitSave command payload is NOT rebuilt (it is a deliberate command, not a record snapshot) and is re-sent exactly as constructed, its onOk cache sync intact; (4) a new saveInFlightPayloadRef (mirroring rothSaveInFlightDeltaRef) lets the unmount flush tell a save queued behind the in-flight one (flush it) from the in-flight save itself (already being written — the queue now stays populated until success, so without this the flush would double-send it). NOT CHANGED: the CAS conflict path (applyConflictRecord still drops the queue and its retry timer, re-hydrates from the refusal's record, and says so — a conflict is a deliberate drop, never retried), the in-flight serialization (300ms re-fire), the 700ms debounce, save timing otherwise, the Tax Plan write-through in the same file, the saved spending, and every stored figure; no pricing, so the 5% anchors do not move. One interplay, traced in review: after Reset/Load, the autosave effect re-queues a form snapshot of the same (just-set) values behind the command save, exactly as before this build; if the command save then fails, the message surfaces and the values still land through that queued snapshot's own save-and-retry — the reset is never silently lost, and a command save that fires with no intervening re-queue retries as itself, onOk included. ## Build v159 (2026-11-02): The Retirement write-through's unmount flush no longer drops a pending edit while a plan field is focused (audit SHOULD S-7)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only (client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx) — no action changed, no engine change, no pricing changed, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged (138). THE DEFECT (internal audit S-7, settled — STANDS): the Retirement view's unmount cleanup flushed the pending Tax Plan write-through (pendingRothSave) only when no plan field was focused (focusFieldRef.current == null || !PLAN_FIELD_KEYS.includes(...)). When the view went away while a plan field still held focus — a tab close, or a navigation that unmounts without a blur firing first — focusFieldRef still read e.g. "spending", the flush was skipped, and the pending edit was silently dropped; the record kept the old value. Normal exits were covered by the focus-change (blur) flush, a tab close was not. THE FIX, following the Tax Plan's own v149 precedent ("leaving the view IS the settle", RothConversion.tsx's unmount flush sends focused or not): (1) the focus condition is REMOVED from the unmount flush — a queued delta now flushes on unmount regardless of focus, with the v151 in-flight distinction unchanged (an edit that IS the in-flight save is already being written; only one queued behind it flushes). (2) The flush now sends DIRECTLY via rothSaveMutateRef in both cases, not through firePendingRothSave: the fire path's settled-value gate would hold the send for the very focus this flush must ignore (removing the cleanup's condition alone would still have lost the edit — the fire would return at its gate and the cleanup then cleared the queue), and its re-check timers cannot run once the view is gone. The payload is still built at flush time from the freshest record via buildRothSavePayload (build v153), and the mutation still reads its CAS base live at the call, so a genuine race resolves as a server conflict, never a silent overwrite. Flushing the QUEUED delta is safe for a half-typed field: the queue only ever holds parsed values that differ from the last-synced ones — a blank or unparseable field carries no delta (computePlanDelta) — so there is no half-typed value in it to persist; that is what the removed gate's "never persist a half-typed value" comment was protecting, and the queue's construction already guarantees it. NOT CHANGED: the saved spending and every stored figure; the fire path's settled-value gate, the focus-change/blur flush effect, the Retirement record's own autosave flush, save timing/debounce, and the M-5 failed-save retry are all untouched — PLAN_FIELD_KEYS.includes now appears exactly twice (the fire gate and the blur flush), both intended. NOT CHANGED: the saved spending and every stored figure; save timing, the settled-value gate, the M-3 fresh-rebuild fire path, and the M-5 failed-save retry are untouched — a network failure still keeps the edit on screen with "Could not save", only a CAS refusal performs the deliberate drop-and-reset; no pricing, so the 5% anchors do not move from this build. ## Build v157 (2026-11-02): The plan engine splits its dividend yield by the stored return's qualified share (audit SHOULD S-1)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine split (server/src/taxEngine.ts simulateRothPlan + server/src/workYears.ts work-year pricer), one new derivation (server/src/taxReturnCore.ts), record-layer threading (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts planInputsFromSaved transient, server/src/actions.ts resolveArgsBalances, the two client plan-input constructions in RothConversion.tsx and Playground.tsx), contract text (TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS), and one new tax-suite fixture. CONTRACT VERSION: 137 → 138 (TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS amendment only; no request or response shape changed). THE DEFECT (internal audit S-1, settled — STANDS): the plan march priced 100% of its dividend yield income as QUALIFIED dividends (qualifiedDividends: dividendIncome at the fill base and at priceWith), but a household's own filed return is only partly qualified (its line 3a is a share of its line 3b total, the rest non-qualified), so the march understated federal tax by pricing too much income on the preferential stack — by the audit's worked difference per year at its worked-example conversion. THE FIX, per the settlement's design decision: split the yield by a qualified share DERIVED from the stored return actuals, consistent with M-1's implied-yield fallback. (1) qualifiedDividendSharePctFromTaxReturn (taxReturnCore.ts) is the ONE derivation: line 3a ÷ line 3b as a %, rounded to 4 decimal places (on the stored return: line 3a ÷ line 3b as a percentage — applying it to that return's own distribution prices exactly its line 3a as qualified); either dividend line unentered, or a $0 total, derives null (no share implied); a line 3a above its total clamps to 100 (the S-8/S-11 impossible-pair rule). (2) The share rides the saved shape as a TRANSIENT (qualifiedDividendSharePct on RothSavedLike, following the yieldFallback precedent — never saved, never in a request schema), threaded by the actions layer's resolveArgsBalances (which now reads the stored record whenever the payload does not already carry a share, entered yields included — the share describes the dividend income's CHARACTER, not its size) and by the two client constructions (RothConversion's working plan sets the engine field directly from its planner read; the Playground's saved-plan years thread the transient through planInputsFromSaved). planInputsFromSaved passes it to the engine as RothPlanInputs.taxableDividendQualifiedPct. (3) THE SPLIT: each priced year computes qualifiedDividendIncome = the year's dividend income × the share (absent/null share = 100, clamped 0–100) and the remainder as non-qualified, passed to priceYear as qualifiedDividends / ordinaryDividends at BOTH of the march's pricing sites (fill base and priceWith, so fills, settlements, and the harvest predicate all price the same character) and at the work-years pricer's one site; the total is counted once, exactly as the single-year pricer splits its entered pair. Detail dividendIncome still reports the TOTAL distribution. NO NEW USER-FACING INPUT, per the settlement — the return-derived share is the fix; no stored figure changed, and the tax-return-pricing-identity fixture still passes (planInputsFromSaved never reads the actuals; only the derived % reaches pricing, so the semantics text now states the actuals have exactly TWO pricing-adjacent roles, both through derived percentages, and the api-tax-return-semantics-content phrase list grows 19 → 22). NEW FIXTURE plan-dividend-qualified-share-s1 pins the audit's worked example END TO END through the march (2026, MFJ born 1975/1985, a round already-converted amount, the filed interest and dividend actuals as the year's income off a constructed pool at a round yield, spending $0, tax from a blank-basis pool so no feedback gains): derivation of the share from the pair / blank null / partial null / over-pair 100; the split march's federal tax, ordinary taxable, and gains taxable as pinned; the same shape with NO share threaded prices the pre-fix figures — a difference of exactly the audit's worked difference, with AGI identical under both. NOT CHANGED: the Playground/December single-year pricing (already split; the December reference case is untouched by construction); the saved spending and every stored figure. CONSEQUENCE, recorded plainly per the brief: this RAISES priced federal tax on the household's real plan (by roughly the audit's worked difference per year at the worked-example conversion) and shifts the ordinary/gains stacks in every march year, so the 5% anchors MOVE and need re-deriving now that S-1 has landed (with M-1, S-8, S-11 already in) — NOT done in this build, per the brief. VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-02, all on the sandbox copy; the live record was never written — every live call was compute-only or a read): (a) The worked example reproduced on a scratch march pre-fixture and live via runRothCompare through the app's actions: the payload carried NO share, so the server's resolveArgsBalances threaded the derived share from the sandbox's stored return (2025); the 2026 year priced federal tax at the split figure plus 1¢ attributable to the call's own interest-yield argument (its yield priced the interest a few cents over the filed figure; at the exact filed figure the fixture pins the split tax to the cent) — with provenance contract 138. The fresh-plan fallback is pinned by the fixture's legacy arm (no share implied → the all-qualified figures, unchanged). (b) December reference case reproduced EXACTLY from the saved console state via runDecemberProjection. (c) Suites, all green: tax census 526/526 (grown from 525 by the one new fixture) — the 6-chunk packaged run passed chunks 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 (438 fixtures, teeth ok, all chunks agreeing on the suite's own derived total of 526) while chunk 2 was OOM-killed (exit 137, standing S-2), so chunk 2's range [176, 264) was re-run on the 12-chunk grid as chunks 4 and 5, 44/44 each with teeth ok — the full range covered with no gaps; packaged main harness 349/349 checks (run directly from the same bundle after the census exit, FPKG_SKIP=tax); via runAccuracySelfCheck on the sandbox — December 81/81, extended 159/159 (incl. the amended semantics fixture at 22 phrases), retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, data-integrity 0 violations (5 checks). The tax-teeth self-check suite was not called (it exceeds the worker's 120s limit, standing S-2); per-chunk teeth ran through the packaged taxtest instead, all ok. (d) Typecheck clean (server + client) on the final tree; the saved record read back untouched (revision 306, annual spending unchanged, the stored tax-return figures for 2025 intact, yield fields still blank). ## Build v156 (2026-11-02): runRothCompare's pretaxOutByChoiceCents excludes tax-bill pre-tax debits (audit SHOULD S-10)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine detail split (server/src/taxEngine.ts) plus the compare readout (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) and one new tax-suite fixture. NO API CONTRACT CHANGE: the published definition (build v127, round-19 finding 11) already stated the correct semantic — this build fixes the CODE to match the doc, so no purpose text, request, or response shape changes and the API contract version stays 137. THE DEFECT (internal audit S-10, settled — STANDS): pretaxOutByChoiceCents is documented as the year's pre-tax money out BY CHOICE — its conversion plus its pre-tax draw for spending, an RMD alone not in it — distinct from runRothFunding's pretaxDrawCents (the extra spending draw PLUS pre-tax amounts applied to the tax bill, excluding the conversion). The computation read detail.extraPreTaxDraw, which the engine defines as the spending draw PLUS the pre-tax debits that paid the tax bill (settlement feedback), so in every year a tax-bill pre-tax debit occurred the readout was overstated by exactly that debit and EQUALLED the funding field — the v127 distinction collapsed. ## Build v155 (2026-11-02): Qualified dividends are clamped to the ordinary total — the excess prices nowhere (audit SHOULD S-8 + S-11)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine clamp in the shared single-year pricer (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts pricePlaygroundYear) plus the December assembly (server/src/decemberCore.ts decemberCaseInputs), contract text (PLAYGROUND_YEAR_SEMANTICS), console notes (client/src/Playground.tsx, client/src/December.tsx), and the runDecemberProjection action description. CONTRACT VERSION: 136 → 137 (PLAYGROUND_YEAR_SEMANTICS amendment only; no request or response shape changed — the Playground result's qualifiedDividends now reports the priced, clamped figure). THE DEFECT (internal audit S-8 + S-11, settled — both STAND): when qualified dividends were entered greater than the ordinary-dividends total, only the non-qualified part was floored at $0 (max(0, total − qualified)) while the qualified amount passed to priceYear WHOLE — so the excess over the total priced as qualified gains, inventing phantom dividends in AGI, MAGI, and the ACA / NIIT bases (S-11: total $1,000 / qualified $5,000 priced AGI $5,000; S-8 example 1a: a YTD qualified figure entered above the saved total priced the excess as qualified income, understating the headline draw by the excess and federal tax by its tax effect). THE FIX — THE LITERAL CLAMP, decided explicitly per the settlement: the entered total is the ceiling. (1) pricePlaygroundYear derives qualifiedDividends = min(max(0, entered qualified), max(0, entered total)) ONCE, before any pricing reads it, and every downstream figure reads the clamped value — the priceYear pass, ltcgPriced, the gains flags' stack, hasGainsTyped, and the result's own qualifiedDividends field (which now reports the priced figure, not the entered excess). The non-qualified derivation is unchanged in form (max(0, total − clamped qualified)) and cashIn still counts the entered total once. This reverses the one prior documented carve-out ("qualified entered with no total still prices once"): under the literal clamp a qualified figure with a $0 total prices $0 — the pair is impossible in either direction. (2) decemberCaseInputs clamps PER PAIR — the year-to-date pair and each case's still-to-come pair separately (ytdQualified ≤ ytdOrdinary, remQualified ≤ remOrdinary), joining the function's existing portion clamps (janPaidCapGain, k1CapGain, rocQualified, janPaidQualified); the summed pair then also satisfies the pricer's clamp by construction. (3) WARNINGS/NOTES: computeDecemberProjection now warns on an impossible pair (year-to-date pair named with its figures; still-to-come pair named per case), matching the Playground's note, and the December console renders matching notes under the year-to-date pair and the still-to-come rows (client display only, reading the form exactly as the priced state clamps it); the Playground's own pair note is reworded to the clamped behaviour ("it prices as {total}, the excess isn't counted, and the non-qualified part prices as $0"). TAX CONSEQUENCE, as the settlement directs: example 1a under the literal clamp preserves the CLAMPED total as qualified (the whole saved total, all preferential), so its federal tax is the clamp figure — NOT the finding's reference figure, which was the reference-pair pricing (the saved pair's qualified part); the draw/MAGI expectations are clamp-invariant and hold exactly. RE-PINS: the tax suite's playground-dividend-split-overage fixture is re-pinned to the clamp (priced/reported qualified $7,000 on a $7,000 total entered as $15,000; ltcgPriced $7,000; AGI $7,000) and a new playground-dividend-clamp-s11-example fixture pins the audit's exact pair ($1,000 / $5,000 → qualified $1,000, ltcgPriced $1,000, AGI/MAGI/ACA MAGI $1,000). Four long-standing fixtures that entered qualified dividends with NO total (playground-rmd-and-watch-outs part (c), playground-chip-fill-gains-dont-shrink, mt-pg2-niit-distinguishing, playground-2027-schema-and-fallback-pricing) had their INPUT pairs made consistent (ordinary total set equal to the qualified amount, all of it qualified) with every expected figure unchanged — the clamp prices their intended stacks identically once the pair is possible. The extended suite's api-playground-year-semantics-content fixture grows 7 → 9 pinned phrases (the clamp sentences). A new December fixture (dec-dividend-pair-clamp-s8) pins both worked pairs at the inputs level plus both projection warnings. CONSEQUENCE, recorded plainly: this changes single-year pricing for impossible pairs only (every possible pair prices bit-identically), so plan-level 5% anchors do not move from this build; the anchors remain stale from the v135/v136 pricing fixes and are re-derived once all pricing fixes land, per the standing plan — NOT done here. ## Build v153 (2026-11-02): The Retirement write-through can no longer defeat CAS — deltas queued, payload rebuilt fresh at fire time, sourced sync guarded (audit MUST M-4)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only — no action changed, no engine change, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged. THE DEFECT (internal audit M-4, settled — STANDS): the Retirement view's Tax Plan write-through (rothSave, a writer of saveRothInputs) built its whole-record payload once at queue time from the record as it was then, but its mutation read the CAS baseRevision live from rothRevisionRef at send time. If another tab saved while the edit sat queued (a plan field still focused, so the settled-value gate held the fire), the refetch advanced the revision ref while the queued payload still held the old field values; on blur the stale payload went out under the fresh base, the server CAS accepted it (base matched), and the other tab's edit was silently reverted with no conflict message — the audit's worked example: a spending raise queued here while the Tax Plan tab saved expected return 5% → 5.5%, and the blur sent the queued 5% under the fresh base, reverting 5.5% → 5%. Two companion defects from the settlement: the sourced effect (RetirementCalc.tsx) re-synced all five plan fields from the refetched record UNGUARDED, clobbering in-progress typing on screen mid-edit; and queueRothSave returned early on a null payload WITHOUT clearing pendingRothSave, leaving the stale payload queued. The server CAS guard itself is sound and untouched; the defeat was client-side. THE FIX (client/src/RetirementCalc.tsx only), the M-3 family shape adapted to five fields: (1) The queue now holds ONLY the local deltas — pendingRothSave stores a RothPlanDelta: for each of the five plan fields, the target value when the field's parsed value differs from planSyncedRef (the record values the fields were last synced to — maintained by hydrate, by the sourced effect, and by a landed write-through, whose per-call onSuccess adopts the payload's five values), else null (no local edit — whatever the record holds at fire time stands). Comparing against the last-synced values, not the current record, is what keeps a field the user never touched from becoming a delta just because another tab moved the record under it; a blank or unparseable field parses to null and carries no delta, so it can never blank a stored value, exactly as before. (2) firePendingRothSave rebuilds the payload at fire time via buildRothSavePayload(delta) from the freshest fetched record (rothQ.data — the same refetch rothRevisionRef is synced from), spreading that record and replacing only the delta's fields; if the fresh record already holds every delta value (another tab saved the same edits first), the build returns null and the fire completes the owed save without sending. (3) Payload/base coherence: because a save result adopts its returned revision into rothRevisionRef one refetch ahead of the fetched record, the fire holds (300ms re-check, the serialization re-arm's cadence) while the new rothFetchedRevisionRef disagrees with rothRevisionRef, so a payload is only ever sent under a base describing the same record it was built from — closing the one narrower window of the same defeat (an own save landing while a disjoint-field edit sat queued behind it). (4) queueRothSave now CLEARS pendingRothSave when no delta is owed (the edit was reverted, or the record caught up with it) instead of leaving a stale payload queued. (5) The sourced effect is per-field and guarded: a field re-syncs from the record only when it is clean (its parsed value still equals its last-synced value) and not the focused field, so a refetch landing mid-edit never clobbers in-progress typing or an unsaved local edit, while untouched fields still follow the record and show the other tab's edit; focusField joins its deps so a focused-but-unedited field catches up once focus leaves it; a write-through conflict sets planForceSyncRef so the stored values replace the form wholesale, exactly as the conflict message states (the deliberate drop). (6) The unmount flush builds its payload from the queued delta at flush time like the fire path; the v151 in-flight distinction now tracks the in-flight delta. Save timing/debounce otherwise untouched: queue on the same field-change effect, fire at once when unfocused, held by the settled-value gate while a plan field is focused, flushed on blur, serialized behind an in-flight save on the same 300ms re-arm; the v151 (M-5) failed-save behavior is preserved and strengthened — the per-call handlers key on the queued delta's identity, success drops only that edit, error re-arms the 3s retry, and every retry rebuilds fresh at its own fire. A genuine race that still lands between the rebuild and the server's CAS check resolves exactly as before: conflict, record re-read, stored values re-shown, plain message. NOT CHANGED: the saved spending and every stored figure; the Tax Plan autosave and the Playground write-through (separate writers, already fixed for M-5/M-3); no pricing — the 5% anchors do not move from this build alone. GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean (server + client); three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff (the third pass added the coherence guard in (3)); the packaged harness and full suites green on the sandbox copy (see below); the December reference case untouched by construction (no December code changed). VERIFICATION COMPLETED (2026-11-02): (a) Suites, all green: via runAccuracySelfCheck on the sandbox copy — December 80/80, extended 159/159, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, extended and retirement teeth pass, data-integrity 0 violations (5 checks); via the packaged harness — main harness 349/349 checks, and the tax census 523/523: the 6-chunk run passed chunks 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 (435 fixtures, teeth ok, all chunks agreeing on the suite's own derived total of 523) while chunk 2 was OOM-killed (exit 137, standing S-2), so chunk 2's range [176, 264) was re-run in two finer slices from the same bundled fixture module (N=12 chunks 4 and 5, 44/44 each, teeth ok) — the full range covered with no gaps. (b) December reference case reproduced exactly from the saved console state through runDecemberProjection on the sandbox; contract version 136 confirmed in the run's provenance. (c) The worked example, executed at the action level on the sandbox copy with exactly the payloads the two client shapes construct: baseline rev 306 (at the saved spending, expected return 5%); "Tab B" saved expected return 5.5% at base 306 → rev 307; the fixed fire's construction — payload rebuilt from the fresh rev-307 record with only annualSpendingCents replaced by the queued raise, base 307 → accepted, rev 308, and the stored record read back (in the refusal record below and on re-read) holding BOTH the raised spending AND expected return 5.5%; a stale-base replay of the old queue-time shape (payload carrying expected return 5%, base 306) was refused with conflict:true and the stored record untouched — the server CAS backstop intact. The sandbox record was then restored to the live values (rev 309: the saved spending, expected return 5%, retirement age 57); the live record was never written by this build. (d) Rendered check: the audit probe loaded the build with no console errors; in the Retirement view the Annual spending field took an in-progress $175,000 edit and KEPT it across repeated observes/refetches while focused (no mid-edit clobber), blur settled it to $175,000.00, and after a full reload the Tax Plan showed "spend $175,000/yr" with "Every field matches the saved plan. Saved" — the ordinary write-through landing end to end through the new delta queue; the probe copy was then restored to the saved spending the same way and the Tax Plan confirmed the saved figure with "Saved". ONE LIMIT, recorded plainly (the same limit the M-3 pass recorded): the literal two-browser-tab interleaving could not be driven in this environment — the audit probe's page and the action sandbox are separate data copies, so no second tab can land a save inside the probe page's focused edit; the race is therefore verified by (c)'s action-level execution of the exact constructions, (d)'s rendered write-through, and the audit's source-level confirmation of the fix, not by a two-tab browser run. Nothing committed or pushed.

## Build v151 (2026-11-02): A failed plan save is no longer silently dropped — it says so, stays queued, and retries (audit MUST M-5)

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only — no action changed, no engine change, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged. THE DEFECT (internal audit M-5, settled — STANDS): the three plan-record save mutations (Tax Plan autosave in RothConversion.tsx, the Playground write-through pgRothSave, the Retirement write-through rothSave — all writers of saveRothInputs) dropped a failed save silently. The Playground and Retirement mutations had no onError at all; the Tax Plan had the v149 error note, but in all three the fire path cleared the pending payload BEFORE the mutate call, so on failure (offline / gateway 500) the payload was gone, nothing retried, and the field kept showing the unsaved value until a reload reverted it. THE FIX, the same shape in all three: (1) onError on every mutation, following the December pattern — the Tax Plan keeps its v149 note ("Could not save — your entries stay on this screen.", already the text its status line reads first), the Playground sets the same text in its spending message line (cleared again when a later save lands), and the Retirement write-through sets it in its plan message line. (2) The payload is kept until a SUCCESS, not until the call: each fire path (firePendingSave / firePendingPgRothSave / firePendingRothSave) no longer clears its pending ref before mutating; a per-call onSuccess drops the queued payload only when it is still that payload (a newer edit queued behind an in-flight save is never dropped; a conflict resolves through the same callback after the mutation-level handler's deliberate drop, so the discard stands), and a per-call onError re-arms a retry of the still-queued payload on the view's shared save timer (3s), so the save lands once the server is reachable again. The settled-value gates, debounce timing, CAS bases, and conflict handling are otherwise untouched: a retry that comes due while a field is focused is held by the same gate and flushed on blur, exactly like a first attempt, and the Tax Plan's retry rides the timer its discard flows already govern (their confirms cancel it, their execute paths drop the payload, so a retry can never land a discarded edit). (3) The Tax Plan and Retirement unmount flushes gained one guard: the pending payload may now BE the save currently in flight (tracked in a new in-flight-payload ref), and that one is already being written, so the flush only fires a payload queued behind it — the previous flush-the-newer-payload-on-unmount behavior is otherwise unchanged. NOT CHANGED: the saved spending and every stored figure; no save timing or debounce behavior beyond keeping a failed save queued for retry. The Retirement view's own record save (saveRetirementCalc) shares the old shape but is outside M-5's settled scope (the audit names the three saveRothInputs writers) and is untouched. GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean (server + client); the packaged harness and full suites run on the sandbox copy as part of this build's verification (see the build report); the December reference case is untouched by construction (no December code changed). ## Build v136 (2026-11-02): A blank yield field prices the implied estimate from the filed return, not $0 (audit MUST M-1)

All user-entered data, no external source. THE DEFECT (internal audit M-1, settled — STANDS): the plan march priced a blank dividend/interest yield field as $0 income, but the household's own stored 2025 return carries real interest and dividend actuals — a blank yield field means "no yield entered", not "no yield income". Pricing it as $0 understated AGI/MAGI by the whole yield income in every plan year and could flip an ACA cliff decision by about a full credit (the audit's Playground worked example: a 2026 conversion filled to cliff − $5,000 kept the reference credit blank, and lost it entirely with the actuals priced). THE FALLBACK, decided explicitly: a blank yield field is filled, where the plan's inputs are assembled for pricing, with the IMPLIED YIELD the stored actuals describe — that line's actual ÷ the plan's resolved taxable pool (the same base that surface's march prices yields on), rounded to 4 decimal places; the dividend yield derives from the line 3b TOTAL, the interest yield from line 2b. The one derivation is impliedYieldPctsFromTaxReturn (server/src/taxReturnCore.ts). RESOLUTION: the derived percentages ride the saved shape as two TRANSIENT fields (yieldFallbackDividendPct / yieldFallbackInterestPct on RothSavedLike, following the spendFromCashSleeveCents precedent — never saved, never in a request schema), threaded by the actions layer's resolveArgsBalances on the server (which reads the stored record's tax-return block and the resolved pool) and by the two client plan-input constructions (RothConversion's working-plan inputs, over the form's priced pool; the Playground's saved-plan years, over the prefill's resolved pool). planInputsFromSaved is the one resolution point for saved shapes: entered yield (explicit 0% included — 0% is a real answer) always wins; blank takes the transient; no transient (no stored actual for the line, or no pool) stays null and the engine prices $0 exactly as before — so the seed (blank yields AND blank actuals) and every fixture shape without transients price bit-identically. The engine's own `?? 0` (taxEngine.ts, workYears.ts) is unchanged and now means "no estimate exists", with comments saying so. PRICING ISOLATION PRESERVED, as the brief directs: the 1040 amounts are still never read by pricing AS amounts — no compute action accepts them, they never enter a scenario, planInputsFromSaved never reads them (the tax-return-pricing-identity fixture still passes unchanged, pinning the conversion's bit-identity with the fields set or blank); only the derived yield percentages reach pricing, through the ordinary yield mechanism. TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS is amended to state exactly this (amounts never enter a priced year as income; the conversion's bit-identity is the pinned isolation; the fallback rule is the one pricing-adjacent role), and the api-tax-return-semantics-content fixture's phrase list grows 16 → 19 to pin the fallback sentences. UI: the two yield-field hints in the Tax Plan no longer claim "Blank = no dividend/interest income is modelled" — they now say blank prices the estimate the filed return implies and that entering 0% models none; the gift section's explainer and the remaining stale comments (rothSeed, parseRothInputs, plan-year detail surfacing) are corrected to match. DECEMBER: the December console has no yield fields anywhere in its input shape — its remaining-income lines are the user's own entered current-year estimates and its projection prices exclusively from console inputs through pricePlaygroundYear — so there is no December yield input for the fallback to fill; the December reference case is untouched and still reproduces exactly (December suite green in the harness). VERIFICATION: new tax-suite fixture blank-yield-fallback pins the derivation on the audit's own figures (the stored actuals over the fixture's constructed pool → the implied yields the derivation produces; blank record and $0 pool derive nulls; a partial record derives the dividend side only), the resolution rules (fallback stands in, entered wins, explicit 0 wins, no-transient stays null), and a Do Nothing march on that pool (2026 dividend and interest pricing back to the filed dollars to the cent — the audit's worked figures; 2028 AGI positive and exactly that year's dividend + interest, where it priced $0 before; legacy and explicit-zero marches price $0). LIVE (sandbox copy of the saved plan, via the app's actions): the record holds blank yields and the 2025 actuals; runPlanYearDetail for 2026 prices dividend and interest at the filed dollars within rounding, with MAGI the combined yield income (was $0) — the implied yields over the server-resolved Taxable+Cash pool pricing the stored actuals in year 1 within rounding — and 2028 prices that year's grown dividend and interest (a full year of yield income inside the plan's cliff-capped year, was $0/$0). The audit's figure for that year is its own reconstruction's (Do Nothing, pool = the Taxable bucket alone, no other flows); the fixture reproduces that reconstruction's figures exactly on its stated terms, and each live surface derives over the pool its own march prices on, so year-1 priced income equals the household's actual income on every surface. GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean (server + client); packaged harness exit 0 — tax census fully green across all 6 chunks with teeth ok (including the new fixture; census total is self-derived), extended / retirement / December / Roth CAS / retirement CAS / UI-state suites and data-integrity all green, seeded example figures unchanged. CONTRACT VERSION: 135 → 136 (TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS amendment only; no request or response shape changed). CONSEQUENCE, recorded plainly: this changes priced AGI, MAGI, ACA credit, and tax in every blank-yield plan year, so the 5% anchors are stale again and will need re-deriving after this and the other pricing fixes land — NOT done in this build, per the brief. The saved spending and every stored return figure were not touched; nothing was committed or pushed.

## Build v135 (2026-11-01): The march funds the ACA premium its own credit pricing implies (fresh-round finding 1)

All user-entered data, no external source. Engine change in the Roth plan march (server/src/taxEngine.ts) plus record-layer derivation (server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) and contract surfacing (server/src/actions.ts, server/src/apiContractCore.ts). The saved spending is NOT changed — the annual figure on the record stays exactly as saved; the fix is the funding mechanism, not any dollar figure. THE DEFECT (settlement, fresh-round finding 1, STANDS): the march fixed each year's spending need at annualSpending, then priced the ACA credit afterward without adjusting spending or balances. Because annualSpending embeds a net ACA premium (the plan's spending was built assuming a particular credit), the march kept funding the same total when its own pricing reduced or eliminated that credit — in the settlement's worked example an over-cliff year needed the spending with the full benchmark premium in place of the embedded net premium — a whole credit more than the march funded, so that much cash outflow was omitted; the buffered plan also underfunded the 2038–2046 spouse-only years and overfunded 2036–2037. THE MECHANISM: (1) A new optional engine input, RothPlanInputs.acaEmbeddedNetPremium (dollars), names the annual net ACA premium already inside annualSpending, separating non-healthcare spending (annualSpending − embedded) from the premium. Absent or null = legacy: the march funds annualSpending verbatim and every figure is bit-identical to before. (2) Inside settlement, each year's effective spending need is reconciled: need − embedded + max(0, benchmark − credit), where the credit is the one the settlement itself prices for that year. The reconciliation runs as a fixed-point driver around the existing settlement (settleYear → settleYearOnce plus a driver): round 1 assumes the credit that makes the funded need exactly the base need (benchmark − embedded, clamped), each later round re-settles with the credit the previous settlement actually priced, up to 8 passes, cycle-safe; an exact fixed point returns as settled, otherwise the closest settlement is kept and the year reports settlementConverged: false. All existing settlement call sites (ceiling convergence, bisections, draw-cap and cash-growth searches) route through the driver unchanged. (3) DERIVATION: acaEmbeddedNetPremiumFor(inputs) derives the embedded premium once, as a property of the plan and never of a strategy: the net premium of the plan's first ACA-active year with a benchmark entered, priced at that year's cliff (400% FPL) — benchmark − credit at MAGI = cliff. planInputsFromSaved derives and sets it for every saved plan, so the optimizer, compare, funding, plan-year detail, Monte Carlo, gift, and work-years paths all reconcile against the same amount; it is derived, never stored, and never a saved field. For the settlement reconstruction shape it derives $15,410.11 (9.96% × the $154,720 cliff), vs the settlement's $14,912.11 buffered-MAGI figure — the brief directs mechanism over specific dollars. (4) SURFACING: RothYearDetail gains acaPremiumEmbedded, acaPremiumNet (benchmark − the kept settlement's assumed credit), and acaPremiumAdjustment (net − embedded, signed; $0 whenever the reconciliation does not engage); funding.spending carries the effective need and the funding identity (sources + spendShortfall + unpaidTax = needs) is unchanged. The plan-year detail action returns the three new fields. The settlementMismatchCents shape was deliberately NOT extended (stays {gains, pretax}); credit non-convergence is reported through settlementConverged: false only — a known, recorded surfacing gap. (5) SCORE: netCostBreakdown is unchanged — it still subtracts lifetimeAcaKept. The credit's cash effect now flows through ending balances and lifetime tax; the score does not read ending taxable/Roth balances, so the −credit term remains the score's only representation of the credit and there is no double count within the score. HARVEST NOTE: the reported credit (acaCreditKept) is still priced after any gain harvest, while the funded premium uses the settlement's own priced credit, so a harvested year's funded premium can differ from the reported post-harvest credit by the harvest's credit effect alone. VERIFICATION (scratch engine runs against the settlement reconstruction, before the suites): derivation returns $15,410.11 exactly; the buffered 2028 year reconciles to an adjustment of −$1.99 (the reconstruction's MAGI lands $20 under the settlement's, moving its credit by $1.99); a true over-cliff family year (MAGI $200,000 past the $154,720 cliff, credit $0) funds the spending with the full benchmark premium in place of the embedded net premium, with an adjustment of exactly the credit; the buffered plan's 2038–2046 spouse-only years each adjust by exactly the difference between the spouse-only net premium and the embedded premium, matching the settlement to the cent; the funding identity foots on all 39 years; every reconciled year reports settlementConverged true; and compare and funding agree on ending balances to the cent. Two new tax-suite fixtures pin the mechanism (tax-aca-premium-reconciliation-pair, tax-aca-premium-reconciliation-derivation), including the legacy bit-identity with the field absent. GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean (server + client). Tax census 522/522: the packaged harness ran chunks 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 at 87/87 each with teeth ok, and chunk 2 — OOM-killed (exit 137) inside the harness process on this machine, the standing S-2 limitation — was verified piecewise from the same fixture module in smaller groups, all 87 accounted for. RE-PINS: 40 existing fixtures moved solely because the reconciliation now engages on their saved shapes (the sample/anchor plans and the work-years goldens all carry marketplace benchmarks): every one was attribution-checked by re-running it against a tree copy with only the derivation disabled — all 40 pass there on otherwise-identical code — and every identity property they pin (absent == null == at-65, pool == tier, blank == zero, dial == direct, zero sleeve == blank) still holds at the new values; each carries a "(Re-pinned under build v135 …)" sentence in its note. The Monte Carlo production fixture's winner is unchanged (win count 221 → 222 of 250 on the pinned seed, median advantage $1,174,980.76 → $1,175,040.43). Packaged harness 349/349 checks with data-integrity at zero violations: extended 159/159, retirement 63/63, Roth CAS 15/15, retirement CAS 16/16, UI-state 19/19, extended and retirement teeth green, contract version 135 confirmed, and the seeded example figures (C14–C21) unchanged. CONTRACT VERSION: 134 → 135 — describeApi gains the ACA_PREMIUM_RECONCILIATION_SEMANTICS convention (response key acaPremiumReconciliationSemantics) and the plan-year detail response gains the three premium fields. CONSEQUENCE, recorded plainly: the march now re-prices the saved plan, so ending balances and the 5% anchors derived at contract 133/134 are stale; re-deriving them is a separate step, not part of this build. The saved spending was not touched.
