## Build v150 (2026-11-01): Playground income dials are year-aware and provenance-tracked; the Form 1040 line leaves the dial labels

All user-entered data, no external source. No engine change and no priced-figure change for any fixed set of dials; the build changes which figure a dial HOLDS when the Tax year changes, and what its label and hint claim. Follow-on to v147, which fixed the prefill's resolution and the hints' year label but not the value path: the three income dials (Interest, Ordinary dividends, Qualified dividends) were remembered, provenance-free values, so the stored 2025 return figures sat in the dials while pricing 2026, under a hint statically claiming they were the return's — the user caught the Qualified dividends dial showing the return's qualified figure as the 2026 estimate. Four parts. (1) PROVENANCE: each income dial now remembers where its current figure came from — a new incomeSources record on the remembered Playground form (the stored return, with its year or null when the record never named one; the saved plan's priced figure for a year; or the user's own typed/pasted value), persisted in the UI-state blob beside benchmarkSource, read leniently so a blob written before it existed parses all three null. Every loader records it: "Start from my numbers" records its resolution's source, the "as filed" preset records the return for the lines it loads, "a year from my saved plan" records the plan year it loads, a paste records "typed", Reset and "Blank year" clear it, and typing in a dial marks that dial "typed" (moneyField's onEdit, which fires only on a real keystroke — never on the blur reformat or a programmatic set). (2) RE-DERIVATION: the prefill's year resolution is extracted into ONE helper (resolvePgIncomeForYear — the return year's own actuals when the chosen year is the return year, else the plan's priced figure for that year when the plan prices it, else the return figures carried forward), and a new effect re-derives every return- or plan-sourced dial through it whenever the Tax year changes or the plan data it reads lands or changes. A typed figure is NEVER overwritten. A dial with no recorded provenance whose value still equals the stored return figure is treated as that return figure (a prefill or the "as filed" preset is how such a value got there), so the remembered form this build inherits re-derives on first open and records the provenance as it goes. The "as filed" preset's partial-load contract is preserved: it loads only the lines the record holds, and a one-shot guard keeps the effect from re-deriving over that load when the preset itself changes the year. (3) LABELS AND HINTS: the labels drop their Form 1040 line suffixes — "Ordinary dividends — total" and "Qualified dividends" (Interest never had one) — because the suffix anchored the field to the filed return when its value is the estimate at the time; the line reference now lives in each dial's hint and info note as a source statement. Hints and info notes are built from the dial's recorded provenance and the year being priced: the return year's own figure reads "From your 2025 return, line 3a — that year's actual."; a plan figure reads "Estimate for 2026 from your saved plan — its priced dividends for that year, from its yield fields."; a carried figure says it is carried from the return because the plan does not price that year and is not that year's figure; a typed figure makes no source claim (only its structural note: the qualified dial's part-of-the-total note, the ordinary dial's counted-once note). The income-stack legend taps follow the new labels (their field ids are label-derived: roth-Ordinary-dividends-total, roth-Qualified-dividends). (4) TAX PLAN NOTE: the note under the three Form 1040 lines in the Tax Plan no longer says the Playground simply "fills its Interest and Dividends fields from them" — it now says they are the Playground's figures for the return year itself (and its "as filed" preset), that other years estimate from the plan's yields, and that the figures carry forward only for a year the plan does not price. The fields themselves stay on the record and in the Tax Plan view in this build: they anchor the year-aware logic and the "as filed" preset (the user separately authorized moving them out of the Tax Plan view into the Playground as a follow-up, queued after this fix). CONTRACT VERSION: 133 → 134 — the remembered-form schema gains the incomeSources record on getRothUiState's response and setRothUiState's request (additive and leniently read, by the same rule as v147's bump); TAX_RETURN_SEMANTICS gains the dial-provenance sentences and the api-tax-return-semantics-content fixture pins them (12 → 16 phrases). GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean; the staged audit passed with no console errors and no finding on the fix (its content review confirmed the mechanism at source level; standing advisories unchanged — the earlier-build review backlog and the pre-existing phone-width sideways scroll in the Spending Quick view, both outside this fix); the extended suite 159/159 and the UI-state suite 19/19 green on the sandbox (the tax suite invocation timed out at the transport limit — no pricing or tax-return-core code changed in this build, and the tax-return content fixture lives in the extended suite). RENDERED CHECK (live probe pass over the staged build, phone viewport, against a sandbox copy of the live data): the Playground opened at 2026 on the remembered form holding the 2025 return figures with no provenance; on open the dials re-derived to the plan's priced 2026 figures (Interest $0, Ordinary dividends $0, Qualified dividends $0 — the plan prices no yield income in its 2026 year, the same figures "Start from my numbers" loads for 2026) with the Qualified dial reading "Qualified dividends" (no line suffix) and the hint "Estimate for 2026 from your saved plan — its priced dividends for that year, from its yield fields."; changing the Tax year to 2025 re-derived the return's actuals with hints "From your 2025 return, line 2b / 3b — that year's actual."; typing $7,777 into Qualified dividends dropped its source claim to the structural note alone, and changing the year back to 2026 re-derived Interest and Ordinary dividends to the plan figures while the typed $7,777 stood; the income-stack legend's Qualified dividends tap still lands on the dial under its new id. All probe edits stayed in the sandbox; the live record and the live remembered form were never written by this verification (the user's live form still holds its figures until he next opens the Playground, when the re-derivation runs there).

## Build v149 (2026-11-01): Tax Plan autosave can no longer strand or silently drop a queued save, and it shows its status

All user-entered data, no external source. Client save wiring only — no action changed, no engine change, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged. Follow-on to v148: after that fix the record still held the previous spending minutes after the user typed the new one in the Tax Plan (the value did land, ~3 minutes late; an earlier attempt may have been dropped entirely). Inspection of the autosave found the delay mechanism: the settled-value gate (build v131) holds a save while an editable field has focus, and three paths could strand the queued save with nothing re-firing it and no status anywhere saying it had not landed. (1) The debounce timer firing into the gate simply returned — the save sat queued until a blur happened to flush it. It now re-arms on a short retry timer: while an editable field genuinely still holds focus (checked against the document's active element) the gate keeps holding, and the moment focus has actually left every editable field — including cases where no blur reaches the root div, such as the focused element being unmounted by a re-render — the retry fires. (2) A blur from a field to a button inside the view cancelled the pending timer outright and kept the gate closed, stranding the save until focus left the whole view. Focus leaving a field for a button means the value is settled, so the blur now re-arms the debounce instead; the discard flows that motivated the old cancel (Back to saved, Reset balances, Reset plan) cancel the timer when their confirm prompt opens — so a save cannot land while the user decides — and their Cancel buttons re-arm it, while their execute paths drop the pending payload exactly as before. (3) The unmount cleanup flushed a pending save only when no field held focus, so an edit whose field still had focus when the view closed was silently dropped. Leaving the view is now the settle: the cleanup flushes the pending payload focused or not (discard flows and the conflict path clear the payload before unmount, so a discarded edit still never lands). SAVE STATUS: the view now shows the autosave's status beside the changed-fields line at the top, on every face — the autosave effect sets "Saving…" when an edit queues a save, a successful save sets "Saved", a conflict clears it (the conflict notice explains), and a failed save reads "Could not save — your entries stay on this screen."; the All settings face's existing status line reads the same note first. The v148 cache invalidation rides along in the same diff (it was live but uncommitted). GATES: `bun run typecheck` clean; the staged audit passed with no console errors and no finding on the fix (its content review read the diff and settled all three parts; standing advisories unchanged — the earlier-build review backlog and the pre-existing phone-width sideways scroll in the Spending Quick view, both outside this fix). RENDERED CHECK (live probe pass over the staged build, phone viewport, against a sandbox copy of the live data): the Tax Plan opened at the saved spending with the new status reading "Saved"; the Yearly spending field was edited to a higher test value and focus moved to the per month toggle button — the exact pre-fix stranding path — the status read "Saving…", then flipped to "Saved" with "Every field matches the saved plan.", and the Playground's top strip showed "Left after a year's spending" at the corresponding negative figure (cash left after tax minus the edited spending); with a second, higher edit, opening Back to saved held the save for over 3 seconds (the confirm still read "nothing is written"), and cancelling the confirm re-armed it and the edit landed ("Saved", fields matching); the sandbox record was restored to the saved value the same way. All probe edits stayed in the sandbox; the live record was never written by this verification (it holds the user's confirmed spending).

## Build v148 (2026-11-01): Tax Plan autosave invalidates the shared plan-record cache, so its edits reach the Playground

All user-entered data, no external source. Client cache wiring only — no action changed, no engine change, no stored value changed by the build itself, so the API contract version is unchanged. ## Build v147 (2026-11-01): Playground dividend dials carry the return year; the current year defaults from the plan's priced year

All user-entered data, no external source. The Playground's three Form 1040 income dials (taxable interest, qualified dividends, ordinary dividends total) showed the most recent filed return's actuals with no year label, and the Playground reused that flat prior-year figure as the dial for the year being priced — so the current year always looked to the previous year. The amounts themselves were correct (the qualified part plus the non-qualified remainder foot to the total) and no stored amount changes in this build. Four parts. (1) The Tax Plan record now stores the return year alongside the three amounts (a new nullable field on the tax-return block, null on records written before it existed — year not recorded; the year is a fact about the amounts, so it is stored with them, never derived from today's date, which would drift every year while the amounts stay put). The Tax Plan view gains a Tax return year field in the Taxes & ACA section, saved with the record like the three amounts, and its note under the three lines names the return year when one is recorded. (2) Each of the three Playground dials shows the return year in its hint and in its info note — the stored return year when the record names one, else "your most recent return" with no year asserted — worded as last year's actual, to update after filing. The label choice follows the inspection's return-year wording rather than the "est. at the time" label suggested earlier, since it names the year. (3) "Start from my numbers" now resolves the three dials for the chosen tax year: when the chosen year is the return year itself, the stored figures load as that year's actuals; otherwise, when the saved plan prices the chosen year, its priced interest and dividends for that year load instead (the yield-based estimate — the same figures "a year from my saved plan" loads, with the plan's dividend income as both the total and the qualified part); when the plan does not price the chosen year, the return figures load as the best available estimate. Every dial stays editable and the stored return figures remain available; only the default changes, never the pricing — the plan's own pricing is untouched (it already models dividends from yields). (4) The "as filed" preset is renamed for the return year it loads and now loads into the return year itself, never the current year — a return for the current year cannot have been filed yet. When the record predates the year field, the preset's name and target year use the last filed year as the best guess, and the dial hints say "your most recent return" until a year is entered. # Data Plan

## Build v137 (2026-11-01): December round-17 defects — harvest from the remaining pool, year-change re-resolution, per-field saves

All user-entered data, no external source. Three settled December-console defects, built in the order that avoids building new inputs on the buggy behavior — per-field saves first, then the year-change re-resolution, then the remaining-pool harvest. (1) The gain harvest sized from the starting taxable pool instead of the pool left after the year's sales: the plan march harvests after the year's draws and conversions have settled, capped by the remaining balance's unrealized gain, so the December harvest now derives the remaining pool and basis from the starting facts less the year's priced taxable sale (proceeds and basis) and the 100%-basis taxable cash — the remaining unrealized gain is exact whether or not the sale basis was entered, because the sale's proceeds less its basis is the year's net gain in every branch, and 100%-basis cash sells pool and basis equally so it does not shrink the harvestable gain. A depleted pool prices a $0 harvest as a fact, never as unpriced. The console copy and the action's purpose text now name the remaining pool. (2) Changing the tax year never re-resolved the year-dependent overlays, so a carry-in resolved for the old year kept pricing a year the gate no longer covers and the old year's education students kept pricing the new year: the year-dependent overlays (education students and the entering capital-loss carryforward) are now extracted into one shared helper used by both load resolution and year-change re-resolution, and the tax-year field re-resolves them for the new year — unedited fields reset to their stored values and re-apply the new year's resolution, edited fields are never touched, and year-independent overlays (beneficiary, balance split, harvest pool facts) are left alone so a deliberately cleared fact is never revived. When the Tax Plan record has not loaded there is no overlay to re-resolve — an overlay can only exist after a hydration that had the record — so the year changes alone. (3) The four carry-in fields shared one edited flag and the two harvest facts shared one, so editing one field permanently saved its untouched siblings as explicit console answers: each of the four carry-in fields and each of the two harvest facts now carries its own edited flag, in the save derivation and in the console's provenance state, so editing one field saves only that field — the grouped flags are gone from every call site. New fixtures pin the corrected behavior for each defect: the remaining-pool harvest (entered sale basis, gain-only sale, depleted pool, 100%-basis taxable funding), the year-change re-resolution (before the plan's first year, a later year, an edited field surviving the change, a cleared harvest fact not revived), and the per-field saves (each carry-in field and each harvest fact alone). No action changed, so the API contract version is unchanged. ## Build v135 (2026-11-01): ChatGPT engines findings batch — saved-plan-year loader, tax-basis survival, split-balance RMD, education-credit net tax, funding readout, tax-exempt funding, Playground credit

All user-entered data, no external source. Seven settled engine findings, built in ranked order — the fixes move priced figures where the old behavior was wrong, and every census pin that moved was re-derived independently and re-pinned with the re-pin recorded in the case's note. (1) The Playground's saved-plan-year loader set the pre-tax money-out dial to the conversion alone and cleared both stock-sale inputs, dropping the extra pre-tax draw that funds spending and the taxable sales that funded spending and taxes, so a loaded year priced no tax at all; the loader now carries the full pre-tax money out (conversion plus the extra draw) and the taxable sales with their basis, and the preset note names the full amount. (2) The plan march clamped the taxable basis down to the market value on a down year, so a recovery then priced a fictitious gain on the next sale; the basis now survives a decline on both the tiered and single-pool paths, floored at zero, and the old basis-within-balance invariant is retired in favor of a non-negative basis invariant. (3) The Playground loader put the combined prior pre-tax balance into one dial and the adapter never supplied the spouse's balance, so the spouse's share was priced on the primary's RMD clock; the loader and adapter now carry the split balances (a new spouse dial beside the primary's, with the saved form, paste payload, projection, and Net Worth prefill all carrying it), the pricer prices each owner's RMD on their own clock, and the spouse dial is gated to married-filing-jointly so a stale spouse balance cannot inflate the cap on a single filing. ## Build v133 (2026-11-01): Retirement view sources its shared plan fields from the Tax Plan record, with taps back to the Tax Plan

The Retirement view no longer keeps its own copies of the five plan fields it shares with the Tax Plan view — annual spending, current age, retirement age, plan end age, and expected return. It reads all five from the Tax Plan record (the single source of truth) and shows them as read-only taps: each value carries a dotted underline and a note naming the Tax Plan as its source, and tapping it switches to the Tax Plan view and jumps to the field it came from (spending, retirement age, and end age in the household section; the birth year for current age, also in the household section; expected return in the Advanced section), opening the section and flashing the field, using the same tap-and-jump mechanism the provenance taps use. The cross-view jump is new: the top-level view holds the jump target (field, section, and a nonce so each tap fires once) and hands it to the Tax Plan view, which jumps once its saved record and its UI state have both loaded. The Retirement record's own stored copies of the five fields are vestigial — still written so the record stays in sync, but ignored on load; nothing is deleted. The other Retirement inputs (portfolio, stocks mix, volatility, spending strategy, guardrails, extra income) are untouched. Reset to defaults does not reset the five sourced fields (they are not Retirement defaults; the reset carries the Tax Plan values through unchanged), and the "Calculated with" defaults comparison no longer lists them as diffs (they ARE the plan values). Loading a saved scenario applies only its Retirement-owned inputs — the five plan fields stay where the Tax Plan has them, so a scenario's compare figures still price with the scenario's stored five fields (independent snapshots) even though loading it does not apply them. The spending per-year/per-month toggle stays as a display-only switch, the "Use trailing" control is gone (the trailing True-cost figure is now shown only for reference in the spending explainer), and changing the stocks mix now follows the blended default for volatility only — expected return no longer follows the blend. No priced figure or engine logic changes; the Tax Plan record is unchanged by this build, and no action changed, so the API contract version is unchanged. Two placement lessons from this build, both found by rendered checks: (1) a hook placed after the Tax Plan view's loading/error early returns does not run on the loading render but does once the plan lands, a hook-count mismatch that crashed the view — the jump effect now sits above those early returns; (2) the jump effect must also run after the UI-state init effect, which overwrites the section-open state from the server — a jump that opened a closed-by-default section before that effect ran was undone, so the effect is declared immediately after it and waits for both the plan and the UI state. ## Build v131 (2026-10-31): Tax Plan autosave settled-value gate

All user-entered data, no external source. One user-approved fix, guard-only — no priced figure changes anywhere in this build, and no engine file is touched. The Tax Plan view's debounced whole-form autosave persisted intermediate keystroke states: it fired 700 ms after the last change with no blur or settled-value gate, so a half-typed number that sat untouched for 700 ms was saved as-is (a half-typed spending entry was saved as a tiny yearly amount, and the saved record had to be restored). The autosave now only persists settled values: the view tracks whether an editable field (input, select, or textarea) currently has focus, and a save that comes due while one does is deferred — the pending payload stays queued and is flushed only once focus leaves the view and the value is settled, or an editable field regains focus and its value settles (which schedules its own save). Moving focus to a non-editable element inside the view (a button) does not flush and cancels the pending timer: the button may discard the edit (Back to saved) or change another value (which schedules its own save), so the pending save stays queued without a live timer. Independent verification found a hole in the first version of this gate: the blur handler did not flush on the move to a button but left the timer live, so the timer fired once focus sat on the button and saved the half-typed value; and clicking Back to saved swaps the focused button for its confirm prompt, whose removal fires a blur with no related target that the old handler treated as leaving the view. Both are fixed: the move to an in-view button now cancels the timer and keeps the gate closed, and a blur whose target is no longer in the document does not flush. The unmount path only flushes a pending save when the form is settled; an unsettled pending save is dropped rather than persisted, keeping the last good saved record. The autosave stays automatic (no Save button, no confirmation dialogs), the save payload shape and the save action contract are unchanged, and the gate covers the whole form (all fields), not one field. Also server/src/actions.ts: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 130 → 131. GATES: three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff (including one fix found and applied during review: the blur handler first flushed on any move to a non-editable element inside the view, which would have flushed a half-typed pending save when the user clicked Back to saved to discard it — the handler now only flushes once focus leaves the view, and a new rendered check covers that path); `bun run typecheck` clean; the tax census totalling 513/513 with a teeth check passing on every slice (the chunks run in parallel batches of six with a sequential fallback for any chunk that fails — chunks 8 and 10 failed under concurrency and chunk 8 passed on sequential retry while chunk 10 passed on a single-chunk alone retry after memory freed); the extended (159/159), December (78/78), UI-state (19/19), Roth CAS (15/15), retirement CAS (16/16), and retirement (63/63) suites green; extended and retirement teeth green; the packaged harness green at 349/349 checks with data-integrity at zero violations; and the stored-record anchors — a direct compare run was not possible from this seat (the stored record is encrypted under the install key held by the platform runtime, and no backup file was available to restore into a scratch copy), so the anchors rest on input-invariance instead: no engine file changed, no save path, schema, or migration was touched, the only changes are the client autosave gating and the contract bump, the guards only defer writes whose value is unsettled and otherwise save exactly what they saved before, and every existing figure is computed identically, so no stored figure moves; the packaged harness's seeded Roth example still prices to its pinned figures, confirming the plan march did not move. ## Build v130 (2026-10-31): Restore-epoch guards on the import path and the view-state setters (round-19 findings 7, 8, 10)

All user-entered data, no external source. Three settled round-19 findings, all guard-only — no priced figure changes anywhere in this build, and no engine file is touched. (F7) `importTransactions` had no restore-epoch guard: a backup restore between the import preview and the confirm could land rows the preview had already cleared as duplicates, because the only dedupe lived in the preview and the batch key cannot catch a restore that never used the key. The action now takes the optional `baseEpoch` the preview observed (the import read's restore epoch, carried by the client from the preview) and refuses the whole batch with the shared restore message before any planning or write, inserting zero rows. Omitting it keeps the previous unchecked behaviour. (F8) `saveImportSettings` and `saveNwImportSettings` were blind whole-blob upserts, and the spending side fires one automatically on every Preview from the panel-open blob, so a panel opened before a restore could auto-save its pre-restore setup over the restored one and silently drop profiles. Both now take the optional `baseEpoch` the panel observed when it loaded its setup (the settings read's restore epoch, which the Net Worth read now also publishes, matching the spending read) and return the conflict shape when a restore has advanced the stored epoch since the load; the panel surfaces the reason as its notice and the import itself is unaffected. (F10) The seven view-state setters — the four Spending collapse-all flags, the Net Worth Accounts and History collapsed flags, and the Net Worth Growth baseline date — were blind upserts with no epoch guard, so a stale tab could silently overwrite a newer pick. All seven now take the optional `baseEpoch` from the view's load and return the conflict shape on a stale write; the client shows the reason in the view's own message line. The Retirement assumptions collapsed setter is not in this batch — it is a separate view-state setter outside finding 10 and stays untouched. Also server/src/actions.ts: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 129 → 130. ## Build v127 (2026-10-31): Round-19 December figures — per-owner split, RMD cash-in, carry-in across years, sale proceeds, compare/funding naming

All user-entered data, no external source. Five settled round-19 findings, all reproduced to the cent before the build. Four correct wrong December figures; one renames a shared field. The December console's per-owner pre-tax split no longer double-counts the spouse's share: when the Tax Plan record's primary balance follows the Net Worth snapshot and the spouse's amount is explicit, the primary is the snapshot's total minus the spouse's amount — the same resolution the plan march applies — in both places the console reads the record's primary (the load-resolution facts and the first-open preseed), via one shared helper the fixtures pin. A stored console whose saved total is allocated by the record's proportions now allocates by the corrected proportions, and a new mismatch note names both totals when this console prices its own explicit split that disagrees with the record's (the two existing notes cover the non-explicit cases). Cash-in no longer counts an RMD already received twice: the received part sits inside other ordinary income and the priced net RMD is the part still to come, so the two together count the gross RMD exactly once — the extra term is removed from the shared single-year engine's cash-in, which the Playground and the December console both read. Cash-in now includes the full proceeds of a stock sale, not just the gain: the console collects the cost basis of the sales behind the year's gains as a new nullable field beside the realized-gain field (blank vs zero distinct; a blob written before it existed parses null and prices exactly as before), and the engine gets the proceeds with the basis beside it, so it nets the same gain for tax while cash-in counts the proceeds — a loss sale still brings its proceeds in, and without an entered basis the old gain-only mapping stands with the field's hint saying cash left counts only the gains. The record's entering capital-loss carryforward now applies when the December year is the plan's first year or any later one: the plan march applies it at its first year unconditionally, so a record saved in a prior year still carries its loss into the current year's December pricing; it still does not apply to a year before the plan's first year, and the separate tax-year-change retention defect is untouched. The compare run's per-year pre-tax field is renamed to state what it is — the year's pre-tax money out by choice (its conversion plus its pre-tax draw for spending) — so it can no longer be confused with the funding run's field of the same old name, which is the extra spending draw plus pre-tax amounts applied to the tax bill and excludes the conversion; both API purpose texts now name the other field, and the only client consumer (the first-draw-year detector) follows the rename. No priced figure moves except where the findings bite, and that movement is the point: a per-owner split now sums to the snapshot, cash left is no longer overstated by a received RMD or understated by a sale basis, and a prior-year carry-in now prices — while the plan-march anchors (ending wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit) are unchanged, because the march is priced by the compare path, not the December console; the shared cash-in change touches only the single-year readouts, and the census and harness confirm the march did not move. Five new December fixtures pin the fixes (the snapshot-followed primary helper and the corrected allocation, the received-RMD cash-in, the prior-year carry-in with its tax delta, the sale proceeds with a loss-sale control, and the basis field's save round trip), and the existing carryforward-resolution fixture is updated to the widened gate (a later year resolves; a year before the plan's first year does not). ## Build v125 (2026-10-31): Taxable cash for the year in the December console, Washington excise tap retarget

All user-entered data, no external source. One new console input plus one tap retarget — no engine change. The December console gains a taxable-cash input: cash taken from taxable at 100% basis for the year, the operating model's tax-from-taxable money. Sizing rule, settled against the console solver: the amount is additional cash ON TOP of the pre-tax draw, not part of it. The solver sizes the pre-tax draw by MAGI room — it varies only the conversion and reads only ACA MAGI — and a 100%-basis amount adds no MAGI, so it uses no room and the solved draw is invariant to it. The harvest precedent is the same rule in the other direction: a gain shrinks the draw by the harvested gain because it adds MAGI; a zero-MAGI item moves the draw by zero. So the pre-tax draw, MAGI, ACA credit, federal tax, total tax, and settlement are unchanged by the input, and cash-in and cash-left rise dollar for dollar with it, in every case. The headline invariant is preserved — the draw still lands MAGI at cliff minus buffer — and the operating model is preserved too: the draw funds next year, the taxable cash pays the tax bill. The input is a plain typed field (a nullable money field, blank vs zero distinct), a plain console answer with no Tax Plan record resolution and no provenance flag, so it saves as displayed with no edited flag; a blob written before it existed parses it as null and prices exactly as before. The console shows it in its own section beside the gain-harvest section, with a line naming its effect on cash left when an amount is entered, and the projected-bill card gains a taxable-cash row (shown when the amount is positive) that taps to the input — the provenance tap on the new figure. The Washington capital-gains excise row on the Playground Tax-for-the-year card is retargeted to the stock-sale input with the same label as the federal gains figure (a user pick: the excise is gains-driven like the federal gains figure, so it lands on the input that drives it). No priced figure changes anywhere in this build — the taxable input moves only cash-in and cash-left by the entered amount, and the retarget is wiring only. Four new December fixtures pin the input: the acceptance (draw, MAGI, credit, tax, and settlement unchanged, cash-in and cash-left up by the entered amount, in every case), the zero identity (explicit zero prices bit-identically to no input), the null settlement contract (cash-in and cash-left stay null when no settlement is shown), and the save round trip (serialize/parse, legacy blob, writer schema, and the plain-answer save rule). Also server/src/actions.ts: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 124 → 125; the December state gains the taxable-cash field and the case assembly adds it to cash-in and cash-left. RENDERED CHECK (live pass over the packaged build in a headless browser, desktop and phone widths): the input renders, persists across a reload, and re-prices cash left by the entered amount with the draw, MAGI, credit, tax, and settlement unchanged; the zero case matches the no-input case; the excise figure lands on the stock-sale input with the outline plus tint for the full three seconds — with the normal cases unchanged, and a fresh edit still saves and deletes cleanly. ## Build v121 (2026-10-31): Restore-epoch guard generalised to the spending editors, deletes, and settings writers

All user-entered data, no external source. Guard only — no priced figure changes, no input changes, and no engine change. The restore-generation guard that previously covered only the two Net Worth snapshot editors now covers every stale-value-sensitive mutation: the spending editors (transactions, yearly expenses and their versions, monthly bills and their versions, cash-out items, month totals, one-off expenses, and the reserve settings), the snapshot delete, and the other unguarded deletes and settings writers (account rename/archive/delete, the property-include toggle, the Net Worth target, and the Retirement spending-unit preference). Each now accepts an optional base epoch — the restore generation the view observed when it loaded — and refuses the write with the same conflict shape the snapshot editors use when a backup restore has advanced the stored epoch since the load, naming the restore and the record, even when the stored value still equals the caller's base (a same-value restore is invisible to the value check alone). The check runs after the existence preflight and before any value check or write, so a refused write leaves the stored data untouched. The three reads that feed the editors now publish the current restore epoch alongside their data (the spending dashboard, the import panel's read, and the Retirement calculator read; the Net Worth read already did). The client freezes the epoch when each editor opens, alongside its existing value base, and passes it back on save; immediate row actions (deletes, category setters, keep-lights-on toggles, due-month) carry the epoch of the data on screen, and a refusal surfaces through the existing per-form or per-section error line instead of closing over the newer value. Pure creates (which append rather than overwrite), display fold state, seeds and wipes, backup management, the restore itself, import settings, and the revision-guarded blob saves (Roth, Retirement, December, scenarios) are unchanged and carry no epoch — the blob saves' same-generation question stays open, named here rather than built. Two new fixtures pin the guard's pure seam: the spending value-ABA (same stored value, moved epoch, refused as an epoch conflict) and the stale delete (pre-restore epoch refused, post-restore epoch allowed, a second restore refusing again). Also server/src/actions.ts: API_CONTRACT_VERSION 120 → 121; the two version-delete responses gain an optional conflict flag, and the three settings-style writes that previously answered with a bare success now answer with the shared success-or-reason shape so a refusal can be carried. ## Build v113 (2026-10-31): Round-17 December-parity fix F3 — the December console models the gain harvest, sized inside the single-year pricer by the plan march's own rule

All user-entered data, no external source. The one fix in this build (finding F3, MUST-FIX, from the settled round-17 December remaining-parity audit; the round's F1+F2 were built at v111 and its F4+F5 at v112 — neither is touched). THE DEFECT: the plan march harvests gains after settlement when its gains-harvest toggle is on (the harvestOn gate in server/src/taxEngine.ts) and reprices tax and ACA on the harvested gain, but the December console had no harvest or basis input at all, so a harvest-on year was priced as if no harvest happened. On the settlement's example (2026 MFJ, ages 60/58, $65,000 ordinary income, $40,000 taxable assets at 75% basis, zero spending, $20,000 benchmark, $10,000 APTC) December priced MAGI $65,000, credit $13,526, tax $3,440, an $86 refund, where the plan prices MAGI $75,000, credit $12,530, the same $3,440 tax, and $910 payable: the $10,000 harvested gain inside the 0% band raises MAGI and costs $996 of credit (9.96% × $10,000) with no federal tax change. THE RULING: model the harvest from the saved plan's taxable-basis facts — do not qualify it as excluded. THE MARCH'S OWN RULE, read from its code before building: (a) the harvest draws on the combined taxable pool the plan assembles (the Taxable bucket plus the Cash bucket — the pool resolvePlanBalances produces), and its available gain is that pool less its basis dollars; the march walks basis tiers only for its year-to-year basis step-up bookkeeping, never for sizing, so one blended basis % (basis dollars ÷ pool) carries the December sizing exactly; (b) harvested gains DO enter the loss-ledger netting — the march's ledger transform runs on the year's total of draws' realized gains plus any injected sale gain plus the harvested gain, so an entering carryforward absorbs harvested gains first; (c) harvested gains ride the long-term-gains stack through the year's pricing, so Washington's excise base (gross gains minus the Washington-attributable absorbed part) and the NIIT base treat them exactly as any long-term gain in the stack. THE FIX (the harvest is sized inside the shared single-year pricer — no December-side harvest math exists): (1) server/src/rothOptimizer.ts — pricePlaygroundYear's inputs gain two optional harvest facts (harvestPoolAmount, harvestPoolBasisPct; either absent = no harvest priced and every figure is the pre-v113 pricing term for term) and its result gains harvestedGain. When both facts are present, the pricer sizes the harvest by the march's own predicate: the largest gain, searched to the cent and capped by the pool's unrealized gain (pool less its basis dollars), whose addition to the year's gross gains leaves the gains priced at 15% and at 20% unchanged — every harvested dollar lands inside the 0% capital-gains band. Trial pricings inside the search read the same gains transform as the final pricing (the shared loss ledger when a carry-in is entered, the identity otherwise), so an entering carryforward absorbs the harvest first, and the year-end carry-out reconciliation runs on the year's gains including the harvested gain, the march's pattern. The march also caps its own search by the strategy's ceilings (a bracket top, an IRMAA tier cap, a custom MAGI cap, the ACA cliff cap); the single-year pricer carries no strategy ceilings — its one ceiling, the ACA cliff, is the cliff solver's own target — so the December harvest predicate is the 0%-band rule alone, stated here so the difference is a decision on record, not an oversight. DRAW-SIZING SEMANTICS (stated explicitly, per the settlement): because the harvest is sized inside every pricing, the cliff solver's trial pricings see it too, and the solved December draw is sized WITH the harvest included — when the cliff target binds and the harvest survives at the solved draw, the draw shrinks by the harvested gain; when the pool's room is the binding cap instead, the draw (ordinary income) crowds the harvest out first, and the maximum-draw solution is the one where the two together exactly fill the room to the target. (2) server/src/decemberCore.ts — the December state gains harvestOn (a plain boolean, default off; a blob written before the field existed parses it off) and the two nullable pool facts (null = no input yet; an entered $0 pool or 100% basis is a real fact that prices a $0 harvest). decemberCaseInputs passes the facts to the pricer only while the toggle is on, so toggle-off prices bit-identically to before. Load resolution follows the v103/v111 overlay discipline with one difference from the carry-in: the pool facts are balance facts, not entering-year balances, so a null console fact resolves from the Tax Plan record's taxable facts in ANY year (no first-year gate) — the record's entered taxable balance when it carries one, otherwise the snapshot-followed pool (Taxable + Cash less any exclude-from-plan amount, floored at $0), exactly the pool resolvePlanBalances assembles, with the basis as the record's tier blend (Σ share × basis ÷ Σ share) when it carries tiers, otherwise its entered basis %; a record with no basis % and no tiers does not answer. Entered console values, a $0 pool included, always win; the toggle itself never resolves. The save derivation gains an edited-harvest flag so an unedited console saves its STORED pool facts, never a load-resolved overlay (the toggle is not provenance — it always saves as displayed). Each case result gains the harvested gain at the headline draw and at a $0 draw. QUALIFICATION (the settlement's rule for unpriced components): exactly one component is qualified, and only in one circumstance — the toggle on with a pool or basis fact missing everywhere (no console entry and no record fact) prices NO harvest, and every case carries gainHarvestUnpriced, the headline bill carries the excludes-gain-harvesting note, and the projection's warnings name it, so the settlement is never presented as a silent $0 harvest. Everything else is priced: an entered $0 pool and an entered 100% basis are priced facts ($0 harvest, no qualification), and a harvest fully absorbed by an entering carryforward is priced (the gain is realized; the ledger nets it). (3) client/src/December.tsx — a "Gain harvest" section after the carryforward section: the toggle, the pool and blended-basis fields on the existing nullable converters (blank vs $0 stay distinct), first-open preseed from the record's facts (the toggle stays off — preseeded facts become stored provenance, the balances pattern), a missing-facts warning while the toggle is on, plain-words copy (selling taxable investments on purpose to realize gains inside the 0% band: no extra federal tax, but the gain counts as income — it raises MAGI, shrinks the ACA credit, and shrinks the safe draw because the draw is sized with the harvest included; an entering carryforward absorbs harvested gains first), a live readout naming the harvest at a $0 draw and at the headline draw, the headline bill's "Gain harvested into the 0% band" row when the headline harvest is positive, the excludes-harvest note on the bill and on every case card while unpriced, and the case cards' harvested-gain line when positive. (4) server/src/actions.ts — API_CONTRACT_VERSION 112 → 113, the three harvest fields join the December case response schema, and the December actions' descriptions gain the harvest sentences; no pricing handler changes. FIXTURES: six new December fixtures (suite 60 → 66): the F3 acceptance pair (harvest on prices MAGI $75,000 / credit $12,530 / tax $3,440 / $910 payable at a $0 draw, harvest off prices $65,000 / $13,526 / $3,440 / $86 refund, and the headline draw shrinks $14,600 → $4,600 with the cliff target binding); the harvest-off identity (entered-but-dormant facts price bit-identically, a legacy blob parses the fields at their inert defaults, an out-of-range basis % reads as no input); the no-facts qualification (figures identical to off, the qualification on every case, the warning present, a partial fact set still qualified, and an entered $0 pool / 100% basis priced with no qualification); the 0%-room-binding case (the room caps the harvest at $66,100, not the pool, and the year's own $60,000 of gains leave only $6,100 of room); the combined carryforward + harvest case (the $20,000 long-term carry-in absorbs the full $10,000 harvest — MAGI moves by the $3,000 allowance alone, carry-out $7,000 against the $17,000 no-harvest control); and the resolution / save rules (any-year resolution, entered $0 wins, the toggle never resolves, an unedited save persists stored values). ACCEPTANCE (execution-based, via artifact actions in the sandbox database — not code-reading alone; never against the user's entered data): the F3 example prices through the live projection action at contract 113 with headline draw $4,600 (harvest on) against $14,600 (off), non-draw MAGI $75,000, and the harvested gain $10,000 at both the $0 draw and the headline draw, with no unpriced qualification; the zero-draw credit / tax / settlement figures are pinned by the acceptance fixture through the same pricer. THE RETIREMENT-AGE PREMISE, verified by execution: a plan record with the default retirement age 57 and ages 60/58 in 2026 resolves through the plan's own input path and marches 2026 as a retirement year in ACA scope — harvest on it realizes $10,000 with MAGI $75,000, credit $12,530, federal tax $3,440, and harvest off MAGI $65,000, credit $13,526, tax $3,440 — the plan-side comparison in the settlement is well-founded, and the plan and the console now agree to the cent. RENDERED CHECK (the audit's live pass over the built console, on the sandbox copy of the stored console state): the Gain harvest section opens with the record's facts preseeded (the snapshot-followed pool and the tier-blended basis), the headline at its stored baseline ; switching the harvest on repriced the console live — every case's MAGI before any draw rose by the $112,726 zero-draw harvest the section's readout names, the federal tax unchanged (the harvest sits in the 0% band), and the headline draw holding at the maximum-draw solution where the draw crowds the harvest to $0, exactly the draw-sizing semantics above; switching it off restored the baseline figures and the stored state exactly. GATES: three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff; the tax census in fine slices totalling 513/513 with a teeth check passing on every slice (the packaged runner's coarser 86-fixture chunk 2 was OOM-killed at exit 137 — the standing S-2 limitation — and its whole range passed in the finer slices; the runner's other five chunks passed their 427); the extended (140/140), December (66/66, including the six new fixtures, every earlier figure unmoved), UI-state (19/19), Roth CAS (15/15), retirement CAS (16/16), and retirement (63/63, both Trinity mixes within tolerance) suites green; the packaged harness green at 349/349 checks with data-integrity at zero violations; and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending after-tax wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit), confirming the plan march did not move (the pricer change is reachable only when a caller supplies the new harvest facts, which no plan path does; the remaining edits are the December assembly and console, the contract version literal, and action descriptions). The added text contains no first names; figures live in fixtures and the settlement record, described qualitatively in prose except the acceptance figures above.

## Build v112 (2026-10-31): Round-17 December-parity fixes F4+F5 — character splits on the two remaining strays: the K-1 amount gains a box 9a long-term-gain portion, and the reclassified return of capital gains a qualified-dividend portion

All user-entered data, no external source. The two fixes in this build (findings F4 and F5, both MUST-FIX, from the settled round-17 December remaining-parity audit; the round's F1+F2 were built at v111 and its F3 is the v113 build — neither is touched). THE DEFECTS: two December strays carried no character split, so amounts the tax law prices at preferential rates were taxed entirely as ordinary income. F4: the K-1 stray (`strayK1`) was added entirely to other ordinary income, so a Schedule K-1 box 9a net long-term capital gain — a part of many K-1 allocations — was taxed at ordinary rates. F5: the reclassified return-of-capital stray (`strayROCOrdinary`) raised only the ordinary-dividends total with no qualified companion (the January-paid stray has carried one since v104), so a reclassified amount the fund reports as a qualified dividend was taxed entirely at ordinary rates. On the settlement's example shape (2026 MFJ, $110,000 of ordinary income plus a $10,000 stray amount) each defect overstated the federal tax by $1,200: December priced $10,040 where the same $10,000 priced as a long-term gain or as a qualified dividend prices $8,840. THE FIX (character splits only, following the v104 January-paid precedent — no new tax math; the portions ride dials the engine already prices): (1) server/src/decemberCore.ts — the December state gains two top-level non-negative dollar fields, `strayK1CapGainAmount` (the box 9a long-term-gain portion of the K-1 amount) and `strayROCQualifiedAmount` (the qualified-dividend portion of the reclassified return of capital), each defaulting to $0 and read leniently so a stored blob written before the fields existed parses them as $0 and prices bit-identically to v111. In `decemberCaseInputs` the K-1 total is split: the gain portion, clamped to the K-1 total (and $0 when the K-1 amount is a loss — a deductible loss reduces ordinary income whole, exactly as before), rides the long-term-gains stack through the same totalGain path the other gain strays use and is removed from ordinary income, so no dollar is counted twice; the rest of the K-1 stays ordinary. The reclassified return of capital stays whole in ordinary dividends (a qualified dividend is a subset of the ordinary total, never an addition), and its qualified portion, clamped to that total, additionally rides the qualified-dividends total into the 0%/15% gains stack — the January-paid pattern exactly. Neither field reads or writes the legacy provenance flags (the v104 precedent: a character-split field does not clear the January-paid or ROC provenance machinery, which governs other splits). (2) client/src/December.tsx — the K-1 stray row gains an "Of which long-term capital gain (box 9a)" field with plain-words copy (box 9a reports the long-term capital gain part of a K-1 amount; that part is taxed at the lower capital-gains rates, the rest as ordinary income), and the reclassified-ROC stray row gains an "Of which qualified dividends" field with plain-words copy (a reclassified dividend can itself be a qualified dividend, as the fund reports it on Form 1099-DIV; that part is taxed at the lower qualified-dividend rates). Both fields ride the existing money converters and appear only when their stray's amount applies. (3) RIDER (from v111): the loss-carryforward semantics paragraph in server/src/apiContractCore.ts no longer ends by saying the single-year Playground has no ledger; it now states precisely that the single-year pricer runs the same ledger when a carry-in is supplied (the December console supplies one since build v111) and that the Playground UI supplies none, so a Playground year still prices its typed year in-year only, exactly as before. (4) server/src/actions.ts — API_CONTRACT_VERSION 111 → 112 and the December actions' descriptions gain the stray character-split sentences; no pricing handler changes. FIXTURES: six new December fixtures (suite 54 → 60): the F4 acceptance (the $10,000 K-1 amount priced $10,040 all-ordinary as the pre-fix control and $8,840 with the full box 9a portion, the $1,200 correction pinned, plus a partial-split leg); the F5 acceptance (the same figures for the reclassified ROC with its qualified portion); a $0-portion identity fixture for each field (a $0 portion prices the pre-fix figure bit-identically, a legacy blob with no new key parses the field $0, the default state carries $0, the writer schema accepts the state, and an entered portion round-trips through the saved blob); a combined case (a K-1 gain portion and an ROC qualified portion on one state — the priced AGI counts each stray once and the federal tax is the fully-split figure, proving no double-count); and a clamp case (a portion entered above its stray total clamps to the total, and a gain portion entered beside a K-1 loss stays inert). ACCEPTANCE (execution-based, via artifact actions in the sandbox database — not code-reading alone; never against the user's entered data): through the live projection action at contract 112, the F4 example (2026 MFJ, ages 60/58, $110,000 ordinary income, a $10,000 K-1 amount with a $10,000 box 9a portion) prices federal tax and settlement at $8,840.00, against $10,040.00 with the portion at $0; the F5 example (the same shape with a $10,000 reclassified ROC amount and a $10,000 qualified portion) prices $8,840.00 against the same $10,040.00 control; on both shapes the stray is counted once in AGI. RENDERED CHECK (the audit's live pass over the built console, on the sandbox copy of the stored console state): entering a $10,000 K-1 amount left the headline federal tax at its stored baseline (an ordinary amount displacing ordinary draw at a MAGI pinned by the cliff solver), and entering the full $10,000 box 9a portion repriced it live to $12,559 with the settlement moving from its stored baseline to −$7,270; entering a $10,000 reclassified ROC amount with its full $10,000 qualified portion repriced the same stored baseline → $12,559; clearing both strays restored the stored baseline and the original stored state exactly. GATES: three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff; the tax census in fine slices totalling 513/513 with a teeth check passing on every slice (the packaged runner's coarser 86-fixture chunk 2 was OOM-killed at exit 137 — the standing S-2 limitation — and its whole range passed in the finer 12- and 24-chunk slices); the extended (140/140), December (60/60, including the six new fixtures, every earlier figure unmoved), UI-state (19/19), Roth CAS (15/15), retirement CAS (16/16), and retirement (63/63, both Trinity mixes within tolerance) suites green; extended and retirement teeth green; the packaged harness green at 349/349 checks with data-integrity at zero violations; and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending after-tax wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit), confirming the plan march did not move (this build changes no file the compare path reads: the December assembly is reachable only from the December actions and fixtures, and the remaining edits are the contract version literal, two action descriptions, one semantics sentence, and the console form). The added text contains no first names; figures live in fixtures and the settlement record, described qualitatively in prose except the acceptance figures above.

## Build v111 (2026-10-30): Round-17 December-parity fixes F1+F2 — the December console takes an entering capital-loss carryforward and runs the plan's shared loss ledger, so the federal and Washington gain bases can differ

All user-entered data, no external source. The two fixes in this build (findings F1 and F2, both High · MUST-FIX, from the settled round-17 December remaining-parity audit; the round's F3, F4, F5 are NOT touched — they are the v113 and v112 builds respectively). THE DEFECTS: the December draw console had no way to enter a capital-loss carryforward from a prior year and priced the year's gains as if none existed. F1: the December state schema had no entering-carryforward field, the case assembly built one signed gain, and the single-year pricer derived its only loss allowance from the current year's own result — the plan's loss ledger was never called, so an entering carryforward was silently dropped: the safe draw came out understated, the tax overstated, and the unused carry-out lost. F2: the planned-sales hint told users to enter gains "net of any prior-year capital-loss carryforward", and that single signed gain then also became Washington's excise base — a carryforward not attributable to Washington could not be represented at all, so the federal base and the Washington base could not differ and the Washington tax (and with it the settlement) came out understated. THE FIX (one unified December year-input model; no loss math forked — the console and pricer reuse the plan's shared ledger): (1) server/src/rothOptimizer.ts — the single-year pricer's inputs gain four optional entering-carryforward dials (short-term and long-term totals, plus the Washington-attributable portion of each; absent or $0 = no carry-in). When any carry-in is positive, the pricer runs the year's own net long-term result through the SAME shared applyLossLedger the plan march uses, with utilization unbounded for the trial pricing (the plan march's own pattern): it takes the ledger's netted result as the priced gain, the ledger's claimed allowance, and a Washington gains base of the gross gains minus only the Washington-attributable part the gains actually absorbed — so the two bases can differ. After pricing, the ledger re-runs once against the priced year's final taxable income before the allowance (the plan's year-end reconciliation pattern) and the result exposes the reconciled carry-out by character, Washington portions included; all four read $0 when no carry-in was entered. With no carry-in the ledger never runs and every figure is the pre-v111 in-year computation term for term, so Playground pricing is bit-identical. The December cliff solver prices through the same pricer, so the ledger applies inside its trial pricings automatically. (2) server/src/decemberCore.ts — the December state gains the four carry-in fields as nullable non-negative dollar amounts (null = no input yet, $0 = explicitly none — distinct facts; a blob written before the fields existed parses them null and prices exactly as before). The case assembly passes them through (null as absent). Each case result gains the four carry-out figures at the headline draw, read off that case's own at-headline pricing. Load resolution follows the education overlay's discipline with one addition: the Tax Plan record's carry-in is the balance entering the plan's FIRST year (its execution year), so the record facts resolve into a null console field ONLY when the console's tax year is that year; entered values including $0 always win; and the save derivation gains an edited-carry-in flag so an unedited console saves its STORED carry-in values, never a load-resolved overlay. (3) client/src/December.tsx — the four fields ride the existing nullable-money converters (blank vs $0 stay distinct), preseed on first open from the record's carry-in cents only when the December year is the execution year (preseeded values become the console's own stored values, the balances pattern), and a new "Capital losses carried into this year" section sits right after the year-to-date actuals with the four inputs and plain-words copy (what a carryforward is; the console nets it against this year's gains and applies the $3,000 yearly allowance; any unused part carries into next year and shows on the case cards). Case cards show the carry-out when positive ("Loss carried into next year", split by character, with the Washington-attributable portion shown only when nonzero). The planned-sales hint is corrected: the label drops "net" ("Forecast gain on planned sales") and the hint now asks for the gain BEFORE any prior-year carryforward, directing the user to the new section — no "excludes carryforward" qualification anywhere. Headline unchanged. (4) server/src/actions.ts — API_CONTRACT_VERSION 110 → 111, the four carry-out fields join the December case response schema, and the December actions' descriptions gain the carry-in/carry-out sentences; nothing else in the file changes. FIXTURES: six new December fixtures (suite 48 → 54): the F1 acceptance example including its pre-fix control legs; the $0/null identity (null and explicit-$0 states price bit-identically, a legacy blob parses the fields null, entered values round-trip); the F2 non-Washington-attributable acceptance including the old net-entry control leg pricing the corrected excise error; the Washington-attributable case pricing the Washington base down through the December path (federal tax unchanged); the zero-taxable-income utilization case (allowance claimed but unused, the full carryforward carries out); and the resolution/save rules (first-year-only resolution, entered values win, an unedited save persists stored values). ACCEPTANCE (execution-based, via artifact actions in the sandbox database — not code-reading alone; never against the user's entered data): the F1 example (2026 MFJ, ages 60/58, $60,000 ordinary income, $10,000 entering long-term carryforward, no new gains, $20,000 benchmark, $12,000 APTC, $5,000 buffer) prices through the live projection action at contract 111 with the ledger-aware headline draw $22,600.00 (was $19,600.00), the carry-out of $7,000.00 preserved on every case, and the non-draw MAGI reduced by exactly the $3,000 allowance; at the common $19,600 draw the fixture pins federal tax $4,832.00 (was $5,192.00) and settlement $4,461.36 (was $5,120.16) from the direct pricer. The F2 example (2026 MFJ, $110,000 ordinary income, $500,000 realized long-term gain, $100,000 entering non-Washington-attributable long-term carryforward, Washington residence) prices through the same action with federal tax $75,555.00, Washington excise $15,540.00 (was $8,540.00), and settlement $91,095.00 (was $84,095.00). GATES: three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff; the tax census in fine slices totalling 513/513 with a teeth check passing on every slice (the full-suite worker call and the in-worker tax-teeth actions time out inside the worker — the standing limitation — and the packaged runner's own coarser 86-fixture chunk 2 was OOM-killed at exit 137, so its census covered 427 of the 513, the same fixtures passing in the finer slices); the extended (140/140), December (54/54), UI-state (19/19), Roth CAS (15/15), retirement CAS (16/16), and retirement (63/63, both Trinity mixes within tolerance) suites green; extended and retirement teeth green; the packaged harness green at 349/349 checks with data-integrity at zero violations; and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending after-tax wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit) in a direct A/B: the same compare run against a v110 build of the stashed pre-edit sources and against this build returned identical figures. The added text contains no first names; figures live in fixtures and the settlement record, described qualitatively in prose except the acceptance figures above.

## Build v110 (2026-10-30): Round-16 optimizer-parity fix F2 — the Monte Carlo check draws the shared 160-shock stride, so the check and the stats action sample the same paths

All user-entered data, no external source. The one fix in this build (finding F2, SHOULD-FIX, from the settled round-16 Monte Carlo parity audit; the round's F1 was built at v109 — no other finding is touched). THE DEFECT: both Monte Carlo surfaces share `rothMcStream` (mulberry32, seed 12345, 250 paths) in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts, but the check drew a variable-length series per path — `rothMcReturnSeries` draws `years = endAgePrimary − age at startYear + 1` normals (11 for the common plan) — while the stats action draws a fixed 160 normals per path (`rothMcShockSeries(MC_STREAM_STRIDE_YEARS, rng)`, each scenario pricing from `z.slice(0, yearsS)`), the stride that exists for the documented batch-independence requirement. Path 1 was therefore paired identically on the two surfaces, but paths 2–250 were different market trials: on the common plan at 20% volatility the check reported a Do Nothing median net cost of $1,757.32 while stats reported $1,966.45 — a $209.13 discrepancy in the reported median (and in the median advantage, the winner being $0.00 on every path). THE FIX (server-side, in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts only; the seed, the path count, the PRNG, the pricing math, the percentile conventions, and stats behavior are all unchanged): `runRothMonteCarloCheck` now adopts the shared stride — per path it draws `MC_STREAM_STRIDE_YEARS` (160) shocks via `rothMcShockSeries` and prices both candidates from the horizon prefix of that vector (the first `years` shocks mapped as expected return + volatility × shock), exactly as stats does, so for an identical strategy, volatility, horizon, and seed the two surfaces sample the same paths. `rothMcReturnSeries` itself is unchanged (it remains the variable-length generator the stats mixed-horizon fixture uses to price the OLD construction). KNOWN CONSEQUENCE (settlement-stated, intended): historical check figures move to the stats values on every plan whose horizon is under 160 years. RE-DERIVED FIXTURES (each re-derived by execution under the new stream, old → new): (1) `mc-check-seeded-small-n` (torpedo plan, volatility 15, N = 40) — wins 34 → 33, win rate 85% → 82.5%, median advantage $130,788.85 → $129,618.70, p10 advantage −$22,890.85 → −$19,638.95, p90 advantage $377,639.32 → $476,377.44, winner median net cost $161,901.10 → $161,454.23, Do Nothing median net cost $308,688.28 → $318,003.38. ## Build v109 (2026-10-30): Round-16 optimizer-parity fix F1 — the Monte Carlo check is gated on the optimizer run's input fingerprint

All user-entered data, no external source. The one fix in this build (finding F1, MUST-FIX, from the settled round-16 Monte Carlo parity audit; the round's F2 is a separate later build — no other finding is touched). THE DEFECT: `setOptResult` had exactly one call site — the optimizer mutation's `onSuccess` in client/src/RothConversion.tsx — and no staleness tracking existed anywhere for the optimizer result, unlike the four sibling sections that each carry a fingerprint comparison. `buildMcRequest` mixed the current plan payload (including any edited inputs) with the retained winner / Do Nothing descriptors, and the check button was enabled whenever a request existed; the check-result fingerprint guarded only the check run, not the optimizer run. So after editing only the heir rate from 25% to 0%, a check re-run presented winner $0.00, Do Nothing $0.00, 0% wins as current validation of a recommendation crowned under the old inputs — a fresh optimizer run on the edited input would tie and crown Do Nothing instead. (The check-result stale notice itself already worked — old figures hid after an edit; the defect landed on the re-run the notice invites.) THE FIX (client-local, in client/src/RothConversion.tsx; no optimizer pricing, check pricing, or exemption/floor logic changed — the version bump below and the platform-v26 action descriptions are the only server-file edits): the optimizer run's inputs are fingerprinted and the check is gated on them, following the file's own sibling-section pattern. (1) A new `optFingerprint` state sits beside `optResult`, and `runOptimizerMut.onSuccess` now stores `JSON.stringify(vars)` — the exact request object the mutation was called with. (2) The current fingerprint is computed the same way the run button builds its request — `JSON.stringify({...buildSavePayload(), fafsaReportableAssetsCents: fafsaReportableAssetsCentsValue()})` — matching the `runOptimizerMut.mutate({...})` call exactly, so any plan input that affects optimizer pricing (balances, basis tiers, ceilings, window, draw order, claiming ages/amounts, heir rate, preserve floor, guardrail, bunching, harvesting, spending, return, ACA/education/survivor settings) is covered. (3) `optStale = optResult != null && optFingerprint !== optFingerprintNow`. (4) While stale, the "Run the check" button is disabled and a plain-words notice sits next to it — the plan changed since the optimizer ran, so this winner was priced on the earlier inputs; run the optimizer again before checking it — and the check-figures block stays hidden even when the check-result fingerprint is current, because a "current" check result is not a validation of a stale recommendation. (5) The button's helper copy no longer says the check "Runs with the plan and the winning strategy exactly as they stand now" while stale; that copy shows only when the optimizer result is current. The existing check-result staleness guard works exactly as before. PLATFORM UPGRADE (v26, applied with this build): every `defineAction` in server/src/actions.ts now carries a one-sentence `description` for the user's agent, each taken from the first sentence of that action's existing ACTION_PURPOSES entry; no action name, schema, handler, or authorization guard changed. ACCEPTANCE (execution-based, via artifact actions in the sandbox database and a rendered pass of the artifact — not code-reading alone; never against the user's entered data): on the F1 example plan (Single born 1966, end age 70, retire 60, $10,000 pre-tax, $0 everything else, 0% return/inflation/state tax, heir rate 25%, $150,000 MAGI cap stop at 65, draw order Taxable → Pre-tax → Roth; the optimizer crowns a winner at net cost $0.00 vs Do Nothing $2,500.00), after editing only the heir rate 25% → 0% the check does NOT present $0.00/$0.00/0% wins as current validation — the run button is disabled with the stale notice shown and a fresh optimizer run is required; with inputs unchanged the check still validates normally (winner $0.00, Do Nothing $2,500.00, 100% wins at volatility 0), and the pre-existing stale-notice behavior for the check result itself is unchanged. ACCEPTANCE GATES: three consecutive clean internal review passes over the final diff; full suites green — tax census 513/513 (fine slices; chunk-2 OOM kills are a standing limitation, re-run killed slices finer), extended 140/140, December 48/48, ui-state 19/19, roth-cas 15/15, retirement-cas 16/16, retirement 63/63 (both Trinity mixes within tolerance), packaged harness 349/349, integrity 0 violations; and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit), confirming the plan march did not move (the fix is client gating plus action descriptions only). API_CONTRACT_VERSION 108 → 109.

## Build v107 (2026-10-30): Round-15 optimizer-parity fix F3 — the claim-floor note states the exemption for a below-floor Do Nothing winner

THE DEFECT: `claimAgeFloorMetFor` deliberately returns true when the winner is Do Nothing — the floor exemption, so Do Nothing stays eligible and can still win — but `jointSearchNote` treated that true value as proof the winning claim was at or after the floor, so when the floor-exempt Do Nothing winner claimed below the floor the note asserted "the winner is the best strategy at a claiming age of 67 or later" while the same note's locked sentence stated the claim was locked at 62 — the note contradicted itself in one paragraph. ## Build v105 (2026-10-30): Round-15 optimizer-parity fix F1 — the harvesting flag is carried when saving or locally re-pricing an optimizer recommendation

THE DEFECT: the optimizer already exposes `gainsHarvest` on every scored candidate and the server stores exactly what the client sends, but both client reconstruction paths dropped the flag. `saveOptimizerScenario` spread the working plan's payload (which carries the WORKING plan's flag) and overrode ceilings, window stop, guardrail, bunching, draw order, and claiming ages/amounts, but never `gainsHarvest` — so a harvest-on winner saved from a harvest-off working plan wrote a harvest-off scenario.
