## Build v104 (2026-10-30): Round-14 pricing-parity fix F5 — January-paid capital-gain distributions keep their long-term-gain character in December

All user-entered data, no external source. The one fix in this build (finding F5, High, from the settled round-14 pricing-parity audit; no other round-14 finding is touched; build v100's F2, v101's F4, v102's F1, and v103's F3 are built on, not redone). THE DEFECT: `decemberCaseInputs` added the whole January-paid stray total (`strayJanPaid`) to ordinary dividends with only a qualified-dividend split, and the state carried no capital-gain character field — so a fund distribution the fund designated as a capital gain dividend was priced as an ordinary dividend. December had the year right and the character wrong: 26 U.S.C. §852(b)(7) deems a distribution declared by a regulated investment company in October, November, or December and actually paid during January to have been received by each shareholder on December 31 of the declaration year, and a capital gain dividend so designated is treated as a long-term capital gain under §852(b)(3). The qualified split mitigated the federal stacking only partially and could never fix Washington, whose capital-gains excise prices long-term gains and never dividends, so a January-paid capital-gain distribution never entered the Washington base at all. THE FIX (character split only — no new tax math): the December state gains one field, `strayJanPaidCapGainAmount`, the capital-gain-distribution PORTION of the January-paid total, alongside the existing `strayJanPaid` total and `strayJanPaidQualifiedAmount`. In `decemberCaseInputs` the portion is clamped to the total, added to the capital result so it rides the same `totalGain` → `stockSold`/`stockBasis` → `ltcg` path `remCapDist` and `strayCapDist` already use (that path is unchanged), and REMOVED from ordinary dividends, so no dollar is counted twice — total income and MAGI are unchanged by the split, only the character moves. The qualified-dividend split now applies to the ordinary remainder only: the qualified portion is clamped to the remainder (total minus the capital-gain portion), never to the whole total. The plan, Playground, and work-years pricing are untouched (they already route long-term gains correctly). THE CONSOLE (client December.tsx): the January-paid stray item gains an "Of which capital-gain distributions" field beside the qualified field, with a plain-words note: a distribution declared in October–December and paid in January counts as received on December 31 of the earlier year, and a capital-gain distribution is a long-term gain, not an ordinary dividend — enter that part so it is taxed as a gain. RELATIONSHIP TO THE LEGACY PROVENANCE MACHINERY (verified in source, decemberCore.ts): the `legacyJanPaidSplitUnconfirmed` flag and the save derivation's `janPaidCharacter` edit flag govern ONLY the qualified-amount provenance — the flag says a stored January-paid amount predates the qualified split and asks the user to confirm the qualified portion, it changes no pricing, and it clears only when the qualified field is edited. The new capital-gain field neither reads nor writes that flag: editing the capital-gain portion does not clear it (the qualified portion may still be unconfirmed), the flag's derivation on pre-format-3 blobs still keys only on the qualified key's absence or $0 default, and a blob's flag state prices exactly as before — the two splits are independent portions of the same total, each clamped in the assembly, so they cannot conflict or double-count. BACK-COMPAT: the field is optional in effect — the lenient parser reads a missing key in the stored encrypted December blob (`december_projection_v1`, revision CAS unchanged) as $0, the default state carries $0, and a $0 portion prices bit-identically to before this build (the whole total rides ordinary dividends); loading, saving, and restoring an existing stored state are unbroken (verified live: the stored console state written before this build reads back with the new field at $0). ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE (re-derived exactly in the settlement, pinned in a fixture): 2026 WA, $1,278,000 of already-recognized long-term gains plus a $100,000 capital-gain distribution declared Dec 2026 and paid Jan 2027. Before the fix the Washington gain base was $1,278,000 − $278,000 = $1,000,000 → excise $70,000.00. After it the base is $1,378,000 − $278,000 = $1,100,000 → 7% × $1,000,000 + 9.9% × $100,000 = $79,900.00 — an understatement of $9,900.00 corrected. FEDERAL CHARACTER DIFFERENCE (left unquantified by the reviewer; quantified in this build from the shared pricer and pinned in a fixture): on the clean shape of $120,000 of wages (MFJ, federal tax $10,040.00 alone) plus a $30,000 January-paid distribution, pricing the distribution as an ordinary dividend adds $5,300.00 of federal tax (taxable income $87,800 → $117,800: $13,000 × 12% + $17,000 × 22% → federal tax $15,340.00), while pricing it as a capital-gain distribution adds $2,835.00 ($11,100 fits the 0% gains space up to the $98,900 top, $18,900 at 15% → federal tax $12,875.00) — a federal character difference of $2,465.00 on that shape. REGRESSION FIXTURES: four new December fixtures named for the mechanism. (a) The WA acceptance example through the December path: the portion rides the stock dials at $1,378,000, ordinary dividends fall to $0, Washington gains $1,378,000, taxable Washington gains $1,100,000, excise $79,900.00 — and the $0-portion leg prices the before-fix $70,000.00, named in the fixture as the corrected error, with the corrected understatement pinned at $9,900.00. (b) The federal character fixture above: both treatments' federal taxes and increments pinned, and the $2,465.00 difference. (c) The $0-portion identity case: the whole total in ordinary dividends, nothing on the gain dials, and the pre-fix federal figures pinned ($2,400.00 of added tax on $100,000 of wages plus a $20,000 January-paid total, the standing qualified fixture's shape), plus back-compat legs — a legacy blob with no capital-gain key parses the portion as $0 and prices the same pre-fix figure, the default state carries $0, the writer schema accepts the state, and an entered portion round-trips through the saved blob. (d) A combined case on one $60,000 January-paid total — a $20,000 capital-gain portion and $15,000 of qualified dividends inside the $40,000 ordinary remainder — proving no double-count at the dial level (the non-qualified ordinary part $25,000 + the qualified part $15,000 + the capital-gain part $20,000 sum to the entered $60,000, and the priced AGI counts the total once at $160,000) and end to end (federal tax $14,975.00, hand-derived), plus clamp legs: a capital-gain portion entered above the total clamps to the total, and a qualified portion entered above the ordinary remainder clamps to the remainder, not the total. No standing fixture was re-derived: no standing December fixture enters a capital-gain portion, the standing qualified-portion fixture's figures are the $0-portion identity this build preserves, and the whole December suite passes with every earlier figure unmoved. RENDERED / LIVE CHECK: the built console's December path was exercised live through the projection action at contract 104 — the WA acceptance shape with a $0 portion prices Washington tax $70,000.00 (federal $292,504), and the same state with the $100,000 portion entered prices Washington tax $79,900.00 with total income and MAGI unchanged at $1,378,000 (character only, no double-count); the audit's rendered pass confirms the January-paid stray item shows the new capital-gain portion field with its explanation in the strays checklist. ## Build v103 (2026-10-30): Round-14 pricing-parity fix F3 — the December console prices education credits and says so when it cannot

All user-entered data, no external source. The one fix in this build (finding F3, Medium, from the settled round-14 pricing-parity audit; no other round-14 finding is touched; build v100's F2, v101's F4, and v102's F1 are built on, not redone). The defect had two halves: the December state carried no education input at all and `decemberCaseInputs` hardcoded `educationStudents: null` — the only education mention in the December core — so every December case priced through the shared Playground year pricer with the §25A credits silently zeroed, while the plan and the Playground price the same students through the same shared path; and the console presented its estimated federal tax bill and filing settlement with no student input and no warning that the credits were unpriced. PART 1 — INPUTS AND PRICING: the December state gains one optional field, `educationStudents`, in the same shape the plan and Playground already use (per-student qualified expenses in dollars plus the household's own AOTC-eligible mark, capped at twelve students) — entered, never inferred from 529 balances, the college-years span, or any other saved field. `decemberCaseInputs` now passes the entered students to `pricePlaygroundYear` instead of the hardcoded null, so the shared `educationCreditsFor` step inside `priceYear` is the only credit math — no §25A rule is re-implemented anywhere in the December path. The refundable AOTC portion is reported on the price result and never netted into the floored federal tax; the December settlement now credits it beside the ACA premium credit exactly as the plan's score identity does — the net settlement is the total tax minus the premium credit still due, plus any excess advance-credit repayment, minus the refundable education credit at the headline draw — so the "estimated amount to settle at filing" reflects it. Each December case result also carries the priced AOTC, LLC, the credit choice, the nonrefundable and refundable parts, and two qualification flags (`hasEducationExpenses`, `excludesEducationCredits`). PRESEED: the console's first open already preseeds from the saved Tax Plan record; that same first-open path now also carries the record's `educationStudents` for the December tax year (the record's per-year cents entries converted to the December dollars shape), and a stored December state that has no education input yet resolves the record's students for that year at load through the same load-resolution overlay the beneficiary fact and legacy balances already use. A user-entered December list — even an empty one — always governs afterwards and is never overwritten by a preseed or a resolution; the save derivation keeps the stored value for the field unless the console's education section was actually edited. BACK-COMPAT: the field is optional in the stored encrypted December blob (`december_projection_v1`, revision CAS unchanged) — an absent field parses as null (no input yet), prices exactly as before this build ($0 credits), and loads, saves, and restores unchanged; the writer schema accepts both null and an entered list. PART 2 — THE CONSOLE (client December.tsx): a new Education credits section carries per-student qualified-expenses entry with an AOTC-eligible checkbox per student, and a plain-words reminder that stays visible: the American Opportunity Credit is worth up to $2,500 per student ($1,500 lowers the tax bill and $1,000 is refundable — it comes back at filing even if no tax is owed), the Lifetime Learning Credit is worth up to $2,000 per tax return (not per student) for students who do not qualify for the AOTC, both credits shrink once married-filing-jointly income passes $160,000 and are gone at $180,000, and qualified expenses are the amounts from Form 1098-T — tuition and required fees actually paid this year. The projected tax bill gains a refundable-education-credit line when one prices, and a note when a nonrefundable credit is already applied against the federal tax. QUALIFICATION: when no education expenses are entered, the settlement carries a visible qualification — in the headline bill, on each case card, and as a server warning on the projection — stating that the settlement excludes education credits and is not a final settlement if anyone in the household paid qualified education expenses this year; the console never presents a settlement as final while the credit is unpriced. ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLES (re-derived exactly in the settlement, pinned in fixtures): 2026, married filing jointly, $60,000 of ordinary income, no phase-out (the range starts at $160,000), tax before credits 10% × $24,800 + 12% × $3,000 = $2,840.00. (a) AOTC on $4,000 of qualified expenses = 100% × $2,000 + 25% × $2,000 = $2,500.00, of which 40% ($1,000.00) is refundable and the $1,500.00 nonrefundable part applies in full against the $2,840.00, giving federal tax $1,340.00 and a settlement improved by exactly $2,500.00 against the no-student case. (b) The LLC variant: $10,000 of eligible expenses on a student not marked AOTC-eligible gives 20% × $10,000 = $2,000.00 nonrefundable, federal tax $840.00. REGRESSION FIXTURES: five new December fixtures named for the mechanism. (a) The AOTC acceptance example end to end through the December path (engine credit $2,500.00, nonrefundable $1,500.00, refundable $1,000.00, federal tax $1,340.00, settlement $340.00 against the no-student $2,840.00 — the $2,500.00 improvement), plus a serialize/parse round-trip of the entered students. (b) The LLC variant ($2,000.00 credit, federal tax $840.00, settlement $840.00). (c) The no-students-entered case: federal tax, total tax, and settlement all $2,840.00 — bit-identical to before this build — with every case carrying the excludes-education-credits qualification and the settlement warning naming it; an explicitly empty list prices identically and still carries the qualification; a legacy blob with no education key parses the field as null; the default state carries null; the writer schema accepts both shapes. (d) A phase-out case proving the shared phase-out prices in December exactly as in the plan: at $170,000 of income (halfway through the $160,000–$180,000 joint range) the $2,500.00 AOTC halves to $1,250.00 (refundable $500.00, nonrefundable $750.00), federal tax $18,990.00 against tax before credits $19,740.00, settlement $18,490.00, and at $180,000 the credit is fully phased out. ## Build v102 (2026-10-30): Round-14 pricing-parity fix F1 — work years price the entered tax-exempt interest for Social Security taxation

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change and no UI change (the plan record already carries the entered amount; only the work-year pricer's wiring changes). The one fix in this build (finding F1, Medium, from the settled round-14 pricing-parity audit; no other round-14 finding is touched; build v100's F2 work-years loss ledger and build v101's F4 Washington attribution are built on, not redone): `priceOneWorkYear`'s single `priceYear` call (inside `priceWithGain`, so the fix covers both a standalone work-year price and every year of the roll) passed `taxExemptInterest: 0` unconditionally — the only tax-exempt mention in the file — so a salary year priced Social Security taxation and MAGI as if the household had no tax-exempt interest, while the plan march passes the entered amount at all three of its pricing sites and the Playground passes its input. CORRECTION (input wiring only, no new calculation): the call now passes `plan.taxExemptInterestAnnual` — the same entered amount every other surface passes — and the shared `priceYear` does the rest exactly as it already does for the march: the amount enters provisional income for §86 taxation (26 U.S.C. §86(b)(1)–(2): modified AGI is AGI increased by the tax-exempt interest received or accrued during the year, plus one-half of benefits, against the $32,000 / $44,000 joint base / adjusted-base amounts) and enters MAGI (and with it the ACA MAGI and the IRMAA lookback seed the roll records from the work-year lines). The stale comments that stated a work year carries $0 of tax-exempt interest (the model note and the priced-MAGI line note) now state the corrected rule. CASH-SIDE PARITY FINDING (verified in source, not assumed): the plan march prices the tax-exempt interest for §86 / MAGI purposes ONLY — its cash-in is RMDs + Social Security benefits + other ordinary income, and the tax-exempt dollars are banked as household cash NOWHERE in the march (they are not in the surplus sweep, not in the settlement's cash channels, and not in the year-funding display's income) — so the work year mirrors that treatment exactly: the amount prices in the salary year and is NOT added to the year's surplus; the fixtures pin this from both sides (the with-interest surplus carries no $6,000 inflow term, and the with-minus-zero surplus difference is exactly the −$350.00 tax difference). UNAFFECTED CASES: a plan with $0 / absent tax-exempt interest prices bit-identically to before — the passed field is $0, exactly the pre-fix literal — and the stored record enters none, so its anchors reproduce bit-identically (below); no standing fixture was re-derived, because no standing work-years fixture enters tax-exempt interest and the whole census passes with every other figure unmoved. ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE (re-derived exactly in the settlement, pinned in a fixture; the reviewer's withdrawn age-62 example is NOT used anywhere in this build): age 64, $80,000 salary, $10,000 Social Security benefits, $6,000 tax-exempt interest, MFJ, no employer contributions. The 2026 stack is $24,500 elective + $8,000 catch-up (age 64 takes the 50+ band, not the 60–63 band) + $9,750 HSA ($8,750 family + $1,000 catch-up) = $42,250 of pre-tax shelter (plus a $37,750 after-tax mega-backdoor), so taxable wages are $37,750; the §414(v)(7) Roth-catch-up mandate is inert (Box-3 wages $70,250 < the $150,000 threshold). Provisional income $42,750 without the interest vs $48,750 with it; taxable Social Security min(0.85 × $10,000, min(0.5 × $10,000, 0.5 × ($44,000 − $32,000)) + 0.85 × excess over $44,000) = $5,000 vs $8,500; AGI $42,750 vs $46,250; taxable income $10,550 vs $14,050 (2026 MFJ standard deduction $32,200; age 64, no 65+ add-on, no senior deduction); federal tax 10% × each = $1,055.00 vs $1,405.00 — a $350.00 understatement corrected. REGRESSION FIXTURES: two new tax fixtures named for the mechanism. (a) The acceptance example end to end: federal tax $1,405.00, MAGI $52,250, taxable Social Security $8,500 (read off the line as MAGI − $6,000 − taxable wages, the work-year line carrying no separate benefits-taxed field), the full stack and FICA ($5,374.13) pinned, the surplus at $3,220.87 with no tax-exempt inflow term, and a one-year roll leg pinning the same tax and MAGI through the roll with the quit-age Taxable at the surplus; the $1,055.00 before-fix figure is named in the fixture note as the corrected error. (b) The $0 identity case on the identical shape: the pre-fix figures themselves ($1,055.00 federal, MAGI $42,750, taxable Social Security $5,000, surplus $3,570.87) plus the cross-leg proving the with-minus-zero surplus gap is exactly −$350.00. ACCEPTANCE: three consecutive clean internal review passes (each re-verifying the fix mechanism in source — exactly one `priceYear` call in the work-years file, now passing the plan's entered amount — the pinned fixtures, the gates, and the anchors); the build's typechecks; the tax census in fine slices totalling every fixture in the suite (513, including the two new ones), each slice with its teeth check passing — one 43-fixture slice was OOM-killed at the coarser slicing and its whole range passed in four finer slices of 11 (the standing S-2 limitation), and the packaged runner's own coarser census likewise lost one 86-fixture chunk to memory, with the same fixtures passing in the finer census slices; the extended (140), December (39), UI-state (19), Roth CAS (15), retirement CAS (16), and retirement (63) suites green, the retirement suite including both Trinity mixes within tolerance, the extended and retirement teeth checks passing, and the integrity checks at zero violations; the packaged harness green across its main-process checks (349 checks); and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit), confirming a plan with no entered tax-exempt interest did not move. RESIDUAL / CAVEAT: none for the priced mechanism — the correction is the march's and Playground's own input, priced by the one shared `priceYear`; the only scope note is the cash-parity rule itself, stated above and pinned in the fixtures: tax-exempt interest is priced for §86 / MAGI on every surface and banked as cash on none, so a household that actually spends those dollars sees them only through the plan's entered spending and balances, exactly as before this build on the march and Playground surfaces. ## Build v101 (2026-10-30): Round-14 pricing-parity fix F4 — the Washington excise base deducts the Washington-allocated loss carryforward the year's gains absorbed

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change (the plan record is a settings blob; the two new inputs ride it as optional keys, absent = $0 on records written before this build). The one fix in this build (finding F4, High, from the settled round-14 pricing-parity audit; no other round-14 finding is touched; build v100's F2 work-years ledger is built on, not redone): when the federal loss ledger was active, the plan engine overrode the Washington base with the year's gross realized gains, so the excise never saw any carryforward, and the in-code comment and the published contract overstated the statute as "Washington takes no carryforward." The statute (RCW 82.87.040(3), verified against the primary source in the settlement) first bars carrying a NEGATIVE Washington amount forward, then provides that a federal loss carryforward directly attributable to losses from sales or exchanges allocated to this state under RCW 82.87.100 IS included in the calculation of adjusted capital gain to the extent it is included in the federal net long-term capital gain computation; RCW 82.87.020(1) starts adjusted capital gain from the federal figure and adds back only the enumerated carryovers — non-Washington sales (1)(c), exempt sales (1)(d), pre-2022 sales (1)(e) — never a Washington-allocated one. NEW INPUTS (allocation-aware, the settlement's scope caveat is load-bearing — this is NOT an unconditional federal deduction): capitalLossCarryInStWaCents / capitalLossCarryInLtWaCents on the saved record (engine dollars capitalLossCarryInStWa / capitalLossCarryInLtWa on the plan inputs) state, for each character, the Washington-attributable portion of the entering carryforward — a portion of, and clamped to, that character's total — entered on the Tax Plan form beside the carryforward totals; blank / absent = $0 = today's behavior. ACCOUNTING INVARIANT, implemented in the ONE shared place (the applyLossLedger transform both ledgerFields transforms and the optimizer's execution-year re-solves call): a year's Washington base = the year's gross realized gains MINUS the Washington-attributable carryforward that year's gains absorbed (equivalently, the netted federal long-term gain plus the non-Washington-attributable absorbed part). Only the absorbed part counts — an attributable dollar that instead rides the §1211(b) allowance against ordinary income, or carries out unused, was not included in the federal net long-term capital gain computation and does not reduce the base. ATTRIBUTION CONVENTION (the engine's stated rule, pinned in a fixture): within a character the pool is fungible, so consumption is attributed pro-rata — the Washington share of each character's gains-absorption, and of its used allowance, is that character's Washington share of the amount consumed — and the attributable remainder threads forward alongside its character in plan years and work years alike. ROUTING: the march's ledgerFields returns waGainsBase = gross − Washington-attributable absorbed, so the fill base, settlement rounds, ceiling re-solves, harvest search, marginal reprices, and the optimizer's execution-year re-solves all price the same base; the absorbed figure is utilization-independent, so trial pricings and the year-end reconciliation agree exactly. WORK-YEAR INTERACTION (handled in this build, per the brief): the work-years roll threads the Washington sub-state through its loss context exactly as it threads the character totals, its ledgerFields prices the same invariant (before this build a work year priced the base at the gross gains for the whole carryforward — the v100 scope boundary — so the two surfaces would have disagreed once the march moved), and the rolled inputs hand the march the CONSUMED Washington portions (the reconciled Washington carry-out after the last work year), never the entering portions priced a second time; a zero-work-year roll consumes nothing and hands the entering portions through untouched. The Playground is unaffected (no ledger; its ltcg is gross by construction) and is not changed. CORRECTED LANGUAGE: the taxEngine waGainsBase and ledger comments, the contract's state-tax semantics, and LOSS_CARRYFORWARD_SEMANTICS now state the RCW 82.87.040(3) rule as above instead of "takes no carryforward"; the standing T4 Washington fixture keeps its figures (it enters no Washington portion, so the whole carryforward is in the addback population and the base stays gross) and its note now says exactly that. UNAFFECTED CASES: a plan with no Washington-attributable carryforward entered prices bit-identically to before — including a plan whose carryforward is entirely non-Washington — because the absorbed Washington part is $0 and the base is the gross gains; the stored record enters no carryforward at all, and its anchors reproduce bit-identically (below). ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE (re-derived exactly in the settlement, pinned in a fixture): 2026, $1,300,000 of taxable WA long-term gains (a full draw of a $2,600,000 account at 50% basis), a $100,000 qualifying post-2021 Washington-allocated long-term loss carryforward in the federal computation, no charitable deduction. Before the fix the base was the gross $1,300,000: $1,300,000 − $278,000 = $1,022,000 → 7% × $1,000,000 + 9.9% × $22,000 = $72,178.00. After it, the base is $1,200,000: $922,000 of taxable Washington gains → 7% × $922,000 = $64,540.00 — an overstatement of $7,638.00 corrected. REGRESSION FIXTURES: four new tax fixtures named for the mechanism, plus the plumbing fixture extended. (a) The acceptance example end to end ($64,540.00 excise, the $72,178.00 before-fix figure named in its note as the corrected error). (b) A non-Washington-only carryforward: the federal netting identical (same $100,000 absorbed, same priced gain), the Washington base at the gross gains, the excise at $72,178.00, and the two runs' state gap exactly $7,638.00 (the runs' final federal bills differ only through the settlement feedback — the larger excise is paid by a larger pre-tax distribution — as the fixture's note states). (c) A mixed case pinning the split three ways on one shape (a $2,000,000 pool meeting $1,300,000 of gains: half attributable → $650,000 absorbed on the Washington side, base $650,000, excise $26,040.00; fully attributable → base $0; none → $72,178.00) plus a two-year leg proving the attribution threads (year 1 absorbs $50,000 of the Washington half and carries $50,000 of it out under an unused allowance; year 2's injected $400,000 gain absorbs it, base $350,000, excise $5,040.00). (d) A work-year case with two exact fixed points on the v100 deficit-sale shape: a mixed leg (gross gain $400,000, $100,000 of a $400,000 carryforward attributable → base $300,000, excise $1,540.00, the roll handing the march $0 of carryforward and $0 of attribution) and a non-Washington leg (gross $450,000 → base stays gross, excise $12,040.00). No standing fixture was re-derived: no standing fixture enters a Washington portion, and the whole census passes with every other figure unmoved. ACCEPTANCE: three consecutive clean internal review passes; the build's typechecks; the tax census in fine slices totalling every fixture in the suite (511, including the four new ones), each slice with its teeth check passing and no slice killed; the extended, December, UI-state, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, and retirement suites green, the retirement suite including both Trinity mixes within tolerance; the integrity checks at zero violations; the packaged harness green across its main-process checks (349 checks, its retirement-teeth and extended-teeth sections passing through the packaged dispatcher), with its own coarser census slices passing except one slice killed for memory (the standing limitation — the same fixtures passed in the finer census slices); and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures (ending wealth, net cost, ending pre-tax, ACA credit), confirming a plan with no entered attribution did not move. RESIDUAL / CAVEAT: the attribution is entered per character as a portion of the entering balance and consumed pro-rata within the character thereafter — the engine keeps no per-lot allocation history, so a household whose Washington losses sit in a specific character consumes them at that character's Washington share, the stated convention the contract and fixture (c) pin; exempt-sale and pre-2022 carryovers are priced as part of the non-Washington remainder unless the household marks them Washington, which is the RCW 82.87.020(1)(d)–(e) addback treatment. The tax-teeth self-check action timed out inside the worker on this build (the standing limitation recorded at v100); the teeth property is proven by the per-slice teeth checks in the sliced census, each of which corrupted a case and confirmed the suite catches it. API_CONTRACT_VERSION 100 → 101.

## Build v100 (2026-10-30): Round-14 pricing-parity fix F2 — capital-loss carryforwards price in the work years

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change; the runWorkYearsCompare response shape is unchanged (the new per-year ledger fields are internal to the roll, like build v98's RMD line fields). The one fix in this build (finding F2, High, from the settled round-14 pricing-parity audit; no other round-14 finding is touched): the work-years roll priced salary years with no loss ledger at all — the single-year work-year pricer passed no capital-loss allowance and no ledger fields into the shared priceYear (which defaults the allowance to $0), and the roll spread the plan into its rolled inputs untouched, so an entering capital-loss carryforward rode into the retirement march unconsumed; the march then initialised its own ledger from the full entering balance and priced it again in full, and the double-count compounded into every later plan year. CORRECTION (the plan march's own pattern, no second ledger invented): the roll threads loss-ledger state through the work years exactly as it already threads the taxable basis ledger and the pending education refund — entering state from the plan's capitalLossCarryInSt/Lt — and each priced year nets its own gains through the SHARED applyLossLedger helper in the tax engine; no netting table or rule is re-implemented. A work year realises gains only on a deficit-funding Taxable sale, and the pricer mirrors the march's trial-pricing discipline (its ledgerFields transform): a trial pricing reads only the netted result and the CLAIMED allowance (utilisation passed as unbounded), and the year's carry-out is reconciled ONCE, at year end, against the final priced year's taxable income before the allowance, exactly as the march's year-end reconciliation does. A year with no gains and no deficit still consumes the allowance against its taxable income — allowance used is the allowance capped at the taxable income before the allowance, floored at $0 — and a year with no taxable income before the allowance uses none of it, so the whole loss carries forward. The roll replaces its ledger state with each year's reconciled carry-out, and the rolled inputs hand the retirement march the CONSUMED carryforward (the year-end carry-out after the last work year), so the march starts from the balance the work years left, not the entering balance; a zero-work-year roll prices no year, consumes nothing, and hands the entering carryforward through untouched, exactly as before. A standalone single work-year price (no roll context) prices from the plan's capitalLossCarryInSt/Lt as its entering state. The work-year line now reports the year's ledger (carry-in by character, the net capital result actually priced, the claimed allowance, the used part, the part absorbed against the year's own gains, and the carry-out by character); the line's long-term-gain figure remains the GROSS realised gain, the figure the ledger nets. SCOPE BOUNDARY (kept, stated in the settlement): the Washington excise base is NOT changed in this build — it stays at the year's gross realised gains, exactly as the march's ledger transform holds it; the Washington-allocated carryforward treatment is round-14 F4, a separate build, and nothing of it is priced here. UNAFFECTED CASES: a plan with no entering banked loss prices bit-identically — the transform is the identity when the carry-in is $0 (no allowance field is passed, no Washington base override is passed), every standing work-years fixture carries no banked loss, and none of them moved; the stored record likewise enters no carryforward, and its anchors reproduce bit-identically (below). ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE (re-derived exactly in the settlement, pinned in a fixture): 2026, married filing jointly, age 45, $100,000 salary, no other income, no gains, a $10,000 entering long-term carryforward. The contribution stack is $24,500 of deferral plus the $8,750 family HSA ($33,250), so taxable wages are $66,750 and taxable income before the allowance is $66,750 − $32,200 = $34,550. Before this fix the year's tax was $3,650.00 (10% × $24,800 + 12% × $9,750); after it, the §1211(b) allowance takes the $3,000 cap, taxable income is $31,550, and the tax is $3,290.00 ($2,480 + 12% × $6,750) — a $360.00 overstatement corrected. The allowance used is min($3,000, $34,550) = $3,000, so the carryforward handed to the following year is $7,000, not $10,000; the settlement's precision note stands — in a no-gain following year the allowance is $3,000 under either balance, so the error the fix removes is in the carry-out balance itself (the year after would have entered with $4,000 against a wrongly carried $7,000), not in a second year's tax figure. REGRESSION FIXTURES: two new tax fixtures named for the mechanism. The first pins the acceptance example end to end — the standalone line's $3,290.00 tax, its claimed and used allowance, and its $7,000 long-term carry-out; the no-carryforward control at the pre-fix $3,650.00; the one-year roll's rolled inputs carrying the consumed $7,000; and a two-year leg proving the threading itself (the second work year enters with $7,000, prices the same tax, and hands the march $4,000). ## Build v99 (2026-10-29): Engine-calendar fix F6 — the Retirement engines price the end-age year, aligned to the plan march's inclusive horizon

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change. Final group of the engine-calendar fix program (finding F6, from the settled round-13 audit): the two engine families counted a plan's span differently. The plan march loops while the primary's age is at or below the end age, applying a growth step at each loop tail, so the end-age year is priced and the ending balance is the value after that year; the Retirement engines ran one growth step per year of the plain age difference, so the ending balance was the value entering the end age — one priced year short on every span, and the same span produced different year counts on different surfaces. Neither loop was internally mis-indexed; the defect was the cross-surface convention mismatch. CONVENTION DECISION (fixed by the brief): the plan march's convention wins — the end-age year is priced and its return is applied — and the Retirement engines are aligned to it. The plan march itself is untouched, and its stored-record anchors reproduce bit-identically (below), confirming no Roth-side figure moved. CORRECTION: one shared helper in the Retirement engines file now derives the priced-year count as the age span plus one, and every end-age-bound loop takes its count from it, so the surfaces cannot drift apart again. LOOPS AUDITED, ONE BY ONE: the detailed simulator behind the Projection tab — aligned; its success-only twin behind the solver's feasibility checks — aligned, so the twin cannot disagree with the simulator; the Historical engine — aligned (its start-year window arithmetic follows the same count: a window must now fit one more year of dataset, so one fewer start year fits on every span, and its dataset-bound check keeps its form); the Monte Carlo engine — aligned (each run now draws one more return from the seeded stream); the Max Spending solver's guardrails scan — its return sequences are built from the same count and aligned, and its winner is re-priced through the aligned engines; the solver's search loops themselves iterate over spending steps, not years, and are unaffected; the solver's pre-retirement window count inside the scan — WINDOW-BOUND, NOT END-AGE-BOUND, left unchanged and documented in code: it counts the years strictly before the first retired year to find the best balance at retirement, the year at the retirement age is a retired year rather than a pre-retirement one, and its horizon cap binds only when retirement is at or past the end age, a combination the solver refuses at entry. ENTRY GUARDS (checked, deliberately unchanged): the input builder's refusal of an end age at or below the current age and the solver's refusal of a retirement age at or past the end age are input-validity guards, not horizon loops — they keep their form, so no save-path or stored-record behaviour changes shape; every plan the app accepts prices one more year than before, and no previously refused plan becomes accepted or the reverse. CALLERS BUILDING RETURN STREAMS (aligned with the engines): the fixture runner's projection stream, the baseline-results action's projection stream, and the Retirement view's own stream lengths for the current plan and for scenario projections all take the inclusive count. UI COPY: the Retirement view's stated year count for a plan (the Historical explainer's sequence length and the no-fitting-run message) now derives from the inclusive count and is correct as written; the two median final-year spending labels, which named the final year as the end age minus one under the old convention, now name the end age itself, which is the final priced year; the projection chart's final point is the after-final-year balance, one age past the end age, exactly as the ending balance is defined; the phased strategy's miniature age-axis span in the view is an axis bound (it positions ages along a line), not a priced-year count, and is genuinely unaffected, left unchanged. TRINITY BENCHMARK (checked, not re-pinned): the anchor case's span now prices one year more than the published payout period it is compared against, so one fewer overlapping window fits the dataset and both mixes' rates are one-year-longer rates set against the published figures — a further explainable-by-method difference, documented at the anchor itself; the case inputs, the published figures, and the tolerance are unchanged, and both mixes still land within the tolerance under the new window arithmetic. REGRESSION FIXTURES: two new projection fixtures named for the mechanism pin the re-derived pure-growth examples exactly — a no-spending balance at a steady return growing by one factor per priced year over the shorter span to the end age and over the longer span to a later end age, at the counts the closed form gives — and a new tax fixture, also named for the mechanism, pins the plan march's own figures for the identical inputs and spans, so the cross-surface equality this fix exists for is itself under test; the march fixture's figures are the untouched engine's pre-existing output, re-derived from the closed form. FIXTURE MOVEMENT (expected, not a defect — enumerated so the push-time diff review can tell convention movement from accidental repricing): of the pre-existing Retirement fixtures, fifty-seven moved and four did not. By group: sixteen of seventeen projection cases moved (the one unmoved case depletes to zero and stays zero), every one of the thirteen historical cases moved, every one of the eleven Monte Carlo cases moved, and seventeen of eighteen solver cases moved (the one unmoved solver case's added year is fully funded by income at its solved figure, so its answer is unchanged). Two display-delta cases run no engine and did not move. Causes, per group: projection endings move by exactly the added year — that year's withdrawal priced and its return applied, no more and no less; historical cases move by the added year in every run plus one fewer fitting window on every span (each case's run count falls by exactly one, and four cases' worst start years move to a neighbouring window); Monte Carlo cases move by the added year plus the seeded stream shift the extra draw per run causes, so their figures move by more than one growth step — that is the stream working as designed, not a second change; solver answers move by small steps in either direction as the longer horizon re-prices feasibility. Boundary consequences, recorded in the affected cases' notes: the two at-risk boundary cases that previously landed just above their cutoffs now land just below them under the longer horizon, and their siblings already pinned the below side, so the pair now pins the below side twice — the cases keep their original identifiers as history and their notes say so; the guardrails equality and genuine-crossing cases each gain a hand-derived added year in their notes, with the pinned discriminating years unchanged; and the solver case that was a one-year plan before this fix is now a two-year plan whose solved figure halves, re-derived by hand in its note from the rail mechanics of the added year. RE-DERIVATION STANDARD: every moved value was verified by an independent from-scratch reimplementation of the affected engines (built outside the repository, from the documented rules and the published historical dataset) agreeing to the cent on every projection, historical, Monte Carlo, and solver case — no expected value was copied from the live engine's output unverified, and several solver notes' stated next-step rates were recomputed and corrected where the longer horizon moved them. ## Build v98 (2026-10-29): Engine-calendar fix F5 — salary years price required minimum distributions on the prior year-end pre-tax balance through the shared helper

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change and no UI copy change. Group 4 of the engine-calendar fix program (finding F5, from the settled round-13 audit): the salary-year pricer passed a zero required minimum distribution unconditionally, so a work year at or past RMD age priced no distribution at all — the year's ordinary income and tax were understated, and no distribution ever left the pre-tax balance during the salary years — while the plan engine computes each owner's distribution through the shared helper from that owner's age and prior year-end balance. CORRECTION — the salary-year pricer and the work-years roll now compute and route the distribution exactly as the plan march does, reusing the same helper rather than any second implementation: no divisor table is re-implemented and no second age table exists. Each owner's distribution is computed per owner on that owner's own clock and that owner's own prior year-end balance: the primary's distribution is selected on the plan's sole-beneficiary fact for the primary, and the spouse's distribution on the plan's sole-beneficiary fact for the spouse with the roles swapped, each read from the same plan inputs the march reads, so the Joint-versus-Uniform selection — the Joint table only when the owner's spouse is the sole beneficiary and strictly more than ten years younger than the owner, the Uniform table otherwise — is the march's own rule applied by the shared helper. DIVISOR-SELECTION FALLBACK (documented because the brief requires an explicit one): no fallback beyond the helper's own rule is needed and none was invented — the salary-year path carries every input the march's selection reads (both birth years and both beneficiary facts); where a fact is absent — the spouse's beneficiary fact is an optional input — the march's own rule applies inside the helper: only an explicit affirmation selects the Joint table and anything else prices the Uniform table, and a household with no spouse birth year prices no spouse distribution at all. PRIOR-BALANCE TRACKING: the roll threads each owner's prior year-end pre-tax balance into every year's pricing, so contributions made during a year never count toward that year's distribution — they count only toward the next year's — exactly as the plan prices; the year's ending balance is the post-distribution balance grown by the year's return with the year's own contributions landing after the growth, preserving the same ordering. A standalone single-year price with no threaded context prices distributions on the plan's starting balances, the same opening-balance convention the taxable context already uses for yields. DISTRIBUTION ROUTING (mirrored from the march, no new routing invented): the distribution is ordinary income inside the shared single-year pricer exactly as the march feeds it; it leaves the pre-tax balance before growth exactly as the march's does; and its cash joins the year's surplus on the same footing as Social Security benefits — it funds the year's spending and taxes through the existing surplus-and-deficit machinery, leftovers bank into Taxable through that machinery, and a deficit year needs that much less in deficit sales — with the year's distribution totals and divisor provenance reported on the work-year line for the roll to consume. STILL-WORKING LIMITATION (named exactly as the settlement states it): no still-working exception is priced, because the engine cannot distinguish employer-plan balances from IRA balances — pre-tax is one aggregated balance per owner — so a qualifying employer-plan-only household that could correctly owe nothing will be priced with distributions; the plan engine has the identical limitation and its computation is unchanged. UNAFFECTED CASES: years below RMD age price a zero distribution on both clocks, so any roll whose work years end before either owner reaches RMD age is bit-identical to before, and no other surface changes — the plan march, the single-year pricer, and the December console are untouched, and the work-years comparison's response shape is unchanged (the new line fields are internal to the roll). REGRESSION FIXTURE: a new tax fixture named for the mechanism pins the re-derived example end to end — three work years ending at the first RMD age, the first two pricing no distribution, the RMD year's prior year-end balance built from the starting balance plus two years of the year's pre-tax contribution stack (the RMD year's own contributions excluded), the distribution at the Uniform divisor for that age, the resulting tax on the stated wage, contribution, and deduction facts, and the quit-age balances showing the distribution left the pre-tax balance while its after-tax cash banked — together with a standalone leg proving a single priced year on the same starting balance derives the same distribution, joint legs proving the Joint table selects on the sole-beneficiary fact with a spouse more than ten years younger and the Uniform table prices when the fact is off, and a spouse leg proving the second owner's distribution prices on her own clock and her own balance while the primary is below RMD age. ACCEPTANCE: three consecutive clean internal review passes; typechecks for both bundles; the tax census in fine slices totalling every fixture in the suite, each slice with its teeth check passing (the packaged runner's own coarser slice was killed for memory, the standing limitation, and the same fixtures passed in the finer slices); the extended, December, UI-state, Roth CAS, retirement CAS, and retirement suites green; the packaged harness green across its main-process checks with the integrity checks at zero violations; and the stored-record anchors — the compare run from the stored record with no scenario overrides — reproduced bit-identically on all four anchor figures, confirming the plan march did not move. The added text contains no first names and no hard-coded dollar figures (figures live in fixtures, described qualitatively in prose). API_CONTRACT_VERSION 97 → 98.

## Build v97 (2026-10-29): Engine-calendar fixes F3+F4 — the single-year pricer's IRMAA block counts participants by premium-year age and grades under the premium year's law row

All user-entered data, no external source; no schema change and no UI copy change. Group 3 of the engine-calendar fix program (findings F3 and F4, from the settled round-13 audit), built together because both live in the same block of the single-year pricer and both are the same class of calendar error: the block priced a premium two years ahead using facts from the wrong year. F3 — the participant count came from the priced year's Medicare flags, so a person who reaches Medicare age only in the premium year counted for nothing and the block reported no surcharge at all for a premium year in which they are on Medicare; the plan engine counts participants by age in the premium year, with a two-year MAGI lookback and the premium year's law row. F4 — independently, the tier was graded and the surcharge priced under the priced year's law row: the shared classifier had already graded the priced MAGI under that row, and the per-person amount was read from it too, so thresholds and rates alike followed the source year, while the plan grades the lookback MAGI under the premium year's row (the carried-forward newest row when the premium year is past the table).
