- Washington capital-gains excise (T3 build, 2026-10-20): RCW 82.87 — an excise on an individual's Washington capital gains, priced by `waCapitalGainsTax` in `server/src/taxEngine.ts` for a plan or Playground year whose state of residence is Washington, INSTEAD of the flat state rate (the flat rate remains the fallback for every other residence). Carried as dated law-row data on each year's row in `taxLaw.ts` (waStandardDeduction / waRatePct / waAdditionalRatePct / waAdditionalThreshold / waCharitableThreshold / waCharitableCap). The base is Washington capital gains: the individual's adjusted (long-term) capital gain as modified by the deductions of RCW 82.87.060 (RCW 82.87.020(16)) — in the engine, the year's realized long-term gains from taxable-account sales. Retirement-account assets are exempt (RCW 82.87.050) and qualified dividends are not capital gains, so neither enters the base; neither do Social Security benefits. Base rate 7% (RCW 82.87.040(1)(a)); from January 1, 2025 an additional 2.9% applies to the portion of Washington capital gains exceeding $1,000,000 (RCW 82.87.040(1)(b), ESSB 5813, ch. 421, Laws of 2025) — the WA Department of Revenue's tiered statement: the first $1,000,000 of TAXABLE Washington capital gains at 7%, the excess at a combined 9.9%. The $1,000,000 threshold is not among the amounts RCW 82.87.150 adjusts annually, so it is statutory and unindexed — carried as a fixed $1,000,000 in every row, and (build v61, correcting the earlier statement here that it was "not deflated") the pricer DEFLATES it in today's-dollars projections for each year the priced year runs past the law row it prices under, like the statute-fixed federal thresholds; the standard deduction and charitable amounts ARE RCW 82.87.150-indexed and price at their nominal row values. Standard deduction (RCW 82.87.060(1)): statutory base $250,000 (one combined amount for spouses/domestic partners, RCW 82.87.120(4)), adjusted annually under RCW 82.87.150; DOR-published adjusted amounts: $270,000 for 2024, $278,000 for 2025. Charitable donation deduction (RCW 82.87.080): donations to qualified organizations above the year's minimum qualifying amount (DOR publishes it as the same amount as the standard deduction), capped — DOR-published caps $108,000 for 2024 and $111,000 for 2025. A year with Washington capital gains below zero owes $0 and carries nothing forward (RCW 82.87.040(3)). The qualified family-owned small business deduction (RCW 82.87.070) is not priced — the engine has no input for it. 2026 ROW DISCLOSURE: DOR had published no 2026 adjusted amounts when this build was sourced (October 2026; its published table runs through 2025), so the 2026 row carries the 2025 amounts ($278,000 / $278,000 / $111,000) forward unchanged under the table's today's-dollars convention — a disclosed carry-forward, not a published 2026 figure.
  Primary sources (verbatim): RCW 82.87.040 — https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/law/RCW/RCW%20%2082%20%20TITLE/RCW%20%2082%20.%2087%20%20CHAPTER/RCW%20%2082%20.%2087%20.040.htm ; full chapter RCW 82.87 (definitions §.020, exemptions §.050, deductions §.060, charitable §.080, annual adjustments §.150) — https://app.leg.wa.gov/rcw/default.aspx?cite=82.87&full=true ; WA Department of Revenue, Capital gains tax page (published standard-deduction and charitable amounts by year) — https://dor.wa.gov/taxes-rates/other-taxes/capital-gains-tax?sourceid=1133970&emci=1168eedd-0d5d-ec11-94f6-0050f2e65e9b&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001&ceid=173477 ; WA Department of Revenue special notice, "New tiered rates for Washington's capital gains tax" (June 30, 2025) — https://dor.wa.gov/forms-publications/publications-subject/special-notices/new-tiered-rates-washingtons-capital-gains-tax
  Spot checks: the DOR special notice's tiered statement ("first $1 million in taxable Washington capital gains … 7% … exceeding $1 million … plus an additional 2.9%") matches the fixture arithmetic in `t3-wa-boundary`; the DOR page's 2025 amounts match the 2025 law row.
- SALT cap for itemized deductions (T5 build, 2026-10-21): IRC §164(b)(6) as amended by §70120 of Public Law 119-21 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act). Carried as dated law-row data on each year's row in `taxLaw.ts` (saltCap / saltCapFloor / saltPhaseOutStart / saltPhaseOutRatePct), priced by the greater-of deduction step in `priceYear` (`server/src/taxEngine.ts`): each priced year deducts the greater of its standard deduction (base + §63(f) age-65+ additional amounts) and its itemized total, where the state-and-local-taxes component is first capped at the row's cap. Statutory figures: for 2025 the cap is $40,000 ($20,000 married filing separately — no MFS row exists in this engine, the same posture the T4 fixtures take), reduced by 30% of modified AGI over $500,000 but not below $10,000; for 2026–2029 the cap and the phase-down start are 101% of the prior year's ($40,400 and $505,000 for 2026), the 30% rate and $10,000 floor unchanged; for tax years after 2029 the cap reverts to $10,000 with no phase-down — a future dated row will carry that when a 2030 table is sourced (no URL is asserted for the statute text in this plan because this build ran with no web access; the citation is the Code section and the amending section of the Public Law). Modified AGI for the phase-down adds back only the §§911/931/933 foreign-income exclusions (§164(b)(6) flush language), which the engine does not model, so the phase-down runs on AGI; tax-exempt interest is NOT added back (contrast §86/§1411 MAGI). The cap figures are statutory and unindexed, so — like the NIIT threshold and the §151(d)(5)(C) senior-deduction figures — they deflate at the plan's inflation rate for each year the priced year runs past the law row it prices under; in a row's own year they apply exactly as published. The temporary senior deduction (§151(d)(5)(C), 2025–2028) is allowed whether or not the filer itemizes, so it is added on top of whichever side of the greater-of wins and is never part of the comparison; the §63(f) age-65+ additional amounts belong to the standard side only.
- Education credits (T6 build, 2026-10-21): IRC §25A — the American Opportunity Tax Credit (§25A(b)) and the Lifetime Learning Credit (§25A(c)), computed on Form 8863 (see also IRS Topic No. 313, "Education credits"). Carried as dated law-row data on each year's row in `taxLaw.ts` (aotcTier1RatePct / aotcTier1Expenses / aotcTier2RatePct / aotcTier2Expenses / aotcRefundablePct / llcRatePct / llcExpenseCap / eduPhaseOutStart / eduPhaseOutWidth), priced by `educationCreditsFor` inside `priceYear` (`server/src/taxEngine.ts`) from the household's entered per-student, per-calendar-year qualified expenses (`educationStudents`) — entered, never inferred from 529 balances, the college-years span, or any other saved field; the household's per-student aotcEligible mark is its own declaration (the engine prices credit math and phase-outs, not enrollment eligibility). Statutory figures (identical in the 2025 and 2026 rows — §25A amounts are not inflation-indexed): AOTC per eligible student = 100% of the first $2,000 of that student's qualified expenses plus 25% of the next $2,000 of those expenses (§25A(b)(1)), a $2,500 maximum per student (the §25A(b)(2) eligible-student definition is the household's to apply — the engine prices from its mark); 40% of the AOTC is refundable (§25A(i)(1)–(2); the §25A(i)(2) exceptions — a student with a felony drug conviction, and a taxpayer under 24 whose earned income is under half their support — are not separately modeled: a named limitation, with the household's eligibility mark governing). LLC = 20% of the first $10,000 of qualified expenses per RETURN (§25A(c)(1)–(2)). Coordination (§25A(g)(2) flush rule and the Form 8863 allocation): the same student's expenses cannot support both credits — the engine prices both statutory allocations (AOTC for the eligible students + LLC over the remaining students' expenses; LLC alone over all students) and takes the larger total benefit, naming the choice in every year output. Phase-out (§25A(d)): both credits reduce ratably as modified AGI runs through $160,000–$180,000 MFJ / $80,000–$90,000 otherwise; MAGI adds back only the §§911/931/933 foreign-income exclusions (§25A(d)(3)), which the engine does not model, so the phase-out runs on AGI and tax-exempt interest is NOT added back. Form 8863 rounds the phase-out ratio to three decimals; the engine uses the exact ratio, its standing treatment of statutory ratios (the §86 and §151(d)(5)(C) phase-outs price the same way). Application ordering (Form 1040): the nonrefundable portion (the AOTC remainder plus the LLC) reduces the year's income tax (ordinary + capital-gains tax) but never below $0 of income tax and never offsets the §1411 NIIT, which arrives afterward as an other tax (Schedule 2); the refundable AOTC portion is reported separately per year and lifetime and is credited in the plan score identity beside the ACA premium credit — never netted into a floored federal tax. All §25A dollar figures are statutory and unindexed, so — like the NIIT thresholds and the SALT cap — the expense caps and the phase-out range deflate at the plan's inflation rate for each year the priced year runs past the law row it prices under; in a row's own year they apply exactly as published. No URL is asserted for the statute text in this plan because this build ran with no web access; the citations are the Code sections (§25A(b), (c), (d), (g), (i)) and Form 8863 / Topic No. 313.
- Alternative minimum tax (T7 build, 2026-10-21): IRC §55, computed on Form 6251 (the tentative tax's capital-gain computation is Form 6251 Part III, the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet treatment). Carried as dated law-row data on each year's row in `taxLaw.ts` (amtExemption / amtPhaseOutStart / amtPhaseOutRatePct / amtBreakpoint / amtRateLowPct / amtRateHighPct), priced by `amtFor` inside `priceYear` (`server/src/taxEngine.ts`) from the year's own priced quantities — no AMT input exists and none is invented. Figures: 2025 (IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40) — exemption $137,000 MFJ / $88,100 unmarried individuals (single and head of household; §55(d)(1)(B) gives head of household the unmarried amount), phase-out from $1,252,700 MFJ / $626,350 unmarried at the long-standing 25% rate (§55(d)(2)), the 28% rate on the taxable excess over $239,100 (§55(b)(1)); 2026 (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32) — exemption $140,200 / $90,100, phase-out from $1,000,000 / $500,000 at 50% (the reset enacted by §70107 of Public Law 119-21, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, amending §55(d)), the 28% rate over $244,500. Cross-check used at build time: each row reproduces its published complete-phase-out amount as phase-out start + exemption ÷ phase-out rate (2025 MFJ $1,252,700 + $548,000 = $1,800,700; 2026 MFJ $1,000,000 + $280,400 = $1,280,400; 2026 unmarried $500,000 + $180,200 = $680,200). Core scope (Decision Point 8 of the expansion spec): AMTI starts from the year's regular taxable income and adds back only the §56(b)(1) adjustments the engine has quantities for — the SALT deduction actually taken (the itemized SALT after the §164(b)(6) cap) in an itemized year, and the standard deduction in a standard year; the §151(d)(5)(C) senior deduction is not an AMT adjustment and is not added back. The tentative tax preserves the preferential 0% / 15% / 20% rates on long-term gains and qualified dividends (§55(b)(3): the 26% / 28% rates apply to the taxable excess reduced by the capital-gain amount, and the gains are taxed on the capital-gain staircase stacked on the remainder). AMT owed = max(0, tentative minimum tax − regular income tax after nonrefundable credits); the §1411 NIIT is not part of the comparison (it never appears on Form 6251) and is added beside the AMT. All §55 figures are inflation-indexed and published per year, so — like the brackets and the standard deduction — they do NOT deflate under the today's-dollars carry-forward. NAMED LIMITATIONS (not modeled; the engine has no inputs for them and invents none): the incentive-stock-option bargain element (§56(b)(3)), tax-exempt interest from private-activity bonds (§57(a)(5)), depreciation differences (§56(a)(1) / (g)), other §56(a) recomputations, the AMT foreign tax credit, and the §53 credit for prior-year minimum tax. Sources consulted at build time for the published figures: the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 and Rev. Proc. 2024-40 AMT tables as published at https://www.taxnotes.com/research/federal/reference-tables/amt-exemption-amounts/2zf7h (retrieved 2026-10-21; the underlying citations are the revenue procedures themselves and IRC §55).
- 2026 deduction trio (Build A, 2026-10-22): three deduction rules from Public Law 119-21 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act), effective for tax years beginning after December 31, 2025 — law years 2026 and later only; a year priced under the 2025 law row takes none of the three. Carried as law data in `taxLaw.ts` (`DEDUCTION_2026`: firstYear, charitableFloorRatePct, nonItemizerCharitableCap, section68Numerator / section68Denominator) plus the year's own bracket row (the §68 threshold), priced by the deduction step in `priceYear` (`server/src/taxEngine.ts`) in statutory order. (1) Charitable floor for itemizers, IRC §170(b)(1)(I): the charitable component of the itemized total is the household's single aggregate charitable input reduced by 0.5% of the contribution base — the engine's AGI (no NOL carryback is modeled) — floored at $0; floor-disallowed amounts do NOT carry forward. (2) §68 limitation, applied AFTER all other limitations (the §164(b)(6) SALT cap, the charitable floor and ceilings, the mortgage rules; home mortgage interest is NOT exempt — the 2025 amendment removed the old carve-outs): the otherwise-allowable itemized total is reduced by 2/37 of the lesser of (a) the itemized total or (b) the amount by which (taxable income determined without regard to §68, increased by the itemized total) exceeds the dollar threshold where the 37% bracket begins for the filing status and law year, read from the law row's bracket data (the top of the 35% bracket; $768,700 MFJ in 2026). The reduced total is the itemized side of the greater-of comparison; the AMT tentative computation keeps using the unreduced figures (AMTI is priced from the taxable income without regard to §68). (3) Non-itemizer charitable deduction, IRC §170(p): when the standard side wins, the charitable input is deductible up to $2,000 MFJ / $1,000 single or head of household; married filing separately is $500 — an ASSUMED figure (the Code's usual halving of the single amount), named as assumed in the API contract; this engine prices no MFS status, so it never prices. Simplifications, all named in the API contract (build v25, itemizedDeductionSemantics): the single charitable input carries no cash/property split, so the whole input is treated as cash contributions for §170(p); the floor never applies to §170(p); §170(p) is placed ABOVE THE LINE (a judgment call — it reduces AGI and therefore MAGI and ACA MAGI; the alternative below-the-line placement, an addition to the standard deduction, is named in the contract); the §151(d)(5)(C) senior-deduction phase-out runs on the AGI the winning side reports; the §86 taxable-benefits amount is struck before §170(p) and not re-struck. Fixtures: the t8-* cases in `server/src/taxFixtures.ts`, hand-derived from the statute and the settlement acceptance probes, plus re-derived T5 (b)/(c)/(g)/(i) and T7 (a)/(g) pins whose cases the new law reprices. One probe figure did not survive independent recomputation: the §68 probe's federal tax was printed as $257,164.41, but the 2026 MFJ bracket arithmetic on its own taxable income ($905,405.41) gives $257,164.50 — the fixture pins the derived figure and names the 9-cent slip. No URL is asserted for the statute text in this plan because this build ran with no web access; the citations are the Code sections (§170(b)(1)(I), §170(p), §68) and Public Law 119-21.

(Pre-E2 the grid covered only owner 72–85 × spouse 60–75 and clamped outside pairs to the nearest covered cell — 70/60 read 28.8 (the clamped 72/60 cell) against the true 29.2, and 90/80 read 16.0 (the clamped 85/75 cell) against the true 12.2.)
- Non-indexed figures (Social Security §86 provisional-income thresholds, NIIT thresholds $250k MFJ / $200k single-HOH) are statutory and deflated in the engine by the plan's inflation input, one deflation step for each year the priced year runs past the law row it prices under (its own row deflates zero steps; a carried-forward year deflates once per year past the newest row). The frozen top IRMAA tier floor is deflated only for the steps through 2028 counted from the row's year (the deflation years are capped at the 2028 step — the floor is fixed through 2028, then inflation-indexed), per the modeling convention disclosed on the Roth Conversion screen.

## 2026-11-08 — Playground projection honors a typed first-year sale basis (ChatGPT SHOULD-2)

- The projection walk (`projectPlaygroundYears` in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) no longer overwrites a KNOWN sale's typed lot basis in its first walked year with the harvest pool's tracked ratio. In the first walked year a positive template sale basis stands; from the second year on, the repeated sale is a modeled sale and retires basis at the pool's tracked ratio, as before. A first-year sale with no typed basis (blank reads zero) still takes the pool ratio, exactly as before, so a plan without a typed first-year sale basis does not move.
- The pool ledger already retires the priced basis after each year, so in year 1 it now retires the typed amount — the lot's basis is not counted again in later years, and the second year's pool ratio reflects the corrected retirement.
- New fixture `tax-engines-playground-projection-first-year-typed-sale-basis` in server/src/taxFixtures.ts (main leg: full-basis lot with harvest facts; control leg: no typed basis; edge leg: typed basis larger than the pool's basis dollars). Built on the shared fictional sample household only.
- Verification: regression gate zero differing leaves across the fixed set; December suite green; full tax census green (589/589, new fixture counted).

## 2026-11-08 — Playground projection stops repeating a received RMD (ChatGPT SHOULD-3)

- The projection walk (`projectPlaygroundYears` in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) no longer repeats a received RMD into every walked year. The received amount is a one-year fact: from the second walked year on, the recurring other ordinary income drops the received amount and the netting input is zero, so the walked year prices its own gross RMD whole. The first walked year prices the template whole, exactly as before. While the walked gross RMD stays above the received amount the two halves cancel exactly as before, so those years do not move; only years whose gross RMD falls below the received amount change — the phantom repeat is gone.
- New fixture `tax-engines-playground-projection-received-rmd-one-year` in server/src/taxFixtures.ts (main leg: account emptied in year 1, year 2 prices nothing; non-empty leg: gross RMD stays above the received amount, year 2 bit-identical; control leg: no received RMD). Built on the shared fictional sample household only.
- Verification: regression gate zero differing leaves across the fixed set; December suite green (96/96); full tax census green (590/590, new fixture counted; P-S4 leg A re-pinned as part of this build — its year-2 net RMD and zeroed counterfactual now pin the corrected decomposition).

## 2026-11-08 — Playground projection resolves the marketplace premium tier per year (ChatGPT SHOULD-1)

- The projection walk (`projectPlaygroundYears` in server/src/rothOptimizer.ts) now resolves the marketplace premium per walked year from the two tiers the template carries — the household amount while both spouses are on the marketplace, the single amount while exactly one is — the plan march's own per-year resolution. Before, the template carried only the one marketplace amount and the walk spread it into every year, so a spouse-only year priced the two-person premium. The enrollment premium resolves to the same amount, so the retained-credit cap keys on the year's own tier.
- The template carries both tiers as new optional facts (`healthPremiumAcaHouseholdAnnual` / `healthPremiumAcaSingleAnnual` on `PlaygroundYearInputs`, stored through `projTemplateCore.ts` and the stored parse in `rothUiStateCore.ts`, supplied by `buildPgInputs` in the Playground view from the dial for the template year's own tier and the record for the other). A template with neither tier entered keeps the old spread, so an older stored template (whose tier fields parse null) reprices bit-identically. When the term is active but the applicable tier was never entered, the year's gross falls back to the template's benchmark — the march's own fallback for a null tier amount; the fallback reads the template's benchmark, and the walk does not resolve benchmarks per year (a pre-existing gap, out of scope here), so the fallback matches the march's rule in kind, not in amount, until that gap is closed.
- Known boundary: a pasted year's tiers are not carried by the paste payload (it carries only the one marketplace amount, as before), so a pasted template re-derives its tiers from the record in `buildPgInputs`, exactly as a prefilled template does.
- New fixture `tax-engines-playground-projection-premium-tier-transition` in server/src/taxFixtures.ts (main leg: both tiers, first transition year at the primary's Medicare birthday; household-only leg: null single tier falls back to the template's benchmark; single-only leg: null household tier; no-premium leg; old-template leg: dial alone spreads as before; reload leg: stored template round-trips identically through the stored parse). Built on the shared fictional sample household only. The extended-fixtures legacy-shape test now also pins the two tier fields at their no-fact values for a pre-tier stored blob.
- Verification: regression gate zero differing leaves across the fixed set; December suite green (96/96); full tax census green (592/592, new fixture counted); extended fixtures green (161/161).

## 2026-11-09 — "Smoothed bills paid" tap opens the settlement-basis breakdown (ChatGPT round-9 SHOULD-2)

- The Smoothed spend breakdown's "Smoothed bills paid this month" line no longer opens the Transactions list filtered to that month's transactions carrying a smoothed-bill link. That filter is on the charge-month basis and cannot show the figure: the figure counts a smoothed bill in the month its money left checking (the settlement month), so for a bill charged to a card the counted transaction is the later checking card payment — which carries no bill link — while the linked card charge sits in the earlier charge month, where the figure counts nothing. The tap now toggles a breakdown panel directly under the Smoothed spend breakdown, following the Slice & dice drill-down's panel pattern (title, close button, line list footing to a Total). The panel states the settlement rule in plain words and lists the month's settlement lines; a month with no settlement shows an explicit nothing-settled message over a zero total, so a charge is never presented as paid in its charge month.
- Server and core: the spending core's FIFO settlement walk (the one that totals the settled-lumps / yearly-paid-out figure) now also yields one line per attribution — a bill paid straight from checking at its full amount, the portion of a checking card payment attributed to one outstanding card charge, or a negative refund-reversal line in the refund's own month — and each month's lines foot exactly to that month's settled total by construction. Transactions optionally carry their id and description into the core for these lines (display only; no total reads them). The existing read action behind the explorer's month drill-down now also returns these lines: a card-payment line's amount is the attributed portion, with the payment's full amount and the settled charge's amount carried as separate context fields, so a payment that settles several bills, or only part of one charge, is never footed at its full amount. The explorer's yearly-paid-out drill composes its lines from the same breakdown (it previously showed the aggregate as a single line), so both surfaces show the same lines for the same month. The dashboard's edit invalidation now also refreshes the breakdown read.
- Scope held: no priced figure, engine, schema, stored format, or other tap changed. The Transactions list's own filtered rendering remains as it was — including the separate known behaviour that the breakdown's cash-out tap does not clear that filter, deliberately untouched by this build — and its filtered notice now states that it lists transactions by their recorded month and points to the breakdown for the settlement basis. The API contract stays at its current version: the only contract change is one additive field on an existing read action's response.
- Verification (completed): the project build is clean, typechecking client and server. The extended accuracy suite is green in full, including one new fixture pinning the breakdown lines on a synthetic multi-bill dataset (a checking-paid bill, one card payment settling two charges in full and a third in part, a refund reversal, and a later payment counting only the still-outstanding portion of its amount; the charge month has no lines and a zero total, and every month's lines foot to its settled total). The review's worked example was then driven live on the staged build's sandbox copy (synthetic rows only, never shipped): with an annual bill charged to a card in one month and a checking card payment settling it the next, the settlement month's dashboard figure is the full amount and tapping it opened the panel showing the card-payment line — naming the bill it settles and the earlier charge as context — over a total footing exactly to the tapped figure; the charge month's figure is zero and tapping it opened the panel's nothing-settled state at a zero total, with the charge nowhere presented as that month's paid amount. The same months read through the drill-down action agree line for line. No console errors at phone width during the live drive.

## 2026-11-09 — Quick view tooltip: Escape really dismisses it (ChatGPT round-9 NICE-7)

- In the Quick view summary cards, the ⓘ badge tooltip (the QuickTile component in client/src/App.tsx, shared by all six tiles) could not be dismissed with Escape by a keyboard user: focusing the badge shows the tooltip through the hovered state, but Escape only cleared the parent's pinned-open state — and the document keydown listener was only attached while pinned — so after Escape the tooltip stayed on screen while the badge's aria-expanded, which was wired to the pinned state alone, read false. The component now carries a dismissed state, set by Escape: tooltip visibility is (pinned-open or hovered) and not dismissed. The document Escape listener is attached whenever the tooltip is showing, pinned or hover-shown; on Escape it clears the pin through the parent's close callback, clears hovered, and sets dismissed, so the tooltip hides and stays hidden while focus remains on the badge, even if the parent's open state lags. Dismissed is cleared only on a fresh deliberate activation or a fresh hover/focus entry — badge mouse-enter, badge focus, badge click/tap (cleared before the toggle), and tooltip-panel mouse-enter — so moving the pointer away and back, tabbing away and back, or tapping the badge reopens it, while merely keeping focus on the badge after Escape does not. The badge's aria-expanded now derives from actual visibility. Tap-to-pin toggling, outside-tap close, hover-open, and panel-hover readability are unchanged.
- InfoTip (beside the "Actual average" label in the True cost section) was checked and left untouched: its keyboard path already clears pinned and hovered on Escape through the button's own keydown handler, and its aria-expanded already derives from its actual visibility. A mouse-hover-only Escape on InfoTip (hover with no focus, so its button-level keydown never fires) remains a known residual gap, out of this build's scope.
- Scope held: client-only, confined to QuickTile; no priced figure, engine, server, schema, or stored data changed.
- Verification (completed): regression gate — the fixed set (the December reference case plus the sample household's full plan priced through the compare and funding paths, per-year per-field to the cent) was priced on the tree as received and again after the change, with the intended change named in advance (the client-only tooltip-behaviour change above; no priced figure may differ): the two dumps are byte-identical, zero differing leaves across the whole set. Typecheck clean (client and server). Exit audit passed with no findings; its content review confirmed the Escape path, the visibility derivation, and that all six tiles share the fixed behaviour. The Escape sequence was then driven live in a real browser session on the staged build at desktop and phone widths, on the True cost tile and repeated on the Keep the lights on tile: focusing the badge opened the tooltip with aria-expanded true; Escape hid it, aria-expanded returned to false, and it stayed hidden on a further look with focus unmoved; tabbing away and back reopened it; at desktop width a fresh hover entry reopened it, hovering the tooltip panel itself kept it open and readable, and hovering away hid it; a click pinned it open, Escape while pinned hid it and it stayed hidden, a fresh click reopened it, a second click toggled it off, and with it pinned open an outside tap (on the month input) closed it; at phone width the tap sequence matched — tap pinned it open, Escape hid it and it stayed hidden, a fresh tap reopened it, a second tap toggled it off, and an outside tap closed a pinned tooltip. ### Follow-up — Engine hardening: cross-check harness + rounding sweep (check registry)
- Server-side only: new `server/src/hardening/` — an independent second implementation of the single-year tax math written from the law tables (not from engine source), a seeded deterministic household generator (seed 12345), a randomized differential (engine vs second implementation across tax, MAGI, credit, gains zones, IRMAA tiers), money-conservation invariants across trajectory years (funding footing, terminal-wealth identity, basis bounds, loss-ledger conservation), and a rounding sweep (cent-quantization pins + the cliff tolerance pin). Registry + runner: `registry.ts` (`runHardeningChecks("fast"|"full")`) and the committed bun script `run.ts` (`bun server/src/hardening/run.ts [--fast|--full]`); wired into `runAccuracySelfCheck` as the `hardening` suite (fast checks: invariants + a small seeded subset) via `server/src/actions.ts`.
- Verification — PASSED on the committed runner (2026-11-09, after the diagnosis and fixes below): both `bun server/src/hardening/run.ts --full` and `--fast` exited 0 with "3/3 checks passed; teeth pass (4 corrupted pins failed as expected)". The differential passed (2000 households, seed 12345: 0 mismatches across 144735 field comparisons. Coverage — IRMAA tiers 335/110/103/129/796/527; AMT>0 20, education 66, itemized 803, WA 520, over-cliff 1368, below-100%-FPL 81, loss years 201, NIIT>0 1278, gains-at-20% 324; within $100 of a boundary — IRMAA floor 36, cliff 10, bracket top 17, LTCG zero top 0.), the invariants passed ("Funding footing max residue 0c over 38 Do-Nothing rows + 38 Fill-12% rows; terminal-wealth identity max diff $0.01 over 3 marches (38 + 38 + 3 years); basis bounds + non-negativity over the same years; loss-ledger conservation over 2000 seeded cases; 0 violations."), and the rounding sweep passed ("Cent-quantization over 2000 households (seed 12345): 220882 money fields checked on both pricers, max deviation 1.49e-8 of a cent, 0 violations. Cliff pin: settled conversion lands MAGI exactly at the cliff, next $1 step over it, tolerance never changes the settled side; 0 violations."). Honest history: the first full run failed on 5 late-year basis rows (Do Nothing 2061–2063, Fill 12% 2062–2063) and the bound was corrected only after the omitted inflow was identified in the march code — the settlement's surplus-cash sweep in `settleYear` (server/src/taxEngine.ts): leftover cash income (RMD + Social Security + other ordinary + tax-exempt interest) beyond the year's spending need and the tax that cash pays is swept into Taxable and added to the basis ledger at 100% (`basisIn(surplusLeft)`), because it is after-tax money. The invariant's cumulative bound now counts that sweep exactly, reconstructed from the year's own exposed fields (the cash-in lines, the funding need, and the funding attribution's applied income); no tolerance was raised and no year is skipped. The generator's boundary targeting was also fixed in the same pass: boundary households now zero the other income components before `otherOrdinary` is set, so the targeted landing is reachable — below-100%-FPL coverage rose 0 → 81 and cliff proximity 1 → 10 (LTCG zero top proximity remains 0). Typecheck clean (`bun run typecheck`, exit 0, re-run by the push agent on the final tree). Regression gate clean on the final tree (0 diffs, 6,725 leaves, baseline hash matched). No engine pricing code changed. Push-agent note: the counts above are the push agent's fresh re-run, after two scrub-driven fixes — the two suite notes were reworded to present tense and the generator's RMD draw ceiling was lowered to a value outside the scrub patterns; the full run and the gate were re-executed from disk after those fixes.
- Two harness-side formulation errors found and fixed by the run itself (the engine was right in both cases): the basis-balance bound did not allow a market decline to leave basis above the shrunken balance (now a cumulative inflow bound governs declining paths), and the loss-ledger carry-out bound omitted the year's own loss as an inflow (now the carry-out is the total loss less the absorbed allowance, with the gains absorption pinned exactly). The boundary generator was likewise corrected so boundary households land near the cliff, the LTCG zero top, and below 100% FPL.

### Follow-up — Engine hardening: sensitivity review (check registry)
- Server-side only: six new `server/src/hardening/sens*.ts` modules registered in `registry.ts` (the registry grows from twenty checks to twenty-six; the `runAccuracySelfCheck` `hardening` suite picks the fast runs up with no wiring change beyond two description strings), plus one shared helper `sensCompareBase.ts` carrying the fictional sample household as a compare base and the conversion-cap ceiling presets. Each module prices a directional/monotonicity probe against the engine and carries its own teeth check (one pin corrupted, exactly that check fails): ending wealth non-decreasing in expected return and non-increasing in annual spending (Do Nothing ladders on the sample household); conversion-cap net-cost ordering stable across a nine-point perturbation grid (spending ±$1,000, return ±0.25%, corners), with a near-tie band inside which a pair may swap; the ACA credit non-increasing in MAGI across the cliff and in pre-tax draw at $1 steps through the December path; Monte Carlo never-out rates agreeing across seeds within four standard errors of binomial sampling noise; and the optimizer's return and heir-rate strips monotone in winner net cost.
- Adjudications and scope notes (all documented in the module headers): the credit is not monotone in MAGI across the 100% FPL edge (below it the credit is $0, at it the full credit appears), so the cliff check scopes its ladder to the cliff region only, by design. The Monte Carlo band is derived from sampling noise, not picked: a fixed ±3pt band would fail the engine's own measured seed spread, so the check asserts agreement within four standard errors (about six points at these rates). Winner names are never asserted on the strips — the return strip's winner legitimately changes brackets as the return moves. The caps check's near-tie band covers exactly one pair (Do Nothing / Fill 12%, the smallest base gap); every other pair's order is pinned strictly. One spending-ladder rung collided with a scrub pattern and was moved to a neighboring value before the build closed (the direction is unchanged and the ladder was re-measured after the move).
- Review pass 3 (NOT CLEAN — two SHOULDs, three NICEs) and their fixes: the teeth of three modules did not exercise their own pins (each used a side-channel assertion instead of corrupting its real comparison) — fixed by reversing the comparison inside the real loops (caps: first pinned pair, nine failures across the nine grid runs; cliff: first ladder pair, one failure; strips: every adjacent pair in both strips, six failures, with teeth now pricing the heir strip too). The caps near-tie exemption was unbounded (a large reversal of the exempt pair would have passed silently) — fixed so an exempt pair may swap only while its perturbed gap stays within the band; holding the order still passes at any gap width. The three NICEs (the Monte Carlo band wording is four standard errors of a single proportion, about 2.8 of the difference; the strips header understated the suite cost; small wording/duplication nits) are recorded, not fixed — NICEs need the user's pick. Passes 1–2 and the fixed code were re-verified (see the verification bullet).
- Verification — PASSED on the committed runner: both `bun server/src/hardening/run.ts --full` and `--fast` exit 0 with twenty-six of twenty-six checks passing and teeth passing (forty-four corrupted pins failed as expected). Regression gate clean (zero differing leaves across the full set, baseline hash matched). Typecheck clean. Scrub zero over the new modules, the shared helper, the registry and actions diffs, and this entry. No engine pricing code changed. Runtime note: the fast suite now takes about a minute (measured 66s fast / 87s full; the strips module re-runs the optimizer search and its teeth now re-prices both strips, about 18s) — still inside the 120-second worker cap. ## Follow-up (2026-11-10): ACA credit band edge classified in integer cents (ChatGPT round-10 F1)

Server-side engine fix, no client change, no API contract change. At exactly 133% of the federal poverty guideline, the ACA credit priced the lower band instead of the edge band's initial percentage, because the income-as-a-percentage-of-FPL comparison was computed in floating point and came out a hair below the edge for some household sizes. The fix classifies band edges in integer cents in all three places that price the credit: the engine (acaCreditFor in taxEngine.ts), the independent second implementation (independentAcaCredit.ts), and the boundary module's hand-derived expectation (deriveExpected in boundaryAca.ts) — the same three-line change in each, with the interpolation fraction and the reported percentage left on the float value. The three sites were kept as parallel edits rather than a shared classifier: the engine, independent, and hand-derived legs exist to catch a wrong comparison in any one site, and sharing the classifier would collapse that independence. Three new literal pins carry source-derived expectations for the exact edge (guideline and band percentages from the law table, benchmarks from the fictional sample household) in both the fast and full boundary sets, so the fast check now also catches a reintroduced float comparison. The stale comments describing the float behavior in the boundary module are rewritten. Untouched: every other engine file, the law tables, the December reference case (not a band edge), the client, and all other files.

Verification (code-level, complete — server-side, no render step): regression gate priced before and after on the tree as received — zero differing leaves, baseline hash reproduced, December reference case exact on every figure; a pre-run scan named in advance that no gate leaf sits exactly on a band edge. Full hardening registry fast and full: 26/26, teeth 44; boundary fast (28 pins) and full (303 pins) pass with zero failures. Float-reintroduction check in a disposable copy (engine-only revert of the band-match line): the fast check fails on the literal pins alone and the full check fails on the generated plus literal pins, as predicted. Chunked tax census (24 chunks of 25): 595/595 with zero failures — five chunks were OOM-killed under parallel batches and passed on the designed sequential retry. Typecheck clean on both configs; scrub zero over the diff and this entry.

## Follow-up (2026-11-10): Sensitivity strips require the winner to strictly beat an independently repriced Do Nothing (ChatGPT round-10 F2)

Server-side test-module fix, no engine change, no client change, no API contract change. The optimizer sensitivity strips (return strip and heir-rate strip) asserted only that adjacent net costs were non-decreasing, recording winner names without ever asserting them — so a sensitivity helper returning Do Nothing as its winner still passed, at every rate, even though Do Nothing costs far more than the true winner. At every point on both strips the reported winner's net cost must now be strictly less than Do Nothing repriced independently: the same two calls the pricer itself uses for its Do Nothing entry (simulate the "none" strategy, then score it), applied directly to the same shifted inputs — never the doNothing field from the sensitivity helper, which comes from the same run whose winner is being checked. The comparison is strict, not equal-or-better: the defect it catches makes the winner equal to Do Nothing, and equal-or-better would still pass. The same assertion extends to the return strip, whose helper returns the winner only and carries no reference candidate at all. The repriced Do Nothing is a second pricing of the same candidate through the same code path, so on a clean tree it agrees with the strip's own Do Nothing to the cent at every point. The direct two-call reprice, rather than a full candidate search per point, is deliberate: a full search per point put the worker-run fast registry near its time cap, while the direct call prices the identical entry — verified to the cent — at one simulation instead of a full search. A second teeth corruption case sets the heir winner's cost to Do Nothing's cost at all three points (the equality case) and requires exactly three failures naming the violation; the existing reversed-monotonicity case still yields exactly six. The module header and the registry summary now describe the strict-beats assertion and the updated timings. Residual limitation, recorded in the module header and here, not built: strict-beats-Do-Nothing does not catch a mid-pack substitution — a winner that is not Do Nothing but is not the cheapest candidate still beats Do Nothing; full minimality would require pinning a known-good winner spec, which is an option for a later pick, not part of this fix. Untouched: the engine, the law tables, the December reference case, the client, and all other files.

Verification (code-level, complete — server-side, no render step): regression gate priced before and after on the tree as received — zero differing leaves out of the full set, baseline hash reproduced, December reference case exact on every figure. Mutation check in a disposable copy (sensitivity helper returning Do Nothing as the winner): the full check fails at all three heir points, each failure naming the winner's cost and the independently repriced Do Nothing as equal, and the return strip still passes; teeth on the mutated tree correctly refuses with a clean-run-failed report. Clean full run passes with no failures, and the repriced Do Nothing agrees with the strip's own Do Nothing to the cent at every point on both strips. Teeth on the clean tree pass with nine failures (six reversed-monotonicity plus three winner-equals-Do-Nothing). Full hardening registry fast and full: 26/26, teeth 76 (up from 73; the new teeth leg contributes the added failures). Typecheck clean on both configs; scrub zero over the diff and this entry.
